title: Advanced Install Methods
description: Alternate, scripted, and unattended Breeze agent installs: ZIP bundles, MSI properties, direct binary enrollment, and the full flag reference.

sections.text:
The [Quick Install](/agents/installation/) page covers the happy path — a pre-configured MSI or PKG built by the dashboard. This page documents the alternate paths used for **silent deployment, MDM, scripted rollouts, air-gapped installs, and environments where Breeze's MSI signing service is not configured**.

If you just want to install on a single machine, use the dashboard installer instead. For end-to-end GPO, Intune, JAMF, and Ansible rollout recipes built on these methods, see the [Mass Deployment guide](/migration/mass-deployment/).

sections.heading: Picking a Method
sections.text:
| Method | When to use |
|---|---|
| [ZIP bundle](#zip-bundle-msi--enrollmentjson--installbat) | Default fallback when no remote MSI signing service is wired up. Self-contained: signed MSI + credentials + script. |
| [MSI with properties](#msi-with-properties-silent-install) | Available when the signing service is configured. Single signed file, properties embedded at sign time or passed at `msiexec`. |
| [Direct binary + `enroll`](#direct-binary--manual-enroll) | Custom packaging, MDM, Ansible/Chef/Puppet, or container images. Most flexible. |
| [Public installer link](/agents/installation/#public-installer-links) | Hand off install to an on-site contact via a token-authenticated URL. |

---

sections.heading: ZIP Bundle (MSI + enrollment.json + install.bat)
sections.text:
When the API does **not** have an MSI signing service configured, the dashboard generates a **zip bundle** instead of a property-injected MSI. The same fallback exists for macOS (PKG + `install.sh`).

This is also the format you get if you call the underlying `buildWindowsInstallerZip` / `buildMacosInstallerZip` paths directly — for example from your own automation calling the enrollment-key download endpoint.

sections.heading: Windows zip contents
sections.text:
- breeze-agent-windows.zip
  - breeze-agent.msi      The unmodified, signed agent MSI
  - enrollment.json       Server URL + enrollment key + secret + site ID
  - install.bat           Calls msiexec, then `breeze-agent enroll`

sections.heading: macOS zip contents
sections.text:
- breeze-agent-macos.zip
  - enrollment.json       Server URL + enrollment key + secret + site ID
  - install.sh            Downloads the arch-matched, notarized PKG, verifies it with Gatekeeper, then calls `installer -pkg` and `breeze-agent enroll`

The PKG itself is no longer bundled in the zip — `install.sh` downloads the architecture-matched package (Intel or Apple Silicon) at install time, so one zip works on both.

sections.heading: Running the bundle
sections.text:
**Windows:**
    Extract the zip to any directory, then run `install.bat` **as Administrator**:

```powershell
    Expand-Archive breeze-agent-windows.zip -DestinationPath C:\breeze-install
    cd C:\breeze-install
    Start-Process -FilePath .\install.bat -Verb RunAs -Wait
```

    The script will:

    1. Run `msiexec /i breeze-agent.msi /quiet /norestart`
    2. Wait 5 seconds for install to settle
    3. Read `enrollment.json` and invoke `"%ProgramFiles%\Breeze\breeze-agent.exe" enroll <key> --server <url> [--enrollment-secret <secret>]`
    4. Delete `enrollment.json` so credentials do not persist on disk

  **macOS:**
```bash
    unzip breeze-agent-macos.zip -d ~/breeze-install
    cd ~/breeze-install
    sudo ./install.sh
```

    The script will:

    1. Detect the Mac's CPU architecture (Intel or Apple Silicon) and download the matching, notarized `breeze-agent.pkg` from the server
    2. Verify the download passes Gatekeeper's notarization assessment (`spctl --assess`) before installing it as root
    3. `sudo installer -pkg breeze-agent.pkg -target /`
    4. Read `enrollment.json` via `plutil -extract`
    5. Invoke `sudo <agent> enroll <key> --server <url> [--enrollment-secret <secret>]`, where `<agent>` is the binary the package installed: `/Library/Breeze/bin/breeze-agent` when the package put it there, otherwise `/usr/local/bin/breeze-agent` (the site comes from the enrollment key; the installer no longer passes the deprecated `--site-id`)
    6. Delete `enrollment.json` and the downloaded pkg

  `enrollment.json` contains a one-time enrollment secret and a usage-limited child enrollment key. Treat the zip the same as you would any short-lived credential — distribute over a trusted channel and let the bundled script delete the file on first run.

sections.heading: `enrollment.json` schema
sections.text:
```json
{
  "serverUrl": "https://breeze.yourdomain.com",
  "enrollmentKey": "64-char-lowercase-hex",
  "enrollmentSecret": "shared-AGENT_ENROLLMENT_SECRET",
  "siteId": "uuid-of-target-site"
}
```

| Field | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `serverUrl` | yes | Passed as `--server` to the agent. Validated server-side at zip generation. |
| `enrollmentKey` | yes | 64 lowercase hex chars. Server-side regex: `^[a-f0-9]{64}$`. |
| `enrollmentSecret` | optional | Only set when `AGENT_ENROLLMENT_SECRET` is required by the server. Maps to `--enrollment-secret`. |
| `siteId` | yes | Site UUID, for reference only. The device always lands in the site the enrollment key resolves to. The installers no longer pass it as `--site-id` (deprecated and ignored by the agent). |

If you write your own wrapper, you can ignore the bundled `install.bat` / `install.sh` and just feed the JSON values straight into `breeze-agent enroll` — see [Direct binary + manual enroll](#direct-binary--manual-enroll).

---

sections.heading: MSI with Properties (Silent Install)
sections.text:
When the API **does** have an MSI signing service configured, the dashboard returns a single signed MSI with credentials baked into the WiX properties at sign time. You can also pass these properties yourself via `msiexec`:

```powershell
msiexec /i breeze-agent.msi /qn `
  SERVER_URL=https://breeze.yourdomain.com `
  ENROLLMENT_KEY=<64-hex-enrollment-key> `
  ENROLLMENT_SECRET=<shared-enrollment-secret>
```

| Property | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `SERVER_URL` | Breeze API base URL. |
| `ENROLLMENT_KEY` | 64-hex enrollment key. Marked `Hidden="yes"` so it does not appear in MSI logs. |
| `ENROLLMENT_SECRET` | Optional `AGENT_ENROLLMENT_SECRET`. Marked `Hidden="yes"`. |

The MSI's `EnrollAgent` custom action runs `breeze-agent.exe enroll "[ENROLLMENT_KEY]" --server "[SERVER_URL]" --enrollment-secret "[ENROLLMENT_SECRET]" --quiet` directly during install — there is no PowerShell wrapper. A WiX `Launch Condition` enforces that `SERVER_URL` and `ENROLLMENT_KEY` are provided together (both or neither).

If neither property is set, the MSI installs the binaries but skips enrollment. You can then enroll later by running `breeze-agent.exe enroll …` manually, which is useful when staging an image for cloning.

  There is no `SITE_ID` MSI property. Site assignment is encoded in the enrollment key on the server, so a key created against site X can only enroll devices into site X.

---

sections.heading: Direct Binary + Manual Enroll
sections.text:
For MDM, configuration management (Ansible, Chef, Puppet, Salt), golden images, or container/VM templates, install the agent binary yourself and call `enroll` once the host is provisioned.

  **Linux:**
```bash
    curl -fsSL -o /usr/local/bin/breeze-agent \
      https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/agents/download/linux/amd64
    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/breeze-agent

    sudo /usr/local/bin/breeze-agent enroll <ENROLLMENT_KEY> \
      --server https://breeze.yourdomain.com \
      --enrollment-secret <ENROLLMENT_SECRET> \
      --quiet

    sudo /usr/local/bin/breeze-agent service install
```

  **macOS:**
```bash
    curl -fsSL -o /usr/local/bin/breeze-agent \
      https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/agents/download/darwin/arm64
    chmod +x /usr/local/bin/breeze-agent

    sudo /usr/local/bin/breeze-agent enroll <ENROLLMENT_KEY> \
      --server https://breeze.yourdomain.com \
      --enrollment-secret <ENROLLMENT_SECRET> \
      --quiet

    sudo /usr/local/bin/breeze-agent service install
```

  **Windows:**
```powershell
    # Older PowerShell/.NET defaults (e.g. Windows Server 2016) can omit
    # TLS 1.2, which makes Invoke-WebRequest fail outright.
    [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = `
      [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol -bor [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12

    Invoke-WebRequest `
      -Uri "https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/agents/download/windows/amd64" `
      -OutFile "C:\Program Files\Breeze\breeze-agent.exe"

    & "C:\Program Files\Breeze\breeze-agent.exe" enroll <ENROLLMENT_KEY> `
      --server https://breeze.yourdomain.com `
      --enrollment-secret <ENROLLMENT_SECRET> `
      --quiet

    & "C:\Program Files\Breeze\breeze-agent.exe" service install
```

On macOS, this manual `service install` path (unlike the `.pkg` installer) always copies the binary to `/Library/Breeze/bin/breeze-agent` and the service runs from there, regardless of whether `/usr/local/bin` would otherwise be safe to run from. The copy you downloaded to `/usr/local/bin` is only used to enroll and install. See [macOS Permissions](/agents/macos-permissions/#agent-path-usrlocalbin-or-librarybreezebin) for when the `.pkg` installer instead leaves the agent in `/usr/local/bin`, and grant Full Disk Access at whichever path applies.

sections.heading: `breeze-agent enroll` — flag reference
sections.text:
| Flag | Required | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `<enrollment-key>` (positional) | yes | Single positional argument. 64-char enrollment key. |
| `--server <url>` | yes | API base URL. May also be set in the config file. |
| `--enrollment-secret <secret>` | optional | The server's `AGENT_ENROLLMENT_SECRET`. Required when configured server-side. |
| `--site-id <uuid>` | deprecated | Ignored: the site comes from the enrollment key. Passing it prints a deprecation warning; the flag will be removed in a future release. |
| `--device-role <role>` | optional | Override the inferred device role (e.g. `workstation`, `server`). |
| `--force` | optional | Re-enroll a host that already has a config. Replaces `agent_id` and `auth_token` only on success — a failed re-enroll leaves the existing config untouched. |
| `--quiet` | optional | Suppress stdout progress output. Errors still go to stderr. Use for unattended installs. |
| `--config <path>` | optional (persistent) | Override the default config path (`/etc/breeze/agent.yaml`, `/Library/Application Support/Breeze/agent.yaml`, or `C:\ProgramData\Breeze\agent.yaml`). |

The agent refuses to enroll with an empty hostname — if your provisioning pipeline runs `enroll` before `hostnamectl` / `scutil --set ComputerName`, set the hostname first.

sections.heading: `breeze-agent service install` — flag reference
sections.text:
| Flag | Platform | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `--no-watchdog` | all | Skip auto-fetching and registering the watchdog, and remember the choice: it writes the `watchdog.disabled` marker in the agent's config directory, so later plain `service install` runs and the running agent's automatic repair also leave the watchdog alone. Use for air-gapped hosts where the agent cannot reach GitHub releases or the Breeze server's watchdog download. |
| `--watchdog` | all | Undo `--no-watchdog`: remove the marker, reset the watchdog install retry state, and install the watchdog. Cannot be combined with `--no-watchdog`. |
| `--strict-watchdog` | all | Exit with code `78` instead of `0` when the agent installed but the watchdog could not be. See [exit codes](#service-install-exit-codes). |
| `--with-user-helper` | Linux, macOS | Also install the per-user desktop helper unit (systemd user unit / LaunchAgent). Not needed on Windows — the helper is spawned per-session by the service. |

`service install` is safe to re-run — it overwrites the binary at the install path, records whether the agent service was running beforehand, and rewrites and re-enables the unit. It starts the service again if it was running before the install or the host is already enrolled; a fresh, unenrolled host is left stopped until you enroll it. If the service was stopped for the install and can't be started again, the command now fails with recovery instructions rather than exiting successfully. It also registers any missing watchdog, which is always restarted so a newly staged binary takes over. Use this to add the watchdog to a previously agent-only install. To install only the watchdog without touching the agent, run `breeze-watchdog service install` directly.

#### `service install` exit codes

| Exit code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | The agent service is installed (and started when it was running before or the host is enrolled). The watchdog either installed, was skipped by `--no-watchdog` or a standing opt-out, or could not be installed and was **deferred** to the running agent. |
| `78` | Only with `--strict-watchdog`: the agent installed, but the watchdog did not. Any watchdog failure counts, whether or not the agent could repair it later. |
| `1` | The agent itself could not be installed, or its service was stopped for the install and could not be started again. This wins over the watchdog outcome: an agent failure is never reported as `0` or `78`. |

When the watchdog is deferred, `service install` prints the usual warning to stderr and one machine-readable line to stdout:

```text
BREEZE_WATCHDOG_INSTALL=deferred reason=<class>
```

`<class>` is one of `network`, `server`, `policy`, `signature`, `checksum`, `dev_build`, `unsupported_os`, `install_cmd`, `locked` or `unknown`. It never contains the error text. A failure while verifying the release download during the first install (before enrollment) often reports `unknown`; the warning on stderr has the detail. Nothing is printed when the watchdog installed or was skipped.

The default is `0` on purpose. The agent did install, and once the host is enrolled the running agent installs the missing watchdog by itself (see [Automatic repair of a missing watchdog](/features/watchdog#automatic-repair-of-a-missing-watchdog)), so reporting failure would break scripted installs that work today. Use `--strict-watchdog` in lanes that must not finish without a watchdog, for example golden-image builds. If the running agent is installing the watchdog at that moment, `service install` leaves the install to it and exits `0` without the marker line, even with `--strict-watchdog`.

On agent v0.110.0 and earlier, `service install` stopped the service and did not start it again. On those versions, follow it with `sudo systemctl restart breeze-agent breeze-watchdog` (Linux), or prefer the in-band auto-update instead.

On **Linux and macOS**, `service uninstall` stops and removes both the agent and watchdog services (and the installed agent binary), but does **not** remove `agent.yaml` or `secrets.yaml` — wipe `/etc/breeze` or `/Library/Application Support/Breeze` manually if you want a clean uninstall. On **Windows**, `service uninstall` only deletes the agent's own SCM service registration — it does **not** touch the watchdog service, the installed binaries, or `C:\ProgramData\Breeze`. Run `breeze-watchdog service uninstall` separately for the watchdog, and remove the binaries/config directory by hand.

---

sections.heading: Encrypted Client Hello (ECH)
sections.text:
Some home and small-office gateways ship a "security" feature (for example Comcast xFi Advanced Security or Spectrum Security Shield) that inspects the TLS server name (SNI) and answers on port 443 with a plaintext HTTP redirect for hosts on a threat feed. The agent then sees plaintext where it expected a TLS handshake and cannot reach the control plane. Encrypted Client Hello hides the server name from the gateway, so the filter has nothing to match.

The agent is **plain-first**. Nothing changes on a network that does not interfere:

- A host flips to ECH only after the agent sees the filter signature (plaintext HTTP answered on the TLS port) twice within 10 minutes, more than 30 seconds apart.
- In ECH mode the agent fetches the host's ECH config over DNS-over-HTTPS (Cloudflare `cloudflare-dns.com`, then Google `dns.google`; the query carries only the control-plane hostname) and caches it in `ech-cache.json` in the agent data directory. If ECH fails for any reason except a TCP connect failure (returned as-is, since plain would fail the same way), that same dial falls back to a plain connection, and a plain success returns the host to plain.
- Three consecutive ECH failures put ECH on a one-hour cooldown (plain only). Mode is kept in memory, so a restart starts plain.
- `enroll`, `bootstrap` and `support` retry with ECH on the first signature, so a first-run enrollment on a filtered network can succeed.

**How to tell:** the `control_plane` health component shows `warning` with the reason "control plane blocked by a network security filter (plaintext HTTP answered on the TLS port)" when the agent has seen the signature in the last 10 minutes and no plain connection has succeeded since, and `healthy` with "reachable via encrypted client hello" when ECH is carrying the connection. Heartbeats also carry `echActive` (true while the most recent successful connection to the control plane used ECH) and `filterSignatureSeenAt` (the last time a filter answered the handshake with plaintext HTTP; omitted once a plain connection has succeeded since).

**Opt out locally** by adding `ech: false` to `agent.yaml` and restarting the agent.

**Server kill switch:** set `AGENT_ECH_ENABLED=false` on the API. Agents receive it in their next heartbeat response and dial plain from then on. Live connections are not torn down; the change takes effect on the next dial. Until then a device still connected over ECH reports `echActive` and a `control_plane` `warning` with the reason "encrypted client hello disabled by control plane; the next reconnect dials plain". Turning `AGENT_ECH_ENABLED` off makes every device that currently depends on ECH dial plain on its next reconnect, so those devices go offline, and turning it back on cannot reach them until they are on an unfiltered network.

ECH needs the host to publish an ECH config in DNS. A self-hosted edge without one stays on plain connections, and `control_plane` keeps reporting the filter warning. ECH is also not applied to connections that go through an HTTP proxy (`HTTPS_PROXY`).

The installer downloaders (`install.sh` and the PowerShell one-liner) cannot use ECH yet; see [#8874](https://github.com/LanternOps/breeze/issues/8874). On a filtered network, download the MSI or pkg on another network, copy it to the filtered machine and run it there. Enrollment inside the installer works.

---

sections.heading: Pre-Staging Without Enrollment
sections.text:
You can install the agent binary and service on an image **without** enrolling, then enroll on first boot. This is the standard pattern for VM templates and golden images.

1. Install the agent binary (or run the MSI/PKG with no `ENROLLMENT_KEY`).
2. Install the service: `breeze-agent service install`. Because the host isn't enrolled yet, the installer enables the unit but leaves it **stopped** rather than starting it — there is nothing to talk to a server about until enrollment happens. It comes up automatically the next time the machine reboots (since the unit is enabled), or you can start it manually.
3. On first boot of a cloned VM, run `breeze-agent enroll <key> --server <url>` from a startup script. Once the agent process is actually running and unenrolled, it polls for `agent.yaml`/`secrets.yaml` on an interval and connects automatically as soon as `enroll` writes them — no restart needed.

If you skip step 2 and run `enroll` after `service install`, the service picks up the new credentials within a few seconds without needing a restart.

---

sections.heading: Programmatic Bundle Generation
sections.text:
If you are building your own provisioning system, the same zip bundles the dashboard produces are available via the enrollment-key API:

```http
POST /api/v1/enrollment-keys/:id/installer-link
```

This issues a token-authenticated download URL that returns either:

- A signed MSI / PKG with properties baked in (when the signing service is configured)
- A zip bundle (`breeze-agent-windows.zip` / the equivalent macOS zip) when not

Both responses set `Cache-Control: no-store` and `Content-Disposition: attachment`. The download is single-use by default and decrements the parent enrollment key's `maxUsage` atomically. See [Enrollment Keys](/agents/enrollment-keys/) for the full API.

title: Building from Source
description: Compile the Breeze agent from source: prerequisites, cross-platform build commands, Windows MSI packaging, version embedding, and testing.

sections.heading: Prerequisites
sections.text:
- Go 1.26.10 or later. With the default `GOTOOLCHAIN=auto`, `go build` fetches 1.26.10 on its own; with `GOTOOLCHAIN=local`, install Go 1.26.10 first.
- Make
- (Optional) `go-winres` for Windows resource embedding
- (Optional) WiX Toolset + PowerShell for MSI packaging

sections.heading: Build Commands
sections.text:
```bash
cd agent

# Build for current platform
make build

# Build for all platforms (Linux, macOS, Windows)
make build-all

# Build for specific platforms
make build-linux    # linux/amd64 + linux/arm64
make build-darwin   # darwin/amd64 + darwin/arm64
make build-windows  # windows/amd64
```

Output binaries are placed in `agent/bin/`.

sections.heading: Cross-Platform Builds
sections.text:
| Target | Command | Output |
|---|---|---|
| Linux amd64 | `make build-linux` | `bin/breeze-agent-linux-amd64` |
| Linux arm64 | `make build-linux` | `bin/breeze-agent-linux-arm64` |
| macOS Intel | `make build-darwin` | `bin/breeze-agent-darwin-amd64` |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `make build-darwin` | `bin/breeze-agent-darwin-arm64` |
| Windows amd64 | `make build-windows` | `bin/breeze-agent-windows-amd64.exe` |

sections.heading: Other Agent Binaries
sections.text:
`make build` (and plain `make build-all`) compiles the main `breeze-agent` binary plus its companion processes in one pass. Each companion also has its own current-platform and all-platforms targets:

| Binary | Purpose | Current-platform target | All-platforms target |
|---|---|---|---|
| `breeze-desktop-helper` | The end-user Helper process (AI chat, screenshots, tray icon) -- see [Helper](/agents/helper/) | `make build-desktop-helper` | `make build-all-desktop-helper` |
| `breeze-backup` | Runs backup, restore, and verify jobs dispatched by the agent -- see [Backup Management](/agents/commands/#backup-management) | `make build-backup` | `make build-all-backup` |
| `breeze-watchdog` | Restarts the agent service if it stops responding | `make build-watchdog` | `make build-watchdog-linux` / `-darwin` / `-windows` |
| `breeze-user-helper` | Windows-only sibling of `breeze-agent` that launches into the logged-in user's session (an `asInvoker` manifest, so it isn't blocked by UAC token filtering) | `make build-windows-user-helper` | -- (Windows-only) |

  `make build-all-desktop-helper` only builds the macOS (darwin amd64/arm64) variants -- there is no Linux or Windows target for it yet. `make build-all-backup` covers all three platforms.

sections.heading: Windows MSI Installer
sections.text:
To build an MSI installer for enterprise deployment:

```powershell
# On Windows with WiX installed:
make build-windows-msi VERSION=0.2.0
```

This produces `dist/breeze-agent.msi` for silent deployment via GPO or SCCM.

sections.heading: Version Embedding
sections.text:
The build embeds the version number via linker flags:

```makefile
VERSION ?= 0.5.0
LDFLAGS := -ldflags "-X main.version=$(VERSION)"
```

Override at build time:

```bash
make build VERSION=1.0.0
```

sections.heading: Display Branding
sections.text:
Operators building their own agent can set the display text Windows and Linux show for the agent and watchdog services, so your own name appears where users and admins read it. This is set at build time and is optional: a build with no branding values is identical to the official one.

Only display text can be branded. Service names (`BreezeAgent`, `BreezeWatchdog`), executable names, folders, the MSI's `ProductName` and `UpgradeCode` stay fixed, so updates, the installer and reliability scoring keep recognising the agent.

**Binaries.** Build through `agent/scripts/build-edition.sh` with any of these environment variables set:

| Variable | Sets |
|---|---|
| `BREEZE_BRAND_AGENT_DISPLAY_NAME` | Agent service display name |
| `BREEZE_BRAND_AGENT_DESCRIPTION` | Agent service description |
| `BREEZE_BRAND_WATCHDOG_DISPLAY_NAME` | Watchdog service display name |
| `BREEZE_BRAND_WATCHDOG_DESCRIPTION` | Watchdog service description |
| `BREEZE_BRAND_AGENT_CLI_SHORT` | One-line summary in the agent's command help |
| `BREEZE_BRAND_WATCHDOG_CLI_SHORT` | One-line summary in the watchdog's command help |

**Windows MSI.** `agent/installer/build-msi.ps1` accepts `-Manufacturer` (the publisher shown in Programs and Features), `-PackageDescription`, `-AgentServiceDisplayName`, `-AgentServiceDescription`, `-WatchdogServiceDisplayName` and `-WatchdogServiceDescription`. A service parameter left blank takes the matching `BREEZE_BRAND_*` value, and a parameter that differs from it is refused, so the MSI and the binaries always carry the same names.

A value is refused if it is longer than 256 bytes or contains a control character, a single or double quote, a backslash or a percent sign. The MSI also refuses square brackets, braces, `$(` and `!(`. Existing Linux installs keep their old service description until a later agent version rewrites the unit.

  The agent source code is in `agent/` at the repository root, **not** in `apps/agent/`. Both directories exist but serve different purposes.

sections.heading: Project Structure
sections.text:
```
agent/
├── cmd/breeze-agent/     # Entry point
├── internal/
│   ├── agent/            # Core agent loop
│   ├── commands/         # Command execution
│   ├── config/           # Configuration management
│   ├── discovery/        # Network discovery scanner
│   ├── heartbeat/        # Telemetry collection
│   ├── ipc/              # Inter-process communication
│   ├── mtls/             # mTLS certificate management
│   ├── pty/              # Terminal PTY handling
│   ├── sessionbroker/    # User session management
│   ├── transfer/         # File transfer
│   └── userhelper/       # User-mode helper process
├── scripts/install/      # Service installation scripts
├── service/              # systemd/launchd unit files
└── Makefile
```

sections.heading: Running in Development
sections.text:
```bash
cd agent
make run
```

This runs the agent directly without installing it as a service. Useful for testing against a local Breeze server.

sections.heading: Testing
sections.text:
```bash
cd agent
make test        # Run all tests
make test-ipc    # Run IPC and session broker tests
make lint        # Run golangci-lint
make fmt         # Format code
```

title: Commands & Config
description: Agent command execution and configuration: process, service, and scheduled task management, Windows event logs and registry, and power actions.

sections.text: The Breeze agent supports **120+ commands** organized into 30+ categories. Commands are sent from the API to agents over WebSocket, each with an `action` string and an optional JSON `payload`. This page documents the commands MSP admins and integrators use most often — it is not an exhaustive reference for every command type the agent implements.

sections.heading: Other Command Categories
sections.text:
The categories below exist in the agent but aren't covered in detail on this page. Most are driven by dedicated features elsewhere in the docs rather than sent ad hoc:

| Category | Actions | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| Software install/update | `software_install`, `software_update` | Push an install or version update for a specific package -- see [Software Inventory](/features/software-inventory/) |
| Backup ops (SQL Server / Hyper-V / bare metal) | `mssql_backup`, `mssql_restore`, `mssql_verify`, `hyperv_backup`, `hyperv_restore`, `hyperv_checkpoint`, `hyperv_vm_state`, `vm_restore_from_backup`, `vm_restore_estimate`, `bmr_recover` | Application-aware backup/restore for SQL Server and Hyper-V VMs, and full bare-metal recovery -- see the [Backup](/backup/overview/) docs |
| CIS remediation | `cis_benchmark`, `apply_cis_remediation` | Run a CIS benchmark scan and apply a specific remediation -- see [CIS Hardening](/features/cis-hardening/) |
| Incident response | `collect_evidence`, `execute_containment` | Collect forensic evidence from a device and isolate/contain it |
| Tunnel / proxy | `tunnel_open`, `tunnel_data`, `tunnel_close`, `http_request` | Relay a TCP tunnel (used for VNC and network-device access) or make a one-shot proxied HTTP request through the agent |
| PAM actuation | `actuate_elevation`, `pam_apply_v2`, `pam_cleanup_v2` | Type an approved elevation credential into the Windows UAC consent prompt, and apply/clean up PAM policy state -- see [PAM](/security/pam/) |
| Wake-on-LAN | `wake_on_lan` | Send a WOL magic packet to wake a sleeping device on the local network |
| Agent rollback | `agent_rollback_v1` | Roll the agent binary back to a previously installed version after a failed update |

sections.heading: Command Flow
sections.text:
```
Dashboard → POST /devices/:id/commands
         → BullMQ job created
         → WebSocket message sent to agent
         → Agent executes command
         → Agent sends result via WebSocket
         → Result stored in database
         → Dashboard receives real-time update
```

Commands with a `term-` prefix bypass the database queue and are sent directly over WebSocket for real-time terminal sessions.

sections.heading: Command Result Format
sections.text:
Every command returns a standard result envelope:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `status` | `string` | `completed`, `failed`, or `timeout` |
| `exitCode` | `int` | Exit code (0 for success) |
| `stdout` | `string` | JSON-encoded result data or script output |
| `stderr` | `string` | Error output (scripts only) |
| `error` | `string` | Error message when `status` is `failed` |
| `durationMs` | `int64` | Execution time in milliseconds |

sections.heading: System
sections.text:
Power management and session locking. Cross-platform.

| Action | Description | Key Payload Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `reboot` | Schedule a system reboot | `delay` |
| `shutdown` | Schedule a system shutdown | `delay` |
| `lock` | Lock the current user session | -- |
| `reboot_safe_mode` | Reboot into Safe Mode with Networking (Windows only) | `delay` |
| `force_reboot` | Reboot now and close running apps (Force reboot now) | -- |

The `reboot` and `shutdown` commands will immediately affect the target device. There is no confirmation prompt on the agent side. Use the `delay` parameter to give users time to save work.

sections.heading: `reboot` / `shutdown`
sections.text:
| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `delay` | int | `0` | Delay in minutes before executing (0-1440, i.e. max 24 hours) |

Platform behavior:
- **Windows**: Runs `shutdown /r /t <seconds>` (reboot) or `shutdown /s /t <seconds>` (shutdown)
- **Linux/macOS**: Runs `shutdown -r +<minutes>` (reboot) or `shutdown -h +<minutes>` (shutdown)

sections.heading: `lock`
sections.text:
No payload parameters. Locks the active session:
- **Windows**: `rundll32.exe user32.dll,LockWorkStation`
- **macOS**: `CGSession -suspend`
- **Linux**: `loginctl lock-session` (falls back to `dm-tool lock`)

sections.heading: `reboot_safe_mode`
sections.text:
Reboot a Windows device into Safe Mode with Networking. Uses `bcdedit` to set the safe boot flag before initiating a shutdown. If the shutdown command fails, the safe boot flag is automatically cleared to prevent accidental safe mode boots.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `delay` | int | `0` | Delay in minutes before rebooting (0-1440) |

  Windows only. Not available on macOS or Linux. The agent automatically clears the BCD safe boot flag if the shutdown command fails, preventing the device from booting into safe mode on the next organic restart.

sections.heading: `force_reboot`
sections.text:
An immediate reboot that closes running applications instead of waiting for them, so unsaved work in open apps is lost. Use it when an unattended device would otherwise stall on "this app is preventing shutdown". Plain `reboot` is unchanged.

No payload parameters, and no delay: it is always immediate. A delayed Windows reboot already closes apps when its countdown ends.

Platform behavior:
- **Windows**: Runs `shutdown /r /f /t 0`. Windows only implies `/f` when `/t` is greater than 0, so an immediate reboot needs it explicitly.
- **Linux/macOS**: Runs `shutdown -r +0`, the same as an immediate `reboot`. `shutdown -r` does not wait on applications, so force changes nothing.

The command result reports `force: true` and the exact `argv` that ran.

  Sent only by the device's **Force reboot now** action (`POST /devices/{id}/force-reboot`). That needs an interactive user session (API keys, MCP and AI agents are refused), `devices:execute`, MFA, and a single-use `device_force_reboot` step-up grant bound to the device. The operator also types the hostname to confirm. It is not available as a bulk action or from the generic command endpoint.

  The device must be online, and its agent must be 0.125.0 or later: an older agent fails `force_reboot` as an unknown command type, so the API refuses it before the grant is used. Like any reboot, it waits behind commands already running on the device. If it is not picked up within 15 minutes it expires, so it never fires hours later.

sections.heading: `set_auto_update`
sections.text:
Enable or disable automatic agent self-updates for the device. When disabled, the agent stops pulling and installing new versions on its own; you can still update it explicitly. The setting is written to the agent config and persists across restarts.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool | -- | `true` to enable auto-update, `false` to disable |

This command is also exposed directly as `POST /devices/:id/auto-update` with body `{ "enabled": <bool> }` — useful for re-enabling auto-update on agents that were left with it turned off (for example after a manual or recovery update).

sections.heading: `refresh_inventory`
sections.text:
Ask the agent to collect a fresh hardware/software inventory snapshot immediately instead of waiting for its scheduled run. The dashboard exposes this as the **Refresh Inventory** button on the device detail page; the API surface is `POST /devices/:id/commands` with `{ "type": "refresh_inventory" }`.

Duplicates are rejected while a `refresh_inventory` command for the device is still in `pending` status (not yet claimed by the agent): a second request returns `409 Conflict` with `code: "ALREADY_PENDING"`. This check only looks at `pending` status — once the agent has claimed the command, a new request is allowed even if the first one hasn't finished running yet. The bulk variant (`POST /devices/bulk/commands`) applies the same check per device and partitions its response into `commands` (newly issued), `skipped` (already-pending refreshes, each with the existing `commandId`), and `failed`.

sections.heading: `filesystem_analysis`
sections.text:
Deep filesystem scan that identifies large files, large directories, duplicate candidates, temp/cache accumulation, old downloads, unrotated logs, trash usage, and safe cleanup candidates.

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `path` | string | Required | Root directory to analyze |
| `scanMode` | string | `"baseline"` | `"baseline"` (deep) or `"incremental"` (targeted) |
| `maxDepth` | int | 32 (baseline) / 12 (incremental) | Max directory depth (1-64) |
| `topFiles` | int | `50` | Number of largest files to return (1-500) |
| `topDirs` | int | `30` | Number of largest directories to return (1-200) |
| `maxEntries` | int | `10,000,000` | Max filesystem entries to scan (1,000-25,000,000) |
| `timeoutSeconds` | int | `20` | Scan timeout (5-900 seconds) |
| `followSymlinks` | bool | `false` | Follow symbolic links |
| `workers` | int | auto | Parallel scan workers (1-32; auto-scaled to CPU count) |
| `targetDirectories` | string[] | -- | Specific directories for incremental scans |
| `checkpoint` | object | -- | Resume a previously interrupted scan |

The response includes `topLargestFiles`, `topLargestDirectories`, `tempAccumulation`, `oldDownloads`, `unrotatedLogs`, `trashUsage`, `duplicateCandidates`, `cleanupCandidates`, and a `summary` with scan statistics. If the scan is interrupted (timeout or max entries), `partial: true` is set along with a `checkpoint` that can be passed to resume.

sections.heading: `system_cleanup_list`
sections.text:
Returns the catalog of OS-native cleanup actions this device can perform. Read-only: it probes for the presence of each tool, checks write access where relevant, and — for the actions that have a non-mutating simulation mode — produces a size estimate. It removes nothing.

Takes no parameters.

The response contains `catalogVersion`, `volumesBefore` (per-volume free space at the time of the check), and an `actions[]` array. Each action carries `id`, `label`, `description`, `os`, `available`, an optional `unavailableReason`, `estimateBytes` / `estimateKnown` / `estimateDetail`, `riskFlags[]` and `affectsVolumes[]`. The Windows `win_cleanmgr` action also carries `subActions[]`, one per Disk Cleanup handler registered on that build.

  **Estimates are labelled by kind.** Measurable cache sizes are upper bounds; DISM component-store overhead, journal usage-minus-target and autoremove package sizes are heuristics. A direct `StartComponentCleanup` has no 30-day grace period, and its freed space is not equal to the reported overhead. `journalctl` vacuums archived journals only, and Time Machine snapshot sizes are unknown. When a parser cannot read a tool's output, the action reports `estimateKnown: false` rather than `0` — "unknown" and "nothing to reclaim" are different answers.

Estimation runs concurrently with an overall three-minute cap; an action whose estimate does not finish inside it reports `estimateKnown: false`.

sections.heading: `system_cleanup_run`
sections.text:
Runs the selected catalog actions **sequentially**, in catalog order, and measures the result.

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `runId` | string | Yes | The `device_filesystem_cleanup_runs` row this result closes |
| `actionIds` | string[] | Yes | A non-empty subset of the catalog's ids |
| `params.journalVacuumBytes` | int | No | Target size for `linux_journal_vacuum` (64 MiB – 4 GiB, default 256 MiB) |

The response contains `runId`, an `actions[]` array (`id`, optional `subActions[]`, `status`, `exitCode`, `durationMs`, `outputTail`, `error`), `volumes[]` (`mount`, `freeBefore`, `freeAfter`) and `freedBytes`.

Per-action `status` values:

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `completed` | The tool ran and exited cleanly |
| `failed` | The tool ran and reported a problem |
| `timed_out` | This action overran its own cap and its process tree was terminated |
| `unavailable` | The tool is not present, or the agent cannot write where it needs to. Never attempted |
| `busy` | Another maintenance operation (a concurrent run, a patch job's package cleanup) held the agent's maintenance lock. Nothing was attempted; retry |
| `not_started` | The run's aggregate budget expired before this action's turn |

`freedBytes` is **measured**, not estimated: it is the sum over affected volumes of free-space-after minus free-space-before, floored at zero. One action failing does not stop the next.

The run is bounded by an aggregate budget — the sum of the selected actions' own timeouts plus ten minutes, capped at three hours — computed when the run is queued and recorded on it. Actions run **sequentially**, serialised across the whole agent process against each other and against package-manager maintenance, so two runs can never rewrite one another's Disk Cleanup selection.

Both command types are delivered **live-only**: a queued command expires after fifteen minutes rather than waiting days for a device to come back, because the cleanup run it belongs to is closed out on its own budget and a command that outlives it would act with nobody watching.

  The action catalog is closed. The only input the server accepts is a set of ids from a fixed list plus one bounded integer; every command line the agent runs is built from constants, with absolute binary paths, no shell, a per-action timeout and a 16 KiB output cap. `cleanmgr` handlers that touch user data or recovery state — Downloads, the recovery image, language packs, and all per-user caches — are excluded in code, and DISM is never invoked with `/ResetBase`.

Both command types require agent **0.115.0** or later. Older agents answer with `unknown command type:`, which the API surfaces as `409 agent_update_required`.

sections.heading: Remote Desktop
sections.text: Two remote desktop modes are available: WebRTC-based (legacy) and WebSocket-based streaming.

sections.heading: WebRTC (Legacy)
sections.text:
| Action | Description | Key Payload Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `start_desktop` | Start a WebRTC desktop session | `sessionId`, `offer`, `iceServers`, `startGeneration` |
| `stop_desktop` | Stop a WebRTC desktop session | `sessionId`, `terminalGeneration` |

#### `start_desktop`

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sessionId` | string | Yes | Unique session identifier |
| `offer` | string | Yes | WebRTC SDP offer |
| `iceServers` | array | No | Array of `{ urls, username, credential }` ICE server configs |
| `startGeneration` | string | No | Monotonic start/terminal generation for this session, as a canonical decimal string (never a JSON number). The agent refuses a start that is not strictly newer than every generation it has already seen for the session. Absent from servers that predate the fence; such starts are admitted. |

Returns `{ sessionId, answer }` where `answer` is the WebRTC SDP answer.

#### `stop_desktop`

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sessionId` | string | Yes | Session to stop |
| `terminalGeneration` | string | No | The generation at which the server declared the session terminal, as a canonical decimal string. The command id is `desk-stop-<sessionId>-<terminalGeneration>`; the agent's `completed` result for that exact id moves the server-side teardown phase from `pending` to `confirmed`. A stop installs a terminal tombstone for the session even when no session is running, so a start that arrives after its own stop is refused. |

Returns `{ stopped: true }`.

sections.heading: WebSocket Streaming
sections.text:
| Action | Description | Key Payload Fields |
|---|---|---|

#### `desktop_stream_start`

| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

#### `desktop_input`

| Param | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

| `event` | object | Yes | Input event object (see below) |

The `event` object fields:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `type` | string | Required. Event type: `mousemove`, `mousedown`, `mouseup`, `click`, `dblclick`, `keydown`, `keyup`, `scroll` |
| `x` | int | Mouse X coordinate |
| `y` | int | Mouse Y coordinate |
| `button` | string | Mouse button: `left`, `right`, `middle` |
| `key` | string | Key name for keyboard events |
| `delta` | int | Scroll delta |
| `modifiers` | string[] | Modifier keys: `ctrl`, `alt`, `shift`, `meta` |

#### `desktop_config`

| Param | Type | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sessionId` | string | Required | Session to update |
| `quality` | int | 1-100 | JPEG quality |
| `scaleFactor` | float | 0.0-1.0 | Image scale factor |
| `maxFps` | int | 1-30 | Maximum frames per second |

At least one of `quality`, `scaleFactor`, or `maxFps` must be provided.

sections.heading: Script Execution
sections.text:
Execute scripts on managed devices. Supports Bash, PowerShell, Python, and other interpreters. Both `script` and `run_script` invoke the same handler.

| Action | Description | Key Payload Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `script` / `run_script` | Execute a script | `content`, `language`, `timeoutSeconds`, `runAs`, `parameters` |
| `script_cancel` | Cancel a running script | `executionId` |
| `script_list_running` | List currently running scripts | -- |

sections.heading: `script` / `run_script`
sections.text:
| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `content` | string | Required | Script source code |
| `language` | string | `"bash"` | Script type: `bash`, `powershell`, `python`, `cmd`, etc. |
| `scriptId` | string | `""` | Reference ID for tracking |
| `timeoutSeconds` | int | `300` | Execution timeout (5 minutes default) |
| `runAs` | string | `""` | User context: `""` (system), `"user"` (interactive user), or a specific username |
| `parameters` | object | `{}` | Key-value map of script parameters |

When `runAs` is set to a username (or `"user"`), the agent forwards the script to the user-mode helper via IPC for execution in that user's session. If no helper is connected, the script falls back to local (system) execution.

sections.heading: `script_cancel`
sections.text:
| Param | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `executionId` | string | Yes | The **original `script` command's id** (`device_commands.id`), not the `script_executions` row id. The agent keys its in-memory running-script map on the command id, so sending the execution row id here is a silent no-op against the deployed fleet. |
| `scriptExecutionId` | string | No | The `script_executions` row id, sent alongside `executionId` for server-side bookkeeping. Older agents (pre-#3525) ignore this field. |
| `graceSeconds` | int | No | Grace period before escalating to a hard kill. `0`-`30`, default `5`. Ignored entirely on Windows — see below. |

Result (always a SUCCESS result, even when the process was not stopped):

```json
{ "executionId": "<the original executionId echoed back>", "outcome": "terminated" | "not_found" | "kill_failed", "cancelled": true | false }
```

`cancelled` is `true` only for `outcome: "terminated"` — the server only ever marks `script_executions.status = 'cancelled'` on this proof. `not_found` most often means the script had already finished and its result is in flight, not that the stop succeeded; `kill_failed` means the device tried and could not kill the process.

**No graceful phase on Windows.** Unix sends `SIGTERM`, waits up to `graceSeconds`, then `SIGKILL`s the process group. Windows skips straight to `TerminateJobObject` regardless of `graceSeconds`, because `GenerateConsoleCtrlEvent` requires a console shared with the target process and script children are launched with `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` — there is no console to signal.

sections.heading: `script_list_running`
sections.text:
No payload parameters. Returns `{ running: [...], count: N }`.

Returns `{ downloadedCount, failedCount, results[] }` with per-patch status. Sends progress events via WebSocket during download.

sections.heading: Reboot Management
sections.text:
Schedule, cancel, and check the status of managed reboots (separate from the immediate `reboot` system command).

| Action | Description | Key Payload Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `schedule_reboot` | Schedule a deferred reboot | `delayMinutes`, `reason`, `source`, `deadline`, `allowDeferral`, `maxDeferrals`, `deferralMinutes` |
| `cancel_reboot` | Cancel a scheduled reboot | -- |
| `get_reboot_status` | Get current reboot schedule state | -- |

sections.heading: `schedule_reboot`
sections.text:
| Param | Type | Required | Accepted range | If absent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `delayMinutes` | int | No | 1-10080 (minutes, up to 7 days) | Defaults to `60` |
| `reason` | string | No | any string | Defaults to `"Scheduled by administrator"` |
| `source` | string | No | `patch_job` (patch installs) or `maintenance_window` (maintenance sweeps) are the values Breeze itself sends | Defaults to `"manual"`. Echoed back on the heartbeat as `rebootStatus.source`, so a value outside `^[a-z0-9_]{1,32}$` is dropped by the server rather than stored |
| `deadline` | string (RFC 3339) | No | must parse as RFC 3339 | Defaults to `now + delayMinutes`. A non-empty but malformed value **fails the command** rather than falling back |
| `allowDeferral` | bool | No | `true` / `false` | **Absent means OFF.** A restart is never postponable unless this key is explicitly `true` |
| `maxDeferrals` | int | Only when `allowDeferral` is `true` | 1-10 | Ignored when `allowDeferral` is absent or `false`. When `allowDeferral` is `true`, an absent or out-of-range value **fails the command** |
| `deferralMinutes` | int | Only when `allowDeferral` is `true` | 5-1440 | Same as `maxDeferrals`: ignored unless `allowDeferral` is `true`, and an absent or out-of-range value then **fails the command** |

`maxDeferrals` and `deferralMinutes` are a hard contract, not a clamp target: a
value outside 1-10 or 5-1440 (respectively) causes the agent to **fail the
`schedule_reboot` command**, not coerce it to the nearest valid bound. The
ranges mirror the API's own CHECK constraints, so an out-of-range value can
only reach the agent via a forged or corrupted payload — clamping it would
mask that instead of surfacing a failed command.

Supported on Windows, Linux and macOS. The agent warns the logged-in user
immediately when the reboot is scheduled, follows up with reminders at 60, 15 and
5 minutes before (only where those land far enough apart to be worth sending),
and fires a final critical notice one minute out — which is also when the OS
shutdown countdown starts, so the countdown the user sees is the one the OS
honours. Every delay produces at least one warning, including delays shorter than
any reminder threshold.

For post-patch reboots the API does not choose the delay itself: it resolves
`rebootDelayMinutes` from the device's effective patch Configuration Policy
(default 15 minutes, range 1-1440), and the maintenance-window reboot path reads
the same setting.

The deferral fields come from the same policy (`rebootAllowDeferral`,
`rebootMaxDeferrals`, `rebootDeferralMinutes`) and are resolved once, when the
restart is scheduled -- editing the policy mid-countdown does not shrink a user's
remaining postponements. They are **off by default**, and an agent that predates
them ignores them, so the restart behaves exactly as it always has. A restart
issued inside a maintenance window has its `deadline` capped at the close of that
window.

sections.heading: `cancel_reboot`
sections.text:
No payload parameters. Returns `{ cancelled: true }` when a restart was
cancelled. When nothing is pending the command still completes, with
`{ cancelled: false, reason: "no_reboot_scheduled" }` — the restart you wanted
off is off, so it is not reported as a failure. Older agents fail that case
with `no reboot scheduled` instead.

Cancellation always stops the agent's own timers. If the OS shutdown countdown
has already started (the final minute), the agent also aborts it where the
platform allows — `shutdown /a` on Windows, `shutdown -c` on Linux. macOS cannot:
BSD `shutdown(8)` has no cancel flag, so the call reports the failure rather than
claiming a cancellation that did not happen.

sections.heading: `get_reboot_status`
sections.text:
No payload parameters. Returns the full `RebootState` object with schedule
details, including `notificationsPlanned` — how many user warnings the current
schedule will emit.

---

sections.heading: Network
sections.text:
Network discovery, SNMP polling, and connectivity checks for monitoring.

| `network_discovery` | Discover hosts on a network | `subnets`, `methods`, `portRanges`, `concurrency` |
| `snmp_poll` | Poll an SNMP device for metrics | `target`, `version`, `community`, `oids` |
| `network_ping` | Ping a host (ICMP with TCP fallback) | `target`, `count`, `timeout` |

| `network_http_check` | HTTP/HTTPS endpoint check | `url`, `method`, `expectedStatus`, `expectedBody`, `verifySsl` |
| `network_dns_check` | DNS record lookup check | `hostname`, `recordType`, `expectedValue`, `nameserver` |

sections.heading: `network_discovery`
sections.text:
| Param | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `subnets` | string[] | Required | CIDR subnets to scan (e.g. `["192.168.1.0/24"]`) |
| `excludeIps` | string[] | -- | IP addresses to skip |
| `methods` | string[] | `arp`, `ping`, `port_scan`, `snmp` | Scan methods: `ping`, `arp`, `port_scan` (or `ports`), `snmp` |
| `portRanges` | string[] | -- | Port ranges for port scanning (e.g. `["22", "80", "443"]`) |
| `snmpCommunities` | string[] | -- | SNMPv1/v2c community strings to try |
| `snmpCredentials` | object | -- | Structured SNMP credential (`version`, `username`, `authProtocol`, `authPassphrase`, `privacyProtocol`, `privacyPassphrase`, `port`, `timeout` in ms, `retries`); tried before `snmpCommunities`. `public` is only used when neither is set |
| `timeout` | int | `2` | Per-host timeout in seconds |
| `concurrency` | int | `128` | Max concurrent scan workers |
| `deepScan` | bool | `false` | Enable deep scanning (more ports, slower) |
| `identifyOS` | bool | `false` | Attempt OS fingerprinting |
| `resolveHostnames` | bool | `false` | Perform reverse DNS lookups |
| `jobId` | string | `""` | Job ID for tracking |

| `privPassword` | string | `""` | SNMPv3 privacy passphrase |
| `oids` | string[] | -- | OIDs to poll |

sections.heading: Backup Management
sections.text:
Run, list, stop, and verify backups using the configured backup provider.

| Action | Description | Key Payload Fields |
|---|---|---|
| `backup_run` | Start a backup job | -- |
| `backup_list` | List backup snapshots | -- |
| `backup_stop` | Stop a running backup | -- |

sections.heading: `backup_run`
sections.text:
No payload parameters. Requires backup to be configured on the agent. Returns `{ jobId, status, snapshotId, filesBackedUp, bytesBackedUp }`.

```json
{ "action": "backup_run", "payload": {} }
```

sections.heading: `backup_list`
sections.text: No payload parameters. Returns `{ snapshots[], count }`.

sections.heading: `backup_stop`
sections.text: No payload parameters. Stops the currently running backup job.

sections.heading: `backup_restore`
sections.text:
| Param | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snapshotId` | string | Yes | Snapshot to restore |
| `targetPath` | string | No | Directory to restore into. Defaults to the original file locations if omitted. |
| `selectedPaths` | string[] | No | Restore only these paths from the snapshot instead of the full snapshot. See [selective restore](/backup/restoring/) for matching behavior. |

Unlike `backup_test_restore`, `backup_restore` writes to `targetPath` (or the original locations) rather than a managed temp directory -- it is the action that actually puts files back in place.

```json
{
  "action": "backup_restore",
  "payload": { "snapshotId": "snap-20260329-0200", "targetPath": "/restore" }
}
```

`backup_test_restore`
`backup_cleanup`

sections.heading: `caller_verify`
sections.text:
Asks the **explicitly selected console user** to confirm a support request on their screen. It needs a current Breeze agent and a Breeze Assist helper that advertises the `callerVerify` capability. The API creates the command in the same transaction as the verification, sends it after commit, and the start request returns while the technician polls status. The command is never queued for an offline device; it expires with the verification.

| Payload field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `verificationId` | Verification UUID |
| `username` | Explicit OS login on that device; there is no "preferred user" fallback |
| `technicianName`, `orgName` | Shown on the card |
| `actionLabel`, `targetLabel` | The exact requested action and account |
| `reverseCode` | Four-digit request code shown on the card |
| `choices` | Three distinct two-digit numbers, in display order |
| `timeoutMs` | 30,000–300,000 ms |
| `deadlineAt` | Optional. The verification's absolute expiry (ISO 8601). A command delivered late counts down only to this time (plus a 5-second clock-skew allowance), never longer than `timeoutMs`, and is not shown at all once it has passed; the agent then reports `"timeout"`. Older agents and helpers ignore it. |

The result (`stdout` JSON) contains `delivered`, an optional `choice` (one of the three numbers, `"not_me"` or `"timeout"`), an optional `principal` (exactly one of `sid` or numeric `uid`, plus `username` and an optional OS-provided `upn`), an optional `helperVersion`, and on `delivered: false` an `error` of `no_session_for_user`, `session_not_console` or `helper_outdated`. The agent reports the OS principal itself; the helper never supplies identity.

- Only the Assist helper in the user's **active console session** can show the card. Remote (RDP/SSH) sessions and native user helpers cannot.
- Closing the window, losing the helper, an unexpected answer or reaching the deadline never approves.
- "This is not me" is honoured even after the command already finished, over either transport.
- An answer from a principal already bound to the contact's directory identity is tier 3; any other workstation answer is tier 1.
- Number matching confirms the request; it does not prove the technician's identity. If unsure, hang up and call the MSP on a number you already have.

The feature stays hidden behind `CALLER_VERIFICATION_ENABLED`. Promote both the agent and the Assist helper before expecting workstation availability; the agent reports readiness in each heartbeat (`helperCapabilities`).

---

sections.heading: Command Timeouts
sections.text:
The API runs a **stale command reaper** every 2 minutes that cleans up commands stuck in `pending` or `sent` status. Each command type has a timeout tier that determines how long the system waits before marking it as failed:

| Tier | Duration | Command types |
|------|----------|---------------|
| **Short** | 5 min | Process management, service management, event logs, scheduled tasks, registry, file operations, screenshots, computer actions, security status collection |
| **Medium** | 30 min | Security scans, patch scans, software uninstall, filesystem analysis, safe mode reboot, self-uninstall, evidence collection, containment actions, reliability metrics, CIS remediation, `backup_restore` |
| **Restore** | 60 min | VM restore/instant-boot, BMR recovery, MSSQL restore, Hyper-V restore |
| **Long** | 2 hours | Patch installation, backup verify/test-restore/cleanup, CIS benchmarks, sensitive data scans, file encryption/secure delete/quarantine |
| **Excluded** | Never reaped | Terminal sessions (`terminal_start`, `terminal_data`, `terminal_resize`, `terminal_stop`) |

Script commands use the script's own `timeoutSeconds` value (default 300s) plus a 5-minute grace buffer, so the server timeout is always slightly longer than the agent-side timeout.

When a command times out, it is marked `failed` with `timedOutBy: 'server'` in the error message.

---

sections.heading: Heartbeat Telemetry
sections.text:
By default, the agent sends a heartbeat every 60 seconds (configurable via `heartbeat_interval_seconds` in `agent.yaml`, clamped to a 5–3600 second range) containing:

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| `cpu` | CPU usage percentage |
| `memory` | Memory usage (used/total) |
| `disk` | Disk usage per mount point |
| `network` | Network interface stats |
| `uptime` | System uptime |
| `os` | OS name and version |
| `hostname` | Current hostname |
| `agentVersion` | Running agent version |
| `rebootStatus` | Scheduled-restart snapshot from the agent's reboot manager (`#3207`). See [Reboot status](#reboot-status) below |

sections.heading: Reboot status
sections.text:
`rebootStatus` is a three-way field, not a plain optional -- its meaning changes
between "the key is missing," "the key is `null`," and "the key holds an
object":

- **Absent from the heartbeat body** -- "no news." An agent built before this
  field existed omits `rebootStatus` entirely, and the server leaves the
  device's stored reboot columns untouched.
- **`rebootStatus: null`** -- there is no restart scheduled: it was cancelled,
  or it already fired. The server clears the stored columns.
- **`rebootStatus: { ... }`** -- the live schedule:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `scheduledAt` | string (RFC 3339, with offset) | Yes | When the restart will fire. The only required member -- a malformed value makes the server drop the whole `rebootStatus` object (treated the same as absent) rather than reject the heartbeat |
| `deadline` | string (RFC 3339, with offset) | No | Absolute cutoff past which the restart happens regardless of remaining deferral budget |
| `source` | string | No | What requested the restart, echoed back from the `schedule_reboot` command that scheduled it: `patch_job`, `maintenance_window`, or the agent's own `manual` default |
| `deferralsUsed` | int (0-10) | No | How many times the signed-in user has postponed this restart |
| `maxDeferrals` | int (0-10) | No | How many postponements this restart allows |

`maxDeferrals: 0` means this restart cannot be postponed at all, which is a
different statement from `maxDeferrals` being absent (an agent that predates
deferral reporting). Do not treat the two as equivalent.

---

sections.heading: User-Mode Helper
sections.text:
The agent includes a user-mode helper process for operations that require user-session context:

- Desktop notifications (`notify_user`)
- User-specific inventory (installed apps, browser extensions)
- Session-aware remote desktop
- Script execution as a specific user (`runAs`)
- System tray icon updates (`tray_update`)

Install the user helper:

  **Linux:**
```bash
sudo make install-user-helper
systemctl --user enable breeze-agent-user
```

  **macOS:**
```bash
sudo make install-user-helper
# LaunchAgent auto-starts at login
```

  **Windows:**
No manual step needed. The MSI installer registers a **Scheduled Task** (`\Breeze\AgentUserHelper`) that launches `breeze-user-helper.exe` at user logon, as part of installing the agent -- there is nothing extra to run.

title: Enrollment Keys
description: Create, scope, rotate, and manage enrollment keys for onboarding Breeze agents, covering TTL, usage limits, site pinning, and per-key secrets.
headings: How Agent Enrollment Uses the Key
The practical consequence: this also shortens the completion window, not just the download window
"Enrollment key must be associated with a site" (400)
Key appears valid but agent fails to connect after enrollment

sections.text:
Enrollment keys are short-lived, usage-limited tokens that authorize new agents to register with the Breeze API. Each key is scoped to an organization and optionally pinned to a specific site, ensuring that agents land in the correct place in the multi-tenant hierarchy without exposing long-lived credentials.

---

sections.heading: Key Concepts
sections.text:
| Concept | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| **Enrollment key** | A 64-character hex string (32 random bytes) presented by the agent during the `POST /api/v1/agents/enroll` call. |
| **SHA-256 + pepper** | The raw key is never stored. It is hashed with a server-side pepper before being written to the database. |
| **TTL (`expiresAt`)** | Time-to-live. After this timestamp the key is rejected. Default: the partner/organization default expiry if one is set in **Device enrollment** settings, otherwise 30 days from creation (see `ENROLLMENT_KEY_DEFAULT_TTL_MINUTES`). |
| **Max usage (`maxUsage`)** | Maximum number of successful enrollments allowed. Default: the partner/organization default device count if one is set in **Device enrollment** settings, otherwise 1. Range: 1 -- 100,000. |
| **Usage count (`usageCount`)** | Incremented atomically on each successful enrollment. Once it reaches `maxUsage`, the key is exhausted. |
| **Site pinning (`siteId`)** | When set, every agent that enrolls with this key is placed into the specified site. The enrollment endpoint requires a `siteId` to be present on the key. |
| **Enrollment secret** | A separate, static secret (`AGENT_ENROLLMENT_SECRET` environment variable) that gates the enrollment endpoint in production. This is independent of the enrollment key itself. |

  Enrollment keys and the enrollment secret serve complementary roles. The **enrollment secret** is a static gate that controls _whether_ the enrollment endpoint accepts requests at all. The **enrollment key** controls _where_ the agent lands (org, site) and _how many_ agents can enroll.

---

sections.heading: Per-Key Enrollment Secrets
sections.text:
Each enrollment key can optionally have its own **enrollment secret**, separate from the global `AGENT_ENROLLMENT_SECRET` environment variable. When a per-key secret is set, it takes priority over the global secret during enrollment.

This is useful when you want to restrict enrollment to specific keys with unique credentials -- for example, giving each customer site its own secret so that a leaked key from one site cannot be used with another site's installer.

Per-key secrets are set when creating or rotating a key. If no per-key secret is set, the global `AGENT_ENROLLMENT_SECRET` is used as usual.

  Per-key secrets and the global enrollment secret serve the same gating purpose. The per-key secret simply lets you scope that gate to individual keys rather than sharing one secret across all enrollments.

---

sections.heading: Installer Downloads
sections.text:
Each enrollment key can generate a pre-configured Windows MSI installer, and — for macOS — a zip containing the **Breeze Installer.app** GUI bundle (see [macOS GUI Installer](/agents/installation/#macos-gui-installer)). Both are pre-loaded with the enrollment key and site assignment, so agents enroll automatically when the installer runs. macOS falls back to the legacy PKG + `install.sh` zip bundle (see [Advanced Install Methods](/agents/advanced-install/#zip-bundle-msi--enrollmentjson--installbat)) when the app-bundle asset isn't available or the server runs on a nonstandard host/port.

When MSI signing is configured on the server, Windows installer downloads are automatically code-signed before delivery — Windows SmartScreen and antivirus tools will recognize them as trusted. See [Code Signing](/deploy/code-signing/) for setup details.

  **Windows MSI filename token.** The Windows MSI embeds the enrollment token directly in its filename as a `(TOKEN@HOST)` block — for example `Breeze Agent (ABCD1234XY@breeze.example.com).msi`. You can rename the file freely **as long as the `(TOKEN@HOST)` block is preserved**. A browser-added dedup suffix like `(1)` is harmless. If the block is removed entirely (e.g. the file is fully renamed without it), the installer falls back to requiring the enrollment key and server URL entered manually during setup. (Older downloads used square brackets, `[TOKEN@HOST]`; the installer still recognizes that legacy form.)

sections.heading: Downloading from the Dashboard
sections.text:
From the enrollment key list or detail view, click **Download Installer** and choose the platform (Windows or macOS). The installer is generated on the fly and downloaded to your browser.

The Enrollment Keys list shows each key's **installer capacity** — how many of the installer's enrollment slots have been used (for example `2 / 7` after downloading an installer for seven devices and enrolling two). The figure and the key's status badge are derived from the installer's **live** (unexpired) enrollment slots, so a fully expired installer shows as expired rather than as unused capacity, and the **Hide expired** filter agrees with the badge.

sections.heading: Downloading via API
sections.text:
```bash
# Download a pre-configured installer for a specific key
curl -OJ https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/enrollment-keys/KEY_UUID/installer/windows \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

curl -OJ https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/enrollment-keys/KEY_UUID/installer/macos \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

sections.heading: Public Download Links
sections.text:
You can generate a shareable, token-authenticated URL so that site contacts can download the installer without needing dashboard access.

```bash
# Generate a public download link
curl -X POST https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/enrollment-keys/KEY_UUID/installer-link \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# The response includes a URL like:
# /api/v1/enrollment-keys/public-download/windows?token=...
```

Share the resulting URL with on-site contacts. Public download links are rate-limited to prevent abuse.

sections.heading: Short Codes (`/s/<code>`)
sections.text:
Public installer links are also issued with a short, human-friendly URL of the form `https://breeze.yourdomain.com/s/<code>`. The short URL automatically detects the requester's platform and serves the correct installer (Windows MSI or macOS PKG), and increments the enrollment key's `usageCount` atomically — so the same `maxUsage` limit applies whether the installer is downloaded via the long-form link or the short link.

Short codes are convenient for sharing in email, chat, or printed runbooks. The platform is selected per-request from the User-Agent and can be overridden with a `?platform=windows` or `?platform=macos` query parameter.

In the dashboard, the enrollment key list shows each key's short code in a **Short code** column with a copy-to-clipboard button — this replaces the previous always-masked KEY column, which never revealed anything useful. A **Hide expired** toggle above the list filters out keys that have already expired.

sections.heading: Installer Bootstrap Tokens
sections.text:
Every installer download, installer-link generation, or short-code redemption mints an `installer_bootstrap_tokens` row: a single-use-by-default token embedded in the installer that authenticates its first-run `/bootstrap` call, independent of the interactive enrollment key that produced it.

**A bootstrap token now outlives its parent enrollment key (#2775):**
  Previously, an installer's usable life was capped to its parent enrollment key's *remaining* life, and redemption returned `404` once the parent expired — so a 30-day installer link minted from the Add Device modal's transient ~60-minute parent key died in under an hour. As of this release, the bootstrap token's own `expiresAt` is the sole authority on whether an installer can still enroll a device; the parent key's expiry is no longer checked at redemption time. Revocation still works exactly as before: deleting the parent enrollment key cascade-deletes (`ON DELETE CASCADE`) every outstanding bootstrap token immediately, so a deliberate delete remains an effective kill switch.

The token's TTL is the admin's chosen expiry, or `INSTALLER_BOOTSTRAP_TOKEN_TTL_MINUTES` (default 7 days) when none is chosen, clamped to the partner's `maxEnrollmentLinkTtlMinutes` cap if one is set — see [Partner & Organization Enrollment Defaults](#partner--organization-enrollment-defaults). It is never more than **30 days** (`43200` minutes):

- `GET /enrollment-keys/:id/installer/:platform` and `POST /enrollment-keys/:id/bootstrap-token` reject an explicit `ttlMinutes` above `43200` with `400` (`ttlMinutes exceeds the installer maximum of 43200 minutes (30 days)`). The same limit applies to the child enrollment key embedded in the legacy macOS zip.
- Installer links (`POST /enrollment-keys/:id/installer-link`) and enrollment keys are not installers and keep their own lifetimes (up to 1 year). Each installer downloaded from a link carries a token that lives for the link's remaining time, at most 30 days.
- Tokens already issued keep the expiry they were issued with. The daily purge sweep also will not delete a parent enrollment key while it still has a live, unexhausted bootstrap token outstanding, even past the key's own grace period — see [Automatic Purge of Expired Keys](#automatic-purge-of-expired-keys).

---

sections.heading: Creating a Key
sections.text:
1. Authenticate with a user session that has the `organizations:write` permission and has completed MFA.
2. Send a `POST` request to `/api/v1/enrollment-keys` with the desired scope.
3. Copy the `key` field from the 201 response. This is the only time the raw key is returned.
4. Embed the key in your agent installer, deployment script, or MDM payload.

```bash
curl -X POST https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/enrollment-keys \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "orgId": "ORG_UUID",
    "siteId": "SITE_UUID",
    "name": "Chicago Office Q1 Deploy",
    "maxUsage": 50,
    "expiresAt": "2026-04-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

**Request body:**

| Field | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|-------|------|----------|---------|-------------|
| `orgId` | `uuid` | Depends | Inferred for org-scoped users | Target organization. Required for partner and system scopes. |
| `siteId` | `uuid` | No | `null` | Pin enrolled agents to a specific site. The enrollment endpoint will reject keys without a `siteId`. |
| `name` | `string` | Yes | -- | Human-readable label (1--255 characters). |
| `maxUsage` | `integer` | No | Partner/org default device count if set, else `1` | Maximum enrollments allowed (1--100,000). |
| `expiresAt` | `datetime` | No | Now + TTL | ISO 8601 absolute expiration. Must be in the future; a past value is rejected with `400` (`Expiry must be in the future`). Mutually exclusive with `ttlMinutes`. |
| `ttlMinutes` | `integer` | No | Now + TTL | Lifetime in minutes from creation (1 to 525600, i.e. up to 365 days). Mutually exclusive with `expiresAt`. |

When neither `expiresAt` nor `ttlMinutes` is supplied, the key expires after the partner/organization default expiry if one is set in **Device enrollment** settings (capped at the partner maximum); otherwise after `ENROLLMENT_KEY_DEFAULT_TTL_MINUTES` (default 43200 — 30 days). The same applies to `maxUsage`: an omitted value uses the configured partner/organization default device count, otherwise 1. Supplying both is rejected so the resolved expiry is unambiguous.

`POST /enrollment-keys` and `POST /enrollment-keys/:id/rotate` reject any field that isn't in the table above — there is no `PATCH` method on enrollment keys; use `rotate` to change `maxUsage`/`expiresAt` on an existing key. A typo like `maxUses` (instead of `maxUsage`) now returns `400 Bad Request` with a precise field-name error rather than silently dropping the value — useful when scripting key creation against earlier API examples that used different field names.

  The default TTL is configurable via the `ENROLLMENT_KEY_DEFAULT_TTL_MINUTES` environment variable (30 days if unset). A partner/organization default expiry set in **Device enrollment** settings takes precedence for keys created with `POST /enrollment-keys`.

  Every path now shares that fallback, including keys minted through the partner-provisioning API and installer child keys. `CHILD_ENROLLMENT_KEY_TTL_MINUTES` remains available to give installer child keys a shorter life than the shared default; leave it unset and they inherit the same 30 days.

  In the dashboard, the **Add Device** modal has a **Link expires in** picker that sets the per-link lifetime without changing the server's environment default. The picker sends `ttlMinutes`. On the **Installer** tab it offers up to 30 days, the most a downloaded installer can carry (earlier releases also offered 90 days and 1 year there); if your partner or organization default is longer, the Installer tab preselects 30 days. On the **CLI** tab, which creates an enrollment key, it offers up to 1 year. Both are further limited by the partner cap.

  In the dashboard, the **Create key** form now includes a required **Site** selector (plus an **Organization** selector when the caller can see more than one org), so keys created in the UI are always correctly site-bound and pass the enrollment endpoint's `siteId` requirement.

**Response (201):**

```json
{
  "id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "orgId": "ORG_UUID",
  "siteId": "SITE_UUID",
  "name": "Chicago Office Q1 Deploy",
  "usageCount": 0,
  "maxUsage": 50,
  "expiresAt": "2026-04-01T00:00:00.000Z",
  "createdBy": "USER_UUID",
  "createdAt": "2026-03-02T12:00:00.000Z",
  "key": "a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a9b0c1d2e3f4a5b6c7d8e9f0a1b2"
}
```

  The `key` field is only included in the response when a key is created or rotated. It is stripped from all other responses. Store it immediately in a secure location.

---

sections.heading: Listing Keys
sections.text:
```bash
# All non-expired keys for the authenticated org
curl https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/enrollment-keys?expired=false \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# Filter by org (partner/system scope)
curl "https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/enrollment-keys?orgId=ORG_UUID&page=1&limit=25" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

**Query parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `page` | `string` | Page number (default `1`). |
| `limit` | `string` | Results per page (default `50`, max `100`). |
| `orgId` | `uuid` | Filter by organization. |
| `expired` | `true` or `false` | Filter by expiration status. |

The response includes a `pagination` object with `page`, `limit`, and `total` fields.

---

sections.heading: Rotating a Key
sections.text:
Rotation generates new key material for an existing record while resetting `usageCount` to zero. Use it to extend a deployment window or reissue a compromised key without changing the key ID.

```bash
curl -X POST https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/enrollment-keys/KEY_UUID/rotate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "maxUsage": 100,
    "expiresAt": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z"
  }'
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `maxUsage` | `integer` or `null` | No | New limit. Pass `null` for unlimited. Omit to keep the current value. |
| `expiresAt` | `datetime` | No | New expiration. Must be in the future (a past value is rejected with `400`). Omit to keep the current value. |

The old key value is immediately invalidated. The response includes the new `key` field.

**Shortening expiry via rotate no longer revokes outstanding installers:**
  Rotating a key to an earlier `expiresAt` used to also kill any installer bootstrap tokens issued from it, via a `parent_already_expired` check enforced at redemption time. That check has been removed (#2775) now that a bootstrap token's own expiry is authoritative — see [Installer Bootstrap Tokens](#installer-bootstrap-tokens). **If you were relying on shortening a key's expiry as a kill switch for installers already in the field, it no longer works** — this is a genuine loss of capability, not a bug. Outstanding installers keep working until their own bootstrap token expires. To revoke them immediately, delete the enrollment key instead: cascade-delete removes its bootstrap tokens right away.

---

sections.heading: Deleting a Key
sections.text:
Enrollment keys are **hard deleted** from the database. This is irreversible.

```bash
curl -X DELETE https://breeze.yourdomain.com/api/v1/enrollment-keys/KEY_UUID \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```
