Keys that stopped working after a sign-out on v0.120.0 are not revived: mint a replacement. See [API Keys](/reference/api-keys/#when-a-key-stops-working-because-of-its-creator).
- **Duplicate built-in alert rules are merged once at upgrade.** The oldest copy is kept; if any copy was switched off, the merged rule is off. Open alerts from removed copies move to the kept rule, and where two were open for the same device the extra one is resolved as `source_retired`. The API logs `#7650: …` warnings with the counts.
- **Metric history.** On the first daily metric-rollup maintenance run, rows in the catch-all `metric_rollups_default` partition move into monthly partitions (rows past your 5-minute retention are discarded, as before). Until it finishes, those older points are missing from charts. Look for `[MetricRollupMaintenance] … drained metric_rollups_default: moved=N discarded=M`.
- **Quick Support** always shows the viewing indicator, whatever the device's remote access indicator setting, and AI screen tools are refused on Quick Support devices. See [Remote Access](/features/remote-access/#quick-support-ad-hoc-sessions).
- **Agent enrollment rate limit** is configurable with `AGENT_ENROLL_RATE_LIMIT` (default 10) per `AGENT_ENROLL_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS` (default 60), per source IP. Raise it for mass deployments behind one NAT address. A non-integer or non-positive value stops the API from starting.
- **Breeze Viewer on Windows.** Viewers on 0.118–0.120 whose in-app update kept failing pick up 0.121.0 on their next launch; no reinstall is needed. A failed update now names the stage and the log path (`%LOCALAPPDATA%\com.breeze.viewer\logs\updater.log`). As a fallback, download `breeze-viewer-windows.msi` from the release and run it once.

#### Environment variables

**No new required variables**, except `IS_HOSTED=false` on `MCP_LLM_PROVIDER=openai-compatible` installs (above). New optional: `AI_PLATFORM_INFERENCE_GEO`, `AI_GATEWAY_HEADERS_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, `AGENT_ENROLL_RATE_LIMIT` and `AGENT_ENROLL_RATE_WINDOW_SECONDS`, all mapped in both Compose files. Deprecated (no longer read): `BREEZE_AI_SCRIPT_REVIEWER_MODEL`, `WORKSPACE_CONTENT_LLM_MODEL`.

#### Migrations

45 idempotent migrations apply on boot (`[auto-migrate] Applied 45 migration(s)`). Some are named earlier than v0.120.0's newest; they still apply, in order. Most are additive: tables for the AI registry cutover and AI chargeback, autopay foundation tables (off for every partner), new columns on AI, billing profile, user and API key tables, a unique index on built-in alert rules, the Partner API ticket groundwork (`ticket_external_refs`, and `tickets:read` / `tickets:write` as allowed service-principal scopes that have no effect yet), and a topology index.

- **Three indexes are built with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY`**, outside a transaction, so writes continue. If the `ai_budget_reservations` build is interrupted, the next start refuses with an "INVALID index" message: run `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY ai_budget_reservations_session_turn_idx;` and restart. The other two have no such guard, so check them after the upgrade:
```sql
  SELECT c.relname, i.indisvalid FROM pg_index i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid
   WHERE c.relname IN ('ai_invocations_chargeable_idx', 'idx_device_commands_install_patches_device_created');
```
  If either is `false`, drop it with `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY <name>;` and re-run the `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` from its migration (`2026-11-26-100150-ai-invocations-chargeable-idx.sql` or `2026-11-19-101100-device-commands-install-patches-index.sql`).
- **Brief locks.** A few constraint and index steps on AI session, budget and egress tables scan while holding a write lock (well under a second at 300,000 rows per table in testing; expect a few seconds of paused AI chat writes on very large tables). No migration sets a lock timeout, so a long idle-in-transaction session on these tables delays boot.
- **Device mTLS certificate repair.** One migration records every device's issued client certificate in the certificate history. It holds only a read lock on `devices`, so agents keep checking in, but it runs inside the boot and can add seconds to minutes on a large fleet. It always logs `WARNING device mTLS history reconcile: demoted <D> stale active rows, imported <I> issued certificates, skipped <S> devices…`. Demoted certificates are revoked at Cloudflare in the background, 200 every 5 minutes.

sections.heading: v0.119.0 — network topology, time sync, Xero, S3 restores through storage sessions
sections.text:
**Before you upgrade: coturn and HTTPS for S3 restores:**
  The v0.118.x Compose files pass `--denied-peer-ip=::` to coturn, which refuses every relayed (TURN) connection. Remove that line on every install, even if you skip v0.119.0; see [Compose file changes](#v01190--coturn-relays-again). S3 restores, test restores and verification now go only through a short-lived storage session, with no fallback: they need HTTPS end to end (MinIO endpoint and agent API), `PUBLIC_API_URL` set and matching, and agents on v0.118.0 or later. See [HTTPS for Restores](/backup/https-restores/).

**Security.** v0.119.0 fixes [GHSA-9qpw-p6rx-5f2h](https://github.com/LanternOps/breeze/security/advisories/GHSA-9qpw-p6rx-5f2h) (High, agent: restoring a Windows backup as a Hyper-V VM could run code from that backup on the host), [GHSA-c445-q84m-rph4](https://github.com/LanternOps/breeze/security/advisories/GHSA-c445-q84m-rph4) (Medium, server on a non-UTC host time zone) and [GHSA-vjq5-x2g3-pjhq](https://github.com/LanternOps/breeze/security/advisories/GHSA-vjq5-x2g3-pjhq) (Low, AI file tools). Upgrade the server and let agents and Breeze Assist update to 0.119.0.

**Upgrade command.** On a digest-pinned install (every `guided-setup.sh` install from v0.112.0), fetch the current `guided-setup.sh` from `main` and run `bash guided-setup.sh --upgrade 0.119.0`; it verifies the signed image inventory and rewrites `BREEZE_VERSION` and all four image digests together. **Do not upgrade by only editing `BREEZE_VERSION`** on a digest-pinned install: that pulls the images you already run. Delete the `APP_VERSION:` line from your own Compose file ([details](#v01190--app_version-comes-from-the-image)). Coming from v0.117.x or earlier, read the v0.118.0 notes first.

#### Behaviour changes

- **Live device inspection needs `devices:execute`.** Process, service, scheduled-task, event-log, file and registry reads, and the live session list, need it (`/devices/:id/sessions/live` also accepts `remote:access`). Org Viewer, Partner Viewer and the two seeded approver roles lose live inspection; custom roles that should keep it need `devices:execute`. API keys with only `ai:read` can no longer trigger live reads.
- **Site scoping.** Fleet security posture, threats, the executive summary and OS distribution respect site-restricted access.
- **Remote consent.** On devices whose policy is **Require consent**, VNC is refused (`409 CONSENT_REQUIRED_TRANSPORT_UNAVAILABLE`) and desktop starts need a consent-capable agent (`409 CONSENT_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`); update those agents before the server. AI screen tools and **Diagnose** are refused on consent-mode devices. Audit actions are renamed: `session_consent_denied` → `session_consent_blocked_unanswered`, `session_consent_bypassed` → `session_consent_blocked_unavailable`. Update saved audit filters and SIEM rules; older rows keep the old names.
- **Approver assurance** becomes the default for high- and critical-risk approvals from **2026-11-05** for partners that never saved an **Approval Security** choice. Move the date with `APPROVER_ASSURANCE_DEFAULT_ENFORCE_FROM`.
- **Settings secrets are encrypted and masked.** Notification secrets in partner, organization and site settings are encrypted by a background sweep after first boot (using `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`) and returned as `********`; integrations that GET then PUT settings must send the marker back unchanged. **If you run a separate `worker` container, roll it together with `api`.**
- **Billing contact.** Invoices and quotes go to the organization contact with the **Billing** role, with no fallback to the primary contact. Fix affected organizations in **Contacts**.
- **Compliance alerts** stay open until the device is compliant. Duplicate rule set names within one policy are refused.
- **Built-in time-sync monitors** are provisioned for every partner but not attached, so nothing alerts until you attach them. Opt out with `BREEZE_BUILTIN_MONITORS_AUTOSEED=false`.
- **AI not configured.** Without a usable model provider, chat and the script builder answer `503 ai_not_configured`.

#### Environment variables

**No new required variables.** New optional: `XERO_CLIENT_ID`, `XERO_CLIENT_SECRET`, `XERO_REDIRECT_URI`, `XERO_WEBHOOK_KEY`, `XERO_DAILY_CALL_LIMIT` (Xero stays hidden until configured), `AI_TOOL_SEARCH` (`auto`, `on`, `off`), `APPROVER_ASSURANCE_DEFAULT_ENFORCE_FROM`, `PRE_ASSIGNMENT_ENROLLMENT_ENABLED` (default `false`) and `METRIC_ANOMALY_EPISODE_MIN_BUCKETS`. `METRIC_ROLLUP_MAX_DELETE_BATCHES` is no longer read. Never set `BREEZE_BINARIES_VERSION`; it is baked into the image. See [Environment Variables](/deploy/environment/).

#### Migrations

50 idempotent migrations apply on boot, all before the API serves. Take a database backup first.

- **Backup history backfill.** One migration writes a reservation row per existing backup snapshot (about 13 seconds per 300,000 snapshots in testing). Check `SELECT count(*) FROM backup_snapshots;` beforehand if your backup history is large.
- **`notification_channels.config` is dropped.** On a v0.118.x image, alert delivery keeps working but creating or editing a notification channel fails. Do not roll back below v0.118.0.
- **Metric history storage.** Older months are rewritten by the nightly maintenance job once their 5-minute data has expired. Set `METRIC_ROLLUP_5M_RETENTION_DAYS=30` (in `.env` and the `api` service's `environment:` block) to reclaim space sooner. If the migration role can't create the `metric_rollups_staging` schema, create it by hand.

sections.heading: v0.120.0 — S3 backups through storage sessions, restore integrity, consent prompt protocol 2
sections.text:
**Before you upgrade: agents and HTTPS for S3 backups:**
  Backups to S3 and S3-compatible storage are now written only through a short-lived, write-scoped storage session, with no fallback. Before upgrading, update every device that backs up to S3 to agent **v0.119.0 or later**, switch MinIO and other S3-compatible endpoints to `https://` (same host and port), and make sure agents reach the API over HTTPS with `PUBLIC_API_URL` set. Local and NAS destinations are unchanged. See [HTTPS for Backups](/backup/https-backups/).

**Upgrade order.**

1. Update every device that backs up to S3 to agent v0.119.0 or later, and move storage endpoints and the agent API to HTTPS (above).
2. Back up the database.
3. Upgrade the server: `bash guided-setup.sh --upgrade 0.120.0` on a digest-pinned install, or set `BREEZE_VERSION=0.120.0` and run `docker compose pull api web portal && docker compose up -d`.
4. Merge the [Compose file changes](#v01200--start-fence-default-and-newly-mapped-api-settings) if you maintain your own Compose file.
5. Let agents and Breeze Assist update to 0.120.0. **Server first:** a server older than this release refuses consent- and notify-mode desktop starts on updated agents.
6. Open each Backup policy's **Destination** section and work through the storage key card: replace each listed key with your storage provider, disable the old one, then use **Check old key** or **I disabled this key**.

#### Backups and restores

- **Who is refused for S3 backups.** A device whose backup component has reported it cannot write through a storage session (`409 helper_update_required` on the on-demand SQL Server and Hyper-V routes; scheduled jobs fail with "Update the Breeze agent on this device, then try again."), an `http://` storage endpoint, a plain-`http://` agent API or a missing `PUBLIC_API_URL`, and providers other than S3 and local. Devices that have not reported yet are held until their first heartbeat. The `manage_backup_configs` AI tool accepts only the `s3` and `local` providers.
- **Restores are checked against the snapshot's integrity record.** Every restore, verify, test restore, VM restore and bare-metal recovery carries the snapshot's integrity expectations, and the updated backup helper checks the manifest and each file before installing it. A snapshot that failed its integrity check is refused; a snapshot without an attestation still restores and is labelled *unattested*. See [Restoring from Backup](/backup/restoring/).
- **Windows restores are stricter.** Reserved Windows names (`CON`, `NUL`, `COM1` and the like), and path components containing `:` or ending in `.` or a space, are refused. A restored security descriptor naming accounts the machine doesn't recognise is replaced with a restrictive one (owner Administrators; SYSTEM and Administrators only), and the result lists those paths. `bmr_recover` on Windows restores files only; system state is applied by a bare-metal rebuild.
- **DR plans.** A **Bare metal rebuild** step now waits up to 24 hours by default (was 4 hours).

#### Remote desktop start fence required by default

- **`REMOTE_DESKTOP_FENCE_REQUIRED` now defaults to `true`.** Remote desktop
  (WebRTC and the WebSocket fallback) starts only on agents that report the
  session start fence, which agents v0.114.0 and later do. On an older agent the
  technician sees "Remote desktop needs an agent update on this device (session
  revocation lease and start fence support)…" (HTTP `503 agent_upgrade_required`,
  or the WebSocket error `AGENT_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`) and no session starts.
  Terminal, Files and every other remote tool are unaffected. Agents update
  themselves; if you pin agent versions below v0.114.0, move the pin, or set
  `REMOTE_DESKTOP_FENCE_REQUIRED=false` until they have updated. If your `.env`
  still carries `REMOTE_DESKTOP_FENCE_REQUIRED=false` copied from an older
  `.env.example`, that line keeps the fence off; remove it. A Compose file from
  an earlier release also passes `false` when the variable is unset, so an
  existing install keeps the fence **off** until you either set
  `REMOTE_DESKTOP_FENCE_REQUIRED=true` in `.env` or take the
  [v0.120.0 Compose change](#v01200--start-fence-default-and-newly-mapped-api-settings).
  New installs get it on. A value that is not a recognized boolean (true/false,
  1/0, yes/no, on/off) now refuses boot.
- **The WebSocket desktop fallback now behaves like WebRTC.** The technician's
  view stays on *connecting* until the agent reports the stream started, so a
  consent prompt is answered before anything is shown; a denial ends the session
  as `denied` with its reason. **End** stops the stream immediately. Updated
  agents also show the notify notice and on-screen indicator on this transport,
  keep the session lease (a Redis or API outage longer than about 90 seconds ends
  the stream, as it already does on WebRTC), and refuse a start that arrives after
  the session was stopped.

#### Consent prompts report whether they were shown

Only devices whose remote access policy uses the **consent** prompt are affected.

- **A signed-in user who cannot be shown the prompt is always refused**, whatever "If no one can respond" says (for example, Breeze Assist not running or a native dialog failing). That setting still applies when nobody is signed in, and when a prompt the user could see went unanswered.
- **On macOS and Linux an unanswered prompt is refused,** because only Windows reports the lock state reliably.
- **Update Breeze Assist with the agent.** An older Assist still handles Allow and Deny, but its unanswered prompts are refused.
- The technician sees a specific message for each outcome, and consent audit events gain `consentOutcome`, `consentOccupancy` and `consentProtocol`, plus the reasons `no_user_session` and `helper_unreachable`. See [Remote Access](/features/remote-access/).

#### Breeze Assist on Windows

- **Console session only.** The agent delivers Assist's credential only over its local channel to the active console session and no longer stores it in `agent.yaml`. Assist in an RDP or other non-console session shows that it has not received its credentials until a later release adds support.
- On first start the agent moves any credential it finds in `agent.yaml` into its protected secrets file and rotates it once. macOS and Linux are unaffected.

#### AI

- **The default model is `claude-sonnet-5-5` with adaptive thinking.** Existing chats keep their stored model, and `BREEZE_AI_SCRIPT_REVIEWER_MODEL` follows the new default. If AI runs through a LiteLLM or other gateway alias, add an alias for `claude-sonnet-5-5` and let the gateway accept or drop the thinking parameters (LiteLLM `drop_params`), or set `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` to your backend's model id. See [Environment Variables](/deploy/environment/).
- `POST /ai/sessions` rejects a model that isn't offered (`400 invalid_model`).
- **AI model registry.** Platform admins get **Admin → AI models** (`/admin/ai-models`). A daily discovery job lists new Anthropic models for review; it never enables, prices or removes anything, and it is skipped when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a gateway. Routing, pricing and billing still come from your existing settings in this release.

#### Other behaviour changes

- **API error codes.** Five codes from device and agent routes now use the standard uppercase form: `SCHEME_NOT_ALLOWED`, `INVALID_CUSTOM_FIELD_VALUE` (was `invalid-custom-field-value`), `RACE_LOST`, `RE_ENROLLMENT_REQUIRED` and `SOFTWARE_INVENTORY_LOCK_TIMEOUT`. HTTP statuses and messages are unchanged; update integrations that match on the old codes.
- **S3-backed binary hosting.** Backup, watchdog, user-helper and recovery-media downloads are served from the `agent/` prefix, and the Breeze Assist installer is synced to `helper/` at boot. The `backup/`, `watchdog/`, `user-helper/` and `recovery-iso/` prefixes are no longer read and can be deleted. An unset `HELPER_BINARY_DIR` now means the agent binaries directory. See [Binary Distribution](/deploy/binaries/).
- **Device restores count against the device limit,** like enrollment.

#### Environment variables

**No new required variables.** `REMOTE_DESKTOP_FENCE_REQUIRED` now defaults to `true` (see above). New optional: `AI_INVOCATIONS_RETENTION_DAYS` (default 400), `AI_INVOCATIONS_RETENTION_BATCH_SIZE` and `AI_INVOCATIONS_RETENTION_MAX_BATCHES`. The audit-chain settings are now passed to the API by Compose; see [Compose file changes](#v01200--start-fence-default-and-newly-mapped-api-settings).

#### Migrations

Twelve idempotent migrations apply on boot. They add tables for portal session revocations, backup storage key history and the AI model registry, seed the platform model catalog, and copy each partner's AI provider setup into the registry. No large rewrites.

- **`ai_sessions` index.** Built with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` outside a transaction. If the build is interrupted, the next start refuses with "ai_sessions offering index build left INVALID index". Run `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY public.ai_sessions_offering_idx;` and restart the API.
- **First start.** The API records the storage key each S3 destination uses and builds the AI registry from your current AI settings, logging one `[startup]` line for each.

sections.heading: v0.118.0 — legacy alerting retired, network checks become monitors
sections.text:
**Before you upgrade: convert everything on v0.117.0:**
  While you are still on **v0.117.0**, open **Alerts → Monitors → Needs conversion**, run **Convert everything**, and review every refusal. After this upgrade, **Undo** in conversion history is no longer available for legacy alert rules, templates, inline policy rules or service/process watches, so fix anything you want to keep while you can still roll a conversion back. Then take a database backup.

**Upgrade order.**

1. On v0.117.0, run **Convert everything** and review the refusals (above).
2. Back up the database.
3. Set `BREEZE_VERSION` to the new release in `.env`, then run `docker compose pull api web portal && docker compose up -d`.
4. Merge the [Compose file changes](#v01180--coturn-peer-restrictions-and-api-stop-grace) if you maintain your own Compose file or coturn configuration.
5. Let every agent and Breeze Helper update to 0.118.0, then rebuild any recovery media you keep.

**Update every agent and Helper.** Many changes in this release take effect on a device only once it runs the 0.118 agent and Helper. Until then, the device keeps its previous behaviour. This covers installer secret handling, Windows local file and pipe checks, PAM file-hash pinning, the new restore path, the Hyper-V, restore-as-VM and instant-boot fixes, consent-prompt reporting, memory module inventory and the macOS binary move. A few paths refuse older agents rather than fall back; they are listed below.

#### Alerting and network checks

- **Legacy alerting is retired.** The policy **Alerts** and **Service & Process Monitoring** tabs are gone, and `/alerts/rules` redirects to **Alerts → Monitors**. Writes under `/alerts/rules*` and `/alert-templates*`, and writes to the retired `alert_rule` and `monitoring` policy feature types, return `410 Gone`. Reads still work, so history stays available.
- **First boot converts what is left.** The API converts any remaining legacy sources for each partner and retires the ones it cannot convert, with a reason for each. A dismissible banner under **Alerts → Monitors** lists them. Recreate what you need as monitors before you dismiss it. Open alerts from retired sources stay open until someone resolves them. Set `BREEZE_LEGACY_ALERTING_SWEEP=false` to skip the conversion at boot; the API still counts what is left.
- **Leftovers are logged on every boot.** If any legacy policy alert rules or service/process watches are still unretired after the sweep, the API logs the counts at error level on every start. Nothing evaluates them any more. Restart the API to run the sweep again (after removing `BREEZE_LEGACY_ALERTING_SWEEP=false` if you set it), or run **Convert everything**.
- **Review alert routing before you upgrade.** Queued legacy alerts and unconverted standalone rules no longer use their old per-rule delivery settings. Delivery follows the monitor's settings, your routing rows and the explicit **Everything else** row. An alert that matches no destination sends no notification.
- **Network checks move to Monitors.** You now create and edit network checks as `network_check` monitors under **Alerts → Monitors**. **Network → Results** is read-only and offers conversion of existing checks. Checks you have not converted keep polling and alerting. Creating or editing a check through the old endpoints returns `410`. An asset cannot be deleted while it still has active or retained checks (`409`). The boot sweep never converts or retires network checks. See [Network Monitors](/features/network-monitors/).
- **Maintenance windows suppress monitor alerts again.** On v0.117.0, **Suppress alerts** in a maintenance window did not stop monitor alerts, including alerts from rules converted to monitors. Expect fewer alerts during maintenance than on v0.117.0.
- **Some monitor thresholds now fire.** Bandwidth, disk I/O, network-error and patch-compliance monitors now evaluate in the units they display. Bandwidth thresholds had been compared about 8× too high, so a bandwidth monitor that never fired may fire now.

#### Dynamic groups as execution targets

Dynamic groups whose rules match on a field the device reports about itself no longer act as execution targets. These fields are hostname, display name, tags, device role, last user, agent version, Helper version, installed software (installed or not installed), and any custom field.

- **Affected:** scripts, automations, software policies and update rings. The automation, software, remote-access, PAM, maintenance, OneDrive and Assist policy features also skip such groups.
- **Not affected:** patch and backup assignments still resolve through these groups. So does every non-execution use of a dynamic group, such as views, filters and reports.
- **Visible in the audit log.** Each skipped group is logged with the fields that caused it. Where the request is interactive, the response also carries a warning.

To keep targeting these devices, rebuild the group on fields Breeze accepts for targeting, such as site, organization, OS, hardware, network facts or metrics. Or use a static group. See [Device Groups](/features/device-groups/#dynamic-groups-as-execution-targets).

#### Backups, restores and DR

- **DR plan steps cannot store credentials.** A step whose restore settings include a recovery token or storage credentials fails when it runs. The upgrade removes those keys from saved steps, and saving a step that includes them is rejected. Open each affected step and save it again without credentials. Breeze resolves the storage destination from the snapshot when the step runs. See [Disaster Recovery](/backup/disaster-recovery/).
- **Commands queued across an org merge or device move.** A backup, restore or verify command that is still queued when its device changes organization is not delivered. This includes devices moved by an organization merge. The command is expired with a reason. Run it again after the move.
- **Restores no longer receive storage credentials.** A restore, verify or test-restore command no longer carries the storage destination. With the 0.118 backup helper, the device fetches each file it needs through a short-lived, read-only link that Breeze issues for that command and device only. Devices whose backup helper predates 0.118 keep using the previous path until they update. See [Restoring from Backup](/backup/restoring/#how-restores-reach-storage).
- **Restore as VM and instant boot report failures.** A restore as VM that cannot place every file now fails before any VM is created, instead of reporting success. Instant boot runs its background sync inside the command, and an incomplete sync reports the VM as degraded. Hyper-V restore refuses a VM name that already exists.
- **New run state: completed with errors.** A backup run that produced a snapshot but could not read or upload some files (up to 10%) is now **Completed with errors**, not **Completed**. API consumers see the new status value `completed_with_errors`. See [Monitoring Backups](/backup/monitoring/).
- **Legal hold blocks erasure.** Erasing an organization's data is refused (`409`) while any of its snapshots is under legal hold, and a legal hold cannot be placed on an organization that is being erased. Permanently deleting a device is refused while one of its snapshots is under legal hold or inside its immutability window.
- **Storage cannot be shared across partners.** A bucket, endpoint or local path already used by an organization under another partner is refused. Organizations under the same partner can still share one.
- **Cove name matches are no longer mapped automatically.** Only a Cove customer whose external code is set to a Breeze organization ID is mapped on sync. Map name-only matches yourself. Mappings made before this release are not changed. See [Third-Party Backup Providers](/backup/backup-providers/#mapping-customers-to-organizations).
- **Recovery bundles verify their helper.** A recovery bundle's launch script checks the included helper binary's signature before running it. Bundles need [recovery signing](/backup/bare-metal-recovery/#recovery-bundle-signing) configured on the server when they are built, and the machine that runs them needs `minisign` (plus `curl` on Linux and macOS). **Rebuild recovery bundles after upgrading.** The recovery console also no longer relaxes its HTTPS requirement for `breeze.insecure=1` in interactive mode.

#### Agent

- **Windows: linked data and log directories are replaced.** If `C:\ProgramData\Breeze\data` or `C:\ProgramData\Breeze\logs` is a junction or symbolic link, the installer and the agent replace it with a real directory that only SYSTEM and Administrators can write to. Files in the old link target are not moved or copied, so copy anything you need first. If the link cannot be removed, **the agent refuses to start** and writes the reason to `C:\ProgramData\Breeze\logs\agent-start-failed.txt`. Remove the link by hand, then start the service.
- **macOS: agent binaries move only when `/usr/local/bin` is unsafe.** Agents 0.118.0 through 0.118.2 moved the agent and watchdog binaries from `/usr/local/bin` to `/Library/Breeze/bin` on every Mac, on first start, which broke Full Disk Access for anyone on that path (macOS ties FDA to a bare binary's file path, not its identity). **Upgrade straight to 0.118.3 or later** — do not promote 0.118.0-0.118.2 to Macs you cannot touch. From 0.118.3, the agent moves only when `/usr/local/bin` (or a directory above it) is not owned by root, or is group- or world-writable — the known case is Homebrew on Intel Macs, which hands that directory to an admin user. A stock Mac (root-owned, non-writable `/usr/local/bin`) never moves and keeps all of its grants. Only a Mac that does move needs Full Disk Access re-granted for `/Library/Breeze/bin/breeze-agent`; the agent logs a warning when it moves and reports a `macos_fda_relocation` self-health warning until the grant lands. A Mac already moved by 0.118.0-0.118.2 stays at `/Library/Breeze/bin` on 0.118.3+ — it is not moved back, so a re-grant already done keeps holding. See [macOS Permissions](/agents/macos-permissions/#after-an-agent-relocation).
- **Helper token file.** On Linux and macOS, the Helper token moves to `helper_token.yaml`.

#### Access, MFA and limits

- **Account changes reach delegated access.** A password change or reset, or an MFA factor reset, ends that user's live remote sessions and invalidates the API keys they created before the change. A role change revokes the user's refresh tokens. Service-principal keys are not affected, and the upgrade itself revokes nothing.
- **More actions need a fresh MFA check:**
  - revealing a disk-encryption key;
  - report email recipients;
  - partner billing profiles and work types;
  - org billing-profile assignment and org billing settings;
  - linking a backup-provider device;
  - topology template library changes;
  - software-policy executable rules, which also need `pam:manage_policy`;
  - AI script policy changes;
  - deactivating a policy.
- **Permissions.** System Tools file-content and registry reads need `devices:execute`, and so do sensitive event-log channels (Security, PowerShell, Sysmon). Reads of the agent's own configuration directory and the SAM and SECURITY registry hives are always refused. Enrollment short codes are shown only to users who can create or rotate enrollment keys. Role, MFA-reset and member actions require the caller to hold every permission of the target user's role.
- **PAM and AI approvals.** An approval for a specific executable without its file hash is denied with a reason. AI elevation requests always wait for a human approver, and a requester cannot approve their own elevation. AI ticket comments are private unless approved as customer-visible. Newly discovered MCP tools must be reviewed before they are enabled.
- **Enrollment and installers.** Rotating an enrollment link issues a new short code, so the old `/s/` and `/i/` links return `404`. A custom-field value used in installer arguments must not contain spaces, quotes or backslashes; otherwise that device's install fails as an unresolved field.
- **Stored credentials stay tied to their destination.** Changing a tool source, backup S3 endpoint, log-forwarding URL or monitoring integration URL to a new origin requires re-entering its credential. Changing an SNMP discovery profile's subnets, exclusions or site requires re-entering or clearing its SNMP secrets.
- **Remote sessions.** Where the remote-access policy requires consent or an on-screen notice, desktop sessions over the WebSocket fallback to agents older than 0.118 are refused until the agent updates.
- **New limits.** Most can be tuned; see [Environment Variables → Agent traffic and ingest budgets](/deploy/environment/#agent-traffic-and-ingest-budgets).
  - public downloads: 600 requests per 5 minutes per route per IP;
  - TURN credentials: 30 per 10 minutes per user;
  - password-reset emails: one per account per 5 minutes;
  - agent WebSocket messages, plus daily agent log, event-log and change-log ingest (`429` when exceeded);
  - Helper screenshots;
  - pending log-forwarding jobs per organization;
  - the partner's organization limit when creating organizations.

#### Other behaviour changes

- Public invoice and quote links stop working while the owning partner is not active.
- Adopting a sending domain that already exists at the email provider needs a DNS TXT record at `_breeze-verify.<domain>`, or the domain listed in `EMAIL_DOMAINS_ADOPT_EXISTING_ALLOWLIST`. Otherwise provisioning ends as `provider_conflict`.
- Organization-scoped users cannot set audit-log retention below 90 days.
- Revoking a topology template is final.
- Inviting an address that already belongs to another tenant returns the normal success response.
- Public download routes, including `install.sh` and `uninstall.sh`, return `503` while Redis is unavailable.
- With `BINARY_SOURCE=local`, the Breeze Helper download is checked against the signed release manifest and returns `503` on a mismatch. Keep the manifest files next to the Helper binaries (`HELPER_BINARY_DIR` is respected).
- Notification channel settings (webhook URLs, bot tokens, routing keys) move to their own table, which only the channel's owner can read. The old column is kept for rollback and is dropped in the next release.

#### Environment variables

**No new required variables.** New optional ones all have defaults; see [Environment Variables](/deploy/environment/#agent-traffic-and-ingest-budgets). The four `OFFLINE_DETECTOR_REEVAL_*` variables no longer do anything: the job that read them was retired with legacy alerting. You can remove them.

#### Migrations

All migrations are idempotent and apply on boot. Migrations that change rows report their counts in the API log. Read these before upgrading:

- **One accounting connection per partner.** The API does not start if any partner has more than one accounting connection. Disconnect the extra provider first.
- **Backup snapshot index.** A new unique index on backup snapshots is built without blocking writes. If duplicate snapshot rows exist, the API logs a warning with the count and skips the index, and tries again on every start until the duplicates are resolved. If an interrupted build left an invalid index, the migration stops with an error. Run `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY backup_snapshots_storage_identity_snapshot_id_uq` and restart.
- **Elevation audit index.** Same pattern. If an interrupted build left the index invalid, run `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY public.elevation_audit_org_created_id_idx` and restart.
- **Stored storage destinations are cleared.** Storage destinations are removed from **finished** device commands, and credential keys from DR plan steps. On an install with a long command history, the first boot takes longer. Queued commands are left alone and cleared when they finish.
- **Patch job results index.** Built without blocking writes, but it can take a while on a large table.
- **Network checks.** A new asset/organization constraint on network checks stops the migration if existing rows already break that pairing. It converts and retires nothing.

**Rolling back** to v0.117.0 means restoring the database backup you took before upgrading, together with the v0.117.0 images.

sections.heading: v0.117.0 — legacy labour-pricing columns dropped
sections.text:
**The six legacy labour-pricing columns are dropped.** The migration removes
`default_billable`, `default_hourly_rate` and `rate_currency` from both
`ticket_categories` and `org_ticket_settings`. Nothing in Breeze has read them
since v0.115.0. Any report, BI query or integration that still selects them
directly from the database fails after this upgrade. Read pricing from the
billing-profile tables (`billing_profiles`, `billing_profile_rules`,
`org_billing_profile_assignments`) or from the values stamped on each time entry
(`time_entries.hourly_rate`, `coverage`, `work_type_id`, `billable_minutes`).

**Nothing is lost: the old values are archived first.** Before it drops the
columns, the migration copies every row that still holds a legacy value into a
new table, `legacy_labour_pricing_archive`. A few values never made it into a
billing profile during the v0.115.0 conversion. For those rows, `skip_reason`
says why:

| `skip_reason` | What the conversion did |
|---|---|
| `org_currency_off_list` | The organization's currency is not on the supported list, so its rate and billable default were skipped entirely. |
| `org_rate_currency_mismatch` | The organization's rate was entered in a different currency from the organization's own, so the rate was not carried over. |
| `non_billable_org_rate` | The organization was non-billable but also had a rate. A non-billable card carries no rate, so the rate was dropped. |
| `non_billable_category_rate` | The category was non-billable but also had a rate. The rate was dropped. |
| `category_rate_currency_unsupported` | The category rate had no currency, or an unsupported one, so it was not carried over. |
| *(empty)* | Converted into a billing profile. The row is kept for reference. |

To see what still needs re-entering on **Settings → Billing → Rates**:

```sql
BEGIN;
SELECT set_config('breeze.scope', 'system', true);  -- the table is row-level secured
SELECT source_table, source_name, default_billable, default_hourly_rate,
       rate_currency, owner_currency_code, skip_reason
  FROM legacy_labour_pricing_archive
 WHERE skip_reason IS NOT NULL
 ORDER BY partner_id, source_table, source_name;
COMMIT;
```

The migration counts what it archived in the API log (`billing profiles W04b:`
lines). It refuses to run, and the API does not start
(`refusing to drop legacy labour-pricing columns`), in two cases. The first is
when any partner was never converted. A normal upgrade path cannot produce
that, because the conversion runs earlier in the same migration sequence. The
second is when manual DDL left only some of a table's three legacy columns in
place, which the migration will not drop without archiving them.

**Rolling back to v0.116 after this upgrade needs a database restore.** The
v0.116 image's tenant-export policy still lists the three `org_ticket_settings`
columns, and tenant export rejects any mismatch between that list and the live
schema, so organization data export fails on a v0.116 image running against an
upgraded database. **Back up your database before upgrading.** To roll back,
restore that backup together with the v0.116 image.

**Billables CSV: two new columns at the end.** The billables export
(`GET /tickets/export/billables.csv`) appends `work_type` and
`included_minutes` (worked minutes of contract-included time, `0` on other
time rows, empty on parts). Existing columns keep their positions. An importer
that rejects unknown trailing columns needs updating.

sections.heading: v0.116.0 — retired labour-pricing fields are rejected
sections.text:
**Breaking API change: `defaultHourlyRate`, `defaultBillable` and `rateCurrency`
are rejected.** In v0.115.0 labour pricing moved from per-organization ticket settings and
per-category defaults to partner-level **billing profiles** (rate cards) with
per-work-type rows. The conversion migration builds the profiles from your
existing rates and assigns one to every organization, so nothing needs
re-entering. From v0.116.0 `PATCH /organizations/:id/ticket-settings`,
`POST /ticket-categories` and `PATCH /ticket-categories/:id` return **400** when
the request carries any of the three retired fields, and the whole request is
rejected — a rename sent alongside a retired field does not land either. The
error names the field and its replacement. Update any integration or script
that writes these fields: assign a profile with
`PUT /organizations/:id/billing-profile`, edit rates under
**Settings → Billing → Rates**, and point a category at a work type via
`defaultWorkTypeId`. `GET` responses no longer return the retired fields.
Breeze's own web, mobile and add-in clients never send them.

  Why there is no grace period: the cut-over already stopped honouring these
  writes, so a request that "succeeded" with 200 was silently discarding a rate
  change — an integration raising a rate would have kept billing at the old
  one. A loud 400 is the safer failure. Background and the resulting
  deprecation policy: LanternOps/breeze#6472.

The six underlying database columns are still present in v0.116.0, so v0.116.0
can still be rolled back to v0.115.0. Nothing reads or writes them any more,
and **they will be dropped in v0.117**, which will carry its own rollback note.
Repoint any report, BI query or integration that reads
`ticket_categories.default_billable`, `default_hourly_rate` or `rate_currency`,
or the same three columns on `org_ticket_settings`, directly from the database
before upgrading to v0.117. Read pricing from the billing-profile tables
(`billing_profiles`, `billing_profile_rules`,
`org_billing_profile_assignments`) or from the values stamped on each time
entry (`time_entries.hourly_rate`, `coverage`, `work_type_id`,
`billable_minutes`). The legacy columns hold only the pre-conversion values.
**Back up your database before upgrading** all the same.

sections.heading: v0.115.0 — billing profiles replace per-organization labour rates
sections.text:
**Labour pricing moved to billing profiles, and the old fields are silently
ignored in this release.** The conversion migration builds partner-level billing
profiles from your existing organization and category rates and assigns one to
every organization; nothing needs re-entering. However, v0.115.0 still *accepts*
`defaultHourlyRate`, `defaultBillable` and `rateCurrency` on
`PATCH /organizations/:id/ticket-settings`, `POST /ticket-categories` and
`PATCH /ticket-categories/:id`, returns **200**, and **discards the value**.
The only signal is a `deprecationWarnings` array in the response body. An
integration that changes a rate through these fields on v0.115.0 keeps billing
at the old rate. Move rate changes to billing profiles
(`PUT /organizations/:id/billing-profile`, or **Settings → Billing → Rates**)
before or during this upgrade. v0.116.0 turns these writes into a 400 (above).

sections.heading: v0.114.0 — evidence reports, network device page, account board
sections.text:
**Navigation moved; old URLs removed.** The Fleet Management entry **Monitoring** is
now **Network Monitor** and holds only network assets, checks and SNMP templates.
Device monitors (CPU, memory, disk, service, process, custom) moved to
**Alerts → Monitors** (`/alerts/monitors`). The pre-v0.114 URLs `/monitoring/monitors`,
`/monitoring/rules`, `/monitoring/delivery`, and `/monitoring/network` were removed
and now return 404. Update bookmarks to `/alerts/monitors`, `/alerts/rules`,
`/alerts/channels`, and `/monitoring`, respectively. If a technician reports that "Monitors disappeared", this is where they
went.

**`catalog_items.unit_price` is dropped.** Catalog sell prices have lived in
`catalog_item_prices` (per-organization price book) since the multi-currency
work landed; `unit_price` on `catalog_items` was a write-only leftover column
that nothing read. The API and catalog UI are unaffected — the `unitPrice`
field on create/update requests is still accepted as an input alias mapped
into the price book. If you have custom SQL, a BI tool, or a script reading
`catalog_items.unit_price` directly, it will break; point it at
`catalog_item_prices` (via `catalog_item_org_pricing`) instead.

  Rolling back to a pre-v0.114.0 image after upgrading is not clean — the
  dropped column does not come back on its own. **Back up your database before
  upgrading** if you might need to roll back.

sections.heading: v0.113.0 — remote desktop stability, AI-authored scripts, service deliverables
sections.text:
**No breaking API changes.** Two settings deserve a decision before you pull:
`APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID` (now a boot refusal for split-role deployments and a
`503` on integration credential saves everywhere else) and
`BREEZE_AI_SCRIPT_AUTHORING_ENABLED`, which is now **on by default**. Read
[Action required](#action-required-in-v01130) before you pull.

**If remote desktop has been dropping every 30–90 seconds since early August, take this release:**
  Since late July the orphan-session sweeper was ending healthy peer-to-peer
  viewer sessions because it only recognised a WebSocket-owned session as
  alive — and the default P2P transport never opens that socket. The fix is
  entirely server-side; **no agent update is needed** for it. The separate
  secondary-monitor fix (input and cursor landing on the wrong monitor on
  Windows hosts with mixed DPI scaling) does need the updated agent and
  helper.

**Pull `api`, `web` and `portal` together, in one pass** (plus `worker` if you
run the [worker split](/deploy/worker-split/)). The customer portal gains two
new sections and the web dashboard gains new navigation, so a mixed set of
images shows menu entries that 404. Afterwards assert version parity on every
`ghcr.io/lanternops/breeze/*` container rather than trusting the service list.

#### Action required in v0.113.0

1. **Set `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID` if you have not already.** The API **refuses
   to boot** without it when `BREEZE_ROLE` is `api` or `worker` or when
   `M365_GRAPH_ACTIONS_TOOLS_ENABLED=true`. Every other deployment boots with a
   warning, but **saving integration credentials returns `503`** — Discord,
   Teams, Grafana, OpsGenie, PagerDuty, monitoring webhooks, ticketing and
   PSA settings — until the key id is set, because those credentials are now
   sealed at rest with key-bound ciphertext and no longer fall back to unbound
   ciphertext. Add any `[A-Za-z0-9._-]+` identifier to `.env` **and** map it in
   the `api` (and `worker`) service's `environment:` block; installs whose
   `guided-setup.sh` run predates the key never had it generated. Setting it
   does not rotate `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. See
   [Environment Variables](/deploy/environment/#authentication--security).
2. **AI script authoring is on by default.** The chat assistant and background
   AI agents can now write a script as a reviewed proposal and, once a human
   approves it on a card, run it. Set `BREEZE_AI_SCRIPT_AUTHORING_ENABLED=false`
   to keep the feature dark. Two related permission changes: approving a
   proposal that matched a **Strict** danger pattern requires the approver to
   hold `scripts:write` **in the proposal's organization** and to have
   completed MFA (the same bar the script library already applies), and
   four-eyes requests for such proposals fan out only to approvers who hold
   `scripts:write` — grant it to whoever decides AI script runs. The
   **unattended lane ships off**: it needs a partner to open the ceiling and
   each organization to opt in, and no environment variable controls it. See
   [AI Script Authoring](/features/ai-script-authoring/).
3. **Two new permissions, `documents:read` and `documents:write`,** gate the
   new organization document library and the **Documents** tab. The migration
   grants both to the built-in **Partner Technician**, **Org Admin** and **Org
   Technician** roles; **custom roles get nothing** until you add them under
   **Settings → Roles**. Service deliverables themselves use the existing
   `contracts:read` / `contracts:write`.
4. **If you take online payments through Stripe**, resetting a payment link,
   recording a manual payment, voiding an invoice or replacing the Stripe key
   now **refuses with `503 STRIPE_REVOCATION_PENDING`** when Breeze cannot
   prove the customer's open Checkout session is dead. A 60-second sweep
   retries, so the refusal is brief; if it ever blocks invoice work during an
   incident, set `STRIPE_SESSION_REVOCATION_MODE=observe` rather than rolling
   back.
5. **Customers with Microsoft 365 Graph-read consent see a re-consent prompt.**
   The `customer-graph-read` manifest moves to v3 with four additional Graph
   permissions for the upcoming posture program. The prompt is
   non-interrupting — existing connections keep working until the customer
   administrator re-consents.

#### Database migrations in v0.113.0

**22 migrations (`2026-10-15-170300` through `2026-10-16-170700`). Take a
database backup first.** All are idempotent, apply automatically on API startup
unless `AUTO_MIGRATE=false`, and have been dry-run as a non-superuser role.
None rewrites a large table. The ones with operator-visible effects:

| Migration | Effect |
|---|---|
| `2026-10-15-170400-documents-permissions.sql` | Seeds `documents:read` / `documents:write` and grants them to the built-in Partner Technician, Org Admin and Org Technician roles (counts logged as Postgres `WARNING`s). |
| `2026-10-16-100000-script-versions-immutable.sql` | Creates one head-version row per existing script and makes script versions append-only — every save now cuts a new immutable version. |
| `2026-10-16-100300-scripts-origin.sql` | Adds `origin` (`human` / `ai` / `system`) to scripts and backfills `system` on the built-in ones. |
| `2026-10-16-160200-checkout-session-revocation.sql` | Marks aged-out pending Stripe Checkout session mappings revoked and pre-existing ones `legacy_unbounded`; adds the revocation-intent bookkeeping. |
| `2026-10-16-170100-mfa-enrollment-grace.sql` | Adds the enrolment-deadline columns on `users`. No rows written. |
| `2026-10-16-110000-portal-branding-service-documents-flags.sql` | Adds the portal **Service** and **Documents** visibility flags, both `false`. |

The rest — organization documents, script proposals and policies, monitor
definitions, the remote-session start generation, M365 tenant-sync foundation,
Fleet Designer and device-function tables — are DDL-only additions with no
backfill.

#### New settings in v0.113.0

Only `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID` (item 1 above) is required, and only for the
configurations listed there. Full descriptions are in
[Environment Variables](/deploy/environment/).

| Variable | Default | Why you might set it |
|---|---|---|
| `BREEZE_AI_SCRIPT_AUTHORING_ENABLED` | **`true`** | Set `false` to keep AI script authoring dark. |
| `BREEZE_AI_SCRIPT_REVIEWER_MODEL` | — | Platform-default model for the independent script reviewer; a partner or organization policy can override it. |
| `STRIPE_SESSION_REVOCATION_MODE` | `enforce` | `observe` is the incident de-escalation lever for item 4 above. |
| `M365_SYNC_CONTINUATION_KEY`, `M365_SYNC_MAX_IN_FLIGHT`, `M365_MAX_IN_FLIGHT` | — / `4` / `32` | Read by the separate `m365-graph-read-executor` sidecar only. Without a continuation key the executor mints one per process and a sync resumes from page 1 after a restart — self-healing, so existing executors need nothing. |
| `BACKUP_GC_ORPHAN_MANIFEST_MAX_AGE_MS`, `BACKUP_BASE_LEASE_MS`, `BACKUP_RESTORE_PIN_LINGER_MS`, `BACKUP_PUBLISH_MARGIN_MS` | 9 d / 7 d / 7 d / 1 h | Lab/test knobs for the backup storage sweep. Production enforces floors and logs when a lower value is ignored. Leave unset. |

**New infrastructure:** one new queue, `script-verify`, consumed by the API
replica that owns the agent socket. No new service, no new port.

#### Rolling back v0.113.0

Prefer roll-forward. Every schema change is additive, so rolling the images
back needs no schema rollback; scripts saved on v0.113.0 keep their version
rows. Do **not** revert the Checkout-session migration to escape a revocation
refusal — flip `STRIPE_SESSION_REVOCATION_MODE=observe` instead, otherwise
the older code ignores the pending intents and re-opens the duplicate-charge
window.

#### Behaviour changes in v0.113.0

- **Navigation.** Automations now live under a top-level **Jobs** entry
  (bookmarked `/automations/*` links redirect); the sidebar's **Network
  Monitor** entry is now **Monitoring**, a hub with **Monitors**, **Network**,
  **Delivery** and **Legacy rules** tabs; **Devices** is now **Devices &
  Assets**, with your last five devices under it and a Cmd+K palette that
  opens on recent devices and pages. See [Automations](/features/automations/)
  and [Monitors](/features/monitors/).
- **Monitors** are the new single object a technician authors — condition,
  severity, delivery and responses in one place — compiled into the alert
  templates, alert rules and automations that already run. Existing alert
  rules keep working; **Legacy rules** offers one-click conversion.
- **Service deliverables and the organization document library** ship with
  two new customer-portal sections, **Service** and **Documents**, both off per
  organization until you turn them on. A daily sweep opens tickets for
  deliverables that come due and for key-date reminders. See
  [Service deliverables](/features/contracts/#service-deliverables) and
  [Customer Portal](/features/portal/).
- **AI Fleet Designer** is a fourth AI-agent kind, `designer`, that reads the
  fleet and writes a **Fleet Design** report. It is inert until an
  administrator creates one for an organization, and nothing in its design is
  applied automatically. It also assesses a **Function** for each device
  (domain controller, kiosk, …), shown next to the billable Device Role. See
  [AI Agents](/features/ai-agents/#fleet-designer).
- **Consecutive supervised Tier-3 approvals need one step-up ceremony** —
  a 120-second grant bound to the approver's session — instead of one per
  decision. Four-eyes approvals still take a fresh ceremony each time.
- **MFA enrolment grace window.** A user who lands in a Force MFA role and has
  never held a factor gets a nonrenewable 14-day window (banner plus email
  notices) before the `428` enrolment wall applies. Inert unless
  `MFA_FORCE_FOR_PARTNER_ADMIN=true`, whose default is unchanged (`false`).
  See [Users & Roles](/reference/users-and-roles/).
- **Backup storage usage starts to drop.** The reclamation sweep now deletes
  retired restore points' exclusive data and orphaned upload prefixes, on top
  of the loose-object grace rules. See [Storage](/backup/storage/).
- **Integration credentials are sealed and masked.** Discord, Teams, Grafana,
  OpsGenie, PagerDuty and monitoring-webhook secrets are encrypted at rest and
  never echoed back to the settings form; re-enter a secret to change it.
- **Alert-correlation views honour the site ceiling and `alerts:read`.** A
  site-restricted or permission-stripped reader no longer sees the whole
  organization's correlation graph.
- **Approver devices** now distinguish **Hardware-attested** from **Not
  attested** platform-bound mobile devices. See
  [Approval Security](/features/approval-security/).
- **M365 tenant-sync foundation** lands schema and executor plumbing only —
  nothing new in the dashboard this release.
- **Remote desktop start and stop commands** are now strictly ordered per
  session on both server and agent. No operator action; a late start can no
  longer win against a terminal decision.

sections.heading: v0.112.0 — Windows MSI fix, security remediations, bare-metal recovery
sections.text:
**No breaking API changes and no new *required* environment variables**, but
this release **removes implicit access and pauses some scheduled work** the
moment the migrations run. Read [Action required](#action-required-in-v01120)
before you pull.

**If you enroll Windows devices with the MSI, take this release now:**
  The agent MSI published with v0.110.0 through v0.111.1 refused **every fresh
  install** on Windows 10, 11 and Server 2016+ with "Breeze Agent requires
  Windows 10 or Windows Server 2016 or later". Already-enrolled agents were
  unaffected (self-update never runs the MSI); only new MSI enrollments were
  blocked. v0.112.0 reads the Windows version from the registry instead of the
  value Windows Installer reports. Replace any installer links or MSIs you handed
  out from those releases. See [Supported Windows versions](/agents/installation/#supported-windows-versions).

**Pull `api`, `web` and `portal` together, in one pass** (plus `worker` if you
run the [worker split](/deploy/worker-split/)). Two changes in this release have
no flag-level rollback: session-binding enforcement (below) and the remote
desktop lease, which expects every replica on the new protocol. **Sequence the
API restart as stop-then-start rather than rolling:** stop the old API
replicas, let the migrations apply, then start only the new ones — an older
API must not resume serving after the installer-token cutover (item 6 below).
Afterwards assert version parity on every `ghcr.io/lanternops/breeze/*`
container rather than trusting the service list.

#### Action required in v0.112.0

1. **PAM auto-approve rules are suspended.** Every rule with verdict
   **Auto-approve** is switched to **Require approval** and badged
   "Auto-approve suspended". Matching elevations wait for a human
   until an admin holding the new `pam:manage_policy` permission clicks
   **Re-approve** on the rule (MFA). See [PAM → Rules](/features/pam/#rules).
2. **New permissions replace implicit access.** `pam:approve`,
   `pam:manage_policy`, `accounting:read`, `accounting:manage`,
   `workspace:read|write|credentials|execute` and
   `connected_apps:read|manage` are granted to the built-in **Org Admin** only
   (Partner Admin holds `*:*`). **Every other built-in role and every custom
   role loses** QuickBooks, Workspace, connected-apps and PAM-approval access
   until you grant the keys in **Settings → Roles**. A Partner Technician or
   Partner Billing user who could browse or sync QuickBooks yesterday gets a
   403 today. See [Built-in permissions](/reference/users-and-roles/#built-in-permissions).
3. **Recurring sensitive-data scan policies are switched off** and any queued
   or running scheduled scan is failed. There is no badge: each affected policy
   simply shows as inactive on the **Scan Policies** tab. A user who holds
   `devices:write` **and** `devices:execute`, with MFA satisfied, re-approves it
   by turning **Active** back on (or re-saving it), which binds the schedule to
   that user's authority. Manual scans are unaffected. See
   [Sensitive Data](/features/sensitive-data/#recurring-scans-need-re-approval-after-upgrade).
4. **Recurring network-baseline scans are paused** with the banner "Recurring
   scan paused: re-approval required". Re-saving the schedule arms it under the
   saving user; **Scan Now** still works. Newly auto-created baselines now start
   with recurrence **off**. See [Network Baselines](/features/network-baselines/#recurring-scans-need-re-approval-after-upgrade).
5. **Office add-in technician bindings are revoked.** Every technician who
   uses the Outlook/Office add-in technician pane repeats the one-time sign-in;
   the account must now have an authenticator-app (TOTP) factor. See
   [AI for Office](/features/ai-for-office/).
6. **Outstanding installer bootstrap tokens are invalidated.** Unused
   bootstrap-derived enrollment keys are deleted. Regenerate any installer
   links or copies you handed out before the upgrade.
7. **Remote desktop needs an updated agent and is capped at 12 hours.** Only
   an agent that reports lease support can start a desktop session; older
   agents show "Remote desktop needs an agent update on this device" (HTTP
   `503 agent_upgrade_required`). Expect up to one heartbeat interval (about a
   minute) per device while agents self-update; **if you pin agent versions,
   desktop sessions are unavailable until you move the pin.** `Max session
   duration` is clamped to 1–12 hours (`0` no longer means unlimited), a
   membership/role/site-scope/MFA change ends a live session within about 25 s,
   and a Redis outage longer than 90 s ends live desktop sessions. Terminal,
   Files and VNC are unaffected. See [Session lease and revocation](/features/remote-access/#session-lease-and-revocation).
8. **`AUTH_BROWSER_TRANSITIONS_ENFORCED` is removed.** Session binding is
   enforced on every issuance path (password, SSO, Cloudflare Access, MFA,
   passkey, refresh, registration, invitation) with no opt-out. Delete the line
   from `.env`; the safety net is an image rollback, not a flag. Existing browser
   sessions self-heal on their next refresh. **Mobile app builds older than
   v0.109.0 cannot sign in** until updated.
9. **Legacy policy execution routes are gone.** `POST /policies/:id/evaluate`,
   `/remediate` and `/activate` are retired; use `POST /automations/:id/trigger`.
   `/deactivate` is unchanged.
10. **Site-restricted technicians** can no longer create or edit organization-wide
    governance objects (webhooks, notification channels, software and peripheral
    policies, configuration policies, PAM config, backup destinations and
    profiles) or manage PSA and DNS-security connections. They can still assign
    an existing policy to their own site.
11. **Check `TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDRS`.** With proxy trust unset, client-IP
    attribution now records the raw socket peer instead of `unknown`. Behind a
    real proxy that peer is the proxy, so make sure the variable is set on every
    deployment that fronts Breeze with one.

#### Database migrations in v0.112.0

**20 migrations. Take a database backup first.** All are idempotent, none abort
on pre-existing data, and all apply automatically on API startup unless you
have set `AUTO_MIGRATE=false`. The ones with operator-visible effects:

| Migration | Effect |
|---|---|
| `2026-10-15-150200-pam-dedicated-permissions.sql` | Suspends every `auto_approve` PAM rule (original verdict kept for re-approval); seeds `pam:approve` / `pam:manage_policy` and grants them to each built-in Org Admin. |
| `2026-10-15-150051-office-addin-binding-mfa-epoch.sql` | Revokes every existing Office add-in technician binding. |
| `2026-10-15-140001` / `140002` / `140003-sensitive-data-*.sql` | Deactivate every recurring sensitive-data policy and fail queued/running scheduled scans. |
| `2026-10-15-141001-installer-bootstrap-credential-generation.sql` | Deletes unused bootstrap-derived enrollment keys and bumps the generation on their parents. |
| `2026-10-15-150030` / `150031` / `150032` and `150500-accounting-dedicated-permissions.sql` | Seed `workspace:*`, `connected_apps:*`, `accounting:read`, `accounting:manage`; grant them to the built-in Org Admin only. |
| `2026-10-15-140004-backup-snapshot-lineage-fk-set-null.sql` | Makes `restore_jobs.snapshot_id` and `recovery_tokens.snapshot_id` nullable and moves five foreign keys onto `backup_snapshots` to `ON DELETE SET NULL`, so retention can finally delete a snapshot that was ever restored, verified or tokened. |
| `2026-10-15-150600-network-baseline-recurring-authority.sql` | Pauses every enabled recurring baseline scan (`reapproval_required`) until an authorized user re-saves the schedule. |
| `2026-10-15-150001-bound-webhook-retries.sql` | Normalizes legacy webhook `retryCount` values into 0–2; the count is logged as a Postgres `WARNING`. |
| `2026-10-15-150050-mobile-refresh-family-binding.sql` | Adds a partial index on `refresh_token_families` **in-transaction** (not `CONCURRENTLY`). Instant at typical sizes; run off-peak if yours is very large. |

The rest (`150010`, `150020`, `150040`, `150100`, `150300`, `160010`) are
additive column adds with no data change. A non-superuser migrating role is
sufficient, as before.

#### New optional settings in v0.112.0

None are required. Full descriptions are in [Environment Variables](/deploy/environment/).

| Variable | Why you might set it |
|---|---|
| `LENOVO_WARRANTY_ENABLED=true` and/or `LENOVO_API_KEY` | Lenovo warranty lookup works for the first time — credential-free via Lenovo's public lookup endpoint, or through the official Warranty API. `DELL_CLIENT_ID` / `DELL_CLIENT_SECRET` and both Lenovo knobs are now mapped through every shipped Compose file, so a value in `.env` is enough. See [Warranty lookups](/deploy/environment/#warranty-lookups). |
| `RECOVERY_MEDIA_WORK_DIR` | Already defaulted to `/data/recovery-work` by the shipped Compose files; moves bare-metal recovery media builds off the container's 64 MB `/tmp`. Override only to relocate it. |
| `BACKUP_GC_GRACE_MS` | Lab/test only. Production enforces a one-hour floor; the 48 h default is unchanged. |

**Removed:** `AUTH_BROWSER_TRANSITIONS_ENFORCED` (see item 8 above).

#### Fresh installs and image pinning in v0.112.0

`.env.example` and `deploy/docker-compose.prod.yml` now expect **signed,
digest-pinned image references** (`ghcr.io/lanternops/breeze/api@sha256:…`)
resolved from the release's signed image inventory. The guided installer
resolves and verifies them itself for 0.112.0 and later (fail-closed). The
current installer refuses releases older than 0.112.0 unless you pass
`--allow-unverified-release`; with that flag it warns and uses tag-tracking refs.
**Existing installs whose
`.env` still carries `…/api:${BREEZE_VERSION}` refs keep working with the
upgrade steps at the top of this page.** If you have already switched to digest
pins, update the four `BREEZE_*_IMAGE_REF` lines from the new release's
inventory on every upgrade — bumping `BREEZE_VERSION` alone changes nothing.
`guided-setup.sh --upgrade` does this in one command (step 4a above).
See [Signed, digest-pinned image references](/deploy/production/#signed-digest-pinned-image-references-v01120-and-later).

Rotating `RELEASE_ARTIFACT_MANIFEST_PUBLIC_KEYS` is a fleet re-enrollment:
agents pin the key they enrolled under and there is no remote revocation. See
[Binary Distribution](/deploy/binaries/).

#### Rolling back v0.112.0

Prefer roll-forward. If you must roll back, **downgrade agents before the
API**: a v0.112.0 agent talking to an older API gets no lease answer and ends
its desktop session after about 150 s. The added columns are additive and need
no schema rollback. Rolling back the network-baseline change resumes every
paused recurring baseline **under no authority** — clear each affected
baseline's schedule first.

#### Other behaviour changes in v0.112.0

- **Bare-metal recovery now restores system state on Linux**, every
  `system_image` backup records a disk-layout manifest with a restorability
  verdict, and a `breeze-backup rebuild` command can provision a disk from a
  snapshot. See [Bare Metal Recovery](/backup/bare-metal-recovery/).
- **Backup exclude patterns with a leading `/` are root-anchored** (gitignore
  semantics) instead of matching at any depth. File backups now capture
  symlinks, directories, ownership and setuid/setgid/sticky bits; manifests
  carrying them use a new format that **older agents cannot read**, so restore
  with a v0.112.0 agent. See [Backup Policies](/backup/policies/#file-backup).
- **Retention GC no longer stops** on the first snapshot that was ever
  restored, verified or tokened. Bucket usage still does not shrink — storage
  reclamation lands in a later release.
- **Webhooks make one HTTP attempt per invocation**; the queue owns retries,
  `retryCount` is capped at 2, and permanent failures (bad configuration,
  SSRF-blocked URL, ordinary 4xx) dead-letter immediately. `/test` and `/retry`
  on a paused webhook return `409`.
- **Org-scoped sessions are now evaluated against the partner IP allowlist.**
- **MCP tool `get_fleet_status` is renamed `get_invite_funnel`.** The old name
  dispatches for one more release but no longer appears in `tools/list`.
- **HP warranty lookup is de-registered** — HP's API is not available to RMM
  vendors, so HP devices stay at `unknown`.

sections.heading: v0.111.1 — hotfix for a v0.111.0 upgrade-blocking migration
sections.text:
**Install v0.111.1, not v0.111.0:**
  If you have not yet upgraded to v0.111.0, install **v0.111.1** instead — it
  contains everything in v0.111.0 plus this fix, and skips straight past the
  problem below. If you are already on v0.111.0 and it started up normally,
  your database was not affected and you can upgrade to v0.111.1 at your
  leisure. Everything else in this guide's [v0.111.0 section](#v01110--offline-work-queue-script-cancellation-organization-record-page)
  still applies.

One of the migrations that shipped in v0.111.0,
`2026-10-14-100100-discovered-assets-manual-source.sql`, backfills a new
provenance column on discovered network assets. On a database where those
`discovered_assets` rows span **more than one organization or partner**, the
backfill's two update statements can request the partner-export lock
hierarchy out of order, which Postgres rejects. The migration transaction
rolls back, `autoMigrate` retries it on the next boot, and **the API never
finishes starting** — a crash loop, not a degraded mode. A single-partner or
empty install is not affected.

v0.111.1 adds a new migration,
`2026-10-14-100050-discovered-assets-source-backfill-prelock.sql`, which sorts
immediately before the failing one. It acquires every partner and
organization lock the backfill will need, up front and in the correct order,
so that by the time the original migration replays, it has nothing left to
do and completes normally.

**If your API is already crash-looping on v0.111.0**, you have two ways out:

1. **Upgrade to v0.111.1** (recommended). The failed migration's transaction
   rolled back cleanly, so nothing is half-applied — pulling v0.111.1 and
   restarting is sufficient on its own.
2. **Apply the fix-forward SQL below by hand** against your database, using
   the same role your migrations run as, then restart the API on v0.111.0
   before upgrading further:

```sql
   BEGIN;

   -- The failed migration rolled back its own CREATE TYPE / ADD COLUMN, so in the
   -- crash-loop state the `source` column does NOT exist yet: create it first
   -- (guarded, so this is also safe where it already exists).
   DO $$ BEGIN
     CREATE TYPE public.discovered_asset_source AS ENUM ('scan', 'unifi', 'manual');
   EXCEPTION WHEN duplicate_object THEN NULL;
   END $$;
   ALTER TABLE public.discovered_assets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS source public.discovered_asset_source;
   ALTER TABLE public.discovered_assets ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS url text;

   -- Required: the lock helpers read organizations, and discovered_assets is
   -- FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY. Without this the discovery SELECTs return no rows
   -- and the UPDATEs match nothing, silently.
   SELECT set_config('breeze.scope', 'system', true);

   -- Acquire every affected partner (shared) and organization (exclusive) export
   -- lock in ascending order BEFORE the backfill, so the per-row triggers find
   -- them already held.
   SELECT public.breeze_partner_export_lock_partners_shared(ARRAY(
     SELECT DISTINCT o.partner_id
       FROM public.discovered_assets d
       JOIN public.organizations o ON o.id = d.org_id
      WHERE d.source IS NULL AND o.partner_id IS NOT NULL
      ORDER BY 1));

   SELECT public.breeze_partner_export_lock_orgs_exclusive(ARRAY(
     SELECT DISTINCT d.org_id
       FROM public.discovered_assets d
      WHERE d.source IS NULL AND d.org_id IS NOT NULL
      ORDER BY 1));

   UPDATE public.discovered_assets a
      SET source = 'unifi'
    WHERE a.source IS NULL
      AND (a.detected_type_source = 'unifi_controller'
           OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.unifi_devices u
                       WHERE u.discovered_asset_id = a.id));

   UPDATE public.discovered_assets SET source = 'scan' WHERE source IS NULL;

   COMMIT;
```

   This is idempotent: on a database where the migration already succeeded,
   every statement is a no-op.

**Recovery for a deployment that is already stuck in the crash loop:**

1. Set `BREEZE_VERSION=0.111.1` in `.env` (or apply the fix-forward SQL above
   against v0.111.0 first, if you cannot upgrade immediately).
2. `docker compose pull api web portal && docker compose up -d binaries-init api`.
3. Wait for the API to report healthy (`curl -sf https://yourdomain/health`).
4. Once the API is healthy, bring the rest of the stack back up:
   `docker compose up -d web portal`.

No schema shape changes beyond v0.111.0: the same enum, the same two columns,
the same constraints. The new migration only moves the backfill earlier and
wraps it in the correct lock order.

sections.heading: v0.111.0 — offline work queue, script cancellation, organization record page
sections.text:
**No breaking API changes and no new *required* environment variables.** But
**five defaults change on upgrade**, and two of them will alter what your
customers and your technicians see the moment the API restarts. Read
[Behaviour changes](#behaviour-changes-in-v01110) before you pull.

**Pull the `portal` container too**, alongside `api` and `web` — and `worker` if
you have opted into the [worker split](/deploy/worker-split/).

**Do these two things before you pull:**
  1. **If you have QuickBooks connected and are not ready for Breeze to write payments into a customer's books**, turn **Payment push** off first (Integrations → QuickBooks). It ships **on**. See [Payment push](/features/accounting-integrations/#payment-push).
  2. **If you run network monitors with alert rules**, review those rules, your notification channels and your escalation policies. Monitor alerts now notify and fire automations where before they only sat in the inbox. See [Network Monitors](/features/network-monitors/#what-a-monitor-alert-now-does).

#### Database migrations in v0.111.0

**35 migrations. Take a database backup first.** All are idempotent and apply
automatically on API startup unless you have set `AUTO_MIGRATE=false`.

**Two migrations deliberately abort the deploy on bad pre-existing data:**
  Both concern custom fields, and both are intentional — the alternative is
  silently picking a winner among rows that are supposed to be unique. Each ships
  with a **preflight** query so you can find out before you pull rather than
  during:

  | Migration | Aborts on | Preflight |
  |---|---|---|
  | `2026-10-10-100300-custom-field-definition-integrity.sql` | Duplicate or ownerless custom-field definitions | `apps/api/migrations/preflight/2026-10-10-100300-custom-field-definition-integrity-preflight.sql` |
  | `2026-10-11-141000-custom-field-no-cross-axis-shadowing.sql` | A custom-field key defined at both the organization and the partner level for the same device | `apps/api/migrations/preflight/2026-10-11-141000-custom-field-shadowing-preflight.sql` |

  Run both against your database **before** you upgrade and reconcile anything
  they report. See [Custom Fields → Uniqueness and shadowing](/features/custom-fields/#uniqueness-and-shadowing).

Six indexes are built **concurrently**, so writes are not blocked while they run —
on a large `audit_logs` or process-sample history they are the long pole and the
API does not serve until they finish. An interrupted build leaves an invalid index
that the next boot reports loudly; recover with `DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY <name>`
and restart.

Three migrations touch existing rows and record what they did as a Postgres
`WARNING`. Read these in the API log after the first boot:

| Log line | What it means |
|---|---|
| `device_custom_field_values backfill: copied N value(s)`, `minted N definition(s) for previously undefined keys`, `N stored key(s) do not match the enforced key pattern` | Custom-field values move into a table of their own. Sized by devices × custom-field keys. Keys written before the naming rules were enforced are deliberately kept in the old projection only, so nothing is lost or renamed under you. |
| `backfilled N discovered_assets rows to source=unifi` / `source=scan` | Every discovered asset gains a provenance column. Sized by your **discovery** inventory, not your device count — on a large scanned estate this is the longest single statement in the set. |
| The Partner Admin forced-MFA stamp | Records the reconcile described under [Behaviour changes](#behaviour-changes-in-v01110). **Enforcement is off this release**, so nothing changes for your admins at upgrade time. |

**One hot-table lock worth planning around:**
  The offline-work-queue migration adds a foreign key and a partial index to the
  agent command table **without** the concurrent/deferred options, so it holds an
  exclusive lock on the agent command path for one sequential scan. At ordinary
  sizes that is seconds. If you retain **millions** of device commands, build both
  by hand before you pull — add the constraint `NOT VALID` then `VALIDATE`, and
  create the index `CONCURRENTLY` under the name the migration uses
  (`idx_device_commands_deliver_by`) — and the migration's guards will no-op at
  boot.

A non-superuser migrating role is sufficient, as in every previous release: the
range creates no roles, extensions, or schema-level grants.

#### New optional settings in v0.111.0

None are required and none fail boot when missing — except `PLAY_INTEGRITY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT`,
which is validated when set. Full descriptions are in
[Environment Variables](/deploy/environment/).

| Variable | Why you might set it |
|---|---|
| Offline work queue | Queueing is always enabled for queueable actions. The former opt-out has been removed; use action-specific offline policies where available. |
| `DEVICE_COMMAND_QUEUE_TTL_HOURS`, `DEVICE_COMMAND_QUEUE_SHORT_TTL_HOURS`, `DEVICE_COMMAND_QUEUE_POWER_STATE_TTL_HOURS` | Shorten or lengthen how long queued work waits for an offline device (7 days / 24 hours / 24 hours). |
| `MFA_FORCE_FOR_PARTNER_ADMIN` | **Now defaults to `false`.** Set `true` to enforce forced MFA for Partner Admins immediately. |
| `AI_OPERATOR_TASKS_ENABLED`, `AI_OPERATOR_RECIPE_SERVICE_RECOVERY_ENABLED` | Turn on the opt-in [AI tasks](/features/ai-tasks/) preview. Both ship off. |
| `READINESS_CACHE_TTL_MS`, `READINESS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` | Tune the new readiness contract. Defaults suit every deployment we know of. |
| `OFFLINE_DETECTOR_WORKER_CONCURRENCY` | Raise offline-sweep concurrency on a very large fleet. |
| `PLAY_INTEGRITY_SERVICE_ACCOUNT` | Verify Android approver devices with Play Integrity as well as hardware Key Attestation. **A malformed value stops the boot** rather than silently reporting "not configured" forever. |

#### Readiness versus liveness

`/health` is unchanged and remains **liveness** — it answers 200 before the
instance can actually serve. `/ready` and `/health/ready` now answer a real
aggregate readiness question, and API admission is gated on the consumers the
process role requires. **If your load balancer or Compose healthcheck should hold
traffic until Postgres, Redis and the background consumers are genuinely up, point
it at `/ready`.** See [Health Monitoring](/monitoring/health/).

#### Behaviour changes in v0.111.0

- **⚠️ QuickBooks starts pushing payments into every connected realm.** The Payment push switch ships **on**, so a connected realm in automatic push mode begins creating QuickBooks Payments as soon as the API restarts — no operator action. Only payments recorded *after* the switch became active are pushed, and a payment **deletion** always propagates regardless of the switches. Turn it off first if you are not ready. See [Payment push](/features/accounting-integrations/#payment-push).
- **⚠️ Network-monitor alerts now notify, escalate and automate.** ICMP/TCP/HTTP/DNS monitor alerts previously landed in the Alerts inbox only.
