sections.heading: Security & device operations (writes)
sections.text:
These tools change security settings or act on devices. They are available in AI chat and to AI agents. Approval follows the tier shown; see [Tool tiers](#tool-tiers) for what each tier means.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `request_elevation` | 3 | Request a temporary admin elevation on a device. Needs a second approver (four-eyes) |
| `revoke_elevation` | 2 | Revoke an active elevation and request cleanup on the device |
| `create_remote_session` | 3 | Open a remote terminal or file session. Needs a second approver (four-eyes), and respects the remote-access policy and the concurrent-session limits |
| `manage_processes` (list) | 2 | List running processes |
| `manage_processes` (kill) | 3 | Terminate a process |
| `manage_scheduled_tasks` (list) | 2 | List scheduled tasks |
| `manage_scheduled_tasks` (run/disable/enable) | 3 | Run, disable or enable a scheduled task |
| `registry_operations` (read_key/get_value) | 2 | Read Windows registry keys and values |
| `registry_operations` (set_value/create_key/delete_key) | 3 | Change the Windows registry |
| `trigger_agent_restart` | 3 | Restart a silent agent through the watchdog (needs `devices.recover_agent`) |
| `trigger_agent_upgrade` | 3 | Bring an agent to the version it is meant to run. It never overrides an agent version pin, never re-pushes a version the agent already has, and never downgrades |
| `manage_software_policy` (list/get) | 1 | Read software policies. No approval needed |
| `manage_software_policy` (create/update/delete) | 3 | Change software policies |
| `manage_browser_policy` (list) | 1 | List browser policies. No approval needed |
| `manage_browser_policy` (create/update/apply) | 3 | Change browser policies or roll one out to devices |
| `manage_peripheral_policy` (create/update/disable/add_exception/remove_exception) | 3 | Create or change peripheral (USB) policies and exceptions |
| `remediate_sensitive_data` (encrypt/quarantine/secure_delete/accept_risk/false_positive/mark_remediated) | 3 | Encrypt, quarantine, delete or close out a sensitive-data finding |
| `remediate_software_violation` | 3 | Uninstall software that violates a policy |
| `assign_security_training` | 2 | Assign security training to a user |
| `configure_network_baseline` | 3 | Configure a network baseline. Needs approval because it schedules recurring discovery scans |
| `acknowledge_network_device` | 2 | Acknowledge a newly discovered network device |

`sync_edr_data` (Tier 2, v0.124.0+) queues an immediate EDR sync — endpoints and detections — for one connection, the connections serving one organization, or every connection of the partner. Results arrive over the following minutes. It is limited to three calls per ten minutes.

Three of these (user risk scores and detail, plus C2C item search from the backup table above) are available in chat but never to autonomous AI agents — see `AGENT_DENIED_READ_TOOLS` in the codebase for the current denylist, which also covers `query_c2c_jobs`, `get_sensitive_data_overview` and two M365 identity reads.

sections.heading: Security policy tools
sections.text:
These tools read security status and compliance, and manage security recommendations, access reviews, audit-policy baselines, security and compliance policies, disk-encryption recovery keys and PAM elevation rules. They are available in AI chat and over MCP. Text they return that came from a device or a person (hostnames, local admin account names, audit deviations, policy and rule names, review notes) is shown to the model as untrusted data, never as instructions.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `get_security_compliance` | 1 | Security dashboard, score breakdown, 7/30/90-day trend, and AV, firewall, encryption, password-policy and local-admin status by device (`view`). Only what agents reported: no estimated firewall rules or encryption volumes |
| `manage_security_recommendations` (list) | 1 | List security recommendations with their status per organization |
| `manage_security_recommendations` (complete/dismiss) | 2 | Mark a recommendation completed or dismissed for one organization. Nothing changes on devices; reopen it in the web app |
| `manage_access_reviews` (list/get) | 1 | View access reviews: each member's role, permissions and recorded decision |
| `manage_access_reviews` (decide_item) | 2 | Record keep (`approved`) or remove (`revoked`) on one member. Nothing changes until a person completes the review in the web app; you cannot decide on your own access |
| `manage_access_reviews` (create) | 3 | Start an access review of every member of the partner or organization. A review cannot be deleted |
| `manage_audit_baselines` (list/compliance/device_results) | 1 | View audit-policy baselines, compliance across the devices you can see, and one device's deviations |
| `manage_audit_baselines` (request_apply) | 2 | Ask for a Windows audit baseline to be applied to devices. A different person approves the request in the web app, and applying it is also done there |
| `manage_audit_baselines` (create) | 3 | Create a baseline. An active baseline replaces the current one for that OS and starts daily audit-policy collection on those devices |
| `manage_compliance_policies` (deactivate) | 3 | Turn off a compliance policy and close its alerts. Permanent: nothing re-enables it. A partner-wide policy needs a second approver (four-eyes) |
| `manage_security_policies` (list) | 1 | List antivirus/EDR security policy templates |
| `manage_security_policies` (create/update) | 3 | Create or change a security policy template. There is no delete; a partner-wide create needs a second approver (four-eyes) |
| `manage_recovery_keys` (list) | 1 | BitLocker or FileVault key escrow status for a device. Never the key itself, and never who revealed it |
| `manage_recovery_keys` (rotate/collect) | 3 | Rotate a Windows BitLocker recovery key (the old key stops working), or re-collect a device's keys into escrow |
| `manage_pam_rules` (list_rules/get_config/list_signer_groups) | 1 | View PAM elevation rules, the default verdict for unmatched requests, and signer groups |
| `manage_pam_rules` (create_rule/update_rule/delete_rule/set_config/create_signer_group/update_signer_group/delete_signer_group) | 3 | Change PAM rules, the default verdict or signer groups. The assistant can never create an auto-approve rule, and in an organization that has one it can only add rules or rename them |

Three actions are never available to the assistant or to MCP, by design: completing an access review (it removes members and ends their sessions), approving an audit-baseline apply request, and revealing a recovery key. Do these in the web app. Writes to access reviews, compliance policies and PAM rules need a session that has completed MFA.

Access reviews and PAM rules are available in chat and over MCP only; AI agents are never offered them. AI agents can read the rest. Their recommendation, security-policy, compliance-policy and recovery-key writes become proposals that a person approves, and they cannot create audit baselines or apply requests. A session limited to some sites or devices cannot change organization-wide records (security policies, recommendation status, compliance policies, audit baselines) or use access reviews.

sections.heading: Software tools
sections.text:
These tools manage the software catalog, search winget and Homebrew, deploy catalog packages, read and change the software installed on a device, review the software inventory, and handle fleet findings and custom fields. They are available in AI chat and over MCP. Package, vendor and version names, finding titles and custom-field values are shown to the model as untrusted data, never as instructions.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `manage_software_catalog` (list/get) | 1 | View catalog packages with their versions and winget/Homebrew install methods. Download links show the host only |
| `manage_software_catalog` (create/update/import_package) | 2 | Add a package (or import one with its install methods) or edit its name, vendor and description. A partner-wide package (`ownerScope: partner`) needs approval |
| `manage_software_catalog` (add_version/update_version/promote_version/add_install_method/update_install_method/delete_install_method/archive) | 3 | Change which installer a package uses, or archive it. Armed auto-install policies and automations pick up the new installer without another approval, so each change is approved. Versions with install scripts, and partner-wide packages, are changed in the web app |
| `search_packages` | 1 | Search winget (Windows) or Homebrew (macOS) for a package id to add as an install method |
| `manage_software_deployments` (list/get/summary/results) | 1 | View software deployments and each device's result |
| `manage_software_deployments` (cancel) | 2 | Cancel a deployment's pending installs |
| `manage_software_deployments` (create/retry) | 3 | Install a catalog package on up to 100 named devices, or retry failed installs. If the package's installer changes after you approve, the deployment is refused |
| `get_device_software` | 1 | Installed software on one device |
| `manage_device_software` (update/uninstall) | 3 | Update or uninstall an application on one device |
| `bootstrap_homebrew` | 3 | Install Homebrew on one Mac (needs a signed-in admin user) |
| `manage_software_inventory` (list/names/devices) | 1 | Software seen across the fleet, its allow/block status, and the devices that have it |
| `manage_software_inventory` (approve/deny/clear) | 3 | Add software to the organization's default allowlist or blocklist, or remove it. If that policy removes unapproved software automatically, this changes what is uninstalled |
| `manage_fleet_findings` (acknowledge/dismiss/reopen) | 2 | Acknowledge, dismiss or reopen a fleet finding (read them with `get_fleet_findings`) |
| `manage_custom_fields` (create_definition/update_definition) | 2 | Create or edit a custom field definition. A partner-wide definition needs approval to create and is edited in the web app |
| `manage_custom_fields` (delete_definition/set_values) | 3 | Delete a definition (every device's value for it is removed), or set values on one device (the previous values are returned) |

Not available to the assistant or over MCP: uploading an installer, the installer download link, pre- and post-install scripts, deploying to groups or a whole organization, fleet-finding remediation, and the managed-software download-origin policy. Every software, fleet-finding and custom-field write needs a session that has completed MFA.

AI agents can read the software tools. Their catalog, deployment, inventory, fleet-finding and update writes become proposals that a person approves. They are never offered uninstall, `bootstrap_homebrew` or `manage_custom_fields` (custom-field values decide dynamic-group membership, which can widen what an agent may act on). A session limited to some sites or devices cannot change the catalog or the inventory allow/blocklists.

sections.heading: Device inventory and ops tools
sections.text:
These tools read a device's activity timeline, agent health and recorded process snapshots, report which other management products are on the fleet, and manage per-device records: a device's function, linked device profiles, hand-entered (manual) assets and warranties. They are available in AI chat and over MCP. Event messages, process names, product names, asset notes and warranty text are shown to the model as untrusted data, never as instructions.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `get_device_events` | 1 | Activity timeline for one device: what ran, changed or failed, and who or what did it. Actor emails, IP addresses and raw event details are not returned |
| `get_device_health` | 1 | The Breeze agent's latest health report for one device: overall state and each component's state and reason |
| `get_process_samples` | 1 | The recorded top-process snapshot for one device at or before a time (default now). History, not a live process list |
| `get_management_posture` | 1 | Other management products (RMM, endpoint security, backup, MDM, ...) detected across the fleet, per organization; pass `product` for the devices running one |
| `search_agent_logs` | 1 | `source: watchdog` returns only the Breeze watchdog's health journal; `source: agent` leaves it out. Without `source` both are returned, as before |
| `manage_device_function` (get) | 1 | One device's function (domain controller, file server, ...) |
| `manage_device_function` (set) | 3 | Set or clear a device's function. Dynamic groups can target devices by function, so the change is approved |
| `manage_device_links` (list/get/for_device) | 1 | Linked device profiles: multi-boot records of one machine, or a VM host and its guests |
| `manage_device_links` (create/update/dissolve) | 2 | Link 2-10 device records, add or remove members, rename, or unlink them all. Each device keeps its own data |
| `manage_manual_assets` (list) | 1 | Hand-entered inventory without an agent (spare laptops, phones, printers) |
| `manage_manual_assets` (create/update/link/unlink) | 2 | Add or edit a hand-entered asset, retire it (`retiredAt`), or link it to an agent device or discovered asset |
| `manage_manual_assets` (delete) | 3 | Permanently delete a hand-entered asset. Retire it instead to keep the record |
| `manage_device_warranty` (get/expiring) | 1 | One device's warranty, or devices whose warranty ends within a number of days |
| `manage_device_warranty` (refresh) | 3 | Re-check one device's warranty with its manufacturer now. The device's serial number is sent to the manufacturer, so the refresh is approved. Devices whose warranty the agent collects (HP) are refused |
| `browse_device_event_log` (list_logs) | 2 | List a Windows device's event logs, read live from its agent (runs without a prompt, with an audit row) |
| `browse_device_event_log` (query/get_event) | 3 | Read event text from a device's live event logs. Security and Application logs can hold credentials and personal data, so every read is approved. `search_logs` reads the ingested copy without reaching the device |
| `manage_tenant_variables` (list) | 1 | Tenant variables that scripts receive as `{{var.key}}`. Secret values are never shown |
| `manage_tenant_variables` (create/update/delete) | 3 | Change a value that every script on the organization's devices receives. Secret variables and partner-wide variables are changed in the web app; a partner-wide variable can be created here |
| `manage_support_sessions` (list/get) | 1 | Quick Support sessions and whether their temporary client is online |
| `manage_support_sessions` (end) | 3 | End a Quick Support session: the temporary client removes itself from the person's machine. Sessions are started in the web app |

Every write, and every live event-log read, needs a session that has completed MFA. A session limited to some sites or devices cannot change tenant variables or use Quick Support sessions.

AI agents can read these tools. Their link-group and manual-asset writes need an allowlist entry; a manual-asset delete and a warranty refresh become proposals that a person approves. Agents are never offered `manage_tenant_variables` writes (an agent that runs scripts must not also choose their inputs) or `manage_device_function` (set): a device's function decides dynamic-group membership, which can widen what an agent may act on. A session bound to specific devices cannot change link groups or use manual assets, and its reads only show the devices it may see.

---

sections.heading: Context-Aware Help Panel
sections.text:
The dashboard includes a slide-out documentation panel that opens the correct docs page based on your current location in the app. Open it with **Cmd+Shift+H** (macOS) or **Ctrl+Shift+H** (Windows/Linux).

| Page you're on | Docs page that opens |
|---|---|
| Scripts | Scripting docs |
| Patches | Patch management docs |
| Devices | Device management docs |
| Configuration Policies | Policy docs |

The help panel coordinates with the AI chat sidebar — opening one closes the other. When the AI assistant references documentation in a chat response, the links open directly in the help panel instead of a new browser tab.

sections.heading: AI Documentation Search
sections.text:
The AI assistant can search all documentation pages using the `search_documentation` tool (Tier 1, auto-execute). The search index is built at compile time and covers all pages in the docs site.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `search_documentation` | 1 | Search documentation pages by keyword and return relevant sections with direct links |

---

sections.heading: Playbook AI Tools
sections.text:
The AI can list and execute remediation playbooks as part of automated incident response.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `list_playbooks` | 1 | List available playbooks, optionally filtered by category |
| `execute_playbook` | 3 | Execute a playbook on a device with runtime variables (requires approval) |
| `get_playbook_history` | 1 | View execution history for a playbook or device |

See [Playbooks](/features/playbooks/) for playbook definitions and step types.

---

sections.heading: Ticketing & Billing AI Tools
sections.text:
Breeze also provides AI tools for the PSA side of the platform — tickets, invoices, the billing catalog, contracts, and quotes:

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `list_invoices` / `get_invoice` / `manage_invoices` | Browse invoices and manage the invoice lifecycle — drafts, lines, assembling a draft from an organization's billable period or a ticket, issuing, voiding, payments, and Stripe pay links |
| `search_catalog` / `get_catalog_item` | Search the partner billing catalog, including per-organization price overrides and bundles |
| `lookup_distributor_product` | Look up live TD SYNNEX price and availability for a distributor SKU that isn't in your catalog yet — handy when pricing a quote line for a product you don't stock. Reseller cost is hidden for organization-scoped callers |
| `list_contracts` / `get_contract` / `manage_contracts` | Browse recurring contracts and manage drafts, lines, and lifecycle (activate, pause, resume, cancel) |

The ticket, quote, billing-catalog, and PSA admin write tools are tiered per action:

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `manage_tickets (list/get/list_work_types/list_links/merge_preview)` | 1 | Search and read tickets, work types, and ticket links |
| `manage_tickets (create/assign/link_alert/unlink_alert/create_from_alert/link_device/draft/link_ticket/unlink_ticket)` | 2 | Open and assign tickets, link alerts, devices, and related tickets, and store a draft reply for human review |
| `manage_tickets (log_time_entry/start_timer/stop_timer/update_time_entry)` | 2 | Track time against tickets |
| `manage_tickets (bulk_update)` | 2 | Assign, change the status of (not resolve), or set the priority of up to 50 tickets that all belong to one organization. A batch spanning organizations is refused whole, and there is no bulk delete |
| `manage_tickets (comment/update_status/update_fields)` | 2 | Internal notes and ticket updates. A public comment (`isPublic: true`), resolving a ticket or setting a custom status, and changing the requester need approval (Tier 3) |
| `manage_tickets (edit_comment/delete_comment)` | 3 | Edit or delete a comment — customer-visible text with no restore |
| `manage_tickets (merge)` | 3 | Merge two tickets of one organization — irreversible, one approver |
| `manage_tickets (move_org)` | 3 | Move a ticket to a different organization (four-eyes) |
| `manage_quotes (create_draft/update/delete_draft/add_block/update_block/delete_block/reorder_blocks/add_manual_line/add_catalog_line/update_line/remove_line/move_line/reorder_lines)` | 2 | Draft a quote: header, content blocks, and lines on a quote that has not been sent |
| `manage_quotes (decline/create_pay_link)` | 3 | Record a customer's decline, or create a payment link |
| `manage_quotes (send)` | 3 | Send a quote to the customer (four-eyes) |
| `manage_billing_catalog (create_item)` | 2 | Add a billing catalog item (inert until a quote, invoice, or contract uses it) |
| `manage_billing_catalog (update_item/archive_item/set_price/remove_price/set_org_price/remove_org_price/set_bundle_components)` | 3 | Change items, price-book prices, organization price overrides, and bundles — contract renewals bill the live price |
| `manage_saved_filters (list/get)` | 1 | List and view saved device filters |
| `manage_saved_filters (create/delete)` | 2 | Create or delete a saved device filter |
| `manage_tags (list)` | 1 | List device tags |
| `manage_tags (add/remove)` | 2 | Add or remove device tags. AI agents can never change tags, because tags can change which devices an agent is scoped to |
| `manage_notification_channels (list)` | 1 | List notification channels |
| `manage_notification_channels (test)` | 2 | Check a channel's configuration (sends nothing) |
| `manage_notification_channels (create/update/delete)` | 3 | Create, repoint, or delete a channel; the approver sees the destination host. Delete is four-eyes |
| `test_webhook` | 3 | Send a real test delivery to a webhook |

sections.heading: Billing lifecycle tools
sections.text:
These tools read and change how your organizations are billed: rate cards and work types, invoice defaults and each organization's tax, terms and billing contact, the agreement templates customers sign, signed agreements, and which contract lines bill a device. They are available in AI chat and over MCP. Rate-card, settings and device-billing tools need a partner-scoped session, as the matching pages do. Template text, rate-card names and notes, invoice footers and signer names are shown to the model as untrusted data, never as instructions.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `manage_billing_profiles` (list/get/list_work_types/get_org_profile) | 1 | Rate cards with their hourly rates per work type, work types, and the card an organization is billed by |
| `manage_billing_profiles` (create/update/archive/set_rows/clone/create_work_type/update_work_type) | 3 | Change rate cards or work types. They price every organization of the partner, so every change is approved and needs full partner access. The previous values come back with the result. Archiving a work type, and AI price-list edits after a card is created, are done in the web app |
| `manage_billing_profiles` (set_org_profile/clear_org_profile) | 3 | Choose, or clear, the rate card one organization is billed by |
| `manage_billing_settings` (get_partner/get_org/currency_impact/reporting_totals) | 1 | Invoice defaults, one organization's tax, terms, billing contact and address, a preview of what an organization currency change would leave behind, and approximate totals across currencies |
| `manage_billing_settings` (update_partner) | 3 | Change invoice defaults for every organization: currency, tax, invoice prefix and terms, footer, terms and conditions, automatic emails and the seller contact. Needs full partner access. Agreement reminder defaults are set on Billing → Agreements |
| `manage_billing_settings` (update_org) | 3 | Change one organization's tax, payment terms, billing contact (who receives its quotes and invoices) or billing address. A currency change and the rate-card assignment are made elsewhere |
| `manage_contract_templates` (list/get/get_version/usage) | 1 | Agreement templates, their versions and where each is used. Version bodies are read one at a time with `get_version` |
| `manage_contract_templates` (create/update) | 2 | Create or rename an organization's agreement template. For a partner-wide template, pass `ownerScope: partner`; the change is then approved and needs full partner access |
| `manage_contract_templates` (create_version/publish/archive) | 3 | Add a draft version, publish it so quotes and signature requests can use it, or archive the template. None of these can be undone. Partner-wide templates are versioned, published and archived in the web app |
| `manage_contract_documents` (list) | 1 | Signed agreements and whether each is filed under a contract. Signer email addresses are not returned |
| `manage_contract_documents` (link) | 3 | File a signed agreement under a contract of the same organization. It cannot be undone |
| `get_device_billing` | 1 | Which active contract lines bill a device, or why it is not billable |

The existing contract and invoice reads gained one view each: `get_contract` with `periodId` returns that billing period's outcome (devices billed, uncovered and flagged, overages), `list_contracts` with `view: currency_mismatches` lists contracts whose currency differs from their organization's, and `get_invoice` with `lineId` pages the devices one invoice line billed.

Rate-card, work-type and settings writes need a session that has completed MFA. A session limited to some sites or devices cannot change an organization's rate card, billing settings or agreement templates, or file a signed agreement.

AI agents can read these tools. Rate-card and settings writes become proposals that a person approves. Agents are never offered template writes or `manage_contract_documents` (link): agreement templates and signed agreements are the legal documents customers sign. Generating an invoice from a contract and pushing invoices to an accounting system are not available yet.

#### PSA configuration and ticket operations

These tools configure the ticketing side of the platform. They are available in AI chat, and AI agents get the read actions. Partner-wide configuration is changed for every organization at once, so every write needs approval; deleting configuration needs a second approver (four-eyes).

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `manage_ticket_config (get_config/get_org_settings/list_categories/list_domains)` | 1 | Read ticket statuses, priorities, an organization's SLA overrides, categories, and customer email domain mappings |
| `manage_ticket_config (update_org_settings/create_category/update_category/delete_category/reorder_categories/create_status/update_status/reorder_statuses/set_priorities/create_domain/update_domain)` | 3 | Change categories, statuses, priority and SLA settings, an organization's SLA overrides, and which organization a sender's domain routes to. Needs full partner access; statuses, priorities and domains also need an admin role |
| `manage_ticket_config (delete_domain)` | 3 | Remove a customer email domain mapping (four-eyes) |
| `manage_ticket_checklist_templates (list/get)` | 1 | Read checklist templates and their steps |
| `manage_ticket_checklist_templates (create)` | 2 | Create an organization checklist template. A partner-wide template needs approval (Tier 3) |
| `manage_ticket_checklist_templates (update/add_item/update_item/remove_item/reorder_items)` | 3 | Edit a template or its steps |
| `manage_ticket_checklist_templates (delete)` | 3 | Delete a template (four-eyes). A template still used by a deliverable is refused |
| `manage_ticket_inbox (list)` | 2 | Review inbound email the router could not place. The sender, subject and error text come from outside and are treated as untrusted |
| `manage_ticket_inbox (convert/dismiss)` | 3 | Turn one email into a ticket in an organization you choose (the sender becomes the requester), or dismiss it. Neither can be undone |
| `manage_ticket_attachments (list)` | 1 | List the files on a ticket |
| `manage_ticket_attachments (read_content/attach_from_artifact)` | 2 | Read the text of an attachment (images, PDFs and other binary files return their details only), or attach an AI run artifact to a ticket. The attachment stays pending until a person posts a comment with it |
| `manage_ticket_attachments (delete)` | 3 | Permanently delete an attachment |
| `manage_ticket_forms (list/available)` | 1 | Read ticket intake forms, and the forms an organization can use |
| `manage_ticket_forms (create/update)` | 3 | Create or change a customer-visible intake form |
| `manage_ticket_forms (delete)` | 3 | Delete an intake form (four-eyes) |
| `manage_ticket_response_templates (list)` | 1 | Read the partner's canned ticket replies |
| `manage_ticket_response_templates (create/update)` | 3 | Create or change a canned reply |
| `manage_ticket_response_templates (delete)` | 3 | Delete a canned reply (four-eyes) |
| `manage_time_suggestions (list)` | 1 | See your own time-entry suggestions from remote sessions for a day |
| `manage_time_suggestions (confirm/dismiss/undo)` | 2 | Log a suggestion as a time entry, dismiss it, or restore a dismissed one. Your own suggestions only |

AI agents can use the read actions. A write an agent attempts becomes a proposal that waits for a person to approve it. Most of these write actions refuse to run under an agent identity, because the record they create or change needs a signed-in person as its author; creating a ticket form and converting an inbound email are the two that run as the approver once approved. Make the other changes in chat or in the web app. Writing the same settings from the web app is unchanged.

#### Alert correlation and signal triage

These tools read how alerts group together and what is behind a device's unusual behaviour, and record the outcome. They are available in AI chat; AI agents get the read actions and can propose the device-level writes.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `get_alert_correlations (groups/get/by_alert/links/analyze/evaluation/explain)` | 1 | See groups of correlated alerts, the correlations around one alert, how well grouping is working, and root-cause evidence for a group (built from the group's alerts and logs, with no AI model call). Log text comes from the device and is treated as untrusted. Not available to a run that is limited to specific devices |
| `manage_alert_correlations (acknowledge_group/resolve_group/acknowledge_related)` | 2 | Acknowledge or resolve every alert in a correlation group you can see, or an alert and its related alerts. Chat and MCP only: an AI agent cannot act on a whole group |
| `manage_alert_correlations (feedback/rca_feedback)` | 2 | Tell Breeze a correlation was split, merged or dismissed, or that a root-cause analysis was helpful, not helpful, edited or used in a ticket |
| `manage_device_anomalies (list)` | 1 | List unusual metric behaviour detected on a device |
| `manage_device_anomalies (dismiss/resolve)` | 2 | Set an anomaly's status. There is no way back to open |
| `manage_device_anomalies (promote)` | 3 | Raise a real alert from an anomaly. The alert notifies your alert channels, so it needs approval |
| `get_fleet_health (history/offenders/evaluation/org_summary)` | 1 | A device's reliability score over time, the services and components behind its score, how well the scores predict real failures, and an organization rollup with its worst devices |
| `reliability_feedback` | 2 | Label a device's reliability score as a confirmed failure, a replaced device, or a false alarm. Changes nothing on the device |

A dry run of an alert rule is not available: the old per-rule test was retired with the previous alerting model.

#### Network topology

These tools read a site's network map and manage its manual entries, recurring checks and monitoring templates. They are available in AI chat and over MCP for people with the topology permissions; AI agents do not get them (an agent keeps the read-only topology investigation tools). Every call names a site and is limited to the sites you can already see.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `get_topology_graph (graph/nodes/node/relationship/evidence/group_members/expansion/health)` | 1 | Read a site's network map: devices and links, one device or link in detail, the evidence behind a link, the members of a group, and health. Addresses and raw collector data are not returned, and names collected from the network are treated as untrusted text |
| `run_topology_diagnostic (collectors/get)` | 1 | See which devices can run a connectivity check, and read a check's result |
| `run_topology_diagnostic (start/cancel)` | 2 | Start a fixed gateway, DNS, internet or trace-route check from a device at the site, or stop one. Runs in your own signed-in session and is rate limited per user, site and organization |
| `manage_topology_manual` | 2 | Add, change or remove a hand-drawn switch, router, access point or link. A stale revision is refused. Nothing here binds a device or moves one between sites |
| `manage_topology_monitoring (list_policies/list_targets/get_settings)` | 1 | View a site's recurring checks, probe targets and effective topology settings |
| `manage_topology_monitoring (upsert_policy/delete_policy/upsert_target/delete_target/patch_settings)` | 2 | Change a site's recurring checks, probe targets or settings. Arming a recurring check stays a person's action in the topology page, and changing a check that is already armed disarms it |
| `manage_topology_templates (list_templates/list_versions/site_options)` | 1 | View monitoring templates (partner-wide or one organization's), their versions, and the published versions a site can apply |
| `manage_topology_templates (create_template/update_template/create_version)` | 2 | Draft a template or a new version. Nothing takes effect until a version is published. Partner-wide templates need full partner access |
| `manage_topology_templates (publish_version/revoke_template)` | 3 | Publish a version so sites can apply it, or revoke a template permanently (this disables every check that uses it). Needs approval |
| `apply_topology_template (preview)` | 2 | Preview what applying a template would change on named sites. Changes nothing |
| `apply_topology_template (apply)` | 3 | Apply a previewed template to its sites, replacing their monitoring configuration. Needs approval. Sites outside the approving session's organization report their own outcome |
| `apply_topology_template (status)` | 1 | See how an application is progressing, site by site |

#### SNMP and network monitoring

These tools read and manage SNMP monitoring templates, read SNMP metric history, check a discovered asset on demand, keep the shared known-guest list, and read or sync the partner's UniFi integration. Template, metric and asset-check tools follow your organization and site access and are also available to AI agents. The known-guest and UniFi tools act on partner-wide state, so they need full partner access and are available in AI chat and over MCP only. Every write needs a signed-in session that has satisfied MFA, the same as the matching page.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `manage_snmp_templates (list/get/browse_oids/validate_oids)` | 1 | View SNMP templates (the OIDs polled per device class), search known OIDs, and check an OID list. Names and descriptions are treated as untrusted text |
| `manage_snmp_templates (create/update/delete)` | 2 | Create, change or delete a custom template. Built-in templates are read-only, a template still used by a device cannot be deleted, and the delete result keeps the old row so it can be recreated. A session limited to some sites or devices cannot change a template, because every site in the organization reads it |
| `get_snmp_metrics (history/dashboard)` | 1 | Bucketed SNMP history (interface traffic, uptime and other OIDs) for one discovered asset, with a capped number of series, or the SNMP dashboard |
| `probe_network_asset` | 2 | Check now: ping a discovered asset from an online agent in the same site and report reachable or not. One probe per asset at a time; waits a few seconds, otherwise reports pending |
| `manage_known_guests (list)` | 1 | View the partner-wide list of known guest MAC addresses that discovery does not flag |
| `manage_known_guests (add/delete)` | 2 | Add or remove a known guest MAC address for every organization of the partner |
| `get_unifi_status (status/hosts/collectors/mappings/telemetry/sync_runs/controller_sites)` | 1 | Read the partner's UniFi integration: connection, consoles and sites (a read-only call to the vendor), collectors, site mappings, device and client telemetry for one site, and the last 20 sync runs. Vendor payloads, keys and error bodies are not returned |
| `trigger_unifi_sync` | 2 | Queue a manual sync of the UniFi integration, then read the outcome with `get_unifi_status` `sync_runs` |

Connecting or disconnecting UniFi, editing site mappings and collectors, and the retired per-device SNMP polling, test and threshold pages are not available as tools. The old SNMP device and threshold endpoints are deprecated; per-asset SNMP settings and network-monitor alert rules replace them.

#### AI agent read tools

These tools let you ask the assistant what the AI has done and is planning. They only read: starting, changing or cancelling a schedule, an operator task or a Fleet Design is a separate, approval-gated action. Text they return (task objectives, hand-off notes, step and timeline text, Fleet Design markdown) is shown to the model as untrusted data, never as instructions.

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `get_device_ai_activity` | 1 | Count the scripts and commands the AI dispatched to one device in the last 7 to 30 days. Add `source` (`execution` or `command`) and `sourceId` to see who started that one action (AI assistant, AI agent or flow). A device you cannot see is reported as not found |
| `list_operator_tasks` | 1 | List the multi-step tasks the AI operator is running or has finished, newest first, with state, objective and what happens next |
| `get_operator_task` | 1 | One operator task: targets, steps, the newest 500 timeline events, the plan it proposed and the agent runs behind it. Credential hand-over details are never shown; an account the task created shows only its credential state |
| `list_ai_agent_schedules` | 1 | When AI agents run on a schedule, including the effective schedule after an organization override of a partner baseline. A partner baseline's fleet-wide run summary is shown only to callers with access to every organization of the partner |
| `list_fleet_designs` | 1 | List completed Fleet Design reports (up to 100) with function, watch and rule counts |
| `get_fleet_design` | 1 | One Fleet Design report as markdown (capped at 60,000 characters), with counts and when it was generated |

The operator task and Fleet Design tools describe a whole organization, so a session limited to some sites or devices cannot use them. The operator task tools are available in AI chat and over MCP only: AI agents are never offered them, because task text is written by people and by other agent runs. The device, schedule and Fleet Design tools are also available to AI agents; a device-bound agent can read only its own device.

All seven tools are now available in the assistant chat, not just over MCP. AI agents get the read actions by default and the write actions only when the agent's tool allowlist names them; tag changes are never available to agents. Public ticket comments, resolving a ticket, and changing a ticket's requester need approval, while internal notes do not. The billing price book tool is `manage_billing_catalog` (renamed from `manage_catalog`; the old name keeps working over MCP for one release).

Financially binding or high-impact actions — issuing or voiding an invoice, recording or voiding a payment, contract lifecycle changes, sending a quote, changing a catalog price, and moving a ticket to another organization — are classified Tier 3, so they wait for a human approval rather than auto-executing. Drafting and editing (create_draft, adding lines, updating a draft) stays Tier 2 no matter how large the draft's total is — the tier boundary here is reversibility, not financial size: a draft is an internal, editable record until the commit action (send/issue/activate) exposes it beyond Breeze. See the [MCP Server documentation](/features/mcp-server/#ticketing-tools) for per-tool tiers, scopes, and required role permissions, including the note on why this differs from the tenant-structure gating on tools like `create_org`.

---

sections.heading: Model refusals
Configuring a refusal fallback
sections.text: An administrator can give a model a **refusal fallback** under **Partner Settings → AI Providers & Models**. The fallback must be another enabled model on the **same connection**, so it never changes who pays for the request. On the Claude API, Breeze asks Anthropic to retry the turn on the fallback model in the same request. On a catalog provider, Breeze retries once itself. The turn is billed at the rate of the model that served it.

sections.heading: Choosing a model in chat
sections.text:
When your partner allows it, the chat composer has a model menu. It lists the models you may use, with each model's context size and price per million tokens. A model your role can't use is shown greyed out with the role that grants it. Next to the menu, set the options the chosen model supports:

- **Effort** — how much the model reasons before answering (adaptive-thinking models).
- **Fast** — a faster, more expensive mode, shown where your administrator enables it and the model supports it; its rate is shown next to the switch.
- **Thinking** — an on/off switch for models that think with a fixed budget.

Your choice applies from your next message. While the model reasons, the chat shows **Thinking…**. Under each answer, the chat shows the model and options that actually answered. A model can decline a request and hand it to another, and Fast can be unavailable for a moment, so this can differ from what you picked.

Administrators can lock a feature to one model under **Partner Settings → AI Providers & Models → Defaults by feature** (turn off **Users may choose**). The menu is then hidden for that feature.

From v0.124.0 a partner can hold more than one Anthropic connection under **AI Providers & Models**. Only the first takes over the features that used the platform key, and models found on a later connection arrive disabled until an administrator enables them. See [Bring your own LLM key](/features/bring-your-own-llm-key/).

sections.heading: Switching models mid-conversation
sections.text: Switching to another model keeps the conversation when the new model is on the same AI connection and the conversation fits its context window. Breeze counts the conversation with the new model before switching. Otherwise Breeze offers **Continue with the new model in a new chat**: the newly chosen model summarises the conversation and a linked chat starts from that summary. Your message is kept either way, and you can choose **Keep the current model** instead.

sections.heading: The model an AI agent uses
sections.text: An agent's settings include a **Model** field: use the AI agents default, or pick one of the models allowed for AI agents. Picking a model that needs a permission requires you to hold that permission.

sections.heading: Backup models
Billing
sections.text: Each attempt is billed to the source that served it: Breeze AI credits for a Breeze-provided model, or your provider account for a model on your own API key. An attempt the provider rejected costs nothing. Failover moves between Breeze credits and your own API key only when **Allow failover between Breeze credits and your own API key** is on for that feature. Before a backup on Breeze credits is used, Breeze checks your credit balance and AI budget again.

sections.heading: Chat
sections.text: A chat message is never re-sent to another model partway through a reply. If a message fails before the model writes anything, the model cools down and your next message uses a backup. A conversation that already has history only moves to a backup on the same AI connection, and only when the conversation fits that model; otherwise it stays on its model. Your own model choice is kept, and Breeze goes back to it once it recovers. If the model you were using was disabled or retired, the conversation moves to the backup for good.

sections.heading: Escalation roles for AI agents
sections.text:
The AI agents feature has three roles, each with its own default and backups:

| Role | Runs |
|---|---|
| **Triage** | Alert verdicts, ticket triage, and sweeps in shadow mode |
| **Analysis** | Investigations, narratives, designs, patch planning, and full runs in shadow mode |
| **Remediation** | Full runs and sweeps in act mode, which can change devices |

A role you leave unset uses the AI agents default. An agent pinned to a specific model in its own settings keeps that model; the role's allowed models and backups still apply to it. An agent run fails over only before the model has written anything or run a tool, so no action is ever run twice.

sections.heading: Organization overrides
sections.text: **Organization Settings → AI → Model defaults** can narrow a feature's backup list (or set it to no backups) and can turn cross-funding failover off. An organization cannot add backups the partner did not allow, and cannot turn cross-funding failover on. An organization that overrides the AI agents default keeps the partner's triage, analysis and remediation defaults, within the models it allows.

sections.heading: Usage
sections.text: The **Failovers** column on the AI usage page counts calls that a backup model served.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
**Tier 3 action pending but never executing**

Tier 3 actions require manual approval. Open **Security → AI Risk → Approval History** and approve or reject the pending request.

**AI Risk Engine dashboard shows no data**

The dashboard requires at least one AI tool execution to have occurred. Ask the AI assistant a question about your fleet to generate initial data.

**Context entries not appearing for a device**

The AI loads context only for the specific device you ask about. Try: _"What do you know about [hostname]?"_ to trigger explicit context loading.

**`set_device_context` not working**

`set_device_context` is Tier 2 (auto-execute + audit logged) and requires `devices:write` permission. Confirm your role includes write access to devices.

title: Alerts
description: Use the inbox to act on problems, monitors to define conditions and responses, and delivery to decide who is notified.

sections.text:
Alerts is one domain with three facets: **Inbox**, **Monitors**, and **Delivery**.
Alerts are raised by **monitors** you define. Configuration policies select the
devices a monitor reaches.

sections.heading: Inbox
sections.text:
Open **Alerts** to review active problems. Filter by severity, device, status or
time, then open an alert to see its context and history. Acknowledge an alert
when someone takes responsibility; resolve it when the problem is fixed.
Suppression and maintenance windows affect notification/evaluation behavior
according to their configured scope. Correlations remain available when enabled.

Condition-based alerts trace to a monitor. Feature engines such as compliance,
warranty, security, patching and backup also raise alerts; their configuration
remains with those features. From v0.124.0 a configuration policy's
[Security Agents](/features/configuration-policies/#security-agents) setting
raises a medium alert when a device falls into a coverage **Gap** (the required
Huntress or SentinelOne agent is missing and the vendor does not report it) or
when the vendor reports the device under a different organization; both resolve
on their own once coverage is restored.

sections.heading: Monitors
sections.text:
Open **Alerts → Monitors** to create a condition, choose its severity and noise
settings, add device-bound responses, and choose delivery and escalation.
Attach the monitor to a configuration policy and assign that policy to devices.
See [Monitors](/features/monitors/) for kinds, deployment and legacy retirement.

Per-monitor responses run on the device whose alert triggered them. For a broad
workflow such as “any critical CPU alert → triage,” open **Jobs → Alert workflows**.
Optional severity and monitor-kind filters narrow which alerts start that workflow.
Compiler-managed automations are hidden from the Jobs list.

sections.heading: Delivery
sections.text:
Open **Alerts → Delivery** for **Channels**, **Routing**, and **Escalation policies**.
A monitor's Notify setting takes precedence; otherwise routing selects the first
matching row. The explicit **Everything else** row supplies the default. New
channels receive no alerts until added to a routing row or monitor override.
See [Notifications and delivery](/features/notifications/).

sections.heading: Legacy alerting retirement
sections.text:
The legacy policy alert and service/process tabs have been removed. Create and
test conditions in **Alerts → Monitors**, then attach them on a policy's
**Monitors** tab. The previous release offered conversion previews; this release
processes remaining legacy sources at startup. Items that cannot convert are
retired with a reason and listed on **Alerts → Monitors** for review.

Open alerts from unconvertible retired sources stay open until someone resolves
them. Source rows and history are retained, but **Conversion history → Undo** is
unavailable for sources whose runtime was removed in this release. See
[Monitors](/features/monitors/#legacy-rules) for replacement and review guidance.

title: Approval Security
description: Set how strongly a technician must prove identity before approving a privileged action by mapping each risk tier to a Breeze Authenticator assurance level.
headings: How it interacts with PAM and Breeze Authenticator

sections.text:
**Approval Security** governs *how strongly an approver has to authenticate* before a sensitive or privileged action is allowed to proceed. When a PAM elevation or an AI tool action lands in the approval queue, Breeze already knows how risky it is -- it carries a **risk tier**. This tab lets you say, for each risk tier, the minimum **assurance level** the approver must clear on their **Breeze Authenticator** device before their "Approve" actually counts.

The idea is step-up verification: a low-risk approval can be a quick tap, but signing off on a critical action should demand your strongest proof of identity. Approval Security is the policy that draws those lines.

Reach it at **Settings → Organizations → (organization) → Security & Access → Approval Security**. The policy set here applies across your MSP -- it is the per-partner enforcement floor, not a per-device setting.

  Approval Security sets the *assurance bar* for a decision. It does not decide *whether* an action needs approval in the first place -- that is [Privileged Access Management](/features/pam/) (the rule chain, the queue, and the auto-approve / require-approval verdicts). PAM decides an action needs a human; Approval Security decides how convincingly that human must authenticate.

sections.heading: Risk tiers and assurance levels
sections.text:
Every approvable action is classified into one of four **risk tiers**. Breeze ships a default **assurance floor** for each -- the minimum verification strength required out of the box:

| Risk tier | Breeze default floor |
|---|---|
| **Low risk** | L1 |
| **Medium risk** | L2 |
| **High risk** | L3 |
| **Critical risk** | L4 |

The four **assurance levels** describe increasingly strong proof, performed on the approver's enrolled Authenticator device:

| Level | What the approver must do |
|---|---|
| **L1 -- session tap** | A simple tap to confirm within an authenticated session. |
| **L2 -- biometric** | A biometric check (Face / fingerprint). |
| **L3 -- biometric + PIN** | Biometric plus a PIN. |
| **L4 -- hardware key + re-auth** | A hardware-attested, platform-bound security key -- Breeze verifies the attestation server-side, not just a claim from the device -- plus fresh re-authentication (password or login MFA). |

  The policy is **raise-only**. For any tier you can require a *higher* assurance level than the Breeze default, but you can never drop below it -- the dropdown simply doesn't offer the weaker options, and the server re-validates the same rule. An override that would weaken the floor is ignored (fail-closed). You also cannot pick a level an approver device can never produce for that tier -- the highest reachable level is L2 for low and medium, L3 for high and L4 for critical -- because such a floor would block every approval at that tier. A previously saved floor above that is treated as the highest reachable level.

An AI-authored script proposal's risk tier comes from its independent reviewer and feeds into this same floor table like any other approvable action. A proposal that matched a strict security pattern additionally requires the approver to hold the Scripts permission and complete a fresh MFA check before they can approve it, regardless of the proposal's risk tier — see [AI Script Authoring & Review](/features/ai-script-authoring/#the-approval-card).

**One ceremony for a run of supervised approvals:**
  From v0.113.0, approving several supervised Tier-3 AI tool calls in a row no longer prompts a passkey or authenticator ceremony for each one. The first ceremony issues a short-lived grant — **120 seconds**, bound to your identity, session and current factors, and separately audited — which the decisions that follow reuse. **Four-eyes approvals are unaffected** and still take a fresh ceremony every time; a grant presented on a four-eyes decision is refused and the normal ceremony runs instead.

sections.heading: Configuring approval assurance
sections.text:
1. Open **Settings → Organizations → (organization) → Security & Access → Approval Security**.

2. For each **risk tier** (Low, Medium, High, Critical), pick the minimum **assurance level** you want to require from the dropdown. Only levels at or above the Breeze default for that tier are selectable.

3. Choose whether an approver device is required:
   - **Platform default** (what a partner that never saved a choice gets) -- high- and critical-risk approvals require a registered approver device from the platform date (5 November 2026 on hosted Breeze; self-hosters can move it with `APPROVER_ASSURANCE_DEFAULT_ENFORCE_FROM`). Low- and medium-risk approvals are allowed below the floor and recorded as downgraded. The tab shows the inherited value and its date.
   - **Required** -- enforce the policy at every risk tier: under-assured approvals (including approvals from a technician who hasn't enrolled an Authenticator device) are blocked rather than merely flagged.
   - **Not required** -- never block; approvals below the floor are allowed and recorded as downgraded. This explicit choice is kept after the platform date.

4. With **Required**, optionally set an **Enforce from** date. This is the grace-window cutoff: before that date the policy is advisory, giving your team time to enroll their devices; on and after it, enforcement is live. Leave it blank to enforce immediately.

5. Click **Save**.

sections.heading: Enrolling an approver device
sections.text:
Registering a Breeze Authenticator (approver) device always requires a **fresh identity check that is independent of the login session** -- possession of a signed-in browser or a stolen token is never enough to enroll a new approval device.

- **From the web dashboard**, registering a device prompts for a step-up in order of strength: a **passkey** tap if you have one enrolled, otherwise your **TOTP code**, otherwise your **password**. If your account has a passkey or TOTP factor, the password fallback is refused -- the server insists on the strongest factor you own (except on deployments with MFA disabled platform-wide, where the password path remains available). A newly registered device shows a **"pending — activates on first approval"** badge until it decides its first request.
- **From the mobile app**, no separate ceremony is needed: signing in (including completing your MFA challenge) authorises the app to register itself as your approver device on that login. If registration couldn't happen at sign-in, the app shows a banner and completes it on your **next login**.

Each device in the list carries a badge -- **Hardware-attested** or **Not attested** -- showing whether Breeze has server-verified proof that its signing key lives in hardware. Only a hardware-attested device can satisfy the **L4** assurance floor for critical-risk approvals; a device marked **Not attested** still works for lower tiers, but critical-tier approvals from it are refused, even if it was already enrolled. On mobile this usually means the app needs an update -- see [Approver Device Registration and Assurance](/features/mobile/#approver-device-registration-and-assurance) for what determines the badge and how the app's own banner explains it. A **passkey / platform authenticator** registered from a browser is treated as hardware-attested for this purpose, as long as it is a single-device, non-backed-up credential.

  Mobile app builds older than v0.99.0 used a flow the server no longer accepts, so registration from an outdated app fails until the app is updated. If a technician's phone stops registering as an approver device after a server upgrade, update the Breeze mobile app. A device that *does* register on an older build still shows **Not attested** and stays capped below L4 until it is updated.

sections.heading: How it interacts with PAM and Breeze Authenticator
sections.text:
When an approver acts on a request from any surface (the [Privileged Access](/features/pam/) console, the Helper desktop app, or the mobile app), Breeze looks up the request's risk tier, resolves the required assurance level from this policy, and demands that level of verification on the approver's **Breeze Authenticator** device before recording the decision.

- **PAM elevations** -- UAC intercepts and Tech JIT admin requests are risk-tiered, so the assurance floor you set here is what an approver must clear to grant them.
- **AI tool actions** -- privileged actions proposed by the Breeze AI agent or Helper carry a risk tier (for example T2 / T3) and are held for a human; the approver must meet the matching assurance level to sign off.
- **Microsoft 365 identity actions** -- the eight account actions added in v0.124.0 (revoke sessions, assign or remove a licence, add to or remove from a group, retire an Intune device, create a user, set an auto-reply) are always **four-eyes**: the requester never approves their own request, and the second approver takes a fresh ceremony every time. A password reset or account disable additionally needs a current [caller verification](/security/caller-verification/) of the target account; without one it is refused -- in chat, over MCP, and again when an approved request is released -- until a verification exists.

Because an approval always requires a *separate* human identity from the requester, Approval Security is what makes "confirmed with MFA" concrete: it defines exactly how strong that confirmation has to be for the risk at hand.

**Platform default:**
  Until a partner saves an enforcement choice, the approvals inbox and this tab show a notice with the date the platform default starts requiring an approver device for high- and critical-risk approvals, and afterwards explain why those approvals ask for one. The server applies the same rule to every surface -- the web console, the mobile app and a direct API call are refused alike.

  If enforcement is live (**Required** past its date, or the platform default past the platform date for high/critical), a technician who has not enrolled a Breeze Authenticator device -- or who can only satisfy a level below the tier's floor -- cannot approve requests at that tier. Make sure your approvers are enrolled before the **Enforce from** date arrives.

sections.heading: Related
sections.text:
- [Privileged Access Management](/features/pam/) -- the rule chain, request queue, and elevation flows whose approvals this policy governs.
- [Users & Roles](/reference/users-and-roles/) -- roles, permissions, and MFA for the technicians who act as approvers.

title: Audit Baselines
description: Establish audit policy baselines, detect configuration drift, and enforce CIS-aligned event log settings across your fleet.
headings: No compliance results appear for devices
Compliance score is lower than expected
Apply request shows "OS mismatch" for devices
"Requester cannot approve their own apply request"
Approval was consumed but commands failed

sections.text:
Audit Baselines let you define the expected audit policy configuration for your managed devices, automatically detect when devices drift from those expectations, and remediate non-compliant systems through an approval-gated workflow. Breeze ships with built-in CIS Level 1 and Level 2 templates for Windows, macOS, and Linux, and supports fully custom baselines for organizations with their own compliance requirements.

The system works in three phases: first, baselines define what the audit policy should look like. Second, the agent periodically collects the actual audit policy state from each device and reports it to the API. Third, a background drift evaluator compares the collected state against the active baseline for that OS type, scores the result, and publishes compliance events. When deviations are found, administrators can review the specific settings that drifted and, for Windows devices, push the baseline directly to the device through an approval-gated apply workflow.

---

sections.heading: Using the Console
sections.text:
Open **Compliance Baselines** from the Security section of the left sidebar. The page has three tabs:

| Tab | What it shows |
|-----|---------------|
| **Dashboard** | Fleet-wide compliance totals and a per-baseline breakdown (device counts, compliant/non-compliant, average score) |
| **Baselines** | The list of configured baselines, with create, edit, and delete controls |
| **Approvals** | Pending, approved, and rejected apply requests, with **Approve**/**Reject** actions on pending rows |

Clicking a baseline opens its detail page with **Overview**, **Compliance**, and **Apply** tabs -- Compliance shows per-device drift for that baseline, and Apply is where you push it to devices:

1. From a baseline's **Apply** tab, select the target devices.
2. Run the preview (dry run) to see which devices are eligible and what would change.
3. Submit the request. It appears in the **Approvals** tab as pending.
4. A different user than the requester approves or rejects it -- Breeze rejects a self-approval attempt.
5. Once approved, the apply executes against the selected devices; the approval record tracks when it was consumed.

---

sections.heading: Profiles
sections.text:
| Profile | Description |
|---|---|
| `cis_l1` | CIS Benchmark Level 1 -- baseline security settings suitable for most environments |
| `cis_l2` | CIS Benchmark Level 2 -- stricter settings for high-security environments |
| `custom` | User-defined settings (requires explicit `settings` object) |

sections.heading: Baseline Fields
sections.text:
| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Unique identifier for the baseline |
| `orgId` | UUID | Organization that owns this baseline |
| `name` | string (max 200) | Human-readable baseline name |
| `osType` | enum | Target OS: `windows`, `macos`, or `linux` |
| `profile` | enum | One of `cis_l1`, `cis_l2`, `custom` |
| `settings` | JSON | Key-value map of expected audit policy settings |
| `isActive` | boolean | Whether this baseline is used for drift evaluation |
| `createdBy` | UUID | User who created the baseline |
| `createdAt` | datetime | When the baseline was created |
| `updatedAt` | datetime | When the baseline was last modified |

Only one baseline can be active per organization per OS type. When you activate a baseline, any previously active baseline for the same org and OS is automatically deactivated.

sections.heading: Compliance Result Fields
sections.text:
| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Unique identifier for the result |
| `orgId` | UUID | Organization ID |
| `deviceId` | UUID | Device that was evaluated |
| `baselineId` | UUID | Baseline the device was evaluated against |
| `compliant` | boolean | Whether the device fully matches the baseline |
| `score` | integer (0-100) | Percentage of settings that match |
| `deviations` | JSON array | List of settings that deviated from expectations |
| `checkedAt` | datetime | When the evaluation was performed |
| `remediatedAt` | datetime | Set when a device returns to compliance after a prior deviation |

sections.heading: Deviation Structure
sections.text:
Each entry in the `deviations` array contains:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `setting` | string | The audit policy setting key (e.g., `auditpol:logon`) |
| `expected` | any | The value defined in the baseline |
| `actual` | any | The value observed on the device (null if missing) |
| `reason` | enum | `missing` (setting not found on device) or `mismatch` (value does not match) |

---

sections.heading: Built-in Templates
sections.text:
Breeze includes six CIS-aligned templates that are seeded for each organization. These provide sensible defaults and can be activated as-is or used as a starting point for custom baselines.

**Windows:**

**CIS L1 (Windows)**

| Setting | Expected Value |
|---|---|
| `auditpol:logon` | `success_and_failure` |
| `auditpol:account lockout` | `success_and_failure` |
| `auditpol:security state change` | `success` |
| `auditpol:system integrity` | `success_and_failure` |

**CIS L2 (Windows)**

Includes all L1 settings plus:

| Setting | Expected Value |
|---|---|
| `auditpol:process creation` | `success_and_failure` |
| `auditpol:credential validation` | `success_and_failure` |

**macOS:**

**CIS L1 (macOS)**

| Setting | Expected Value | Comparison |
|---|---|---|
| `audit_control.flags` | `lo` | includes |
| `audit_control.naflags` | `lo` | includes |
| `audit_control.policy` | `cnt` | includes |
| `audit_control.filesz` | `5` | >= |

**CIS L2 (macOS)**

| Setting | Expected Value | Comparison |
|---|---|---|
| `audit_control.flags` | `aa` | includes |
| `audit_control.naflags` | `lo` | includes |
| `audit_control.policy` | `cnt` | includes |
| `audit_control.filesz` | `10` | >= |

**Linux:**

**CIS L1 (Linux)**

| Setting | Expected Value | Comparison |
|---|---|---|
| `auditd.enabled` | `true` | equals |
| `auditd.failure_mode` | `single`, `1` | in |
| `auditd.max_log_file_action` | `keep_logs`, `rotate` | in |
| `auditd.space_left_action` | `email`, `syslog`, `single` | in |

**CIS L2 (Linux)**

| Setting | Expected Value | Comparison |
|---|---|---|
| `auditd.enabled` | `true` | equals |
| `auditd.failure_mode` | `single`, `2`, `panic` | in |
| `auditd.max_log_file_action` | `keep_logs` | equals |
| `auditd.space_left_action` | `email`, `single`, `halt` | in |
| `auditd.admin_space_left_action` | `single`, `halt` | in |

---

sections.heading: Comparison Operators
sections.text:
Baseline settings support rich comparison operators for flexible compliance rules. When a setting value is a plain scalar (string, number, boolean), it is compared using deep equality. When the value is an object with an `op` field, the specified operator is used.

| Operator | Description | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `equals` | Exact deep equality | `{ "op": "equals", "value": "success_and_failure" }` |
| `in` | Value matches any item in a list | `{ "op": "in", "values": ["keep_logs", "rotate"] }` |
| `includes` | String contains the value, or array contains the element | `{ "op": "includes", "value": "lo" }` |
| `gte` | Numeric value is greater than or equal to threshold | `{ "op": "gte", "value": 5 }` |
| `lte` | Numeric value is less than or equal to threshold | `{ "op": "lte", "value": 100 }` |
| `regex` | String matches a regular expression (case-insensitive) | `{ "op": "regex", "value": "^success" }` |

---

sections.heading: How Drift Detection Works
sections.text:
1. **Agent collects the audit policy state**

   A background job (`audit-policy-collection`) runs daily at 03:00 UTC and sends a `collect_audit_policy` command to all online devices that have an active baseline matching their OS type. The agent executes the command and returns the current audit policy settings as JSON in the command result.

2. **API persists the policy state**

   When the command result arrives, the API calls `insertAuditPolicyState()` to store the collected settings in the `audit_policy_states` table. Each record captures the device ID, org ID, OS type, normalized settings, raw output, and collection timestamp.

3. **Drift evaluator compares against the active baseline**

   The drift evaluator runs every hour (and also immediately when a baseline is created or updated). It:

   - Retrieves the latest collected policy state for each device.
   - Finds the active baseline for the device's org and OS type.
   - Compares each expected setting against the actual collected value using the appropriate comparison operator.
   - Computes a compliance score: `(passed settings / total expected settings) * 100`.
   - Records the result in `audit_baseline_results` with the full list of deviations.

4. **Compliance events are published**

   - If the device is non-compliant, a `compliance.audit_deviation` event is published with the baseline ID, device ID, score, and deviation details.
   - If the device was previously non-compliant but is now fully compliant, a `compliance.audit_remediated` event is published and the `remediatedAt` timestamp is set on the result.

The compliance score is a percentage. A score of 100 means every setting in the baseline matches the device. A score of 75 means 75% of settings match. The `compliant` flag is only `true` when the score is 100 (zero deviations).

---

sections.heading: Applying Baselines to Devices
sections.text:
For Windows devices, you can push the baseline audit policy settings directly to the device. This requires a two-step approval workflow to prevent accidental or unauthorized changes.

1. **Create an apply request**

   Call `POST /audit-baselines/apply-requests` with the baseline ID and target device IDs. The API validates that the baseline exists, verifies OS compatibility (only Windows is currently supported), and creates a pending approval record.

   Devices with a different OS than the baseline are skipped and returned in the `skipped` array with the reason.

2. **Approve or reject the request**

   A different user (the requester cannot approve their own request) calls `POST /audit-baselines/apply-requests/:approvalId/decision` with `decision: "approved"` or `decision: "rejected"`.

   Approving needs MFA when your MFA policy requires it: if the approver's session has not completed MFA, the API returns `403` with `code: "MFA_REQUIRED"`. API keys and other non-interactive principals have no MFA session, so they cannot approve apply requests while MFA is enabled. Rejecting a request does not need MFA.

   When approving, every device in the request must still exist in the organization. If any device has since been removed (decommissioned or deleted) or moved to another organization, approval returns `409` and the request stays pending. Reject it and have the requester submit a new one. Only a pending request can be decided. If another decision or the expiry lands first, the API returns `409` ("Apply request was already decided").

   Approval requests expire after a configurable duration (default: 60 minutes, range: 5-1440 minutes). Expired requests are automatically marked as `expired` and cannot be approved.

3. **Execute the apply**

   Call `POST /audit-baselines/apply` with the baseline ID, device IDs, and the `approvalRequestId`. The API:

   - Verifies the approval is in `approved` status and has not been consumed or expired.
   - Verifies the device set matches the originally approved set, and that every approved device still exists in the organization and is not decommissioned. Otherwise it returns `409` and leaves the approval unconsumed.
   - Atomically marks the approval as `consumed` (preventing double-use).
   - Queues an `apply_audit_policy_baseline` command for each eligible device with the baseline settings as the payload.

4. **Dry run mode**

   You can preview the apply operation by setting `dryRun: true`. This returns the list of eligible and skipped devices without creating commands or consuming an approval.

sections.heading: Approval Statuses
sections.text:
| Status | Description |
|---|---|
| `pending` | Waiting for an approver to review |
| `approved` | Approved by a different user than the requester |
| `rejected` | Rejected by a reviewer |
| `expired` | The approval window elapsed before a decision was made |
| `consumed` | The approved request was used to execute the apply |

---

sections.heading: API Reference
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/audit-baselines` | List baselines (filterable by org, OS type, profile, active status) |
| `POST` | `/audit-baselines` | Create or update a baseline |
| `GET` | `/audit-baselines/compliance` | Get compliance summary across devices and baselines |
| `GET` | `/audit-baselines/devices/:deviceId` | Get baseline compliance results for a specific device |
| `POST` | `/audit-baselines/apply-requests` | Create an apply approval request |
| `GET` | `/audit-baselines/apply-requests` | List apply approval requests (filterable by status, baseline) |
| `POST` | `/audit-baselines/apply-requests/:approvalId/decision` | Approve or reject an apply request |
| `POST` | `/audit-baselines/apply` | Execute a baseline apply (requires approved request) |

sections.heading: GET /audit-baselines
sections.text:
**Query parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `orgId` | UUID | Filter by organization (optional for partner/system scope) |
| `osType` | enum | Filter by `windows`, `macos`, or `linux` |
| `profile` | enum | Filter by `cis_l1`, `cis_l2`, or `custom` |
| `isActive` | boolean | Filter by active status |

**Response (200):**

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "...",
      "orgId": "...",
      "name": "CIS L1 Audit Baseline (Windows)",
      "osType": "windows",
      "profile": "cis_l1",

      },

      "createdBy": "...",
      "createdAt": "2026-01-15T10:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-03-01T08:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

sections.heading: POST /audit-baselines
sections.text:
Creates a new baseline or updates an existing one. If `id` is provided, the existing baseline is updated. If the profile is not `custom` and no `settings` are provided, the built-in template settings are used automatically.

**Request body:**

```json
{
  "orgId": "...",
  "name": "Custom Windows Audit Baseline",
  "osType": "windows",
  "profile": "custom",
  "settings": {
    "auditpol:logon": "success_and_failure",
    "auditpol:process creation": "success"
  },
  "isActive": true
}
```

**Query parameters:**

**Response (200):**

---

sections.heading: Background Jobs
sections.text:
Two recurring background jobs manage the audit baseline lifecycle:

| Job | Schedule | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `audit-policy-collection` | Daily at 03:00 UTC | Sends `collect_audit_policy` commands to all online devices with an active baseline for their OS |
| `audit-drift-evaluator` | Every hour (on the hour) | Evaluates the latest collected policy state against active baselines and records compliance results |

Both jobs can also be triggered on demand (e.g., drift evaluation runs immediately when a baseline is created or updated).

---

sections.heading: Permissions
sections.text:
| Action | Required Scope | Required Permission |
|---|---|---|
| List baselines | `organization`, `partner`, or `system` | `audit:read` |
| Create/update baseline | `organization`, `partner`, or `system` | `organizations:write` |
| View compliance summary | `organization`, `partner`, or `system` | `audit:read` |
| View device compliance | `organization`, `partner`, or `system` | `audit:read` |
| Create apply request | `organization`, `partner`, or `system` | `devices:write` |
| Approve/reject apply request | `organization`, `partner`, or `system` | `devices:write` |
| Execute apply | `organization`, `partner`, or `system` | `devices:write` |

---

sections.heading: No compliance results appear for devices
sections.text:
- Verify that at least one baseline is active (`isActive: true`) for the target OS type and organization.
- Check that the `audit-policy-collection` job has run. The daily collection runs at 03:00 UTC. You can trigger it manually by creating a baseline or updating an existing one (which enqueues an immediate drift evaluation).
- Ensure target devices are online. The collection job only targets devices with `status: online`.

sections.heading: Compliance score is lower than expected
sections.text:
- Review the `deviations` array in the compliance result to see which specific settings drifted.
- Settings with `reason: "missing"` indicate the agent could not find that setting on the device. This may mean the audit policy category is not configured at all.
- Settings with `reason: "mismatch"` show both the expected and actual values. Verify the baseline settings use the correct comparison operator.

sections.heading: Apply request shows "OS mismatch" for devices
sections.text:
- Baseline apply is currently supported on Windows only. Devices running macOS or Linux will be listed in the `skipped` array with the reason.
- Ensure the `osType` on the baseline matches the target devices' OS type.

sections.heading: Apply request expired before approval
sections.text:
- The default expiration is 60 minutes. Use `expiresInMinutes` (range: 5-1440) when creating the request to set a longer window.
- Once expired, you must create a new apply request. Expired requests cannot be approved.

sections.heading: "Requester cannot approve their own apply request"
sections.text: - This is a deliberate security control. The user who created the apply request must have a different user approve it. This ensures a four-eyes principle for audit policy changes.

sections.heading: Approval was consumed but commands failed
sections.text:
- Check the `failed` array in the apply response. Each entry includes the device ID and error message.
- Common causes: device is offline (command cannot be queued), device already has a pending command of the same type.
- Once an approval is consumed, it cannot be reused. You must create a new apply request and go through the approval process again.

title: Automations
description: Define event-driven, scheduled, and webhook-triggered automations that run actions against target devices and platform services in your fleet.
headings: Adding an automation feature to a policy

sections.text:
Automations let you define rules that execute automatically when something happens across your managed environment. A trigger — a scheduled time, a platform event, an inbound webhook from an external system, or an explicit manual request — causes the automation to run one or more actions against a set of target devices or platform services.

Automations appear in the left nav as **Jobs**. Older `/automations` links redirect.
