- A **Device** chip marks a conversation bound to a device.
- A conversation already open on the other surface is labelled **Open in Breeze AI** (in the side panel's History) or **Open in side panel** (in the Breeze AI list). Picking it moves it there.
- Topology investigations are listed in the side panel only. Script-authoring and MCP sessions are not chat conversations and do not appear in either list.

Opening a conversation from another organization does not change the organization switcher.

sections.heading: Links to a conversation
sections.text:
`/ai/chat#session=<conversation id>` (old `/workspace#session=...` and `/wisp/chat#session=...` links redirect) opens that conversation on the Breeze AI page, or switches to its tab if it is already open. The address follows the tab you are on, so you can copy the link or reload the page and land on the same conversation.

| Message | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **This conversation isn't available** | The conversation does not exist or you cannot access it. |
| **This conversation was closed** | The conversation has ended and can no longer be continued. |
| **Close a tab to open this conversation** | The Breeze AI page already has five tabs. Nothing is closed for you. |
| **Investigations open from the topology map** | Topology investigations live in the side panel; the message offers to open it there. |
| **Continue in side panel to choose a model** | The next message needs a model choice, which is made in the side panel. |

Both surfaces need the **`ai_sessions:use`** permission (see [Who can approve](/features/ai/#who-can-approve)). Signing out clears both surfaces in that browser: the next sign-in starts with no tabs and an empty side panel.

**For self-hosters:**
The conversation list now shows only chat conversations: script-authoring and MCP sessions no longer appear in the side panel's History, and the mobile app's history list changes the same way. API users: `GET /api/v1/ai/sessions` and `/search` return only chat sessions and now include `orgId`, `type` and `deviceId` (search also `status`), and `GET /api/v1/ai/sessions/:id/stream` is a new read-only route that follows a conversation's current reply. No environment variable, migration or proxy change is needed beyond what `POST …/messages` already requires for streaming.

---

sections.heading: Suggested fixes and fix memory
sections.text: On an alert or anomaly, **Suggested Fixes** lists things a technician could do about it. The panel groups suggestions as **Proven fixes** (fixes your fleet has already seen work), **AI suggestions** (from the built-in research agent), **Similar fixes**, and a collapsed **Earlier keyword matches** group. AI suggestions carry an **AI researched** badge. The feature is controlled by the `ml.remediation_suggestions.enabled` flag (see [ML Insights](/features/ml-insights/)); research also needs AI credits (or the organization's AI budget) to be available, and a manual request needs the `ai_sessions:use` permission.

sections.heading: Generate and Research deeper
sections.text:
- **Generate** attaches proven fix memory first: a fix that worked for the same kind of problem on the same operating system is suggested straight away with its track record. It then also starts a **quick** research run, whether or not a proven fix exists, provided you have `ai_sessions:use`. Without that permission the panel tells you so.
- **Research deeper** starts a **deep** research run for the same alert or anomaly. It gets a larger turn and budget ceiling than a quick run, and is meant for when the first answer was not enough.

AI triage consults fix memory first as well, behind the same `ml.remediation_suggestions.enabled` flag. When an alert already has a proven fix that can be attached, shadow-mode triage attaches it instead of starting a triage run. Triage verdict and full alert runs see the alert's proven fixes and their track record, and a full run proposes a proven fix (through the normal approval path) before researching alternatives.

Every attempt ends in an explicit state on the panel, never a silent blank: researching; "AI found no safe fix for this problem"; research failed, with a **Retry** button; still researching after about five minutes ("check back", with **Refresh**); busy, when concurrency or rate limits are reached; no permission; or one of the other reasons a run could not start, such as the feature being off for the organization, AI credits being used up, or the alert having no single device. Asking again while a run is active shows that run instead of starting a second one.

**Research never runs anything.** The research agent is read-only: it can look at device details, logs, your script and playbook catalog and proven fixes, and it submits suggestions. It cannot execute, change or draft a script on its own. A technician always chooses what to accept and run.

sections.heading: What a suggestion can be
sections.text:
| Kind | What it is |
|---|---|
| Catalog script or playbook | One from your own catalog that runs on the device's operating system. Anything else the agent names is dropped by the server. |
| Built-in action | One of `reboot`, `restart_service`, `kill_process` or `disk_cleanup`, with typed parameters (a service name, a process name, or cleanup action IDs). |
| Manual steps | A short list of steps for a person to follow. |
| Script draft request | A brief for a script that does not exist yet. |

**Built-in actions and approval.** Running a built-in action needs `devices:execute` in addition to `scripts:execute`. Each action has a minimum risk level the server enforces regardless of what the agent proposed: `reboot` is always high risk, so it always goes through approval before it runs; `restart_service` and `kill_process` are at least medium; `disk_cleanup` is low. `kill_process` resolves the process by name when you run it and refuses if none or more than one process matches.

**Draft a script.** On a script draft request, **Draft a script** opens the script builder with the brief and language pre-filled (it needs `scripts:write`). If the hand-off cannot be stashed in your browser, the brief is copied to the clipboard as a prompt instead. Nothing is sent or saved until you do it yourself.

sections.heading: Written by AI and reviewed steps
sections.text: Manual steps written by the research agent are labelled **Written by AI — review before following**, and that label stays on the suggestion. After checking the steps, a user with `scripts:write` and partner-wide management rights can use **Save as reviewed steps** to keep a reusable copy for an operating system. When a technician later marks a manual-steps suggestion **Done**, a picker offers the reviewed steps (or "Steps as written (not shared)"). The choice is recorded with the outcome, and once verified outcomes accumulate the fix appears as a proven fix labelled with the reviewed title, visible to your organizations' users. The research agent does not read reviewed steps; it only sees that a proven manual-steps fix exists and its track record.

sections.heading: The Fix memory page
sections.text: **Fix memory** (in the AI Agents section of the navigation) has two tabs. **Fixes** lists what Breeze has learned from observed outcomes, each with its condition, operating system, kind, scope (this client or all clients), status (including Demoted and Stale) and track record. **Reviewed steps** lists the saved reviewed steps and lets you retire them. Only counts are shared across clients, never another client's details. Retire an entry to stop it being suggested. Retiring a fix on the **Fixes** tab needs the AI agents write permission and MFA, and retiring an all-clients fix also needs partner-wide management rights. Saving reviewed steps, and retiring a saved entry on the **Reviewed steps** tab, each need partner-level access, `scripts:write`, partner-wide management rights and MFA.

sections.heading: The "Fix research (built-in)" agent
sections.text:
- **Provisioned for you.** Each partner gets one built-in agent, named "Fix research (built-in)", created the first time research is requested. It cannot be created by hand at partner level.
- **Only a few things are editable.** You can enable or disable it, rename it and adjust its research caps. Its instructions, tools and mode are fixed.
- **Default ceilings.** A quick run is limited to 4 turns and 5 cents; a deep run to 10 turns and 25 cents. These are configurable ceilings, not typical costs. There are also per-hour and concurrency limits.
- **Organization override.** An organization can have its own override of the agent, for example to disable it or set tighter caps for that client. The override carries only those same editable settings.
- **Automatic research.** For **high** and **critical** alerts where no proven fix could be attached, research starts on its own at quick depth, once per alert, and is capped per organization per hour (6 by default). Medium and low alerts are only researched when a technician asks.
- **Credits.** Research runs are billed like other AI agent runs. If credits are exhausted, runs are refused and the panel says why.

---

sections.heading: Device context memory
sections.text: The AI can remember device-specific facts across conversations. When you ask the AI about a device, it automatically loads that device's context entries and incorporates them into its analysis — so it won't re-alert on known quirks or forget about open follow-ups.

sections.heading: Context types
sections.text:
| Type | Purpose | Example |
|---|---|---|
| `issue` | Known problems to track | "Recurring BSOD on boot since Jan 2026" |
| `quirk` | Normal but unusual behaviour | "Slow startup is expected due to a legacy driver" |
| `followup` | Pending actions | "Check disk health after replacement on 2026-03-01" |
| `preference` | User or device preferences | "Maintenance window: Sundays 2 AM–4 AM only" |

sections.heading: Managing context
sections.text:
Context is managed through Breeze AI — there is no separate UI. Ask naturally:

- _"Remember that this device has a recurring BSOD issue."_
- _"Mark the disk check follow-up as resolved."_
- _"What do you know about HOSTNAME?"_

Context entries can have an **expiry date**, which is useful for time-bound follow-ups. Expired entries are excluded from future queries but are not deleted.

The AI uses three tools internally to manage context:

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `get_device_context` | Tier 1 | Load context entries for a device |
| `set_device_context` | Tier 2 | Create a new context entry |
| `resolve_device_context` | Tier 2 | Mark an existing entry as resolved |

  Context is scoped to your organisation. Entries created by one user are visible to all users in the same organisation when they ask the AI about the same device.

  Direct REST endpoints for device context are not yet available. Context is currently managed exclusively through Breeze AI.

title: Bring Your Own LLM Key
description: Connect a partner-owned Anthropic API key (directly or through a platform-vetted endpoint), choose which models each AI feature uses, connect your own OpenAI-compatible endpoint, or configure an instance-wide backend on a self-hosted deployment.
headings: Hosted: use your own Anthropic key
Route your key through a platform-vetted endpoint
Default model and the offered model list

sections.text:
Breeze supports three ways to use your own LLM provider configuration:

- **Anthropic connections** let a partner use its own Anthropic API key for Breeze AI, directly or through a platform-vetted endpoint.
- **OpenAI-compatible connections** let a partner connect its own vLLM, Ollama, LiteLLM, or OpenRouter endpoint with full tool calling.
- **Self-hosted instance configuration** routes platform-keyed AI usage to an Anthropic-compatible or OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

A partner's connections and per-feature defaults decide where each AI request goes. Instance environment variables seed the platform connection on a self-hosted deployment; they never override a partner's connection.

sections.heading: Hosted: use your own Anthropic key
sections.text:
When you connect your own Anthropic API key, all AI features for your partner use that key and are billed directly to your Anthropic account. Breeze AI credits are not consumed.

Knowledge indexing also uses your configured AI provider, so it's billed the same way as your other AI features and appears in your AI usage.

sections.heading: Requirements
sections.text: You must be a partner admin with access to all organizations and the billing management permission. You must also complete MFA when you connect, replace, or disconnect a key.

sections.heading: Connect a key
sections.text:
1. Open **Partner Settings → AI Providers & Models** and click **Add connection** in the **Connections** card.

2. Choose **Anthropic API key**, give the connection a name, and paste the key into the write-only field.

3. Click **Save** and complete MFA. Breeze verifies the key with Anthropic before storing it.

Your first Anthropic connection takes over every AI feature that was using the Breeze platform key (patch testing stays on the platform key). Pick a different model for any feature under **Defaults by feature**. You can add more than one Anthropic connection, for example a second key for another region; only the first takes over features from the platform key, and models discovered on a later connection arrive disabled until you assign them.

The page shows that your key is active and displays only its last four characters. Breeze never returns the full key after you save it.

To rotate a key, open the connection's drawer, paste the replacement and save; Breeze verifies it before replacing the stored key, so a failed verification leaves the working key in place. **Disconnect** (with MFA) moves the features that used this connection back to the same models on the Breeze platform key and revokes the stored key. Breeze never switches back on its own.

sections.heading: Usage, budgets, and failures
sections.text:
Organization AI budgets and rate limits still apply. With BYOK enabled, those controls limit usage billed to your own Anthropic account rather than consumption of Breeze AI credits.

While the partner key is active, the AI usage page shows the note **"Billed to your key — AI usage goes to your own Anthropic account, not Breeze AI credits."**

  If the key is invalid, revoked, or rejected by Anthropic, AI is unavailable and Breeze shows an error banner. Breeze never silently falls back to the platform key, because doing so could consume Breeze AI credits without your intent. Replace the key or disconnect it explicitly to restore service.

sections.heading: Route your key through a platform-vetted endpoint
sections.text:
Once a key is connected, partners on deployments with the endpoint catalog enabled can send their AI traffic through a third-party endpoint instead of Anthropic directly — for example an OpenRouter or LiteLLM deployment that Breeze has verified against the Anthropic `/v1/messages` API. Your Anthropic key is still what gets billed; the endpoint only changes where the traffic is routed.

Breeze maintains this list itself. **You choose from the list — you never enter a URL.** Every entry is a platform-vetted endpoint that Breeze has run through its own fidelity and safety checks before it can appear as an option; there is no free-form "custom endpoint" field anywhere in the partner UI.

1. Open the connection's drawer in the **Connections** card and choose an **Endpoint**: Anthropic (direct) or one of the vetted endpoints. Breeze checks that the endpoint serves the model your **chat** feature uses before switching. Switching keeps the same connection and its feature assignments.

2. Selecting Anthropic (direct) applies immediately — it always requires zero confirmation, since it is the safe fallback.

3. Selecting a third-party endpoint opens a confirmation dialog. If the endpoint has a data-handling note, the dialog quotes it verbatim and requires you to check **"I understand my AI traffic and content will be processed by \<endpoint name\>"** before you can confirm. The note describes what that specific endpoint does with your traffic and content — read it before agreeing, since it varies per endpoint and Breeze cannot vouch for a third party's own data handling beyond the technical checks it ran.

4. Confirm. As with connecting or disconnecting a key, changing your endpoint requires MFA.

While a third-party endpoint is selected, the AI usage page's "billed to your key" note also names the endpoint, so it's clear both that billing goes to your Anthropic account and which endpoint carried the traffic.

  **If Breeze delists an endpoint you're using, AI is paused — not silently rerouted.** Breeze shows a banner explaining the endpoint was delisted, and no further AI requests succeed until you either pick another listed endpoint or switch back to **Anthropic (direct)**. The same fail-loud behavior applies if your selected endpoint stops verifying a model you rely on: Breeze pauses AI for that model rather than silently falling back to the platform key or a different provider.

This platform-vetted endpoint list is a hosted-only feature. If you're self-hosting, you point the instance at any Anthropic-compatible or OpenAI-compatible endpoint yourself with environment variables — see [Self-hosted: configure an instance-wide provider](#self-hosted-configure-an-instance-wide-provider) below for the variable matrix. Hosted partners can also [connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint](#connect-an-openai-compatible-endpoint) of their own. There is no vetting step on self-hosted deployments: you're trusting whatever endpoint you configure.

sections.heading: Connect an OpenAI-compatible endpoint
sections.text:
Connect any server that speaks the OpenAI `chat/completions` API with function calling, such as vLLM, Ollama, LiteLLM, or OpenRouter. Once a model passes verification, every AI feature works on it, including tools: chat, the helper, the script builder, AI agents, and Office chat.

1. Open **Partner Settings → AI Providers & Models → Connections** and click **Add connection → OpenAI-compatible endpoint**.

2. Enter a **name**, the **base URL** (it ends at the API root, for example `https://llm.example.com/v1`), and optionally an **API key** (at least 8 characters). The key is write-only.

3. Get models onto the connection. Breeze discovers them from `GET {base_url}/models`, or you can click **Add model** and enter a model ID by hand. Discovered and manual models arrive **disabled, unpriced, and unverified**.

4. Open the model and set a **price** in US dollars per million tokens. `0` is fine for a local model. A model without a price cannot be enabled.

5. Click **Verify**. Breeze runs a fidelity test through the endpoint, including a tool call. This spends a few thousand tokens on your own endpoint; Breeze does not bill for it.

6. Enable the model, then assign it as the default for the features you want under **Defaults by feature**.

Until a model is verified it has no tool calling and cannot be used for chat, the helper, the script builder, AI agents, or Office chat. If you change a connection's base URL, its models are marked **Re-verify: endpoint changed** and must be verified again. Rotating the API key does not require re-verification.

  These models do not support thinking or effort controls, documents and PDFs in chat, or server tools such as web search. A partner with **Require data residency** switched on cannot use them, because Breeze cannot attest where your endpoint processes data.

#### Network and key security

- **Hosted Breeze connects only to public `https` endpoints.**
- **Self-hosted deployments** may use private (RFC 1918 / ULA) addresses only when `IS_HOSTED` is explicitly set to `false`. Cleartext `http` is allowed only to a private address.
- **Loopback, link-local, and cloud-metadata addresses are never reachable**, in either mode. Redirects are not followed.
- **Your key stays on the Breeze API server** and is never given to the agent process. Requests go through Breeze's loopback model gateway, which attaches the key on the way out.

#### Troubleshooting

| Message | Cause and fix |
|---|---|
| **Verification failed: no tool_use block** | The server or model does not support function calling. For vLLM, start the server with `--enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser <parser>`. For Ollama, use a model that supports tools, such as `qwen2.5`. |
| **egress_blocked** | The address is not allowed for this deployment: a private address on hosted Breeze, a private address on a self-hosted install without `IS_HOSTED=false`, `http` to a public address, or a loopback/link-local address. Use a public `https` URL, or fix the deployment setting. |
| **Re-verify: endpoint changed** | The connection's base URL changed after the model was verified. Click **Verify** again. |

sections.heading: Default model and the offered model list
sections.text:
The platform default model is **Claude Sonnet 5.5** (`claude-sonnet-5-5`) with adaptive thinking at medium effort (v0.120.0+; earlier releases defaulted to Sonnet 4.6). A self-hosted `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` still overrides the default. Existing chats keep the model they were started with; only new chats pick up the new default.

A new chat can only use a model the platform offers, the configured default, or (on a vetted endpoint) a model that endpoint maps. Requesting anything else when creating a chat returns `400` with code `invalid_model`, and no chat is created.

sections.heading: Platform AI models (platform administrators)
sections.text:
Platform administrators manage the models Breeze knows about at **Administration → AI Models** (`/admin/ai-models`, v0.120.0+). Each row shows the model's discovery status (**Available**, **Missing**, or **Retired**), its thinking support, its input and output price per million tokens, whether it is offered, and whether it is the platform default. Open a row to edit:

- **Prices** in US dollars per million tokens (input, output, cache read, cache write). Breeze asks you to confirm any change of more than 10× from the stored value, to catch unit mistakes.
- **Fast mode prices**, optional. Fast mode can't be selected for a model until all four fast prices are set.
- **Option support**: effort levels, thinking display, fast mode, and inference geographies.
- **Minimum plan** that may use the model, and the **prompt profile** Breeze uses with it.
- **Offered on the platform key**. A model can only be offered once all four standard prices are set.
- **Platform default**. In v0.120.0 this choice is recorded but does not yet change routing; the deployment default still comes from `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` or the built-in default.

Every change requires MFA. The **AI Providers & Models** settings and the **LLM Provider Catalog** page read their model lists from this catalog.

**Discovery.** Once a day (06:38 UTC) Breeze lists the models available to the platform Anthropic key. A model it has not seen before appears with a **New** badge and the platform operators are alerted. Discovery only flags models for review: it never offers, prices, or removes a model on its own, and a new model stays unpriced and offered to no one until you set it up. A model that stops appearing is marked **Missing** after several successful checks and two days, and **Retired** after 14 days; a model discovery has never seen is never moved. **Refresh models** queues a discovery run immediately. Discovery is skipped when no platform key is configured or when `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at a gateway rather than Anthropic.

sections.heading: AI Providers & Models
sections.text: **Partner Settings → AI Providers & Models** is the single home for where AI requests are sent, which models are available, and which model each feature uses. It requires the billing management permission. The sections below describe each card. Per-model spend by feature, technician, and organization is under **Settings → AI Usage**.

sections.heading: Connections and residency
sections.text: The **Connections** card lists the Breeze platform connection plus any connection you add, with its status, key state, inference region, and who is billed. Adding or editing a connection opens a drawer where you can set a name and inference region, replace the write-only API key, pick a catalog endpoint, or disconnect; **Refresh models** queues a fresh model discovery for that connection. The **Require data residency** switch restricts every feature to models that can keep data in the required region. Before it applies, Breeze shows which features and organization overrides would stop working so you can confirm or cancel.

sections.heading: Models
sections.text: The **Models** card groups the models each connection offers, with context size and per-1M-token prices. The switch on a row enables or disables the model and saves immediately; a model with no price cannot be enabled, and disabling a model that is still a feature default asks you to confirm and lists the affected features. A row's details drawer sets a display name, price, premium flag, default and allowed effort or speed options, and an optional refusal fallback, which must be another enabled model on the same connection.

sections.heading: Defaults by feature (and org overrides)
sections.text: The **Defaults by feature** card sets the default model, effort, and speed for each AI feature (chat, helper, script builder, script reviewer, and so on), which models are permitted, and whether users may choose their own. Changing the script reviewer's model requires the approvals decide permission. Each organization can narrow these under **Settings → Organizations → (organization) → Model defaults**: leave a field on **Inherit** to follow the partner default, or override it. An organization can only narrow what its partner allows, and the partner can lock user choice. The script-authoring and client-AI policy pages link here instead of holding their own model fields.

sections.heading: Self-hosted: configure an instance-wide provider
sections.text:
Self-hosted operators can configure an LLM backend for platform-keyed usage with environment variables. These settings configure the platform connection: the default model for new partners and the backend platform-key traffic goes to. A partner's own connection is never overridden by them.

If you're a hosted partner instead, see [Route your key through a platform-vetted endpoint](#route-your-key-through-a-platform-vetted-endpoint) above — hosted deployments select from Breeze's vetted catalog rather than setting these variables.

sections.heading: Anthropic-compatible endpoint with tool calling
sections.text:
Use this path to route the full, tool-capable Breeze Agent through an endpoint that implements the Anthropic `/v1/messages` API, such as vLLM 0.23+ or LiteLLM.

| Variable | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | Yes | Base URL for the Anthropic-compatible endpoint. It must be a valid HTTP or HTTPS URL. |
| `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` | As required by the endpoint | Authentication token sent by the Anthropic SDK. |
| `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` | Optional | Overrides the default model ID, including for a raw vLLM model name or a LiteLLM alias. |

`ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` is self-hosted only. Breeze refuses to start with this variable set unless `IS_HOSTED` is explicitly set to `false` (or another recognized false value). Hosted deployments cannot use a custom per-partner or instance-wide base URL.

sections.heading: Instance-wide OpenAI-compatible endpoint
sections.text:
Use this path to give every partner on a self-hosted instance a shared OpenAI-compatible backend. At boot, Breeze creates an **env-managed connection** for each partner from these variables. It appears in **AI Providers & Models → Connections** as read-only, labelled *managed by environment*, with one priced, enabled model that Breeze verifies automatically.

| Variable | Required | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `MCP_LLM_PROVIDER` | Yes | Set to `openai-compatible`. Breeze refuses to start with this value unless `IS_HOSTED` is explicitly set to `false` (an unset `IS_HOSTED` is refused too). |
| `MCP_LLM_BASE_URL` | Yes | Base URL for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint. It must be a valid URL. |
| `MCP_LLM_MODEL` | Yes | Model ID exposed by the endpoint. |
| `MCP_LLM_API_KEY` | Optional | API key used to authenticate with the endpoint. Leave unset for a keyless local server; when set it must be at least 8 characters. |
| `MCP_LLM_PRICE_INPUT_PER_M_USD` | Optional | Input-token price in USD per million tokens. Defaults to `0`. |
| `MCP_LLM_PRICE_OUTPUT_PER_M_USD` | Optional | Output-token price in USD per million tokens. Defaults to `0`. |

Both price values must be zero or greater.

- **Chat moves to this model only where chat used the platform default.** A partner that picked its own model or connection keeps it.
- **The old chat-only runtime is removed.** The model now runs through the same verified path as a partner-added connection, so tools work.
- **Partners cannot change the endpoint, key, prices or models** of an env-managed connection; they can enable or disable its model.
- **If you remove the variables**, each env-managed connection stays in place, still read-only, and keeps working until a partner admin disconnects it. Setting the variables again picks the same connection back up; chat is not moved a second time.
- **A model that fails tool verification cannot serve chat.** See [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting) above; the most common cause is a server started without function calling enabled.
- The same network rules apply as for a partner-added connection: loopback is never reachable, and private (RFC 1918 / ULA) addresses and cleartext `http` to a private address require `IS_HOSTED=false`. Point `MCP_LLM_BASE_URL` at the model host's container service name or LAN address, not `localhost`.

  A partner's own connection always wins: features assigned to it never use the instance settings. The instance settings apply to features on the platform connection.

title: Browser Security
description: Browser extension inventory, risk assessment, policy-based compliance, and violation tracking across your managed fleet.

sections.text:
Browser Security gives you visibility into every browser extension installed across your managed devices. An inventory source reports each extension's name, version, source, permissions, and risk level to the API via `PUT /browser-security/inventory/:deviceId`. You can create policies that define which extensions are allowed, blocked, or required, and Breeze evaluates the reported inventory server-side and tracks violations when devices fall out of compliance. The risk summary dashboard aggregates extension data across the fleet so you can quickly identify high-risk or unauthorized extensions.

**Status:**
  The built-in agent collector for browser extensions has not shipped yet. Today, inventory must be submitted by an external source (a script, MDM export, or a custom integration) calling the inventory endpoint directly.

---

sections.heading: Extension Risk Levels
sections.text:
Each browser extension is assigned a risk level based on its permissions, source, and known threat intelligence:

| Risk Level | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `low` | Extension requests minimal permissions and comes from a trusted source |
| `medium` | Extension requests moderate permissions (e.g., read browsing history) |
| `high` | Extension requests sensitive permissions (e.g., read/modify all site data, access cookies) |
| `critical` | Extension is flagged as malicious, known malware, or requests excessive permissions |

sections.heading: Extension Sources
sections.text:
| Source | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `webstore` | Installed from the official browser web store (Chrome Web Store, Firefox Add-ons, etc.) |
| `sideloaded` | Installed manually outside the official store (developer mode, enterprise deployment) |
| `policy` | Installed or enforced by a browser management policy (Group Policy, MDM) |
| `unknown` | Source could not be determined |

sections.heading: Policy Target Types
sections.text:
Policies can be scoped to different levels of your organizational hierarchy:

| Target Type | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| `org` | Policy applies to all devices in the organization |
| `site` | Policy applies to devices at specific sites |
| `group` | Policy applies to specific device groups |
| `device` | Policy applies to individual devices |
| `tag` | Policy applies to devices with specific tags |

A site-restricted technician only sees extension inventory and violations for devices in their assigned sites, and may only create, update, or delete `site`-targeted policies that fall entirely within their site allowlist.

---

sections.heading: How It Works
sections.text:
1. **An inventory source reports extension data** for each device via `PUT /browser-security/inventory/:deviceId`, including extension IDs, names, versions, permissions, enabled state, and risk level. Extensions are upserted -- new extensions are added, and existing ones are updated with the latest version and state.

2. **Create browser policies** to define allowed, blocked, and required extension lists. Policies are scoped to your organization, sites, groups, devices, or tags.

3. **Breeze evaluates compliance** automatically when inventory data arrives or policies change. Policy violations are detected and tracked in the `browser_policy_violations` table.

4. **Review violations and risk** through the API. Unresolved violations surface devices that are out of compliance. The extension summary dashboard shows risk distribution across your fleet.

---

sections.heading: How Extensions Are Reported
sections.text:
An inventory source submits browser extension data for a device to the API. Each extension submission includes:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `browser` | string | Browser name (e.g., `chrome`, `edge`, `firefox`) |
| `extensionId` | string | Unique extension identifier from the browser |
| `name` | string | Human-readable extension name |
| `version` | string | Extension version string |
| `source` | string | Installation source: `webstore`, `sideloaded`, `policy`, `unknown` |
| `permissions` | string[] | Requested permissions (e.g., `tabs`, `cookies`, `webRequest`) |
| `riskLevel` | string | Risk supplied by the inventory source: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` (defaults to `low` if omitted) |
| `enabled` | boolean | Whether the extension is currently enabled |

Extensions are uniquely identified by the combination of organization, device, browser, and extension ID. When the inventory source reports an extension that already exists, the existing record is updated with the latest version, permissions, risk level, and enabled state. The `firstSeenAt` timestamp is preserved while `lastSeenAt` is updated.

sections.heading: Querying Extensions
sections.text:
```bash
GET /browser-security/extensions?riskLevel=critical&browser=chrome&limit=100
```

sections.heading: Extension Query Parameters
sections.text:
| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `deviceId` | UUID | Filter extensions for a specific device |
| `browser` | string | Filter by browser (e.g., `chrome`, `edge`, `firefox`) |
| `riskLevel` | string | Filter by risk level: `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` |
| `limit` | integer | Results per page (1-500, default 100) |

The response includes both a risk summary and the list of matching extensions:

```json
{
  "summary": {
    "total": 342,
    "low": 280,
    "medium": 45,
    "high": 12,
    "critical": 5
  },
  "extensions": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "orgId": "uuid",
      "deviceId": "uuid",
      "deviceName": "DESKTOP-ABC123",
      "browser": "chrome",
      "extensionId": "abc123def456",
      "name": "Suspicious Extension",
      "version": "1.2.3",
      "source": "sideloaded",
      "riskLevel": "critical",
      "enabled": true,
      "lastSeenAt": "2026-02-15T10:30:00Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

  The risk summary counts are computed across all matching extensions, giving you an at-a-glance view of the risk distribution. Use the `riskLevel` filter to drill down into specific categories.

---

sections.heading: Browser Policies
sections.text: Browser policies define which extensions are allowed, blocked, or required across your fleet. When a device's extension inventory violates a policy, a violation record is created for tracking and remediation.

sections.heading: Creating a Policy
sections.text:
```bash
POST /browser-security/policies
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "name": "Standard Browser Policy",
  "targetType": "org",
  "allowedExtensions": ["ublock-origin", "lastpass"],
  "blockedExtensions": ["hola-vpn", "web-of-trust"],
  "requiredExtensions": ["ublock-origin"],
  "settings": {
    "blockSideloaded": true,
    "maxRiskLevel": "medium"
  },
  "isActive": true
}
```

sections.heading: Policy Fields
sections.text:
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Yes | Policy name (max 200 chars) |
| `targetType` | string | Yes | `org`, `site`, `group`, `device`, or `tag` |
| `targetIds` | string[] | No | IDs matching the target type (omit for org-wide policies) |
| `allowedExtensions` | string[] | No | Extension IDs that are explicitly permitted |
| `blockedExtensions` | string[] | No | Extension IDs that are explicitly prohibited |
| `requiredExtensions` | string[] | No | Extension IDs that must be installed |
| `settings` | object | No | Additional policy settings (e.g., `blockSideloaded`, `maxRiskLevel`) |
| `isActive` | boolean | No | Whether the policy is active (default `true`) |

  When a policy is created or updated, Breeze automatically triggers a policy evaluation job through BullMQ. The evaluation checks all devices in the policy's scope against the updated rules and creates or resolves violation records as needed.

sections.heading: Updating a Policy
sections.text:
```bash
PUT /browser-security/policies/:policyId
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "blockedExtensions": ["hola-vpn", "web-of-trust", "suspicious-toolbar"],
  "isActive": true
}
```

All fields are optional in updates -- only the provided fields are changed. The policy evaluation is re-triggered after every update.

sections.heading: Deleting a Policy
sections.text:
```bash
DELETE /browser-security/policies/:policyId
```

Deleting a policy removes the policy record. Associated violation records reference the policy by ID and retain a `policyId` foreign key, but they remain in the database for historical tracking.

---

sections.heading: Policy Violations
sections.text: Violations are created when a device's installed extensions conflict with an active policy. Each violation record tracks the device, the policy that was violated, the type of violation, and when it was detected.

sections.heading: Querying Violations
sections.text:
```bash
GET /browser-security/violations?deviceId=uuid&policyId=uuid
```

The violations endpoint returns only unresolved violations (where `resolvedAt` is null), sorted by detection time with the most recent first.

sections.heading: Violation Response Fields
sections.text:
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `id` | UUID | Unique violation identifier |
| `orgId` | UUID | Organization ID |
| `deviceId` | UUID | Device that is out of compliance |
| `deviceName` | string | Hostname of the device |
| `policyId` | UUID | Policy that was violated |
| `violationType` | string | Type of violation (e.g., `blocked_extension_installed`, `required_extension_missing`, `sideloaded_extension`) |
| `details` | object | Additional details about the violation (extension name, ID, etc.) |
| `detectedAt` | ISO 8601 | When the violation was first detected |

  Violations are automatically resolved when the underlying condition is corrected -- for example, when a blocked extension is uninstalled or a required extension is installed. The `resolvedAt` timestamp is set and the violation no longer appears in the unresolved violations query.

---

sections.heading: Extensions
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/browser-security/extensions` | List extensions with risk summary (requires `devices:read`) |
| PUT | `/browser-security/inventory/:deviceId` | Inventory source reports extension data (requires `devices:write`) |

sections.heading: Policies
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/browser-security/policies` | List all browser policies for the organization (requires `devices:read`) |
| POST | `/browser-security/policies` | Create a new browser policy (requires `devices:write`) |
| PUT | `/browser-security/policies/:policyId` | Update an existing policy (requires `devices:write`) |
| DELETE | `/browser-security/policies/:policyId` | Delete a policy (requires `devices:write`) |

sections.heading: Violations
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/browser-security/violations` | List unresolved policy violations (requires `devices:read`) |

  All browser security endpoints require authentication and one of these scopes: `organization`, `partner`, or `system`. Organization-scoped tokens are automatically restricted to their own organization's data.

---

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
**Extensions not appearing for a device.**
An inventory source must submit extension data via `PUT /browser-security/inventory/:deviceId` before extensions appear in the API. Verify the inventory source is running and reporting successfully, and check its logs for submission errors.

**Risk level shows `low` for a known malicious extension.**
Risk levels are supplied by the inventory source at submission time, not computed by Breeze. If the source does not send a `riskLevel`, it defaults to `low`. You can still enforce compliance through browser policies by adding the extension to the `blockedExtensions` list.

**Violation not created for a blocked extension.**
Policy evaluation runs asynchronously through BullMQ when a policy is created or updated. If the BullMQ worker is not running, violations will not be generated. Verify that Redis is connected and the browser security worker is processing jobs. Also check that the policy's `isActive` field is `true` and the `targetType` and `targetIds` correctly scope the device.

**Extensions showing stale data.**
Extensions are updated on upsert when the inventory source reports. The `lastSeenAt` timestamp indicates when the extension was last reported. If this timestamp is old, the inventory source may not be running or may be having connectivity issues. Extensions that are uninstalled are not automatically removed -- they retain their last known state until a new inventory submission excludes them.

**Policy evaluation not triggering after update.**
Policy evaluation is triggered through BullMQ when a policy is created or updated. If the evaluation job fails to enqueue (e.g., Redis is unavailable), the policy is still saved but compliance will not be evaluated until the next trigger. Check the BullMQ dashboard for failed jobs in the browser security queue.

title: Change Tracking
description: Detect and audit software installs, service changes, network modifications, and configuration drift across your fleet.

sections.text:
Change Tracking gives you a continuous audit trail of what changed on every managed device. The Breeze agent monitors eight categories of system changes -- software installs and removals, Windows service modifications, startup item additions, network adapter changes, scheduled task updates, user account mutations, hardware changes, and OS version changes -- and ships them to the API in compressed batches. Every change is fingerprinted with a SHA-256 hash to prevent duplicates, then stored with before/after snapshots so you can see exactly what was modified.

This feature is designed for compliance auditing, troubleshooting, and drift detection. When a user reports that something stopped working, you can pull up the device's change timeline and see that a critical service was disabled 20 minutes earlier. When you need to prove to an auditor that no unauthorized software was installed, the change log provides cryptographically deduplicated evidence.

---

sections.heading: Viewing Changes in the Console
sections.text:
Open a device's detail page and select the **Change History** tab to browse its change timeline without querying the API directly.

Each row shows:

- **When** the change was detected.
- **Type** -- a colored badge for one of the eight change categories (Software, Service, Startup, Network, Scheduled Task, User Account, Hardware, OS Version).
- **Action** -- Added, Removed, Modified, or Updated.
- **Subject** -- what changed (e.g. "Google Chrome 122.0.6261.69").
- **Before -> After** -- the previous and new values side by side; an addition shows only the new value, a removal shows the old value struck through.

Use the **Type** and **Action** dropdowns above the table to narrow the list, and **Load more** to page through older changes beyond the initial 100.

---

sections.heading: Change Types
sections.text:
| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `software` | Application installed, removed, or updated |
| `service` | Windows service or system daemon added, removed, or modified |
| `startup` | Startup program or launch agent added, removed, or changed |
| `network` | Network adapter configuration changed (IP, DNS, gateway) |
| `scheduled_task` | Scheduled task or cron job added, removed, or modified |
| `user_account` | Local user account created, deleted, or modified |
| `hardware` | Memory, processor, storage, or BIOS/firmware version changed |
| `os_version` | Operating system version updated |

sections.heading: Change Actions
sections.text:
| Action | Description |
|---|---|
| `added` | A new item was detected (software installed, user created, etc.) |
| `removed` | An existing item was deleted (software uninstalled, user removed, etc.) |
| `modified` | An existing item's properties changed (service startup type, scheduled task trigger, etc.) |
| `updated` | A version update was applied (software upgraded, definition file refreshed, etc.) |

sections.heading: Change Record Fields
sections.text:
| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Unique identifier for the change record |
| `deviceId` | UUID | Device where the change was detected |
| `orgId` | UUID | Organization the device belongs to |
| `fingerprint` | string (64 chars) | SHA-256 hash for deduplication |
| `timestamp` | datetime | When the change occurred on the device |
| `changeType` | enum | One of the six change types above |
| `changeAction` | enum | One of the four change actions above |
| `subject` | string (max 500) | Human-readable description of what changed (e.g., "Google Chrome 122.0.6261.69") |
| `beforeValue` | JSON | State before the change (null for `added` actions) |
| `afterValue` | JSON | State after the change (null for `removed` actions) |
| `details` | JSON | Additional context (installer path, registry key, etc.) |
| `createdAt` | datetime | When the record was stored in the database |

---

sections.heading: How Changes Are Collected
sections.text:
1. **Agent detects a change.** The agent periodically snapshots system state (installed software, services, startup items, etc.) and compares against the previous snapshot. Differences are formatted as change records.

2. **Agent ships changes in a batch.** Changes are serialized as JSON, gzip-compressed, and sent to the API via `PUT /api/v1/agents/:id/changes`. Up to 50,000 changes per request by default (configurable via `CHANGE_INGEST_MAX_ITEMS`, up to a hard ceiling of 200,000), with a 5 MB compressed body limit and 10 MB decompressed limit.

3. **API deduplicates and stores.** Each change is fingerprinted by hashing the combination of timestamp, change type, action, subject, before/after values, and details. A unique constraint on `(deviceId, fingerprint)` prevents the same change from being inserted twice. Changes are inserted in batches of 200.

4. **Partial success handling.** If some changes in a batch fail to insert (e.g., database error on a subset), the API returns HTTP 207 with a `partial: true` flag, the count of successfully inserted records, and the total submitted.

  The gzip compression typically reduces payload size by 80-90%, making it practical for agents to ship hundreds of changes per batch even over constrained connections.

---

sections.heading: Querying Changes
sections.text: The changes API supports filtering by device, time range, change type, and action, with cursor-based pagination for efficient iteration through large result sets.

sections.heading: Basic Query
sections.text:
```bash
curl "/api/v1/changes?deviceId=DEVICE_UUID&changeType=software&limit=50" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

sections.heading: Available Filters
sections.text:
| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `deviceId` | UUID | Filter to a single device |
| `startTime` | ISO 8601 datetime | Only changes at or after this time |
| `endTime` | ISO 8601 datetime | Only changes at or before this time |
| `changeType` | enum | One of: `software`, `service`, `startup`, `network`, `scheduled_task`, `user_account`, `hardware`, `os_version` |
| `changeAction` | enum | One of: `added`, `removed`, `modified`, `updated` |
| `limit` | integer | Results per page (1 -- 500, default 100) |
| `cursor` | string | Opaque cursor for the next page |

sections.heading: Response Format
sections.text:
```json
{
  "changes": [
    {
      "id": "uuid",
      "deviceId": "uuid",
      "hostname": "DESKTOP-ABC123",
      "timestamp": "2026-02-15T14:30:00.000Z",
      "changeType": "software",
      "changeAction": "added",
      "subject": "Visual Studio Code 1.96.2",
      "beforeValue": null,
      "afterValue": {
        "version": "1.96.2",
        "vendor": "Microsoft Corporation",
        "installLocation": "C:\\Program Files\\Microsoft VS Code"
      },
      "details": null
    }
  ],
  "total": 1847,
  "showing": 50,
  "hasMore": true,
  "nextCursor": "eyJ0aW1lc3RhbXAiOiIyMDI2..."
}
```

sections.heading: Cursor-Based Pagination
sections.text:
The API uses cursor-based pagination for stable results when new changes arrive during iteration. The `nextCursor` field is a base64url-encoded JSON object containing the timestamp and ID of the last returned record. Pass it as the `cursor` query parameter to get the next page.

```bash
# First page
curl "/api/v1/changes?deviceId=DEVICE_UUID&limit=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"

# Next page (using nextCursor from the previous response)
curl "/api/v1/changes?deviceId=DEVICE_UUID&limit=100&cursor=eyJ0aW1lc3RhbXAi..." \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

---

sections.heading: Agent Ingest Endpoint
Ingest Response Codes
sections.text:
| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `200` | All changes accepted (or empty batch) |
| `207` | Partial success -- some changes inserted, some failed |
| `400` | Invalid request body or decompression failure |
| `404` | Agent/device not found |
| `413` | Request body exceeds 5 MB compressed or 10 MB decompressed |
| `500` | All changes failed to insert |

---

sections.heading: Fingerprint Deduplication
sections.text:
Every change is assigned a SHA-256 fingerprint computed from a stable concatenation of:

1. Canonical ISO 8601 timestamp
2. Change type
3. Change action
4. Subject
5. Stable-sorted JSON of `beforeValue`
6. Stable-sorted JSON of `afterValue`
7. Stable-sorted JSON of `details`

This fingerprint is stored in a `VARCHAR(64)` column with a unique index on `(deviceId, fingerprint)`. When the agent ships the same change twice (e.g., after a retry), the database `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` clause silently skips the duplicate.

Within a single request, the API also deduplicates by fingerprint before attempting insertion, so batch payloads with repeated entries are handled efficiently.

---

sections.heading: query_change_log (Tier 1)
sections.text:
A read-only tool the AI assistant uses to search device configuration changes -- software installs/updates, service changes, startup drift, network changes, scheduled task changes, user account changes, hardware changes, and OS version updates.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `deviceId` | string (UUID) | Scope results to a single device. Optional. |
| `startTime` | ISO 8601 datetime | Lower time bound (inclusive). Optional. |
| `endTime` | ISO 8601 datetime | Upper time bound (inclusive). Optional. |
| `changeType` | enum | One of the eight change types above. Optional. |
| `changeAction` | enum | `added`, `removed`, `modified`, or `updated`. Optional. |
| `limit` | number | Max results to return (default 100, max 500). |

The AI uses this tool to answer questions like "What changed on this device in the last 24 hours?" or "Was any software installed on the finance team's laptops this week?" without you having to open the Change History tab yourself.

---

sections.heading: API Reference
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/api/v1/changes` | List changes with filters and cursor pagination |
| `PUT` | `/api/v1/agents/:id/changes` | Agent ingest endpoint for shipping change batches |

---

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
**Changes not appearing for a device**
Verify the agent is enrolled and the device exists in the platform. The ingest endpoint looks up the device by `agentId`, not by device UUID. If the agent is not enrolled, the endpoint returns 404.

**Duplicate changes appearing**
This should not happen due to fingerprint deduplication. If you see exact duplicates, check whether the agent is sending changes with different timestamps for the same event (e.g., using local time vs. UTC). The fingerprint includes the timestamp, so a one-second difference produces a different hash.

**Large change volumes after a software deployment**
This is expected. Mass deployments (e.g., pushing a new application to 500 devices) will generate 500 `software:added` change records. Use the `changeType` and `changeAction` filters to focus on specific categories, and cursor pagination to iterate efficiently.

**207 partial success responses**
A 207 means some changes in the batch were inserted and some failed. This can happen if the database has transient issues. The agent should not retry the entire batch because the successfully inserted changes would be deduplicated anyway. Check server logs for the underlying database error.

**Request body too large (413)**
The ingest endpoint limits compressed payloads to 5 MB and decompressed payloads to 10 MB. If agents are hitting this limit, reduce the batch size or increase the shipping frequency. These limits can be tuned with the `CHANGE_INGEST_MAX_BODY_BYTES` and `CHANGE_INGEST_MAX_DECOMPRESSED_BYTES` environment variables.

title: CIS Hardening
description: CIS benchmark compliance scanning with baselines, per-check findings, scores, and approval-gated remediation for Windows, macOS, and Linux.
headings: Who a scheduled scan runs as

sections.text:
CIS Hardening evaluates your managed devices against Center for Internet Security (CIS) benchmarks and produces compliance scores, per-check findings, and remediation recommendations. You define baselines that specify a CIS benchmark version, security level, and optional exclusions. Breeze then scans devices against those baselines, producing a compliance score and a detailed list of passed and failed checks. When checks fail, you can request remediation actions that go through an approval workflow before being dispatched to the agent for execution.

The system supports Windows, macOS, and Linux benchmarks at both Level 1 (essential security) and Level 2 (defense in depth) profiles, plus custom baselines with specific check exclusions. Scans can be triggered on demand or scheduled to run automatically at configurable intervals.

---

sections.heading: Using the Console
sections.text:
Open **CIS Benchmarks** from the Security section of the left sidebar. Summary cards at the top show fleet compliance, active baselines, and pending remediations, above three tabs:

| Tab | What it shows |
|-----|---------------|
| **Compliance** | Every scanned device with its latest compliance score, searchable and filterable by OS |
| **Baselines** | Configured baselines (benchmark, level, OS, schedule), with create/edit and an on-demand **Scan** action per baseline |
| **Remediations** | A read-only, status-filterable log of remediation requests and their approval/execution state |

1. From the **Baselines** tab, click **New Baseline**.
2. Choose the OS type, CIS level (L1, L2, or Custom), and any check exclusions.
3. Optionally set a scan schedule (interval or cron).
4. Save, then click the **play** icon on the baseline row to trigger an immediate scan, or wait for the schedule.

A partner-scope user can own a baseline **partner-wide** so it applies across every organization the partner manages.

Requesting a remediation and approving or rejecting it are API-only today (see [Remediation](#remediation) below) -- the **Remediations** tab surfaces the resulting queue but has no request or decision buttons.

---

sections.heading: Operating System Types
sections.text:
| OS Type | Description |
|---------|-------------|
| `windows` | Windows Server and Windows Desktop benchmarks |
| `macos` | macOS benchmarks |
| `linux` | Linux distribution benchmarks (Ubuntu, RHEL, CentOS, etc.) |

sections.heading: Baseline Levels
sections.text:
| Level | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `l1` | **Level 1** -- essential security settings that can be applied broadly with minimal impact on functionality. Recommended as a baseline for all systems |
| `l2` | **Level 2** -- defense-in-depth settings that may restrict some functionality. Recommended for high-security environments |
| `custom` | **Custom** -- based on L1 or L2 with specific checks excluded via `customExclusions` |

sections.heading: Check Statuses
sections.text:
Each individual CIS check produces one of these results:

| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `pass` | The device meets the benchmark requirement |
| `fail` | The device does not meet the benchmark requirement -- remediation recommended |
| `not_applicable` | The check does not apply to this device (e.g., a domain-specific check on a standalone workstation) |
| `error` | The check could not be evaluated (e.g., insufficient permissions, missing utility) |

sections.heading: Check Severities
sections.text:
| Severity | Description |
|----------|-------------|
| `low` | Informational or hardening recommendation with minimal security impact |
| `medium` | Moderate security setting -- should be addressed in a reasonable timeframe |
| `high` | Important security control -- failure represents a significant gap |
| `critical` | Essential security control -- failure represents an immediate risk |

sections.heading: Remediation Statuses
sections.text:
| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `pending_approval` | Remediation requested but awaiting administrator approval |
| `queued` | Approved and queued for dispatch to the agent |
| `in_progress` | Agent is executing the remediation |
| `completed` | Remediation completed successfully |
| `failed` | Remediation failed during execution |
| `cancelled` | Remediation was rejected or cancelled |

sections.heading: Approval Statuses
sections.text:
| Status | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `pending` | Awaiting approval decision |
| `approved` | Approved by an administrator -- remediation will proceed |
| `rejected` | Rejected by an administrator -- remediation will not proceed |

---

sections.heading: Baselines
sections.text: A baseline defines the CIS benchmark, security level, and optional exclusions for a set of devices. Each baseline targets a specific operating system and is owned either by a single organization or **partner-wide**.

sections.heading: Baseline ownership: organization vs. partner-wide
sections.text: When creating a baseline you choose its scope: **a single organization** or **all organizations** (a partner-wide baseline). A partner-wide baseline applies to devices in every organization under your partner and shows an **"All orgs"** badge in the baseline list. Ownership is chosen at creation and is immutable afterwards — to change scope, create a new baseline. Creating or editing partner-wide baselines requires full-partner access (technicians restricted to a subset of organizations can't manage them).

sections.heading: Who a scheduled scan runs as
sections.text:
Saving a baseline arms its recurring scan, and remediation queues hardening commands on endpoints, so both are device-execution actions: creating or editing a baseline, requesting a remediation and approving one need the `devices:execute` permission and MFA. A scheduled baseline runs under the user who last saved it, and that user must be able to run commands on every device it targets.

A schedule keeps running only while that user is active and still holds `devices:execute`. Baselines created before v0.122.1 keep running under the user who created them on the same terms. Otherwise the **Baselines** tab shows **Needs re-approval** on the schedule and scheduled scans pause until a user with `devices:execute` and MFA saves the baseline again. On-demand scans are not affected.

sections.heading: Creating a Baseline
sections.text:
```bash
POST /cis/baselines
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "orgId": "uuid",
  "name": "Windows Server L1 Baseline",
  "osType": "windows",
  "benchmarkVersion": "3.0.0",
  "level": "l1",
  "customExclusions": [],
  "scanSchedule": {
    "enabled": true,
    "intervalHours": 24,
    "nextScanAt": null
  },
  "isActive": true
}
```

sections.heading: Baseline Fields
sections.text:
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `ownerScope` | string | No | `organization` (default) or `partner` for a partner-wide baseline. Create-only — ownership cannot be changed later |
| `orgId` | UUID | For org-owned baselines | Organization ID (auto-resolved for org-scoped tokens). Omitted and ignored when `ownerScope` is `partner` |
| `name` | string | Yes | Baseline name (max 200 chars) |
| `osType` | string | Yes | Target OS: `windows`, `macos`, `linux` |
| `benchmarkVersion` | string | Yes | CIS benchmark version (e.g., `3.0.0`, `2.1.0`) |
| `level` | string | Yes | Security level: `l1`, `l2`, `custom` |
| `customExclusions` | string[] | No | Check IDs to exclude from evaluation (max 200) |
| `scanSchedule` | object | No | Scan schedule configuration |
| `isActive` | boolean | No | Whether the baseline is active (default `true`) |

sections.heading: Scan Schedule Configuration
sections.text:
| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `enabled` | boolean | Whether scheduled scanning is enabled |
| `intervalHours` | integer | Scan interval in hours (1 to 168 / one week) |
| `nextScanAt` | ISO 8601 | Next scheduled scan time (null to let the system calculate) |

sections.heading: Updating a Baseline
sections.text:
To update an existing baseline, include the baseline `id` in the request body:

```bash
POST /cis/baselines
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "id": "existing-baseline-uuid",
  "orgId": "uuid",
  "name": "Windows Server L1 Baseline (Updated)",
  "osType": "windows",
  "benchmarkVersion": "3.0.0",
  "level": "l1",
  "customExclusions": ["1.1.1", "1.1.2"],
  "isActive": true
}
```

sections.heading: Listing Baselines
sections.text:
```bash
GET /cis/baselines?osType=windows&active=true&limit=50
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `orgId` | UUID | Filter by organization |
| `osType` | string | Filter by OS type: `windows`, `macos`, `linux` |
| `active` | boolean | Filter by active status |
| `limit` | integer | Results per page (1-200, default 100) |
| `offset` | integer | Pagination offset |

---

sections.heading: Triggering a Scan
sections.text:
```bash
POST /cis/scan
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "orgId": "uuid",
  "baselineId": "baseline-uuid",
  "deviceIds": ["device-uuid-1", "device-uuid-2"]
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `orgId` | UUID | No | Organization ID (resolved from baseline if not provided) |
| `baselineId` | UUID | Yes | Baseline to evaluate against |
| `deviceIds` | UUID[] | No | Specific devices to scan (max 500). If omitted, scans all matching devices in the organization |

  If `deviceIds` is provided, every device must belong to the baseline's organization and match the baseline's `osType`. The API validates this before enqueuing the scan. The scan is dispatched through BullMQ and runs asynchronously on each target device.

The response includes the BullMQ job ID for tracking:

```json
{
  "message": "CIS scan queued",
  "jobId": "bullmq-job-id",
  "baselineId": "baseline-uuid"
}
```

---

sections.heading: Organization Compliance Overview
sections.text:
Get a consolidated view of CIS compliance across all devices, including average scores, passing/failing device counts, and individual device results:

```bash
GET /cis/compliance?orgId=uuid&baselineId=uuid&minScore=0&maxScore=100&limit=100
```

sections.heading: Compliance Query Parameters
sections.text:
| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `orgId` | UUID | Filter by organization |
| `baselineId` | UUID | Filter by baseline |
| `osType` | string | Filter by OS type: `windows`, `macos`, `linux` |
| `minScore` | integer | Minimum compliance score (0-100) |
| `maxScore` | integer | Maximum compliance score (0-100) |
| `limit` | integer | Results per page (1-500, default 200) |
| `offset` | integer | Pagination offset |

sections.heading: Compliance Response
Device-Level Report
sections.text:
Get the CIS scan history for a specific device with full findings detail:

```bash
GET /cis/devices/:deviceId/report?baselineId=uuid&limit=10
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `baselineId` | UUID | Filter results to a specific baseline |
| `limit` | integer | Number of recent results to return (1-200, default 50) |

The response includes the device information and a list of scan results paired with their baseline definitions. Each result contains the full `findings` array with individual check details.

sections.heading: Finding Detail
sections.text:
Each finding in a scan result contains:

| Field | Type | Description |
|-------|------|-------------|
| `checkId` | string | CIS check identifier (e.g., `1.1.1`, `2.3.17.1`) |
| `title` | string | Human-readable check title |
| `severity` | string | `low`, `medium`, `high`, `critical` |
| `status` | string | `pass`, `fail`, `not_applicable`, `error` |
| `evidence` | object | Platform-specific evidence of the check result |
| `remediation` | object | Recommended remediation (action, command type, payload, rollback hint) |
| `message` | string | Additional context or error message |

---

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.text: When CIS checks fail, you can request remediation actions that are dispatched to the agent after approval. This two-step workflow (request then approve) prevents accidental system changes from being applied without review.

sections.heading: Requesting Remediation
sections.text:
```bash
POST /cis/remediate
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "orgId": "uuid",
  "deviceId": "device-uuid",
  "baselineId": "baseline-uuid",
  "baselineResultId": "result-uuid",
  "checkIds": ["2.3.17.1", "2.3.17.2", "18.9.4.1"],
  "action": "apply",
  "reason": "Quarterly hardening pass for production servers"
}
```

sections.heading: Remediation Request Fields
sections.text:
| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `orgId` | UUID | No | Organization ID (resolved from device if not provided) |
| `deviceId` | UUID | Yes | Target device |
| `baselineId` | UUID | No | Baseline to reference (resolved from latest result if not provided) |
| `baselineResultId` | UUID | No | Specific scan result to remediate against (uses latest if not provided) |
| `checkIds` | string[] | Yes | CIS check IDs to remediate (1-100). Must be currently failing checks |
| `action` | string | No | `apply` (default) or `rollback` |
| `reason` | string | No | Reason for the remediation request (max 1,000 chars) |

  The requested `checkIds` must all be currently failing in the referenced baseline result. If any check ID is passing or not found in the result, the request is rejected with the list of invalid check IDs.

The response creates one remediation action per check ID, all in `pending_approval` status:

```json
{
  "message": "Created 3 CIS remediation action(s) pending approval",
  "deviceId": "device-uuid",
  "baselineId": "baseline-uuid",
  "baselineResultId": "result-uuid",
  "actionIds": ["action-uuid-1", "action-uuid-2", "action-uuid-3"],
  "approvalStatus": "pending"
}
```

sections.heading: Approving or Rejecting Remediations
sections.text:
```bash
POST /cis/remediate/approve
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "actionIds": ["action-uuid-1", "action-uuid-2"],
  "approved": true,
  "note": "Approved for production hardening window"
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `actionIds` | UUID[] | Yes | Remediation action IDs to approve or reject (1-500) |
| `approved` | boolean | Yes | `true` to approve (queue for execution), `false` to reject (cancel) |
| `note` | string | No | Approval or rejection note (max 1,000 chars) |

**When approved:**
- Status changes from `pending_approval` to `queued`
- Approval status changes from `pending` to `approved`
- Actions are dispatched to the agent through BullMQ
- If any individual action fails to queue, it is rolled back to `pending_approval`

**When rejected:**
- Status changes from `pending_approval` to `cancelled`
- Approval status changes from `pending` to `rejected`
- No commands are sent to the agent

  Only actions in `pending_approval` status with `pending` approval status can be approved or rejected. Actions that have already been approved, rejected, queued, or completed are skipped. The response includes both the processed and skipped action IDs.

sections.heading: Approvals that go stale
sections.text:
An approved remediation is dispatched under its approver's authority. It returns to `pending_approval` (approval status `pending`) instead of running when:

- the approver is no longer active or no longer holds `devices:execute`; or
- it was approved more than 7 days ago and still has not been dispatched.

Someone with `devices:execute` and MFA must approve it again.

sections.heading: Listing Remediation Actions
sections.text:
```bash
GET /cis/remediations?status=pending_approval&deviceId=uuid&limit=50
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `orgId` | UUID | Filter by organization |
| `status` | string | Filter by status: `pending_approval`, `queued`, `in_progress`, `completed`, `failed`, `cancelled` |
| `approvalStatus` | string | Filter by approval status: `pending`, `approved`, `rejected` |
| `deviceId` | UUID | Filter by device |
| `baselineId` | UUID | Filter by baseline |
| `limit` | integer | Results per page (1-200, default 100) |
| `offset` | integer | Pagination offset |

Each remediation action in the response includes the device hostname, baseline name, check ID, status, approval details, and execution timestamps.

---

sections.heading: Baselines
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/cis/baselines` | List baselines (requires `devices:read`) |
| POST | `/cis/baselines` | Create or update a baseline (requires `devices:execute` and MFA) |

sections.heading: Scanning
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/cis/scan` | Trigger a CIS scan (requires `devices:write`) |

sections.heading: Compliance
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| GET | `/cis/compliance` | Organization compliance overview with device results (requires `devices:read`) |
| GET | `/cis/devices/:deviceId/report` | Device-level scan history with findings detail (requires `devices:read`) |

sections.heading: Remediation
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/cis/remediate` | Request remediation for failing checks (requires `devices:execute` and MFA) |
| POST | `/cis/remediate/approve` | Approve or reject pending remediation actions (requires `devices:execute` and MFA) |
| GET | `/cis/remediations` | List remediation actions with filtering (requires `devices:read`) |

  All CIS hardening endpoints require authentication and one of these scopes: `organization`, `partner`, or `system`. Organization-scoped tokens are automatically restricted to their own organization's data.

---

sections.heading: macOS Sharing & Security Checks
sections.text:
Breeze includes 15 CIS checks aligned with the **CIS Apple macOS Benchmark Level 1** sharing and security controls. These checks evaluate whether common macOS sharing services and firewall settings are configured securely. They run automatically as part of any macOS baseline scan.

| Check | What It Evaluates |
|-------|-------------------|
| Screen Sharing | Whether Screen Sharing is disabled (CIS recommends off unless actively needed) |
| Remote Login (SSH) | Whether Remote Login is disabled for all users |
| File Sharing (SMB) | Whether the built-in SMB file sharing service is disabled |
| AirDrop Discoverability | Whether AirDrop is restricted to contacts only or fully disabled |
| Remote Management | Whether Apple Remote Desktop remote management is disabled |
| Remote Apple Events | Whether Remote Apple Events are disabled |
| Internet Sharing | Whether Internet Sharing (NAT gateway) is disabled on all interfaces |
| Content Caching | Whether the content caching service is disabled |
| Media Sharing | Whether media sharing (Home Sharing / shared library) is disabled |
| Bluetooth Sharing | Whether Bluetooth file sharing is disabled |
| Printer Sharing | Whether shared printers are disabled |
| Firewall Enabled | Whether the application firewall (socketfilterfw) is turned on |
| Firewall Stealth Mode | Whether stealth mode is enabled so the device does not respond to probing requests |
| Handoff | Whether Handoff is disabled (prevents data leakage between devices) |
| Wake for Network Access | Whether Wake for Network Access is disabled to reduce remote attack surface |

  These checks cover the sharing-related controls from CIS macOS Benchmark Level 1 Sections 2 and 3. If your macOS baseline is set to `l2`, additional defense-in-depth checks beyond sharing services are also evaluated.

When a sharing service is found enabled, the finding includes the current service state in the `evidence` field and a recommended remediation command (typically a `defaults write` or `launchctl` invocation) that can be dispatched through the standard approval workflow.

---

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
**Scan queued but no results appearing.**
After triggering a scan, the BullMQ job dispatches the baseline configuration to the agent. If results do not appear, verify the target device is online and the agent is connected. Check that the baseline's `osType` matches the device's operating system. Review BullMQ dashboard for failed jobs in the CIS scan queue.

**Compliance score is 100 but device has known security gaps.**
A score of 100 means all checks in the baseline passed. Verify that the baseline uses the correct benchmark version and level for your requirements. If you are using a `custom` level with `customExclusions`, the excluded checks are not counted and do not affect the score. Consider using the `l2` level for more comprehensive coverage.

**Remediation request rejected with "checkIds are not currently failing."**
The requested check IDs must be present in the referenced baseline result's `findings` array with a `fail` status. If the checks were passing, not applicable, or errored, they cannot be remediated. Get the device report to see the current check statuses: `GET /cis/devices/:deviceId/report`.

**Approved remediation stuck in `queued` status.**
After approval, remediation actions are dispatched through BullMQ. If the action remains in `queued` status, verify that the CIS remediation worker is running and processing jobs. Check Redis connectivity and BullMQ queue health.

**Remediation approval rolled back after queue failure.**
If the BullMQ dispatch fails for approved actions, their status is automatically rolled back to `pending_approval` with `pending` approval status. The response includes a `failedActionIds` array listing the affected actions. Resolve the BullMQ issue and retry the approval.

**Baseline scan schedule not triggering.**
Verify the `scanSchedule.enabled` field is `true` and `intervalHours` is set to a valid value (1-168). The `nextScanAt` timestamp indicates when the next scan is expected. If the scan scheduler is not running, scans will not trigger automatically -- check that the BullMQ scheduler worker is active.

**Device report shows old results but device was recently scanned.**
The device report returns results ordered by `checkedAt` descending. If the latest scan failed or is still in progress, results from previous scans will be shown. Check `GET /cis/compliance` to see the latest result status for the device.

title: Community Ecosystem
description: Open-source projects that work with Breeze through its public APIs. Listed when they meet published criteria, maintained by their own authors, and not endorsed or supported by Breeze.

sections.text:
Open-source projects that connect to Breeze through its public interfaces. A project is listed here because it meets the [listing criteria](#listing-criteria) below, and any project that meets them can be added the same way.

**Community-maintained:**
  These projects are built, maintained, and supported by their own authors. Breeze does not review, audit, or endorse them, and a listing is not a security assessment. Before you grant a project access, read its documentation and check the scopes it asks for. Report problems to the project's own issue tracker, not to Breeze.

sections.heading: Weavestream
sections.text:
Self-hosted IT documentation, asset management, and data intelligence platform. It syncs Breeze organizations, sites, devices, inventory, configuration policies, scripts, backup configurations, and custom fields into its own relational documentation model.

| | |
|---|---|
| **License** | AGPL-3.0 |
| **Connects through** | [Partner API](/reference/api/#partner-api-service-principals), read-only |
| **Scopes it requests** | `organizations:read`, `sites:read`, `devices:read`, `inventory:read`, `configuration:read`, `scripts:read`, `backup-configuration:read`, `custom-fields:read` |
| **Compatibility** | Weavestream 1.9.10 or later. Earlier releases reject the fields Breeze v0.111+ adds within `schemaVersion: "1"`. |
