| **Setup guide** | [Breeze integration docs](https://github.com/Weavestream/Weavestream/blob/main/docs/integrations/breeze.md) |
| **Source and issues** | [github.com/Weavestream/Weavestream](https://github.com/Weavestream/Weavestream) |

The scope list comes from Weavestream's own setup guide. Check it there before you create the service principal, since the project may change what it needs.

sections.heading: Listing criteria
sections.text:
A project is listed when all of these hold:

1. **Open source.** The code that talks to Breeze is published under an [OSI-approved license](https://opensource.org/licenses).
2. **Public interfaces only.** It connects through documented Breeze surfaces: the [Partner API](/reference/api/#partner-api-service-principals), [webhooks](/features/webhooks/), the [MCP server](/features/mcp-server/), or the [extension SDK](/features/extensions/). It never reads the Breeze database directly or calls undocumented endpoints.
3. **Least privilege, stated up front.** Its documentation lists the exact scopes or permissions it needs and what each one is used for. It uses a service principal or API key, never a Breeze user's password or session.
4. **Tolerates additive API changes.** It ignores fields it does not recognize, per the [Partner API compatibility rule](/reference/api/#schema-versioning-and-compatibility), so a routine Breeze upgrade does not break it.
5. **Reachable maintainers.** It has its own public documentation and issue tracker.
6. **Maintained.** It has had a release or commit in the last 12 months.

These criteria are about how a project connects to Breeze. They say nothing about its quality or fitness for your environment.

sections.heading: Adding or removing a project
sections.text:
To add a project, open a pull request against this page ([`apps/docs/src/content/docs/features/community-ecosystem.mdx`](https://github.com/LanternOps/breeze/blob/main/apps/docs/src/content/docs/features/community-ecosystem.mdx)). Add an entry with the same fields as the ones above, and include a link that shows each criterion is met. Maintainers of a project can ask for its listing to be updated or removed the same way.

An entry can be removed when the project no longer meets the criteria, for example when it stops working with current Breeze releases or has had no activity for 12 months. Before removing an entry, we open an issue on the project's tracker and wait 30 days for a response.

title: Configuration Policies
description: Bundle patch, alert, maintenance, compliance, and backup settings into hierarchical policies with scoped assignments and automatic drift remediation.
headings: Which policies can be a parent
Overriding and reverting an inherited feature
MFA and inherited patch / maintenance settings
Defaults in the Effective Configuration tab

sections.text:
Configuration Policies let you bundle device settings — patches, alerts, maintenance windows, compliance rules, and more — into reusable templates and apply them to any scope of your fleet. Policies evaluate automatically on a schedule and can auto-remediate drift without manual intervention.

Policies are **hierarchical**: settings cascade from the broadest scope down to the most specific, and more specific assignments always win.

```
Breeze Defaults  (lowest priority — read-only, always present)
  └── Partner
        └── Organization
              └── Site
                    └── Device Group
                          └── Device  (highest priority — always wins)
```

sections.heading: Policy ownership: organization vs. partner-wide
sections.text:
A policy is owned at one of two scopes:

- **Organization** — the policy belongs to a single customer organization and can only be assigned within that org's hierarchy. This is the default.
- **Partner-wide (all orgs)** — the policy belongs to your partner account and can apply across **every** organization you manage. Use this for fleet-wide standards you want enforced everywhere without recreating the policy per customer.

You choose the ownership scope when creating the policy. Partner-wide policies can only be created and managed by partner-level users with full access to every organization under the partner (not users restricted to a subset of organizations); organization-scoped users see partner-wide policies in their effective configuration but cannot edit them.

Backup settings cannot be configured on a partner-wide policy — see [Backup](#backup) below.

sections.heading: Baseline policies (inheritance)
sections.text:
A policy can optionally have one **parent** — a baseline policy it inherits feature settings from. This lets an MSP define a standard baseline once (e.g. "Standard Workstation Baseline") and have every customer-specific policy build on it, instead of copy-pasting the same patch schedule, alert thresholds, and maintenance windows into every org.

**Effective links of a policy** = the policy's own feature links, plus, for any feature type the policy has no link of its own for, the parent's link for that type. In other words: a child's own configuration always wins; anything the child hasn't touched falls through to the parent.

You set the parent when **creating** a policy: choose **Link to Existing** on the New Policy screen and pick a baseline from the list. The parent cannot be changed after the policy is created.

sections.heading: Which policies can be a parent
sections.text:
| A child that is... | ...can inherit from |
|---|---|
| Organization-owned | a policy in the **same organization**, or a **partner-wide** policy owned by the same partner |
| Partner-wide | only another **partner-wide** policy owned by the same partner |

Only **one level** of inheritance is supported — a baseline policy cannot itself have a parent. If a candidate baseline already has a parent, it won't appear as an eligible baseline for a new policy.

sections.heading: Overriding and reverting an inherited feature
sections.text:
Open any feature tab on a child policy. If the feature comes from the parent, the tab shows a **Configured (inherited)** badge and the settings are shown read-only, seeded from the parent's configuration:

- Click **Override** to save a copy of the inherited settings as the policy's own link — the tab becomes editable and future parent changes no longer affect this policy for that feature.
- Click **Revert to Parent** on an overridden feature to delete the policy's own link and fall back to the parent's again.

  **The parent's `Active`/`Inactive`/`Archived` status does not gate inheritance.** Archiving a baseline policy does not silently strip security, patch, or backup configuration from every policy that inherits from it — only the *child's own* status controls whether its assignments are evaluated, exactly as for a policy with no parent. Before archiving a widely-inherited baseline, check its Overview tab for the "Inherited by N policies" list to see the blast radius.

sections.heading: Deleting a baseline
sections.text: A policy that other policies inherit from cannot be deleted while those children still reference it — the delete is refused with a list of the policies that need to be moved off it first (deleted, or given a different or no parent) before the baseline itself can be removed. This prevents deleting a widely-used baseline from silently un-configuring every policy built on it.

sections.heading: MFA and inherited patch / maintenance settings
sections.text: If a baseline carries a Patch Management or Maintenance Windows feature — both of which require a session with satisfied multi-factor authentication to add or change directly — creating a **new** policy linked to that baseline requires the same MFA session, since the new policy immediately gains that gated configuration through inheritance.

sections.heading: Feature types
sections.text:
A policy can bundle multiple feature types:

| Feature | What it controls |
|---|---|
| **Patch Management** | Schedule, reboot policy, exclusive Windows Update control; patch approval rules live on the linked [update ring](/features/update-rings/) |
| **Maintenance Windows** | Recurrence, duration, alert/patch/automation suppression |
| **Compliance Rules** | Desired-state rules, enforcement level, remediation script |
| **Backup** | Schedule and retention |
| **Security** | Security policy settings |
| **Monitors** | Attaches [monitors](/features/monitors/) -- objects that bundle a condition, severity, delivery, and response actions -- to this policy's scope |
| **Automation** | Event triggers, cron schedules, bulk actions |
| **Privileged Access** | Windows UAC elevation prompt capture for [privileged access management](/features/pam/) |
| **Vulnerability Scanning** | Turns on daily CVE correlation for the scope (off by default) -- see [vulnerability management](/features/vulnerability-management/) |
| **Event Log Forwarding** | Destination and filters for shipping device event logs to an external store -- see [Event Log Forwarding](/features/event-log-forwarding/) |
| **Software Policy** | Allowlist/blocklist/audit enforcement evaluated during software inventory scans -- see [Software Policies](/features/software-policies/) |
| **Sensitive Data Discovery** | Scan schedule and rules for PII, credentials, and other sensitive data on endpoints -- see [Sensitive Data Discovery](/features/sensitive-data/) |
| **Peripheral Control** | USB, Bluetooth, and Thunderbolt device allow/block rules -- see [Peripheral Control](/features/peripheral-control/) |
| **Warranty** | Warning and critical expiry thresholds that raise alerts before a device's warranty lapses -- see [Warranty Tracking](/features/warranty-tracking/) |
| **Breeze Helper** | Tray icon and menu options (portal link, device info, request support) for the [Breeze Helper](/agents/helper/) app |
| **Remote Access** | MFA and consent requirements for Remote Desktop and Remote Terminal sessions -- see [Remote Access](/features/remote-access/) |
| **OneDrive Helper** | Silent sign-in, Files On-Demand, Known Folder Move, and SharePoint library auto-mount -- see [OneDrive Helper](/features/onedrive-helper/) |
| **Device Lifecycle** | Days to retain a removed device before it is permanently purged |
| **System Protection** | Whether Breeze asks Windows devices for a System Restore checkpoint before patch installs, scripts and software installs -- see [System Protection](#system-protection) |
| **Workload inventory** | Lists the containers and VMs on a host (Docker, Podman, Hyper-V, Proxmox); off by default -- see [Workload Inventory](/features/workload-inventory/) |
| **Security Agents** | Keeps Huntress or SentinelOne installed on every in-scope device, using the keys from that vendor's integration -- see [Security Agents](#security-agents) |

Each feature can be configured in one of two modes:

- **Linked** — points to an existing policy object by ID (e.g., an existing update ring). Changes to the linked object propagate automatically.
- **Inline** — settings are stored directly in the policy. Useful for simple configurations that don't need to be shared. Required for `backup` and `security` feature types.

sections.heading: Monitors and alerting
sections.text:
A single policy carries every alert condition — service and process watches,
thresholds, offline detection, event-log patterns — as monitors attached on its
**Monitors** tab, plus one agent-collection setting, *Check interval*.
See [Monitors](/features/monitors/).

Select **Add to inherited monitors** for cumulative deployment, or review
**Replace inherited monitors** when preserving converted inline-rule behavior.
Broad reactive automation belongs to **Jobs → Alert workflows**.

sections.heading: Enforcement modes
sections.text:
Compliance rules support three enforcement levels:

| Mode | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `monitor` | Report non-compliance only. No alert, no action. |
| `warn` | Raise a **medium** alert for each non-compliant device. It is delivered like any other alert and resolves itself once the device is compliant again. |
| `enforce` | Raise a **high** alert and auto-remediate using the linked remediation script. Without a script it behaves like `warn` at high severity. |

Compliance alerts always belong to the device's organization, including for partner-wide policies. Changing a rule to `monitor` resolves the alerts it already raised at its next evaluation.

sections.heading: Creating a policy
sections.text:
1. Navigate to **Fleet Management → Config Policies**.

2. Click **New Policy**, then choose **Configure New** to start from scratch, or **Link to Existing** to inherit from a baseline policy (see [Baseline policies](#baseline-policies-inheritance) above). Choosing **Link to Existing** adds a picker of eligible baselines — filtered to the ones your chosen ownership scope is allowed to inherit from.

3. Enter a **Name** and optional **Description**.

4. If you're a partner-level user with full access to every organization, an **Apply to** picker appears: choose **All organizations (partner-wide)** to apply the policy across every organization you manage, or **A specific organization** and pick the target org from the dropdown. Users scoped to a single organization (or with access to only some organizations) don't see this picker — their policy is always scoped to their own organization. Note that Backup settings can't be configured on a partner-wide policy.

5. Set **Status** to **Active**. Inactive and archived policies are not evaluated by the scheduler.

6. Click **Save** to open the policy detail editor.

sections.heading: Adding features to a policy
sections.text: Open the policy detail editor and click the tab for the feature you want to configure.

sections.heading: Patch Management
sections.text:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Schedule** | Frequency (daily/weekly/monthly) and time of day for patch runs |
| **Reboot policy** | How to handle required reboots after patching |
| **Manage Windows Update exclusively through Breeze** | Windows-only. Off by default. When on, the agent suppresses the device's native Windows Update automatic-install channel (it sets the `NoAutoUpdate` registry value under `HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows\WindowsUpdate\AU`) so that device only receives updates through Breeze's schedule and approval rings — no surprise reboots or out-of-band patches. Turning it back off returns update control to native Windows Update. |

There is no auto-approve setting on this tab. Patch approval — automatic approval, severities, deferral days and per-application rules — is configured only on the [update ring](/features/update-rings/) the policy links to.

Patch Management is available on partner-wide (all organizations) policies — an [update ring](/features/update-rings/) can be linked directly, and the policy patches devices across every organization you manage. Behind the scenes, deployments are still tracked per organization: creating a deployment job from a partner-wide policy produces one job per organization with matching devices, so each customer's patch history and compliance reporting stay separate even though the schedule and approval rules are defined once.

sections.heading: Monitors
sections.text:
Open **Monitors**, attach an existing definition or create one, then save the
policy. Configure the condition, responses and Notify settings on that monitor.
Use [Delivery](/features/notifications/) for shared notification routing.
During conversion, review **Needs conversion** before confirming; resolve every
blocked or unconvertible row deliberately.

sections.heading: Maintenance Windows
sections.text:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Recurrence** | Day of week or month when the window applies |
| **Start time** | Local time the window begins |
| **Duration** | Length of the window in **hours** |
| **Suppress Alerts** | Silence alert notifications during the window |
| **Suppress Patching** | Skip scheduled patch jobs during the window |
| **Suppress Automations** | Skip automation triggers during the window |
| **Suppress Scripts** | Skip scheduled script execution during the window |

sections.heading: Compliance Rules
sections.text:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Name** | A label for this rule |
| **Rule definition** | The desired-state condition to evaluate |
| **Enforcement level** | `monitor`, `warn`, or `enforce` |
| **Check interval** | How often to re-evaluate (minutes) |
| **Remediation script** | Script to run when `enforce` mode detects non-compliance |

sections.heading: Backup
sections.text:
Backup is **not available on partner-wide (all organizations) policies**. Backup settings are always tied to a single organization, so a policy owned at the partner level has no organization to attach them to — attempting to add or save a Backup feature link on a partner-wide policy is rejected. Configure Backup on an organization-owned policy instead.

Backup feature links use **inline settings** stored in the `config_policy_backup_settings` table (one row per feature link).

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| **Backup Mode** | enum | What to back up: `file` (default), `hyperv`, `mssql`, or `system_image` |
| **Schedule** | JSONB | Frequency (`daily`, `weekly`, `monthly`), time (`HH:MM`), timezone, day of week/month |
| **Retention** | JSONB | `keepDaily`, `keepWeekly`, `keepMonthly` snapshot counts |
| **Paths** | JSONB array | Directories to include (file mode only) |
| **Targets** | JSONB | Mode-specific targeting with optional exclude lists (Hyper-V and MSSQL modes) |

**Backup modes:**

- **File** — backs up directories listed in the Paths field.
- **Hyper-V** — exports all discovered VMs by default. Set `targets.excludeVms` to skip specific VMs by name.
- **MSSQL** — backs up all discovered databases by default. Set `targets.excludeDatabases` to skip specific databases.
- **System Image** — full system image capture with no additional targeting needed.

Hyper-V and MSSQL modes use **all-by-default targeting** — newly created VMs or databases are automatically included on the next scheduled backup run without any policy changes.

When a backup feature is linked to a configuration policy, the schedule, retention, and mode settings in the policy override whatever is set on the standalone backup configuration. The policy system resolves which backup settings apply to a device using the same hierarchical precedence rules as other feature types (device-level wins over group, site, org, partner).

  Use the effective configuration endpoint to verify which backup schedule a specific device will receive: `GET /configuration-policies/effective/:deviceId`

sections.heading: Security, Monitoring, Automation
sections.text:
Configure security policy settings for **Security**; check intervals and targets for **Monitoring**; and event triggers, cron schedules, and action chains for **Automation**.

Saving **Security** settings with IOC auto-quarantine turned on needs `devices:execute` and MFA, and scheduled scans quarantine only under a user who still holds that permission; otherwise they run detect-only. See [Auto-quarantine runs under an approving user](/features/security/#auto-quarantine-runs-under-an-approving-user).

sections.heading: Vulnerability Scanning
sections.text:
The **Vulnerability** feature is a single on/off toggle that controls whether the devices in the policy's scope are scanned for CVEs. It is configured **inline** (the on/off state lives in the policy) and is **off by default** -- a device with no vulnerability policy is never scanned, and its Vulnerabilities tab stays empty.

Open the policy's **Vulnerability** tab, switch **Enable vulnerability scanning** on, save, and assign the policy. Because resolution is closest-wins, a device- or group-level setting of *off* overrides an organization-wide *on*. Once a scope is enabled, Breeze correlates its software and OS inventory against the CVE feeds once a day. If a policy exists but no device resolves to *on*, the daily job is simply a no-op -- it never falls back to scanning everything. The findings themselves are reviewed and acted on in [Vulnerability Management](/features/vulnerability-management/), not on this tab.

sections.heading: Security Agents
sections.text:
The **Security Agents** tab (v0.124.0) keeps a vendor's endpoint agent installed on every device the policy reaches. It is configured **inline**: switch **Deploy Huntress** or **Deploy SentinelOne** on and save. Control D and NextDNS are listed but marked **Coming soon** and cannot be turned on yet.

What happens after you save:

- Every in-scope **Windows** device whose organization is mapped in that vendor's [integration](/features/edr-integrations/) gets the agent installed with that organization's own keys — Huntress organization keys, SentinelOne site tokens. Keys never live in the policy. Organizations that are not mapped are skipped and read **Not applicable**, with no failed deployments.
- Breeze generates a **read-only managed software policy** for the deployment. It appears under **Software → Policies** with a **Managed by configuration policy** badge; change it here, not there.
- Each device's coverage is evaluated on a schedule and shown on the **Software → Policies** compliance view under **Security agent coverage**, as one of **Covered**, **Gap**, **Vendor only**, **Vendor offline**, **Mismatched org**, **Not applicable** or **Pending**, with a reason (for example *Install pending*, *Awaiting vendor report*, *Organization not mapped to the vendor*). See [Software Policies](/features/software-policies/#managed-security-agent-policies).
- A device that moves from covered to **Gap** raises a medium alert ("*Vendor* coverage gap on *device*"); a device the vendor reports under a different organization raises one too. Nothing is reinstalled automatically in the mismatched case — reassign the agent in the vendor console. Both alerts resolve on their own when coverage is restored.
- macOS devices show **Not applicable** for Huntress (it needs MDM approval, so Breeze does not install it automatically) and are not supported for SentinelOne. Linux is not supported for either.

Saving the tab with a vendor turned on needs permission to run commands on devices, with MFA. The save is refused with a link to **Connect the integration** when that vendor's integration is not set up for your partner. **SentinelOne** also needs the built-in SentinelOne package to have a Windows MSI as its **latest** version, with install arguments that include `SITE_TOKEN={s1_site_token}`; otherwise the save is refused with a link to the package's **Versions** tab (**Software → Deployment → SentinelOne**). Breeze does not provide the installer. An organization with no SentinelOne site mapping reads **Organization not mapped to the vendor**.

Turning a vendor off stops enforcement but never uninstalls the agent. With no vendor enabled, devices reached by the policy are opted out of every security agent. A policy assigned closer to a device (site, group or device, or an inheriting child policy) that has its own Security Agents settings replaces these settings entirely for those devices; a vendor left out there is not enforced. The tab can be set on a **partner-wide (all orgs)** policy.

#### DNS filtering vendors

**Control D** and **NextDNS** are DNS-filtering clients configured through the same tab. They show **Coming soon** and cannot be turned on yet: the integration is built end to end, but the switch stays disabled until the vendor lab validation is complete. Once it opens up, they can be turned on for **Windows** devices only, with these requirements:

| Vendor | Built-in package | Tenant variable | Windows service |
|---|---|---|---|
| Control D | Control D (Windows) | `controld_provisioning_code` | `ctrld` |
| NextDNS | NextDNS CLI (Windows) | `nextdns_profile_id` | `nextdns` |

- **Catalog first.** Add the client to your partner's software catalog from **Software → Catalog → Built-in packages**. Turning the vendor on without it is refused with a message pointing there.
- **One variable per organization.** Set the variable under **Settings → Variables**, either on each organization or once as a partner-wide default that organizations inherit (an organization's own value wins; for example `<provisioning-code>` or `<profile-id>` as the value). Create it as a normal variable, **not** a secret one: enrollment values are non-secret by design, and a secret variable is never placed in an install script. An organization without the variable is skipped and reads **Not applicable** with the reason **Deployment variable missing**; a variable marked secret reads **Deployment variable is marked secret**.
- **Presence comes from the service.** These clients are zip installs with no Add/Remove Programs entry, so Breeze uses the Windows service check described under [Service compliance](/features/software-policies/#service-compliance). No service found means the client is missing and is installed automatically. A stopped service reads **not running** and is never reinstalled; an armed policy's service watch restarts it. A running service is compliant. With no recent service telemetry the device reads **service unverified**, and nothing is installed until the service is observed.
- **Coverage is limited.** Breeze does not sync the Control D or NextDNS consoles, so the **Security agent coverage** panels show only whether each device can receive the client (**Pending** or **Not applicable**). Install and service state appear in the generated software policy's compliance.
- **Agent version.** Devices need agent 0.125.0 or newer. An older agent fails the device with `agent_update_required` and nothing is installed; its service results also read **service unverified** rather than missing.
- **Platforms.** Control D on macOS is not offered yet, NextDNS is Windows only, and Linux is not supported.

Turning a DNS vendor off never uninstalls the client. Uninstall manually from an elevated prompt or script: `C:\ControlD\ctrld.exe uninstall` for Control D, or `"C:\Program Files\nextdns\nextdns.exe" uninstall` for NextDNS.

sections.heading: System Protection
sections.text:
**Checkpoints need agent 0.124.0:**
  Windows devices take System Restore checkpoints and report the outcome from **agent 0.124.0**. On a device still running an older agent, saving this policy only records what Breeze *asks for*: every attempt stays at **Awaiting the device**, and no outcome is reported. Do not read an "Awaiting" entry on an out-of-date device as a failure, and do not read a saved policy as a restore point that exists — only a **Restore point creation confirmed** badge means one was made.

The **System Protection** feature controls whether Breeze asks a Windows device for a System Restore checkpoint just before it takes a risky action. The device takes **one restore point per command**, just before the first change a patch run, script or software install makes; a command that changes nothing spends no restore point. The outcome is reported back on that command. Checkpoints are best-effort and reporting-only: a restore point that cannot be created is reported, and the command still runs. It is configured **inline** and has three toggles:

| Toggle | Default | Applies before |
|---|---|---|
| **Before patch installs** | On | Installing operating system updates |
| **Before scripts** | Off | Running a script on the device |
| **Before software installs** | Off | Installing or updating software |

It also has a **Checkpoint label prefix** (up to 64 characters, blank means the default) that is shown at the start of each restore point's description in Windows.

Like other features, System Protection resolves closest-wins (Device → Device Group → Site → Organization → Partner) and can be set on a **partner-wide (all orgs)** policy, so one policy can cover every organization you manage. With no System Protection feature in scope, the platform default applies: a checkpoint is requested before patch installs only.

**What stays the same for patching.** Patch installs keep their existing best-effort checkpoint behavior. A device whose command carries no System Protection setting is treated the legacy way: patch installs are requested, scripts and software installs are not. Turning **Before patch installs** *off* cannot be enforced on a device until that device's agent reports support for the setting (agent 0.124.0 or later), and the policy tab says so. Scripts and software installs take no checkpoint until you switch them on **and** the device runs agent 0.124.0 or later.

#### What System Restore does and does not do

System Restore protects system files, the registry, installed programs and settings. **It is not a backup and does not protect personal files.** Windows limits restore-point creation to once every 24 hours by default, so a second action inside that window reuses the existing point; Breeze reports this as **Existing point reused** and never as a new checkpoint. A restore point that was created can later be removed by Windows or become unusable. Breeze reports what happened at the moment of each action and makes no promise about anything later.

#### Where you see the result

- **Patch history, script execution details and software deployments** show a one-line badge for the attempt that belongs to that action.
- The device's **System Restore** tab lists every request recorded for the device: when it was requested, what triggered it (patch install, script run, software install) and the outcome.

#### Status reference

The badge text is what a technician sees on the patch, script or deployment and on the device's **System Restore** tab.

| Badge text | What it means and what to do |
|---|---|
| Awaiting the device | Breeze asked; the device has not reported back. A row that stays here for a device that has been online means the agent is older than 0.124.0, the release that takes checkpoints and reports outcomes. Update the agent. |
| Restore point creation confirmed | The device reported that Windows created a restore point and that it could be found afterwards. Treat it as a record of that moment only; it can be removed or become unusable later. |
| Existing point reused | Windows' 24-hour limit meant no new point was made, and an earlier one was accepted. Nothing to do. The badge shows the age of the reused point when the device reports it. |
| Skipped — System Restore is turned off on this device | System Restore is off for the system drive. **Breeze will not turn System Restore on for you.** If you want checkpoints on this device, enable System Protection for the system drive in Windows (System Properties → System Protection, or `Enable-ComputerRestore` from an elevated PowerShell) and the next action can request one. |
| Skipped — definitions-only update | The patch run only contained definition updates, which do not need a checkpoint. Nothing to do. |
| Not needed — no changes were made, so no restore point was created | The command stopped before it changed anything (for example the package was already installed, or the request was rejected during validation or preflight), so no System Restore point was needed. Nothing to do. |
| Not available on this device | System Restore is not present on this Windows edition (for example the system library or provider is missing). Nothing to enable. See the support matrix below. |
| Skipped — the volume snapshot service was in use | Another volume snapshot operation held the service. Retry the action later if you want a checkpoint. |
| Skipped — not enough privileges | The agent was not running with the rights System Restore needs. Check how the agent service runs on this device. |
| Could not be verified | A request was made but the device could not confirm that the restore point exists. Do not assume one exists; check Windows directly (`Get-ComputerRestorePoint`). |
| Failed — *message* | Windows or the agent returned an error, shown in the badge. Use the message to troubleshoot. |

A checkpoint outcome never blocks the action it was requested for. A badge value your console does not recognise (for example after a partial upgrade) shows as "Outcome not recognised by this version of the console".

#### Support matrix

This table records what was observed when the native System Restore call was tested on real Windows builds. It is **documentation only: Breeze never gates by Windows edition.** At run time the agent checks whether the system library, the entry point, the WMI provider and the enabled state are actually present and reports what it found. A row here does not turn a device on or off.

| OS and build | Provider present | Creation succeeded | Badge Breeze is designed to report | Caveat |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Windows Server 2022 Standard 21H2, build 20348.5256 | No — `srclient.dll` is absent and the `SystemRestore` WMI class is invalid | Not applicable — the provider is absent, so there is nothing to call | **Not available on this device** | Observed with agent 0.124.0 before the release: only the unsupported and skipped paths were exercised, because Server 2022 has no System Restore. |
| Windows 11 Pro 25H2, build 26200.8653 | Yes | Yes, with System Restore enabled on the system drive | **Restore point creation confirmed** when enabled; **Skipped — System Restore is turned off on this device** when it is off (the call returns error 1058, service disabled) | Tested with a diagnostic tool on one physical machine, with the 24-hour limit lifted for the test only. The Breeze agent itself has not yet been run there. |
| Windows 10 22H2 | Not yet verified | Not yet verified | — | Tracked in [#8265](https://github.com/LanternOps/breeze/issues/8265). |
| Windows Server 2025 | Not yet verified | Not yet verified | — | Tracked in [#8265](https://github.com/LanternOps/breeze/issues/8265). Do not infer from Server 2022. |

The badge column is a design mapping, not an observation on that build. Agent 0.124.0 reports these outcomes; the created path has not been verified on real hardware with the agent before the release, so report a regression on the linked issue.

sections.heading: Assigning a policy
sections.text: Open the policy detail editor → **Assignments** tab. What you see depends on who owns the policy.

sections.heading: Partner library policy
sections.text:
The tab is an organization checklist, not a level picker.

1. Optionally set **Role Filter** and **OS Filter**. Leave them empty to apply to every device in the chosen organizations.

2. Turn on **All organizations (partner-wide)** to apply the policy across every organization you manage, or check individual organizations.

3. Assigned rows show the role and OS filters that were saved with that assignment. To change filters, turn the assignment off and on again with the new chips selected.

A partner-wide "servers only" assignment reaches server-role devices in every assigned organization. Workstations skip it. You cannot put two different role sets on the same policy at the same target; make a second policy if servers and workstations need different settings.

sections.heading: Organization policy
sections.text:
1. Choose a **Level**: Organization, Site, Device Group, or Device.

2. For Site, Device Group, or Device, select the specific target. An organization-level assignment always targets the policy's own organization.

3. Optionally set the same **Role Filter** and **OS Filter**. Empty means every device in that target.

4. Set a **Priority** number. When two policies at the same level both define the same feature, the lower priority number wins (priority `1` takes precedence over priority `2`). On an exact tie, the assignment created first wins.

5. Click **Assign**.

  A device-level assignment always takes precedence over all group, site, organization, and partner assignments, regardless of priority number. A partner-wide assignment is the broadest scope and is overridden by any more-specific assignment.

sections.heading: Per-device compliance status
sections.text:
Each device's detail page surfaces how that device measures against every compliance rule from its assigned policies — separate from the Effective Configuration view. Open any device page and select the **Compliance** tab to see a row for every assigned policy's compliance rules, including the rule name, current status (compliant, non-compliant, pending, or error), the last evaluation time, and any remediation attempts. This makes it easy to audit a single machine's standing without leaving the device page.

The underlying endpoint is:

```
GET /policies/compliance/device/:deviceId
```

sections.heading: Breeze Defaults baseline
sections.text:
Every Breeze deployment ships with a built-in set of **Breeze Defaults** that sit at the bottom of the resolution hierarchy. These defaults are read-only — you cannot edit or delete them — but every policy you create at any level overrides them.

To inspect the current defaults, navigate to **Fleet Management → Config Policies → Defaults** (or go directly to **/configuration-policies/defaults**). The page lists every setting that Breeze ships with, shows its current value, and indicates whether it is **Active** (in effect for devices with no overriding policy) or **Not enforced** (the feature is present in defaults but not turned on by default).

Examples of shipped defaults:

| Setting | Default state |
|---------|---------------|
| Remote Access | Active (on) |
| PAM / UAC capture | Not enforced (off by default) |
| Vulnerability Scanning | Not enforced (off by default) |

Each row on the Defaults page includes a **Create override policy** shortcut that opens the policy editor pre-configured for that feature, so you can add a partner- or org-level override without navigating away.

sections.heading: Defaults in the Effective Configuration tab
sections.text: When a device has no policy assigned for a particular feature, the **Effective Configuration** tab on the device page attributes that value to **Breeze Defaults** and shows a **Not enforced** badge next to it, making it clear that the setting comes from the built-in layer rather than an explicit policy.

sections.heading: Viewing effective configuration
sections.text:
To see the merged settings a specific device will receive:

1. Navigate to the device's detail page.
2. Open the **Effective Configuration** tab.
3. The page shows the resolved settings for each feature type and which policy in the inheritance chain provided each value — including **Breeze Defaults** for any feature not covered by an assigned policy. When the assigned policy itself has no link for a feature and the value came from its [baseline parent](#baseline-policies-inheritance) instead, the card also shows **"Inherited from <baseline name>"** — two different kinds of inheritance can stack: the hierarchy chain (which *policy* is assigned) and the baseline relationship (which *policy's own settings* apply).

```
GET /configuration-policies/effective/:deviceId
```

Use `POST /configuration-policies/effective/:deviceId/diff` to preview how a policy change would affect a device's effective configuration before saving. The request body accepts:

```json
{
  "add": [{ "configPolicyId": "uuid", "level": "site", "targetId": "uuid", "priority": 1 }],
  "remove": ["assignment-uuid"]
}
```

The response returns both `current` and `proposed` effective configurations for comparison.

sections.heading: Patch jobs
sections.text:
Policies with a Patch Management feature can trigger deployment jobs:

```
POST /configuration-policies/:id/patch-job
```

Request body:

```json
{
  "deviceIds": ["uuid-1", "uuid-2"],
  "name": "Optional job name",
  "scheduledAt": "2026-03-01T02:00:00Z"
}
```

For each device, Breeze checks:

- Whether the device exists and is accessible — inaccessible devices are listed in `skipped.inaccessibleDeviceIds`
- Whether the device is inside an active maintenance window with patching suppression — suppressed devices are listed in `skipped.maintenanceSuppressedDeviceIds`
- Whether the device ID is valid — invalid IDs are listed in `skipped.missingDeviceIds`
- Whether the device belongs to the policy's organization (org-owned policy) or to an organization under the policy's partner (partner-wide policy) — devices outside that scope are rejected with a `403` rather than silently skipped, since patching someone else's fleet is never allowed

The job is created with the schedule defined in the policy's patch settings (e.g., weekly on Sunday at 2 AM). Targeting devices from a partner-wide policy creates one job per organization that has matching devices, so a single request can produce several jobs — the response lists every job created, each with its own `orgId` and device count.

sections.heading: API reference
sections.text:
All paths are relative to `/api/v1`.

| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| GET | `/configuration-policies` | List policies |
| POST | `/configuration-policies` | Create policy |
| GET | `/configuration-policies/eligible-parents` | List baseline policies eligible as a parent for a given ownership scope (`?ownerScope=organization&orgId=…` or `?ownerScope=partner`) |
| GET | `/configuration-policies/:id` | Get policy — includes `parentPolicyId`, an embedded `parentPolicy` (read-only, with its own feature links), and `childPolicies` |
| PATCH | `/configuration-policies/:id` | Update metadata |
| DELETE | `/configuration-policies/:id` | Delete (cascades to features and assignments). Returns `409` with the list of dependent policies if any policy still inherits from this one. |
| GET | `/configuration-policies/:id/features` | List feature links |
| POST | `/configuration-policies/:id/features` | Add feature |
| PATCH | `/configuration-policies/:id/features/:linkId` | Update feature settings |
| DELETE | `/configuration-policies/:id/features/:linkId` | Remove feature |
| GET | `/configuration-policies/:id/assignments` | List assignments |
| POST | `/configuration-policies/:id/assignments` | Assign policy to a target |
| DELETE | `/configuration-policies/:id/assignments/:aid` | Unassign |
| GET | `/configuration-policies/effective/:deviceId` | Resolve effective config for a device |
| POST | `/configuration-policies/effective/:deviceId/diff` | Preview change diff |
| GET | `/configuration-policies/assignments/target` | List assignments for a target |
| POST | `/configuration-policies/:id/patch-job` | Create patch deployment job |
| GET | `/configuration-policies/:id/patch-settings` | Get patch settings for a policy |
| GET | `/configuration-policies/:id/resolve-patch-config/:deviceId` | Resolve patch config for a specific device |

When creating a policy, set `ownerScope` to `organization` (the default) or `partner`. With `ownerScope: "partner"` the policy is owned partner-wide and any supplied `orgId` is ignored — the partner is always derived from the caller's own token, never trusted from the request body. Creating a partner-wide policy requires partner scope (a `403` is returned otherwise). When assigning a partner-wide policy, use `level: "partner"`; the target is resolved from the caller's own partner, so no `targetId` is required.

To create a policy that inherits from a baseline, pass `parentPolicyId` in the create request body — see [Baseline policies](#baseline-policies-inheritance) above for which parents a given ownership scope may reference. An invalid, cross-tenant, or already-nested parent is rejected with `400 { "error": "INVALID_PARENT_POLICY" }` — a single error for every rejection reason, so the response can't be used to probe which policy IDs exist.

When calling the features endpoints, the `featureType` value must be one of: `patch`, `backup`, `security`, `maintenance`, `compliance`, `automation`, `event_log`, `software_policy`, `sensitive_data`, `peripheral_control`, `warranty`, `helper`, `remote_access`, `pam`, `onedrive_helper`, `vulnerability`, `device_lifecycle`, `monitors`, `hardware_monitoring`, `security_agents`. `monitors` is the authoring/deployment feature. The retired values `alert_rule` and `monitoring` are rejected with `410 Gone`.

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
**Policy not applying to a device**

Check that the policy is assigned at some level in the hierarchy. Open the device's Effective Configuration tab — if the policy is not listed in the inheritance chain, it has not been assigned to any scope the device belongs to.

**Compliance check not running**

Ensure the policy status is **Active** and `checkIntervalMinutes` is set. The evaluation worker scans for due policies every 60 seconds; setting `checkIntervalMinutes` to 1 means a rule will be checked within 60 seconds of becoming due.

**Patch job skipping devices**

Check all three skipped lists in the response: `missingDeviceIds`, `inaccessibleDeviceIds`, and `maintenanceSuppressedDeviceIds`. A device in an active maintenance window with **Suppress Patching** enabled will be skipped automatically.

**Enforcement not remediating**

Enforcement mode must be set to `enforce` and a remediation script must be linked. Without a script, `enforce` falls back to `warn` behaviour.

**Feature type conflict between policies at the same level**

When two policies at the same hierarchy level both define the same feature type, the one with the lower **Priority** number wins (priority `1` beats priority `2`). If the assignments tie on every ranking key, the one created first wins. Before v0.122.1 an exact tie had no defined winner, so a device decided by one may change once after upgrading. Assign distinct priorities to make the choice explicit.

title: Recurring Contracts
description: Managed-services agreements that generate invoices automatically on a schedule, with live per-device and per-seat counts for accurate recurring revenue.

sections.text:
Recurring Contracts automate your managed-services billing. Define what a customer is charged and how often, and Breeze generates the invoices on schedule -- resolving per-device and per-seat counts at billing time so the amount always reflects the customer's actual environment. Open **Contracts** from the sidebar.

Contracts are **partner-scoped** and bound to a customer organization.

Contracts, along with the rest of the Billing section, are only available when the **Service Management** module is enabled for your account; see [Service Management mode](/reference/partner-management/#service-management-mode).

sections.heading: How a Contract Bills
sections.text:
Two settings determine the rhythm:

- **Billing timing** -- *in advance* (bill at the start of each period) or *in arrears* (bill at the end).
- **Interval** -- monthly, quarterly, annually, or a custom number of months.

From these, Breeze computes the **next billing date**. When that date arrives, a billing period is created, line quantities are resolved, and -- if **auto-issue** is on -- an invoice is generated automatically.

sections.heading: Contract Statuses
sections.text:
| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| Draft | Being set up; not yet billing |
| Active | Billing on schedule |
| Paused | Billing temporarily stopped |
| Cancelled | Ended |
| Expired | Past its end date |

sections.heading: Contract Lines
sections.text:
Each line is one charge on the contract. Lines can resolve their quantity in different ways:

| Line type | How quantity is determined |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| Flat | A fixed amount each period, regardless of count |
| Per device | Counts the customer's devices at billing time × unit price |
| Per device role | Counts the customer's devices whose role is in the line's set (for example switch + router + firewall, or workstation + server) at billing time × unit price |
| Per device group | Counts the members of one device group at billing time × unit price. Static groups bill their current members; dynamic groups are evaluated from their filter when the estimate or invoice is computed |
| Per seat | Counts the customer's seats/users at billing time × unit price |
| Block hours | A prepaid bank of support hours for each billing period at a flat price. Technician time draws it down; hours beyond it bill at an overage rate. See [Block hours](#block-hours) |
| Manual | A fixed quantity you set × unit price |

Per-device and per-device-role lines can be scoped to a specific **site** so you bill only the devices at that location. A per-device-group line is not site-scoped: make the group itself site-bound instead. Per-seat lines always bill the organization's whole active-user count and cannot be site-scoped. A line can link to a [catalog item](/features/product-catalog/), which prefills its description and price.

**Editing a line.** On a draft or active contract you can edit a line in place -- its description, price, tax flag, quantity, site, device roles, device group and catalog link -- from the contract editor. The line keeps its identity, so invoices already generated from it stay linked to it and any allowance you set later is preserved. **The line type cannot be changed**: remove the line and add a new one instead. A catalog-linked line keeps the price it was given when it was added; use **Refresh price from catalog** to re-price it. Clearing a catalog link asks you for a unit price, because nothing re-prices the line afterwards. Edits apply from the next billing period onward; invoices that have already been generated are never rewritten. Adding, changing, or removing a line is recorded in the [Audit Trail](/reference/audit-logs/) against the contract — the entry names which fields changed, and the old and new unit price when the price moved. There is no per-line history on the contract page itself.

sections.heading: Included quantity and overage
sections.text:
Any line that counts something — per device, per device role, per device group or per seat — can carry an **included quantity**: "up to 25 devices included". With an included quantity set, the line bills that quantity **every period, even when fewer are counted** — it is a fixed inclusion, not a cap on a variable count. Anything above it is handled one of two ways:

- **Bill extras.** A second, customer-visible line is added to the invoice for the units above the included quantity, at the overage price you set, directly under the line it belongs to. It is an ordinary line: it follows the base line's tax treatment, it counts toward margin, and you can edit or remove it on a draft invoice.
- **Flag extras for review.** Nothing extra is invoiced. The excess is reported on the contract estimate, on the result of a manual **Generate now**, and in the nightly billing log, so somebody can decide whether to raise the included quantity or add a line.

The overage price must be valid in the contract's currency (a yen contract cannot have a ¥12.50 rate), and an overage price of zero is allowed — the extras are itemised on the customer's invoice at no charge. An included quantity must be a whole number greater than zero (a Block hours line takes fractional hours), and cannot go on a flat or manual line. While any line carries an overage price, the contract's currency cannot be restamped: clear the allowance (or the lines) first, because an overage price you typed by hand cannot be re-derived from a price book.

Dynamic groups on a contract are evaluated live when the estimate or invoice is computed, not from the member list cached on the Device Groups page, so a device that changed since the group was last refreshed is still billed correctly. The one exception is a filter condition that tests membership in *another* group, which reads that group's cached list. A group billed by a draft, active or paused contract cannot be deleted until the line is removed; a group deleted after a contract ended stays on that contract's lines by name.

Device roles come from the agent's automatic classification, a network discovery scan, or a manual override on the device. A device whose role is still **Unknown** is never billed by a per-device-role line, though a per-device or per-device-group line bills it like any other machine. The contract's estimate and each generated invoice report how many devices on the organization are not billed by any line, broken down by role -- and each role in that breakdown is a **link** to the devices list, already filtered to that role in that customer's organization, so you can classify them or add a line before the next period. The link carries the organization, so opening it in a new tab switches your org scope to the contract's customer.

Coverage is worked out **live** every time you look at it -- nothing is stored -- and only **active** contracts count. A device covered by a draft contract still reads "no active contract line bills this device" on its own page until the contract is activated, even though the draft contract's own estimate counts it: the two answer different questions.

sections.heading: Creating a Contract
sections.text:
A contract is priced in the customer organization's billing currency, which the organization inherits from your partner currency when it is created. Every line must be in that currency, and the invoices the contract generates inherit it.

1. Go to **Contracts** and click **New contract**.
2. Select the customer organization, name the contract, and set the billing timing, interval, and start date.
3. Add lines -- choose flat, per device, per device role, per device group, per seat, or manual, and set the price (and quantity, roles or group where applicable). Link a catalog item to prefill description and price. You can edit any line later from the same screen while the contract is a draft or active.
4. Add any **terms** and notes.
5. Review the **estimated value this period** -- per-device, per-device-role and per-seat lines resolve to live counts so the estimate is real, not a placeholder, and any devices no line bills are called out.
6. **Activate** the contract to start billing.

The contract list shows an **estimated monthly recurring** strip across active contracts (normalized for cadence) and a per-contract **estimate** column, so you can see recurring value at a glance.

sections.heading: From an Accepted Quote
sections.text:
When a customer accepts a quote or proposal that includes recurring (monthly or annual) line items, Breeze automatically creates a **draft contract** from those recurring lines — so an accepted proposal turns straight into the agreement that bills it, with no re-keying.

- Monthly and annual lines are split into **separate draft contracts** (one billing cadence each).
- The draft inherits the quote's terms, currency, and the prices the customer agreed to.
- It lands as a **draft** for you to review, adjust lines, and **activate** when you're ready to start billing.

A recurring quote line that bills a device set becomes a contract line of the matching type (per device, per device role, per device group or per seat) instead of a fixed-quantity line, with the accepted unit price frozen, so the contract bills the actual count every period.

Any one-time charges on the same quote become an invoice instead, not a contract.

sections.heading: If a site is deleted
sections.text:
A contract line scoped to a site records the site's name as well as its id. If that site is deleted, the line **stops billing and says so**. The contract detail shows "site deleted," and generating an invoice refuses instead of quietly falling back to billing every device in the organization. Nothing is written — the whole generation run stops, so you never get a partial invoice. Re-scope the line to another site, or remove it, and generation resumes.

The refusal currently surfaces as the raw message from the server, naming the internal line id and the deleted site — technical-looking, but it tells you exactly which line to fix.

A line whose site was deleted *before* this behavior shipped cannot be recovered because its site name was never recorded. It stays organization-wide until a technician re-scopes it.

sections.heading: Block hours
sections.text:
A **Block hours** line sells a prepaid bank of support hours for each billing period -- for example "10 hours a month for a flat price". Your technicians' time draws the bank down, and hours beyond it bill at an overage rate you set on the line.

| Setting | Meaning |
|---------|---------|
| Included hours | Hours in the block each period. Fractions are allowed (for example 7.5) |
| Overage rate | Price per hour beyond the block, in the contract's currency. Required, and overage is always billed on an invoice |
| Rollover | **None**: unused hours expire when the period ends. **Carry forward**: unused hours join the next period, optionally capped at a number of hours |
| Alert at | Optional percentage (1 to 100). Your team is notified once when the open period's usage reaches it |

A customer can have **one live block at a time**, across all of their contracts, drafts included. To draft next term's contract with a block, retire the current block first.

**What draws the block down.** Billable time entries for the customer that have ended inside the period and have not been billed yet. Approval is not required, so unapproved time draws down too (the contract page shows how much of the used hours is still unapproved). Each entry's hours are rounded to two decimals and then added, so three 20-minute entries count as 0.99 hours. Non-billable and no-charge time never draws down, and time with no hourly rate still does, because the unit is hours. Time already marked as included by its work type does not draw the block down. Time stamped in a different currency than the contract still draws hours -- no money is converted -- and is flagged on the contract page.

**When a period closes.** After a period has ended, the next invoice run closes it: the entries it drew are marked as covered by the contract, the period's figures are frozen, and any overage is added to the invoice as a line that names the period, for example "Support hours -- hours over block, 2026-08-01 -- 2026-09-01". A closed period is never recalculated. Once an entry has been drawn by a block it can no longer be edited or deleted.

**Advance billing runs one period behind.** On a contract billed in advance, the block fee is invoiced at the start of the period, but that period's overage lands on the *following* invoice, because the hours had not been worked when the first invoice was cut. On a contract billed in arrears the fee and the overage appear together on the same invoice.

**Rollover.** Unused hours (the period's included hours plus anything carried in, minus the hours used) carry forward under **Carry forward**, up to the cap if you set one. Carried hours do not expire separately, and the first period of a block carries nothing in.

**Held entries on ad-hoc invoices.** While a period is open, the time it will draw is reserved for the block. A hand-built invoice or a ticket invoice leaves those entries out and reports how many hours were held, so the customer is not charged ad hoc for hours the block already covers.

**Entries made after a period closed.** A closed period never reopens. Time that was entered for work done in a period that has already closed is not drawn from the block; it bills ad hoc as usual, and the contract page shows how many hours were entered after close.

**Retire or delete.** Removing a block line that has closed periods (or a claimed period) *retires* it instead of deleting it: it stops billing its fee, keeps its history, and any period it had already billed still closes. A block that never billed anything is simply deleted. Cancelling or expiring a contract retires its block. When a contract ends, the final period is closed by a daily sweep and any overage is put on a **draft** invoice that is never issued automatically, so someone reviews it first.

**Moving time between customers.** Moving a ticket or a device to another organization is refused (`HOUR_BLOCK_DRAWN_TIME`) while it holds time a block has already drawn. The message names how many entries are affected.

**Alerts.** With **Alert at** set, your team gets an in-app notification (event `contract.hour_block_threshold`) the first time the open period's usage reaches the percentage -- once per period and threshold, however many times the daily check runs. Recipients are the users who can read contracts and have access to the customer, or the contract's creator if none do. Changing the percentage mid-period can notify once more for the new level.

**Customer visibility.** The customer can see their balance in the portal. See [Support hours](/features/portal/#support-hours-block-hours).

sections.heading: Managing the Lifecycle
sections.text:
| Action | Effect |
|--------|--------|
| Activate | Move a draft to active and set the next billing date |
| Pause | Temporarily stop generating invoices |
| Resume | Continue billing from a paused state |
| Cancel | End the contract |

You can also **generate now** to create the current period's invoice immediately rather than waiting for the schedule.

  When auto-issue is enabled, generated invoices can be emailed to the customer automatically if a billing email is configured. Otherwise they land as drafts for you to review and send.

sections.heading: What each billing period recorded
sections.text:
Breeze records the exact devices behind every auto-counted line **at generation** and never re-derives them. Reclassifying, deleting or moving a device afterwards cannot change what a past invoice says it billed. If that invoice is voided and reissued, its recorded device evidence is copied to the replacement rather than recalculated.

Each billed period also records how many devices no line on that contract billed, **by role**, together with the flagged and billed overage totals. The contract's billing history shows this outcome for each period.

**Uncovered device identity is not stored.** A period says *how many* devices were uncovered and *by which role*, never *which ones*. To answer "Which devices are uncovered right now?", use the device **Billing** panel or the contract's coverage notice. Both check today's fleet live.

Periods billed before this feature was available have no recorded outcome and show **Not recorded**. A period on a contract with no device-counted line shows **No device lines**. That means no measurement was taken, not that zero devices were measured.

sections.heading: Auto-Renewal
sections.text:
A contract with an **end date** can be set to renew itself automatically instead of expiring. When auto-renew is on, Breeze extends the contract's term in place on its end date, before the first period of the new term is billed. Billing continues without a gap and you never have to recreate the agreement. The final period of the current term is billed as usual. The contract stays **Active** afterwards and does not expire.

To enable it, give the contract an end date, then turn on **Auto-renew at end of term** and set:

- **Renewal term (months)** — how far each renewal extends the end date (for example, 12 to renew for another year).
- **Advance notice (days)** — how many days before the end date Breeze warns you that a renewal is coming. Defaults to 30.

On the contract's detail page, the **Renewal** summary shows the current setting (the renewal term, the current end date, and the notice lead time) or that the contract does not auto-renew.

  Renewal notices go to your team (the MSP), not to the customer. As a renewal approaches, the contract's organization and partner users get an **advance notice**; once Breeze extends the term, they get a **confirmation**. To stop a renewal, turn off auto-renew before the end date. (Clearing the end date also turns auto-renew off.)

sections.heading: Bulk Actions
sections.text:
Select contracts using the checkboxes in the contract list to reveal a bulk action bar.

| Action | Permission required |
|--------|---------------------|
| **Cancel** | Contract management |
| **Delete drafts** | Contract write |

Actions run per-item in isolation, so partial success is possible.

sections.heading: Service deliverables
Defining a deliverable
sections.text:
1. Open the organization's **Service** tab and click **Add deliverable**.
2. Name it, describe it, and optionally pick the **Contract** it belongs to (or leave **Not tied to a contract**).
3. Choose a **Cadence** — Monthly, Quarterly, Every six months, Annually or One time — and the **First due date**. **Effective from / until** bound the schedule; **Lead time** controls how many days before the due date the occurrence opens, and **Grace period** how long after it a late delivery still counts before it is **Missed**.
4. Decide how an occurrence completes: **Marked delivered by a technician**, or **Delivered when the linked ticket resolves**. Turn on **Evidence required before marking delivered** if a report, screenshot or PDF must be attached first; **Attach report runs as evidence** files matching report runs automatically.
5. Optionally set an **Owner** and a **Ticket category** — the daily sweep opens a ticket for each occurrence that comes due, assigned and categorised from these — and **Show in customer portal**.

Each deliverable rolls up to a status of **On track**, **Due soon**, **Late**, **Missed** or **Inactive**. Each occurrence is **Scheduled**, **Open**, **Awaiting evidence**, **Delivered**, **Missed** or **Waived**; from an occurrence you can **Mark delivered**, **Waive**, **Reopen**, **Reschedule**, or **Add** / **Remove evidence**. Evidence is a PDF, JPEG, PNG or WebP up to 10 MB and is filed in the organization's [document library](/features/portal/#documents) as it is attached.

sections.heading: Key dates
sections.text: The **Service** tab also keeps the organization's **key dates** — insurance renewals, vendor contract ends, compliance deadlines, audits, or anything else. Give each one a label, a date, a **Remind (days before)** lead, and optionally an owner, notes, **Repeats every year** and **Show in customer portal**. When the reminder window opens, the daily sweep raises a ticket (once per date) for the owner; annual key dates roll forward to the next anniversary after they pass.

sections.heading: Template sets
sections.text:
Define a service tier once and apply it to any customer. Under **Settings → Deliverable Templates**, create a **template set** — owned by **All organizations (partner-wide)** or **This organization only** — and add the deliverables it contains. From an organization's **Service** tab, **Apply template set** creates every deliverable in the set for that organization (optionally tied to a contract, with an effective-from date and an owner) and reports what it created and what it skipped because it was already present. Managing partner-wide sets requires full partner organization access.

A template item's evidence source can also be set to one of the automated [evidence reports](/features/reports/#scheduled-auto-evidence) (identity & access review, vulnerability management, endpoint management review, threat detection review). Every organization the template applies to then gets a period-correct evidence artifact generated automatically for that deliverable, instead of a technician needing to run and attach a report by hand each period.

**Tickets only when Service Management is on:**
  The daily sweep records every occurrence and reminder regardless, but only opens tickets when the organization's Service Management is on. If an owner or ticket category can no longer be used, the ticket is opened without it rather than stalling the sweep.

sections.heading: Agreements
sections.text: The legal document a customer signs with a proposal -- your MSA or standard terms -- is an **agreement template**, and the copy they signed is a **signed agreement**. Both live in their own area now: see [Agreements](/features/agreements/). A signed agreement is filed against the contract the accepting quote created, and appears in the **Signed agreements** section of that contract.

sections.heading: Permissions
sections.text:
Contract access is governed by role permissions: viewing requires contract read access, creating and editing requires contract write access, and lifecycle actions (activate, pause, resume, cancel) require contract management access. Service deliverables ride on the same contract permissions, and attaching evidence to a deliverable additionally needs the **Documents: write** permission (`documents:write`), because evidence is filed in the organization's document library.

Agreement templates and signed agreements have their **own** permissions (`agreements:read` / `agreements:write`), documented on the [Agreements](/features/agreements/#permissions) page. Splitting them lets you grant one without the other: a technician who needs a customer's signed MSA does not need contract billing authority, and a billing clerk who runs recurring contracts does not need to author legal terms.

**Upgrading:**
  Nothing is taken away on upgrade. Any role that already held contract write access gains **Agreements: write** and **Agreements: read**; any role that held contract read access gains **Agreements: read** — including roles you created yourself. The built-in **Partner Billing** role gets both, **Partner Billing Viewer** gets read, and **Partner Admin** is unaffected (it holds everything). Review the split under **Settings → Users & Roles** if you want to tighten it.

Assign these through **Settings → Users & Roles**.

sections.text:

- [Online Payments](/features/online-payments/) -- let customers pay generated invoices online

title: Custom Fields
description: Define custom metadata fields for devices to track organisation-specific information beyond built-in attributes.
headings: Writing custom fields from a script
Filtering and columns on the device list
Filtering devices by custom field values
Values in exports and the partner API
"Provide either orgId or partnerId, not both"
Custom field values not appearing on device
Deleted a definition and the values are gone

sections.text:
Custom Fields let you attach structured metadata to devices that goes beyond the built-in attributes (hostname, OS type, tags, etc.). You define field definitions at the organisation or partner level, then set values on individual devices. This is useful for tracking asset numbers, purchase dates, warranty expiry, department assignments, compliance status, and any other data specific to your environment.

Migrating custom fields in bulk from another RMM? See [Migrating to Breeze](/migration/overview/#alongside-this-phase-backfill-custom-fields-from-the-incumbent) for the **Import from another RMM** wizard, which drives the same definitions and values endpoints this page documents.

---

sections.heading: How it works
sections.text:
Custom Fields has two layers:

1. **Field definitions** -- created via the `/api/v1/custom-fields` endpoints. A definition declares the field's name, key, data type, validation options, and which device types it applies to. Definitions are scoped to either an organisation or a partner, and a `fieldKey` is unique **per owner** -- see [Uniqueness and shadowing](#uniqueness-and-shadowing).
2. **Field values** -- stored in a dedicated `device_custom_field_values` table, one row per device/definition pair, and validated against the definition's declared type on every write. The `custom_fields` JSONB column on the device record is maintained as a trigger-rebuilt projection of that table (plus any pre-existing key that doesn't match the enforced `field_key` pattern, preserved as-is) for backward compatibility -- every existing reader of `devices.custom_fields` keeps working unchanged. Values are set by patching the device via `PATCH /api/v1/devices/:id` with a `customFields` key-value map. Values are merged with any existing custom fields on the device rather than replacing them.

---

sections.heading: Field types
sections.text:
Every field definition has a `type` that controls what values are accepted:

| Type | Description | Example value |
|---|---|---|
| `text` | Free-form string up to 10,000 characters | `"Rack A, Shelf 3"` |
| `number` | Numeric value (integer or decimal) | `42` |
| `boolean` | True or false | `true` |
| `dropdown` | One of a predefined list of choices | `"Finance"` |
| `date` | Date string | `"2026-06-15"` |

---

sections.heading: Validation options
sections.text:
When creating a field definition you can supply an `options` object to constrain accepted values:

| Option | Applies to | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `choices` | `dropdown` | Array of allowed string values. Example: `["Finance", "Engineering", "Sales"]` |
| `min` | `number` | Minimum numeric value |
| `max` | `number` | Maximum numeric value |
| `pattern` | `text` | Regular expression that text values must match |
| `placeholder` | `text`, `number`, `date` | Placeholder hint displayed in the UI |

You can also set a `defaultValue` on the definition. If a device does not have an explicit value for the field, the default is used. Setting `required: true` indicates that the field should always be populated for applicable devices.

  Every value is validated against the field's declared `type` and `options` on every write path -- `PATCH /api/v1/devices/:id`, `PATCH /api/v1/devices/:id/custom-fields`, and script write-back. See [Accepted value types](#accepted-value-types) for the rejection codes.

---

sections.heading: Uniqueness and shadowing
sections.text:
Two rules keep a `fieldKey` unambiguous, both enforced in the database and returned as `409` -- both predate this page's bulk importer and are what the importer relies on rather than re-implementing, since a mismatched key is otherwise silently ambiguous data corruption:

- **`fieldKey` is unique per owner.** Two definitions cannot share a key on the same axis (two organisation-owned fields, or two partner-wide fields). Creating a duplicate returns `409 { code: "field-key-duplicate" }`.
- **An organisation-owned key cannot shadow an all-organisations key, or vice versa.** If `asset_tag` already exists as a partner-wide field, no organisation under that partner can also define an organisation-owned `asset_tag` (and the reverse). Creating a shadowing definition returns `409 { code: "field-key-shadowed" }`.

Both rules exist because a value can only be attributed to one definition. Without them, a device could resolve two different definitions for the same key -- disagreeing on `type` -- with no way to tell which one a stored value belongs to.

---

sections.heading: Device type targeting
sections.text:
A definition can optionally include a `deviceTypes` array to limit which operating systems it applies to. Accepted values are `windows`, `macos`, and `linux`.

When `deviceTypes` is omitted or set to `null`, the field applies to all device types.

```json
{
  "name": "BitLocker Recovery Key",
  "fieldKey": "bitlocker_recovery_key",
  "type": "text",
  "deviceTypes": ["windows"]
}
```

---

sections.heading: Scoping and multi-tenancy
sections.text:
Field definitions are scoped to one of:

| Scope | Who can create | Visibility |
|---|---|---|
| **Organisation** | Organisation-scoped users or partner users with access to the organisation | Visible only within that organisation |
| **Partner** | Partner-scoped users | Visible to the partner and all organisations the partner can access |

  You must provide either `orgId` or `partnerId` when creating a field -- not both. The API returns a `400` error if both are supplied. For organisation-scoped users the `orgId` is automatically inferred from the authentication context.

sections.heading: Access rules
sections.text:
- **Organisation users** see definitions scoped to their own organisation plus any definitions scoped to their parent partner.
- **Partner users** see definitions scoped to their partner plus definitions scoped to any organisation they can access.
- **System-scoped users** see all definitions.

Editing and deleting a definition requires ownership: organisation users can only modify definitions belonging to their organisation, and partner users can only modify definitions belonging to their partner.

---

sections.heading: Creating a field definition
sections.text:
1. Choose a human-readable `name` (1--100 characters) and a machine-readable `fieldKey`. The key must start with a lowercase letter and contain only lowercase letters, digits, and underscores (regex: `^[a-z][a-z0-9_]*$`).

2. Pick a `type` from the supported list: `text`, `number`, `boolean`, `dropdown`, or `date`.

3. Optionally set `options`, `required`, `defaultValue`, and `deviceTypes`.

4. Send the request:

  **cURL:**
```bash
curl -X POST /api/v1/custom-fields \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Department",
    "fieldKey": "department",
    "type": "dropdown",
    "options": {
      "choices": ["Finance", "Engineering", "Sales", "Support"]
    },
    "required": true
  }'
```

  **Response:**
```json
{
  "data": {
    "id": "a1b2c3d4-...",
    "orgId": "org-uuid-...",
    "partnerId": null,
    "name": "Department",
    "fieldKey": "department",
    "type": "dropdown",
    "options": {
      "choices": ["Finance", "Engineering", "Sales", "Support"]
    },
    "required": true,
    "scriptWrite": false,
    "defaultValue": null,
    "deviceTypes": null,
    "createdAt": "2026-02-18T12:00:00.000Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-02-18T12:00:00.000Z"
  }
}
```

---

sections.heading: Setting values on devices
sections.text:
Values are set by sending a `PATCH` request to the device endpoint with a `customFields` object whose keys correspond to field keys. The request/response shape is unchanged from before this feature's normalized storage landed: you still read and write the same `customFields` object on the device record -- see [Database schema](#database-schema) for where it's actually stored now.

```bash
curl -X PATCH /api/v1/devices/<device-id> \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "customFields": {
      "department": "Engineering",
      "asset_number": "AST-2026-0042",
      "purchase_date": "2025-11-01"
    }
  }'
```

  Values are **merged** with existing custom fields. If a device already has `{"location": "HQ"}` and you patch with `{"department": "Engineering"}`, the result is `{"location": "HQ", "department": "Engineering"}`. To remove a field, set its value to `null`.

sections.heading: Accepted value types
sections.text:
Each value must first match the Zod wire schema (`string`, `number`, `boolean`, or `null` -- `null` removes the field), then be validated against the **target definition's own declared `type` and `options`**. A value that fails either check is rejected -- not silently stored -- with `400 { error, code: "INVALID_CUSTOM_FIELD_VALUE", fields: [{ fieldKey, reason }] }`. `reason` is one of:

| Reason | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `unknown_field` | No custom field definition visible to this device's organisation owns that key. |
| `invalid_type` | The value's shape doesn't match the field's declared `type`. |
| `out_of_range` | A `number` value falls outside the field's `min`/`max`. |
| `not_a_choice` | A `dropdown` value isn't one of the field's declared `options.choices`. |
| `too_long` | A `text` value exceeds the fixed 10,000-character limit. (`options.maxLength` on a definition is a client-side UI hint only -- it is not enforced by this check.) |
| `invalid_date` | A `date` value doesn't parse. |
| `not_applicable_to_device` | The field's `deviceTypes` excludes this device's OS. |
