title: Identity Console
description: Connect a customer's Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 tenant, view identity posture, and run AI-assisted identity actions with approval gating.

sections.text:
The Identity Console connects a customer's Google Workspace domain and Microsoft 365 tenant to Breeze so your technicians can run real helpdesk identity work -- looking up users, checking security posture, resetting passwords, suspending accounts, managing groups and licenses, and offboarding leavers -- directly from the in-app AI assistant. Connect a tenant once, and from then on a technician can describe what they need in plain language. Credentials are verified against the live provider before they are stored, encrypted at rest, and never returned to the browser. Read-only lookups run automatically; anything that changes an account is gated behind a human approval step with a mandatory reason and a full audit trail.

**Off by default:**
  The Identity Console is feature-flagged off by default. A host operator must enable `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_ENABLED` (Google Workspace) and/or `M365_ENABLED` (Microsoft 365) before the connectors appear. While a flag is off, the connector is completely dark -- its screens and AI actions are unavailable. Even with the flag on, an organization must have a verified connection before any identity action will run.

**Not the same as Cloud-to-Cloud Backup:**
  The Identity Console performs **live administration** of a customer's identity directory -- it reads posture and acts on accounts in real time. It does **not** copy or store mailbox or file data. That is a separate product, **Cloud-to-Cloud Backup**, which schedules backup and restore of the customer's Google and Microsoft 365 *data*. One feature manages accounts now; the other protects data over time.

---

sections.heading: Connecting a Tenant
sections.text:
Both connectors live in the organization's **Integrations** area as dedicated cards -- one for Google Workspace and one for Microsoft 365. Each card shows a **Connected / Not connected** status, an inline walkthrough for gathering the required credentials, the connection form, and (once connected) a read-only details summary. There is one connection per organization for each provider.

  **Google Workspace:**
    To connect a Google Workspace domain you provide:

    | Field | Description |
    |---|---|
    | **Primary domain** | The customer's domain, e.g. `example.com` |
    | **Super-admin email** | A super-admin account in the domain that the integration impersonates |
    | **Service-account key** | The full service-account JSON key, pasted into a masked field |

    The card walks you through creating a Google Cloud service account, downloading its JSON key, enabling the required Google APIs (Admin SDK, Gmail, Calendar, Enterprise License Manager), and authorizing **domain-wide delegation** with the exact OAuth scopes Breeze displays for you to copy into the Google Admin console.

    On save, Breeze makes a **live Directory API call** to confirm the key works and that domain-wide delegation is correctly authorized. The connection is only stored if that check succeeds.

    Breeze repeats that check about every six hours (v0.124.0+). If Google later rejects the service account -- domain-wide delegation revoked, the admin account removed -- a **Verification failed** incident opens in the **Connection health** panel on **Integrations**; saving the connection again clears it. A rate limit or an outage at Google does not open one. See [Connection Health Checks](/features/notifications/#connection-health-checks).

  **Microsoft 365:**
    To connect a Microsoft 365 tenant you provide:

    | Field | Description |
    |---|---|
    | **Tenant (Directory) ID** | The tenant **GUID** (the `contoso.onmicrosoft.com` form is rejected) |
    | **Application (client) ID** | The client ID of an Entra (Azure AD) app registration |
    | **Client secret** | The app's client secret, entered in a masked field |

    The card covers creating the Entra app registration, copying the tenant and client IDs, generating a client secret, and granting **admin consent** for the required Microsoft Graph permissions. It also maps which permissions back which capabilities -- reads need directory and audit-log read scopes, while disabling a user or resetting a password additionally require user read/write and the **User Administrator** role.

    On save, Breeze acquires a token and makes a **live Microsoft Graph call** to confirm the credentials and admin consent are in place before storing anything.

    This is the direct, single-tenant client-secret method. Breeze also supports two separate delegated-consent connection profiles -- **Customer Graph Read** (read-only) and **Customer Graph Actions** (adds write permissions) -- that avoid managing a client secret yourself; see [Cloud Tenant Integrations](/features/identity-integrations/) for that flow. If both a direct connection and a delegated profile exist for the same tenant, the direct connection takes precedence.

  Connecting or disconnecting a tenant requires MFA and an organization-write permission, and every connect or disconnect is written to the audit log. Stored secrets are encrypted at rest and never returned -- when you re-save a connection, the secret field shows a "stored, encrypted -- leave blank to keep" placeholder.

---

sections.heading: Viewing Identity Posture
sections.text: Once a tenant is connected, technicians can ask the AI assistant to read identity data. These lookups are read-only and run automatically.

sections.heading: Google Workspace
sections.text:
| View | What you see |
|---|---|
| **User lookup** | Full name, suspended status, super-admin flag, 2-step-verification enrollment, last login, org-unit path, aliases |
| **Group membership** | Every group a user belongs to |
| **License assignments** | Who holds a given product or SKU |
| **Security drift report** | A domain-wide posture scan that buckets users into: no 2-step verification, super-admins, suspended, never logged in, and stale (no login past a threshold, default 90 days) |

The security drift report can be viewed in the chat or emailed. Emailed reports are locked to the connection's own admin address so directory data cannot be sent elsewhere.

sections.heading: Microsoft 365
sections.text:
| View | What you see |
|---|---|
| **User lookup** | The user's profile |
| **Recent sign-in activity** | A user's recent sign-ins |
| **Group memberships** | The groups a user belongs to in the tenant |

---

sections.heading: AI-Assisted Identity Actions
sections.text:
Every identity action carries one of two tiers:

| Tier | Behavior |
|---|---|
| **Read** | Runs automatically -- lookups and reports that do not change anything |
| **Mutating** | Requires a human approval step plus a mandatory reason, and is recorded in the audit log |

  Mutating actions will not run without a reason, and every one flows through Breeze's AI approval gate. They are never executed silently.

sections.heading: Google Workspace actions
sections.text:
**Read (automatic):** user lookup, list a user's groups, list license assignments, security-drift scan, email the drift report.

**Mutating (approval + reason required):**

- Reset password (temporary password, force-change at next sign-in)
- Suspend or restore (un-suspend) a user
- Sign a user out of all sessions
- Set or disable mail forwarding; set an out-of-office responder
- Update a user (name, recovery email/phone, aliases); rename a user (change primary email)
- Add to or remove from a group
- Move a user to a different org unit
- Reset (turn off) 2-step verification for a user who lost their second factor
- Add or remove a mailbox delegate
- Assign or remove a license
- Share a calendar
- **Guided offboarding** -- a best-effort sequence over a departing user: set out-of-office and forwarding, revoke third-party OAuth grants, remove from all groups, perform a BYOD-safe wipe of corporate mobile data only, sign out of all sessions, then suspend. Each step reports success or failure, and a partial failure is surfaced as a failure
- **Stolen-device remote wipe** -- a full factory reset of a user's enrolled mobile devices, kept separate from offboarding and intended for lost or stolen hardware only

sections.heading: Microsoft 365 actions
sections.text:
**Read (automatic):** user lookup, recent sign-in activity, group memberships.

**Mutating (approval + reason required):**

- Disable a user (block sign-in)
- Reset a password (temporary password, force-change at next sign-in)
- Revoke all sign-in sessions and refresh tokens
- Assign or remove a licence (assigning fails closed when no seat is free)
- Add to or remove from a group
- Retire an Intune-managed device (removes company data and unenrols it; not a full wipe)
- Create a user (temporary password, force-change at next sign-in)
- Set, schedule or disable a mailbox automatic reply (out of office)

The eight actions beyond disable and reset arrived in v0.124.0 and are **four-eyes** actions: a second approver decides them every time, never the requester. A tenant whose Admin actions were granted on an earlier release must re-consent once to the current permission set; until then those eight are refused with a "consent upgrade required" error while disable and reset keep working. See [Cloud Tenant Integrations](/features/identity-integrations/).

**Reset and disable need a verified caller:**
  From v0.124.0 a password reset or account disable is pinned to one Entra account and runs only against a fresh [caller verification](/security/caller-verification/) of that account -- a verification link by SMS or email, a callback attestation, or an administrative disable with an MFA step-up. Without one the action is refused with "caller verification required" in chat, over MCP, and again when an approved request is released. Approved resets or disables created before upgrading to v0.124.0 are not pinned to a target and fail at release; recreate them.

sections.heading: Retrieving a Microsoft 365 reset password
sections.text:
When an approved Microsoft 365 password reset runs through the durable approval path (for example, it was approved after your chat session ended), the temporary password is stored encrypted and surfaced as a **one-time reveal**:

- Open **Security → AI Risk → Approval History** and find the executed reset. A **Reveal temporary password** button appears on it.
- Normally, only the technician who **requested** the reset can reveal it. If the reset was raised without a specific requesting user (for example, by an API key or MCP client), any user who can approve requests for that organization may reveal it instead. Either way it can be revealed **exactly once** -- copy it when it is shown, because it will not be shown again.
- An un-revealed password expires after **7 days** and is then permanently discarded.

The reset always sets **force-change at next sign-in**, so the temporary credential is only good for one first login.

  Self-hosted operators: the one-time reveal requires `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY_ID` to be configured on the API. Without it, the reset itself still succeeds but the temporary password is deliberately discarded rather than stored, and the reveal reports it as unavailable. See [Environment Variables](/deploy/environment/).

---

sections.heading: Fix with AI
sections.text:
**Fix with AI** opens the AI assistant bound to a specific device: it sets that device as the session context, starts a fresh chat, and creates a device-scoped session for the technician to type an instruction into. It is the bridge between the Identity Console and on-device remediation -- you start an AI session already pointed at the device in question. Site-level access scoping is respected, so a site-restricted technician cannot bind to a device outside their site.

  Fix with AI is being introduced as the device-task dispatch foundation. The session-binding behavior is in place; expect it to surface more prominently in the device experience in a later release.

---

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
**The Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 card does not appear.**
The connector is feature-flagged off by default. Ask your host operator to enable `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_ENABLED` or `M365_ENABLED`. While the flag is off, the connector and its AI actions are unavailable.

**The connection fails to save with a credentials error.**
Both providers verify credentials live before storing them. For Google Workspace, confirm the service-account key is valid and that domain-wide delegation has been authorized with the exact scopes shown on the card. For Microsoft 365, confirm the tenant ID is the GUID (not the `.onmicrosoft.com` form), the client secret has not expired, and admin consent has been granted for the required Graph permissions.

**A mutating action will not run.**
Mutating actions require a reason and a human approval step. Supply a reason and approve the action when prompted. Confirm the connected service account or app registration has the write permissions and admin role required for that action.

**I connected a tenant but identity actions still do not work.**
A verified connection is required in addition to the feature flag being on. Re-open the connector card and confirm it shows **Connected**. If it shows **Not connected**, re-enter and save the credentials.

**Is mailbox or file data backed up by this feature?**
No. The Identity Console only administers accounts in real time. To back up and restore Google or Microsoft 365 data, use the separate Cloud-to-Cloud Backup feature.

title: Cloud Tenant Integrations — Google Workspace & Microsoft 365
description: Connect Google Workspace and Microsoft 365 (Entra) tenants on the Integrations → Cloud tenants tab so Breeze and its AI assistant can administer users and groups.

sections.text:
The **Cloud tenants** tab of the Breeze Integrations page (formerly **Identity**) is where you connect a customer's Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 tenant to Breeze. It has two sub-tabs — **Google Workspace** and **Microsoft 365**. Microsoft 365 offers two connection methods: **consent-based** (Read access, plus optional Admin actions) uses customer-administrator consent without asking you for a reusable secret, while **Legacy direct** accepts a tenant-specific app client secret for existing read and action workflows.

Open it at **Integrations → Cloud tenants** (`/integrations#cloud-tenants`; the old `/integrations#identity` link still works). The two sub-tabs deep-link to `/integrations#google` (Google Workspace) and `/integrations#m365` (Microsoft 365).

**This page is about *connecting* a tenant:**
  This page documents the connection step only — the credential fields and the connect/verify/disconnect flow. For what you can *do* once a tenant is connected (viewing identity posture, the full list of read and mutating AI actions, guided offboarding, and the approval gate), see the [Identity Console](/features/identity-console/). This page and the Identity Console describe the same two connectors from two angles: setup here, day-to-day use there.

**Off by default:**
  Both provider sub-tabs are feature-flagged off by default. A host operator must enable `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_ENABLED` (Google Workspace) and/or `M365_ENABLED` (Microsoft 365). Consent-based Microsoft 365 connections have an additional organization allowlist; if they are not enabled for your organization and nothing is connected yet, the sub-tab shows the legacy direct card followed by a single line: "Consent-based connection isn't available on this Breeze instance yet." Host operators self-hosting Breeze: the environment variables that turn Customer Graph Read on are documented under [Customer Microsoft 365 Graph-read consent](/deploy/environment/#customer-microsoft-365-graph-read-consent-optional).

---

sections.heading: Connecting a tenant
sections.text:
There is one Google Workspace connection per organization. Microsoft 365 can have one Customer Graph Read connection and one separate legacy direct connection per organization. Connecting, re-consenting, retesting, or disconnecting requires organization write permission and current MFA where shown.

  **Google Workspace:**

Google Workspace lives on the sub-tab at `/integrations#google`. Breeze authenticates as a Google Cloud **service account** that uses **domain-wide delegation** to impersonate a super-admin in the customer's domain.

sections.heading: Credentials required
sections.text:
| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Primary domain** | The customer's domain, e.g. `example.com` |
| **Super-admin email (impersonated)** | A super-admin account in the domain that the service account impersonates |
| **Service-account JSON key** | The full service-account JSON key file, pasted into a masked field |

sections.heading: Connect
sections.text:
1. Set your scope to the customer organization, then open **Integrations → Cloud tenants → Google Workspace**.
2. In the **Google Cloud Console**, open **IAM & Admin → Service Accounts** and create (or pick) a service account.
3. On that service account, open the **Keys** tab and choose **Add key → Create new key → JSON**. The JSON downloads once — that file is what you paste into Breeze. Note the service account's numeric **Client ID** (its unique ID); you will need it in the next step.
4. Enable the APIs the identity tools use: **Admin SDK**, **Gmail**, **Calendar**, and **Enterprise License Manager**.
5. In the **Google Admin Console**, go to **Security → Access and data control → API controls → Manage domain-wide delegation**. Add the service account's **Client ID** and authorize the exact OAuth scopes Breeze shows in the walkthrough (copy them straight from the card).
6. Back in Breeze, enter the **Primary domain**, the **Super-admin email** to impersonate, and paste the **service-account JSON key**.
7. Click **Save & Verify**. Breeze makes a live Directory API call to confirm the key works and that domain-wide delegation is correctly authorized, then stores the connection.

sections.heading: Domain-wide delegation scopes
sections.text:
The walkthrough card displays the exact comma-separated OAuth scope list to authorize. It covers directory user/group read and write, user security, aliases, mobile-device actions, Gmail settings (basic and sharing), Calendar ACLs, and Apps licensing — the scopes the Google identity tools actually call. Authorize the full list so every supported action works.

  **Microsoft 365:**

Microsoft 365 lives on the sub-tab at `/integrations#m365`. What you see depends on what this Breeze instance offers:

- **Consent available:** a **tenant panel** leads the sub-tab. Its header shows the connected tenant (name, tenant ID with a copy button, last verified) or "No Microsoft 365 tenant connected to *organization*". Below it are two steps: **Step 1 · Read access** and **Step 2 · Admin actions**. The legacy direct method sits under **Advanced: use your own app registration (legacy)** at the bottom.
- **Consent not available:** the legacy direct card is the main card, followed by a one-line note that consent-based connection isn't available on this instance.
- **Legacy connection already exists:** the legacy card is always shown expanded with a **Legacy** badge. When a legacy direct connection and a consent connection exist for the same tenant, the legacy direct connection takes precedence.

The two steps are independent consents; connecting or disconnecting one does not change the other. Read access is recommended first because AI lookups and reports depend on it.

sections.heading: Step 1 · Read access (Customer Graph Read)
sections.text:
Customer Graph Read uses Breeze's dedicated multitenant, certificate-backed application. You do not enter a tenant ID, client ID, client secret, certificate, scope, or vault location. A customer **Global Administrator** or **Privileged Role Administrator** reviews Microsoft's permission screen and grants consent.

1. Set your Breeze scope to the customer organization and find **Step 1 · Read access** in the tenant panel.
2. Review what it enables (open **Show Microsoft permissions** to see the thirteen required permissions), then choose **Connect tenant**.
3. Complete Breeze MFA and sign in to Microsoft as a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator **of the customer's tenant**. Breeze verifies who you are and which tenant your account belongs to before anything is consented. An account without either role stops here.
   The first Microsoft sign-in shows a **user-level consent screen** for Breeze's application ("View your basic profile", "Maintain access to data you have given it access to", and, for administrators, an optional **Consent on behalf of your organization** checkbox). This only lets Breeze read who you are; it grants no tenant data access. Accept it, or tick the checkbox to stop other users in the tenant from seeing it. If the tenant has user consent disabled, Microsoft shows an *Approval required* / *Need admin approval* message instead (AADSTS90094 or AADSTS65001): a Global Administrator must complete this sign-in themselves, and can tick **Consent on behalf of your organization** to clear it for everyone.
4. Breeze shows the tenant you signed in to (tenant ID and username) and asks you to confirm it. If it is your own MSP tenant rather than the customer's, choose **Cancel, wrong tenant** and sign in again with the customer's admin account. Otherwise choose **Continue to Microsoft consent**.
5. Review Microsoft's consent screen carefully and accept only if it shows the expected application and exact permissions below. The screen is for the tenant you just confirmed and no other.
6. Breeze verifies its own access to that tenant (application token, organization probe, exact grants) and only then connects the tenant to the organization.
7. Confirm Read access shows **Active**, the tenant panel header shows the expected tenant, the manifest is version 3, and there are no missing or unexpected permissions.

**Guest accounts sign in to their own tenant:**
Microsoft signs an account in to the tenant it belongs to. If you are a guest administrator in the customer's tenant, signing in with that account verifies **your** home tenant, and the confirm step shows that tenant. Cancel and use an account that belongs to the customer's tenant.

Reconnecting a tenant that is still connected, or approving new permissions, signs in at that tenant directly and skips the confirm step: the tenant is already known. Signing in there with another tenant's administrator stops with a tenant-mismatch message before any consent screen.

If the customer's Conditional Access policy interrupts the sign-in (for example a device check), the card says so instead of reporting a generic failure. Try again from a browser the tenant trusts, or ask the customer's administrator.

Customer Graph Read requests exactly these Microsoft Graph **application** permissions:

| Permission | Why it is requested |
|---|---|
| `Application.Read.All` | Read the dedicated application's authoritative app-role assignments for drift detection |
| `AuditLog.Read.All` | Read audit and sign-in inventory |
| `Device.Read.All` | Read Entra device inventory |
| `DeviceManagementConfiguration.Read.All` | Read Intune configuration inventory |
| `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.Read.All` | Read Intune managed-device inventory |
| `Group.Read.All` | Read groups and memberships |
| `Organization.Read.All` | Verify and read the customer organization |
| `Sites.Read.All` | Read SharePoint site inventory |
| `User.Read.All` | Read users and directory profiles |
| `AuditLogsQuery.Read.All` | Run unified audit log queries on request |
| `Policy.Read.All` | Read Conditional Access policies and named locations |
| `RoleManagement.Read.Directory` | Read directory role assignments to identify administrators |
| `SecurityEvents.Read.All` | Read Microsoft Secure Score and its control profiles |

The card shows required, observed, missing, and unexpected grants. **Active** requires exact equality. If Microsoft cannot complete authoritative reconciliation—for example, because `Application.Read.All` was removed—the card becomes **Degraded** and labels the retained observed list **Last-known**, rather than presenting it as current.

Use **Retest** to check an already-bound tenant. Use **Re-consent** when permissions were changed or the manifest is stale. Customer Graph Read is read-only and does not authorize password resets, user disablement, other Graph mutations, Exchange PowerShell, or delegated mail/Teams access.

#### Tenant sync and "as of" semantics

Once a tenant is connected, Breeze keeps a scheduled snapshot of it rather than
querying Microsoft on every page load. Six domains sync independently:

| Domain | Default cadence | What it stores |
|---|---|---|
| Users | 6 hours | Directory profile, licenses, MFA registration state, admin roles |
| Intune devices | 6 hours | Managed devices, compliance state, and the link to the Breeze device |
| Conditional Access | 24 hours | Policy definitions and enabled / report-only / disabled state |
| Licenses | 24 hours | Purchased and consumed seats per SKU |
| Secure Score | 24 hours | Daily score and per-control detail, backfilled 90 days on first sync |
| Sign-in activity | 24 hours | Last **successful** interactive sign-in per user |

Every figure Breeze shows carries an **as of** time — the last run that
completed a full enumeration of that domain, not the last time anything was
written. A domain that returned only part of the tenant (a very large tenant,
or Microsoft throttling mid-pull) is labelled **partial** and never causes a
user or device to be marked as gone. A domain whose permission has not been
approved yet is labelled **needs consent** and is simply not scheduled; the
other five keep running.

Cadences adapt on their own: a domain that truncates or runs slowly backs off,
a domain that has been quiet drifts back toward its default. You can force a
refresh from the card at most once every 15 minutes per organization.

**Sign-in activity requires Microsoft Entra ID P1 or higher.** On a tenant
without it, Breeze shows "Sign-in activity needs Entra ID P1" rather than an
empty or zero value — the data does not exist to be read. Sign-in activity is
also the one domain Microsoft rate-limits per application rather than per
tenant, so on large fleets it refreshes less often than the others and its
"as of" date is the honest answer to how current it is.

Disconnecting a tenant deletes the stored users, devices, policies and license
rows immediately. Secure Score history and the daily posture rollups are kept
and stay stamped with the tenant they came from, so reconnecting a different
tenant never mixes the two.

Breeze stores no sign-in logs, no IP addresses, and no audit-log rows. User
records are customer data of the customer's own tenant: they are included in an
organization export, erased with the organization, deleted on disconnect, and
purged 30 days after a user disappears from the tenant.

sections.heading: Step 2 · Admin actions (Customer Graph Actions)
sections.text:
Admin actions uses a separate Breeze application with write permissions so the AI assistant can run account actions -- reset a password, disable sign-in, revoke sessions, assign or remove a licence, add to or remove from a group, retire an Intune device, create a user, and set a mailbox auto-reply -- always behind the approval step described under [After connecting](#after-connecting). From v0.124.0 the permission set is seven Microsoft Graph application permissions: `User.ReadWrite.All`, `User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All`, `User.RevokeSessions.All`, `GroupMember.ReadWrite.All` (membership only -- Breeze cannot create, delete or edit a group), `DeviceManagementManagedDevices.PrivilegedOperations.All` (used to retire a device only; there is no wipe path), `MailboxSettings.ReadWrite`, and `Organization.Read.All` (the licence seat check before an assignment). It can be granted at any time, but AI lookups and reports need Read access, so connect Step 1 first.

1. In the tenant panel, choose **Grant admin actions…**. Nothing is sent to Microsoft yet.
2. Read the pre-flight panel: what Breeze will be able to do, who must sign in (a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator for the customer tenant), and how to revoke it later.
3. Choose **Continue to Microsoft** (or **Cancel** / Esc to back out), complete Breeze MFA, and sign in as an administrator of the customer's tenant.
4. Confirm the tenant Breeze shows is the customer's (the same confirm step as Read access), then grant consent on Microsoft's screen.
5. Confirm Admin actions shows **Active** for the same tenant.

**Tenants that granted Admin actions before v0.124.0:**
  An earlier grant covers password reset and disable only. Those two keep working, but the actions added in v0.124.0 are refused with a "consent upgrade required" error until the tenant re-consents once to the current permission set -- choose **Grant admin actions…** again from the tenant panel and walk the same steps. A consent that was started on v0.121.x or earlier and never completed now answers "The consent session could not be verified. Start consent again."; start it over.

sections.heading: Legacy direct (existing client-secret method)
sections.text:
When consent-based connection is available, this method is under **Advanced: use your own app registration (legacy)** at the bottom of the sub-tab. Disconnecting it asks for confirmation.

Legacy direct uses a customer-specific **Entra app registration** and the client-credentials flow. You create the app in the customer's tenant, grant its permissions, and give Breeze the tenant ID, client ID, and client secret. This method remains available for existing identity read and action workflows.

#### Credentials required

| Field | Description |
|---|---|
| **Tenant ID** | The tenant's Directory (tenant) ID — a GUID. The `contoso.onmicrosoft.com` domain form is rejected; use the GUID from the Entra app registration's Overview page |
| **App (client) ID** | The Application (client) ID of the Entra app registration |
| **Client secret** | The app's client secret value (not the secret ID), entered in a masked field |

#### Connect legacy direct

1. Set your scope to the customer organization, then open **Integrations → Cloud tenants → Microsoft 365**.
2. In the **Microsoft Entra admin center** (entra.microsoft.com) or the Azure portal, open **Microsoft Entra ID → App registrations** and pick an existing app or click **New registration**. Give it a name and choose "Accounts in this organizational directory only."
   After you click **Register**, find the app under **All applications**. The **Owned applications** list can lag by several minutes; if the app is not there yet, wait. Do not register a second time, or you will end up with duplicate registrations.
3. On the app's **Overview** page, copy the **Directory (tenant) ID** and the **Application (client) ID** into the Breeze fields.
4. Go to **Certificates & secrets → Client secrets → New client secret**. Set a description and expiry (24 months max), then copy the secret **Value** immediately — not the secret ID; it is shown only once.
5. Under **API permissions**, add the Microsoft Graph **application** permissions listed below, then click **Grant admin consent**.
6. Back in Breeze, enter the **Tenant ID**, **App (client) ID**, and the **client secret**.
7. Click **Save & Verify**. Breeze acquires a token and makes a live Microsoft Graph call to confirm the credentials and admin consent are in place, then stores the connection.

#### Legacy direct Microsoft Graph permissions

The connection card spells out which permissions back which capabilities:

| Capability | Graph application permissions |
|---|---|
| **Reads** (user lookup, group memberships, sign-in activity) | `User.Read.All`, `Group.Read.All`, `AuditLog.Read.All` |
| **Disable user / reset password** | additionally `User.ReadWrite.All` + `User-PasswordProfile.ReadWrite.All`, plus the **User Administrator** Entra role |

Grant admin consent for these in the app registration before saving, or the live verification (and later actions) will fail.

  Google Workspace and legacy direct secrets are encrypted at rest and never returned to the browser. Customer Graph Read never asks the browser for a reusable Microsoft credential: its certificate is confined to a private executor and only safe connection health is returned.

---

sections.heading: Remove Customer Graph Read consent
sections.text:
**Disconnect from Breeze** immediately revokes Breeze's local connection, clears its executable tenant/grant state, and rejects delayed callbacks. It does **not** delete the Microsoft Enterprise application or remove tenant-wide admin consent.

To remove Microsoft consent separately, a customer Entra administrator must:

1. First choose **Disconnect from Breeze** in **Step 1 · Read access** and confirm it shows **Revoked**.
2. Open the Microsoft Entra admin center for the verified customer tenant.
3. Go to **Identity → Applications → Enterprise applications**, find the dedicated Breeze Customer Graph Read application by its verified name and application ID, and open it. Do not modify an unrelated app registration.
4. Use the Enterprise application's delete/remove option to remove that tenant's service principal and tenant-wide application consent. Microsoft labels can vary by portal version; verify the tenant and application before confirming.
5. Confirm the Enterprise application is no longer present. If Breeze had not already been disconnected, a subsequent **Retest** would report an application verification failure; local status alone is not proof that Microsoft consent was removed.

Removing an individual permission is different from removing tenant-wide consent. In particular, removing only `Application.Read.All` prevents Breeze from authoritatively reading the current assignment set, so the card reports reconciliation unavailable and retains the prior list as last known.

---

sections.heading: After connecting
sections.text:
Once a sub-tab shows **Connected**, technicians work with the directory through the in-app AI assistant rather than through this Integrations page. Read-only lookups (user details, group memberships, security posture, Microsoft 365 sign-in activity) run automatically; anything that changes an account is gated behind a human approval step with a mandatory reason and a full audit trail. The two providers are **not** at parity — Google Workspace exposes a much broader mutating action set than Microsoft 365.

For the complete list of what you can view and do — including guided offboarding, the security-drift report, and the read-vs-mutating tiers — see the [Identity Console](/features/identity-console/).

---

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
**The Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 sub-tab shows "not enabled on this instance."**
The connector is feature-flagged off. Ask your host operator to enable `GOOGLE_WORKSPACE_ENABLED` or `M365_ENABLED` on the API server, then reload the page.

**The Microsoft 365 sub-tab says "Consent-based connection isn't available on this Breeze instance yet."**
Consent-based onboarding is turned off on this Breeze instance, or your organization is not on its allowlist. It is not something you can change from the organization. Self-hosting operators enable it with the variables under [Customer Microsoft 365 Graph-read consent](/deploy/environment/#customer-microsoft-365-graph-read-consent-optional); this also requires the Graph executor sidecar to be deployed.

**The connection fails to save with a credentials error.**
Both providers verify credentials live before storing them. For Google Workspace, confirm the service-account JSON key is valid and that domain-wide delegation was authorized with the exact scopes shown on the card, using the service account's numeric Client ID. For Microsoft 365, confirm the tenant ID and client ID are correct, the client secret **Value** (not the secret ID) was copied and has not expired, and admin consent has been granted for the required Graph permissions.

**Customer Graph Read says an eligible administrator is required.**
Sign in as a Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator of the customer tenant. Breeze checks the role when you sign in, before any consent screen; other directory roles stop there.

**The confirm step shows the wrong tenant.**
You signed in with an account that belongs to a different tenant, usually your own MSP tenant or, for a guest account, its home tenant. Choose **Cancel, wrong tenant**, then **Connect tenant** again and sign in with an account from the customer's tenant. Nothing is consented or connected until you continue past the confirm step.

**Microsoft blocked the sign-in (Conditional Access).**
The customer's Conditional Access policy interrupted the sign-in, for example with a device check. Nothing was connected. Try again from a browser or device the tenant trusts, or ask the customer's administrator to complete the sign-in.

**Customer Graph Read is degraded.**
Review missing and unexpected grants on the card. Restore the exact thirteen-permission manifest, choose **Re-consent**, then **Retest**. If the card says reconciliation is unavailable, restore `Application.Read.All` first; the displayed observed list is last known, not a current assignment inventory.

**Retest says the verification service is unavailable.**
This does not mean Microsoft consent was removed. Existing active state is preserved during a transient executor outage. Ask the Breeze operator to restore the private verification service, then Retest again.

**Save is disabled.**
A fresh connection requires all fields. For Google Workspace: primary domain, super-admin email, and the service-account key. For Microsoft 365: tenant ID, client ID, and client secret. When updating an existing connection, the secret field may be left blank to keep the stored value.

**I connected a tenant but AI identity actions still do not work.**
A verified connection is required *in addition to* the feature flag being on. Re-open the sub-tab and confirm the badge reads **Connected**. Also confirm the service account or app registration carries the write permissions and admin role required for the specific action (see the permissions tables above).

---

- [AI in Breeze](/features/ai/) — how read and mutating actions, approvals, and the audit trail work

title: Incident Response
description: Create, investigate, contain, and close security incidents with evidence tracking and AI-assisted response.
headings: Promoting a finding to a tracked incident

sections.text:
Incident Response provides a structured workflow for handling security incidents — from initial detection through containment, evidence tracking, and closure. Every action is recorded in the incident timeline, and the AI assistant can create incidents, dispatch containment actions to the agent, and generate reports on your behalf.

---

sections.heading: Incident Lifecycle
sections.text:
Incidents progress through five statuses with enforced transitions:

| Status | Meaning | Allowed transitions |
|--------|---------|---------------------|
| `detected` | Incident discovered and triaged | `analyzing`, `contained` |
| `analyzing` | Investigation in progress | `contained`, `recovering` |
| `contained` | Containment actions executed | `recovering`, `closed` |
| `recovering` | System recovery underway | `contained`, `closed` |
| `closed` | Incident resolved | (terminal) |

sections.heading: Classifications
sections.text:
| Classification | Description |
|----------------|-------------|
| `malware` | Malware infection |
| `ransomware` | Ransomware attack |
| `phishing` | Phishing or social engineering |
| `data_breach` | Data exfiltration or exposure |
| `unauthorized_access` | Unauthorized system access |
| `denial_of_service` | Service disruption attack |
| `insider_threat` | Internal threat actor |
| `other` | Unclassified incident |

sections.heading: Severity Levels
sections.text:
| Level | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `p1` | Critical — immediate response required |
| `p2` | High — respond within hours |
| `p3` | Medium — respond within business day |
| `p4` | Low — respond within normal workflow |

---

sections.heading: Unified Incident Feed
sections.text:
The Incidents view shows a single feed that mixes two kinds of rows:

- **Tracked incidents** — full incident records created and managed inside Breeze, following the lifecycle described above.
- **EDR findings** — raw detections surfaced read-only from a connected EDR provider (Huntress or SentinelOne). These aren't Breeze incidents yet — they're detections your EDR reported that haven't been brought into Breeze's incident workflow.

Both row types are sorted together by severity and detection time. Each EDR finding shows which provider it came from and **links out to the originating console** — clicking a Huntress finding opens that detection in Huntress; clicking a SentinelOne finding opens it in the SentinelOne console.

sections.heading: Promoting a finding to a tracked incident
sections.text:
Findings are read-only until you decide one is worth tracking. Finding rows in the feed are read-only and show **Promote from the EDR view** (or a **View in …** link to the source). Promote a finding from the EDR view to create a real tracked incident from it — the new incident references the originating finding (via `sourceType` / `sourceRef`, see [Creating an Incident](#creating-an-incident)) so Breeze knows it's already been handled.

Promoting the same finding a second time is blocked — Breeze returns a conflict ("This finding has already been promoted to an incident") instead of creating a duplicate. If you see this, look for the existing tracked incident in the feed rather than retrying.

sections.heading: Who sees what
sections.text:
- **Tracked incidents** are visible to anyone with permission to view alerts.
- **EDR findings** additionally require permission to view devices, because a finding exposes the device that triggered it. A user with alerts access but not device access sees only tracked incidents — no Huntress or SentinelOne rows. This is expected: it's normal for two users to see different row counts in the same feed.
- EDR findings are also scoped to sites. If your account is restricted to specific sites, you'll only see findings for devices in sites you have access to. Findings that aren't tied to a specific device remain visible regardless of site restrictions.

You can filter the feed by row type or provider (`?kind=tracked`, `?kind=finding`, `?source=huntress`, `?source=s1`) via `GET /incidents/feed`.

---

sections.heading: Creating an Incident
sections.text:
```bash
POST /incidents
Content-Type: application/json
Authorization: Bearer <token>

{
  "title": "Suspicious process on web-server-01",
  "classification": "malware",
  "severity": "p2",
  "summary": "Agent detected unknown process communicating with external IP.",
  "relatedAlerts": ["alert-uuid-1"],
  "affectedDevices": ["device-uuid-1"],
  "assignedTo": "user-uuid"
}
```

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `title` | string | Yes | Short description |
| `classification` | string | Yes | Incident type (see classifications above) |
| `severity` | string | Yes | `p1`, `p2`, `p3`, or `p4` |
| `summary` | string | No | Detailed description |
| `relatedAlerts` | UUID[] | No | Related alert IDs |
| `affectedDevices` | UUID[] | No | Affected device IDs |
| `assignedTo` | UUID | No | User to assign |
| `sourceType` | string | No | `huntress_incident` or `s1_threat` — set when promoting an EDR finding into a tracked incident |
| `sourceRef` | string | No | The originating finding's ID from the EDR provider — set together with `sourceType` when promoting |

The incident is created with status `detected` and an initial timeline entry.

Setting `sourceType` and `sourceRef` together is how a finding is promoted into a tracked incident — it's what promoting a finding from the EDR view does under the hood. Breeze only lets a given finding be promoted once: submitting the same `sourceType`/`sourceRef` pair again returns `409 Conflict` rather than creating a second incident for the same finding.

---

sections.heading: Containment Actions
sections.text:
Record a containment action taken against an incident.

```bash
POST /incidents/:id/contain
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "actionType": "process_kill",
  "description": "Killing suspicious svchost.exe (PID 4832)",
  "executedBy": "user-uuid",
  "approvalRef": "approval-123"
}
```

This endpoint is a status/record call: it inserts a containment action row, appends a timeline entry, and (when the reported status counts as success) moves the incident to `contained`. It does not itself reach the device -- use it to log an action you or the AI assistant already took.

sections.heading: Action Types
sections.text:
| Action | Description | Requires Approval |
|--------|-------------|-------------------|
| `process_kill` | Terminate a process by PID | Yes |
| `network_isolation` | Isolate device from network | Yes |
| `account_disable` | Disable a compromised user account | Yes |
| `usb_block` | Block USB device access | Yes |

All containment actions require an `approvalRef` parameter. Actual on-device dispatch happens through the AI assistant's `execute_containment` tool (see [AI-Assisted Incident Response](#ai-assisted-incident-response)), which queues an agent command. Of the four action types, only `process_kill` is implemented on the agent today -- `network_isolation`, `account_disable`, and `usb_block` return a platform-specific-implementation error.

sections.heading: Action Statuses
sections.text:
| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `pending` | Awaiting execution |
| `in_progress` | Executing on device |
| `completed` | Successfully executed |
| `failed` | Execution failed |
| `cancelled` | Cancelled before execution |

---

sections.heading: Evidence Collection
sections.text:
Attach forensic evidence to an incident by reference for investigation and compliance. The caller (a person, a script, or the AI assistant) supplies the storage path and a SHA-256 hash; Breeze does not collect the evidence itself.

```bash
POST /incidents/:id/evidence
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "evidenceType": "log",
  "description": "System event logs from 2026-03-28",
  "collectedAt": "2026-03-28T14:00:00Z",
  "collectedBy": "user-uuid",
  "hash": "sha256-hash-of-content",
  "storagePath": "s3://evidence-bucket/incident-001/logs.tar.gz"
}
```

sections.heading: Evidence Types
sections.text:
| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `file` | File artifacts |
| `log` | System or application logs |
| `screenshot` | Device screenshots |
| `memory` | Memory snapshots |
| `network` | Network connection data |

Evidence integrity is validated using SHA-256 hashes. Storage paths must use approved URI schemes (`s3://`, `gs://`, `r2://`, `azblob://`, `immutable://`, `https://`). Path traversal sequences are blocked.

---

sections.heading: Incident Timeline
sections.text:
Every incident maintains a timeline that records all events:

| Entry Type | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `incident_created` | Incident was opened |
| `containment_executed` | Containment action completed successfully |
| `containment_attempted` | Containment action was attempted but failed |
| `evidence_collected` | Evidence was attached |
| `incident_closed` | Incident was closed with summary |

Each entry includes a timestamp, actor (`user`, `brain`, or `system`), summary, and type-specific metadata.

View the full timeline:

```bash
GET /incidents/:id
```

The response includes the incident details, timeline array, all containment actions, and all collected evidence.

---

sections.heading: Closing an Incident
sections.text:
```bash
POST /incidents/:id/close

{
  "summary": "Malware removed, device re-imaged, credentials rotated.",
  "lessonsLearned": "Detection delay was 4 hours. Adding process monitoring rule.",
  "resolvedAt": "2026-03-28T18:00:00Z"
}
```

Closing records a `resolvedAt` timestamp, updates the status to `closed`, and adds a closure entry to the timeline.

---

sections.heading: Incident Reports
sections.text:
Generate a structured report for an incident:

```bash
GET /incidents/:id/report
```

Returns:
- **Report metadata** — title, classification, severity, duration
- **Actions summary** — total, completed, failed, pending, action types used
- **Evidence summary** — total count, breakdown by type
- **Full timeline** — chronological event list

---

sections.heading: AI-Assisted Incident Response
sections.text:
The AI assistant provides five tools for incident management:

| Tool | Tier | Description |
|------|------|-------------|
| `create_incident` | Tier 2 | Create a new incident with classification and severity |
| `execute_containment` | Tier 3 | Run a containment action on a device (requires approval) |
| `collect_evidence` | Tier 2 | Collect forensic evidence from a device |
| `get_incident_timeline` | Tier 1 | View the full incident timeline |
| `generate_incident_report` | Tier 1 | Generate a structured incident report |

The AI can also trigger playbooks as part of incident response. Ask the AI to run a playbook against an affected device, and it will execute the playbook with the incident ID in the execution context for traceability.

  `execute_containment` is Tier 3 and requires human approval before execution. The AI will create a pending approval request that must be reviewed in the AI Risk Engine dashboard. On approval the tool queues an agent command; today the agent only implements `process_kill` -- `network_isolation`, `account_disable`, and `usb_block` come back as a platform-specific-implementation error.

---

sections.heading: API Reference
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| POST | `/incidents` | Create a new incident (or promote a finding, via `sourceType`/`sourceRef`) |
| GET | `/incidents` | List incidents (`?status=&severity=&classification=&assignedTo=&startDate=&endDate=&page=&limit=`) |
| GET | `/incidents/feed` | Unified feed of tracked incidents and EDR findings (`?kind=&source=&orgId=&page=&limit=`) |
| GET | `/incidents/:id` | Get incident with timeline, actions, and evidence |
| POST | `/incidents/:id/close` | Close an incident |
| GET | `/incidents/:id/report` | Generate incident report |
| POST | `/incidents/:id/contain` | Execute containment action |
| POST | `/incidents/:id/evidence` | Collect and attach evidence |

All endpoints require authentication and are scoped to the caller's organization.

---

sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
**AI-dispatched containment action stuck in pending.**
This is expected when the target device is offline: `execute_containment` (like `collect_evidence`) queues the command and delivers it automatically on the device's next successful heartbeat, up to a **7-day** deadline. It's visible and cancellable from the device's **Queued actions** list in the meantime. If the device is actually online and the action is still stuck, check device connectivity.

**Evidence upload rejected.**
The storage path must use an approved URI scheme (`s3://`, `gs://`, `r2://`, `azblob://`, `immutable://`, `https://`). Path traversal sequences (`..`) are blocked.

**Cannot close incident.**
Only incidents in `contained` or `recovering` status can be closed. Progress the incident through containment before closing.

**AI containment not executing.**
`execute_containment` is Tier 3 and requires human approval. Check **Monitoring → AI Risk Engine → Approval History** for pending requests.

**Promoting a finding fails with "already promoted".**
This is expected, not a bug — the finding has already been promoted to a tracked incident (by you or a teammate). Look for the existing tracked incident in the feed instead of promoting again.

**Some users don't see Huntress/SentinelOne findings in the feed.**
Seeing tracked incidents only requires permission to view alerts. Seeing raw EDR findings additionally requires permission to view devices, and findings are scoped to the sites a user has access to. If a technician is missing device permission or site access, they'll see fewer rows than an admin looking at the same feed — this is expected.

title: Integrations
description: Connect Breeze to PSA ticketing platforms, communication channels, and monitoring endpoints, with per-organization or partner-wide scoping.

sections.text:
Integrations connect Breeze to the tools your team already uses -- PSA platforms for ticketing, communication channels for alerting, and monitoring endpoints for telemetry forwarding. Most integrations are scoped to an organization and configured independently, so MSPs can tailor connections per customer without cross-tenant interference; PSA connections can also be owned **partner-wide**, so one connection serves every organization under the partner (see [PSA Integrations](/features/psa-integrations/#connection-ownership)). PSA credentials are encrypted at rest using AES-256-GCM, and every configuration change is recorded in the audit log.

**Implementation Status:**
  **PSA integrations** are fully database-backed with encrypted credential storage. **Communication, monitoring, and ticketing integrations** currently use in-memory storage and do not persist across API restarts. A migration to database-backed persistence for non-PSA integrations is planned.

---

sections.heading: Integration Types
sections.text:
Breeze supports three categories of integrations, each served by a dedicated set of API routes.

| Category | Providers | Purpose |
|----------|-----------|---------|
| **Communication** | Slack, Microsoft Teams, Discord | Alert notifications, status updates, and on-call messaging |
| **PSA / Ticketing** | Jira, ServiceNow, ConnectWise, Autotask, Freshservice, Zendesk | Connection management and credential storage today; ticket sync is not implemented yet (see [PSA Integrations](/features/psa-integrations/)) |
| **Monitoring** | External monitoring endpoints | Forward device telemetry and health data to third-party observability platforms (see [Monitoring & Observability Integrations](/features/monitoring-integrations/)) |
| **Accounting** | QuickBooks Online | Connect your accounting platform (see [Accounting Integrations](/features/accounting-integrations/)) |
| **Distributors** | Pax8, TD SYNNEX | Sync licenses and pull live distributor pricing into your [Product Catalog](/features/product-catalog/) -- see [Distributor Integrations](/features/distributor-integrations/) |
| **Network** | UniFi (Ubiquiti Site Manager cloud, or a self-hosted controller) | Discover UniFi fleet inventory and WAN health via the cloud, or connect a self-hosted controller directly through a Breeze agent -- with optional agent-collected deep telemetry either way (see [UniFi Network Integration](/features/unifi-integration/)) |

  Communication and monitoring integrations are configured through the `/integrations` routes. PSA connections use the dedicated `/psa` routes, which provide full CRUD, credential encryption, ticket mapping, and sync management.

  Every write route across communication, monitoring, ticketing, and PSA integrations -- saving or testing a provider, and creating, updating, or testing a PSA connection -- requires an **MFA-verified session**. If your account signed in without completing MFA, these actions are rejected until you do.

---

sections.heading: Connection Health
sections.text:
The **Connection health** panel at the top of **Integrations** (v0.124.0+) lists every connection that is currently broken -- a failed sync, a revoked authorization, a webhook whose retries ran out, a Google Workspace service account that Google no longer accepts -- each with a **Fix** link to the place where it is repaired, and a **Recently resolved** list underneath. Breeze checks connections every 15 minutes and clears an incident on its own once the connection works again. The people who can fix an incident also get an in-app notice and a daily digest email.

The **Health notifications** card on the same page decides whether the admins of a customer organization also hear about their own organization's connections: off by default, with a partner default and a per-organization override. The checks, the digest and the opt-outs are described under [Connection Health Checks](/features/notifications/#connection-health-checks).

---

sections.heading: Communication Integrations
sections.text: Communication integrations push notifications from Breeze into your team's messaging platform. Each provider is configured with a POST request containing the webhook URL and any provider-specific settings.

sections.heading: Setting Up a Provider
sections.text:
**Slack:**
```bash
    POST /integrations/slack
    Content-Type: application/json

    {
      "webhookUrl": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T00/B00/xxxx",
      "channel": "#breeze-alerts",
      "username": "Breeze RMM",
      "notifyOn": ["alert.critical", "alert.warning", "device.offline"]
    }
```

  **Microsoft Teams:**
```bash
    POST /integrations/teams
    Content-Type: application/json

    {
      "webhookUrl": "https://outlook.office.com/webhook/...",
      "notifyOn": ["alert.critical", "device.offline"]
    }
```

  **Discord:**
```bash
    POST /integrations/discord
    Content-Type: application/json

    {
      "webhookUrl": "https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...",
      "notifyOn": ["alert.critical", "alert.warning"]
    }
```

Each provider endpoint accepts an optional `"test": true` flag in the request body. When present, the API queues a test notification to the configured webhook. Note that the configuration is saved to the in-memory store before the test is executed, so sending `"test": true` does persist the settings for the lifetime of the current API process.

```bash
POST /integrations/slack
{
  "webhookUrl": "https://hooks.slack.com/services/T00/B00/xxxx",
  "test": true
}
```

Response:

```json
{ "success": true, "message": "slack test notification queued." }
```

sections.heading: Retrieving Communication Settings
Monitoring Integration
sections.text: The monitoring integration forwards device telemetry to an external observability platform. Configuration is stored as a freeform JSON object, so you can include whatever fields your monitoring endpoint requires.

sections.heading: Saving Monitoring Settings
sections.text:
```bash
PUT /integrations/monitoring
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "orgId": "<uuid>",
  "endpoint": "https://monitoring.example.com/ingest",
  "apiKey": "mon_xxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "metricsEnabled": true,
  "forwardEvents": ["cpu", "memory", "disk", "network"]
}
```

sections.heading: Retrieving Monitoring Settings
sections.text:
```bash
GET /integrations/monitoring?orgId=<uuid>
```

Returns the stored configuration object, or an empty object `{}` if nothing has been configured.

sections.heading: Testing Monitoring Connectivity
sections.text:
```bash
POST /integrations/monitoring/test
```

Returns `{ "success": true, "message": "Connection successful." }` when the monitoring endpoint is reachable.

---

sections.heading: Ticketing Integration
sections.text: The ticketing integration provides a lightweight configuration store for generic ticketing systems that are not covered by the dedicated PSA routes.

sections.heading: Saving Ticketing Settings
sections.text:
```bash
POST /integrations/ticketing
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "orgId": "<uuid>",
  "provider": "custom",
  "apiUrl": "https://tickets.example.com/api",
  "apiKey": "tk_xxxxxxxxxxxx",
  "projectKey": "BREEZE",
  "autoCreate": true
}
```

sections.heading: Retrieving Ticketing Settings
sections.text:
```bash
GET /integrations/ticketing?orgId=<uuid>
```

sections.heading: Testing Ticketing Connectivity
sections.text:
```bash
POST /integrations/ticketing/test
```

Returns `{ "success": true, "message": "Connection successful. Credentials validated." }`.

---

sections.heading: PSA Integrations
sections.text: PSA (Professional Services Automation) integrations are the most fully featured integration type. They are backed by a dedicated database table (`psa_connections`) with encrypted credential storage, sync tracking, and ticket mapping. Use the `/psa` routes for all PSA operations.

sections.heading: Supported PSA Providers
sections.text:
| Provider | Enum Value | Typical Credentials |
|----------|------------|---------------------|
| **ConnectWise Manage** | `connectwise` | Company ID, public key, private key, site URL |
| **Datto Autotask** | `autotask` | Username, secret, integration code |
| **Jira** | `jira` | Email, API token, site URL, project key |
| **ServiceNow** | `servicenow` | Instance URL, username, password or OAuth token |
| **Freshservice** | `freshservice` | Domain, API key |
| **Zendesk** | `zendesk` | Subdomain, email, API token |

  Credentials are encrypted using AES-256-GCM before being stored in the database. The encryption key is derived from the `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` environment variable, which is required in every environment -- the API will refuse to start without it.

sections.heading: Creating a PSA Connection
sections.text:
1. Choose a provider from the supported list above.

2. Send a POST request with the connection name, provider, and credentials:

```bash
   POST /psa/connections
   Content-Type: application/json

   {
     "orgId": "<uuid>",
     "provider": "connectwise",
     "name": "ConnectWise — Contoso",
     "credentials": {
       "companyId": "contoso",
       "publicKey": "pk_xxxx",
       "privateKey": "sk_xxxx",
       "siteUrl": "https://na.myconnectwise.net"
     },
     "settings": {
       "defaultBoard": "Service Board",
       "defaultStatus": "New"
     }
   }
```

3. The API encrypts the credentials and returns the new connection (without credentials in the response):

```json
   {
     "id": "uuid",
     "orgId": "uuid",
     "provider": "connectwise",
     "name": "ConnectWise — Contoso",
     "settings": { "defaultBoard": "Service Board", "defaultStatus": "New" },
     "createdAt": "2026-02-18T...",
     "updatedAt": "2026-02-18T...",
     "lastTestedAt": null,
     "lastSyncedAt": null,
     "hasCredentials": true
   }
```

4. Test the connection to verify credentials are valid (see [Testing Connections](#testing-connections) below).

sections.heading: Updating a PSA Connection
sections.text:
Update the name, credentials, or settings of an existing connection. Only the fields you include will be changed.

```bash
PATCH /psa/connections/:id
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "name": "ConnectWise — Contoso (Production)",
  "settings": {
    "defaultBoard": "MSP Board",
    "defaultStatus": "New",
    "autoSync": true
  }
}
```

  When you update credentials, the new values are encrypted before storage. The previous credentials are replaced entirely -- partial credential updates are not supported.

sections.heading: Credential Handling
sections.text:
PSA credentials follow a strict security model:

| Behavior | Detail |
|----------|--------|
| **Encryption** | All credentials are encrypted with AES-256-GCM using the `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` before being written to the database |
| **Response redaction** | List and detail endpoints never return raw credentials. The `hasCredentials` boolean indicates whether credentials are stored |
| **Rotation** | Update credentials via `PATCH /psa/connections/:id` with a new `credentials` object. The old encrypted value is replaced atomically |
| **Deletion** | Deleting a connection removes the encrypted credentials and all associated ticket mappings from the database |

---

sections.heading: Accounting Integrations
sections.text: Connect Breeze to your accounting platform from the **Accounting** tab on the Integrations page. Accounting integrations are a partner-level feature -- they're set up once for your practice, not per customer.

sections.heading: QuickBooks Online
sections.text:
QuickBooks Online connects through Intuit's standard OAuth consent flow:

1. Open **Integrations → Accounting** and click **Connect to QuickBooks**.
2. You're taken to Intuit's consent screen to authorize Breeze; approving it returns you to Breeze with the connection established.
3. The tab then shows the connection status, the connected environment, and a **Disconnect** option. You can also choose whether issued invoices push to QuickBooks automatically or manually.

#### Importing customers

Once QuickBooks is connected, you can bring your existing QuickBooks customers into Breeze as organizations -- no re-typing. Each imported customer becomes one Breeze **organization** (customer type) with a default **site**, carrying over the billing contact and address.

1. On the connected **QuickBooks Online** panel, open the **Import customers** section and click **Load customers**.
2. Tick the customers you want to import. Customers you've already imported show an **Already imported** badge and are skipped automatically (select-all excludes them).
3. Click **Import selected**. Breeze reports how many were imported, skipped, and failed, with an inline list of any failures.

The import is idempotent -- it keys off the QuickBooks customer id, so re-running it never creates duplicates. It requires partner scope, and one QuickBooks company (realm) is connected per partner.

  QuickBooks requires Intuit OAuth credentials configured on the server (`QBO_CLIENT_ID`, `QBO_CLIENT_SECRET`, `QBO_REDIRECT_URI`, `QBO_ENVIRONMENT`). Until those are set, the connect option reports that QuickBooks isn't configured on this instance. See the [environment reference](/deploy/environment/). On Breeze-hosted accounts this is already configured.

---

sections.heading: Distributor Integrations
sections.text: Distributor integrations live on the **Distributors** tab of the Integrations page and let you bring vendor licenses and pricing into Breeze. They're partner-scoped.

sections.heading: Pax8
sections.text:
Pax8 syncs your clients and their subscription/license quantities, which you can map to organizations and link to recurring contract lines. After connecting your Pax8 account and mapping companies to Breeze organizations, open the **Subscriptions** tab to manage how each subscription connects to a contract line.

Each subscription row offers these actions:

| Action | Description | Requires MFA |
|--------|-------------|:------------:|
| **Link for observation** | Connect the subscription to an existing contract line, or create a new manual line on the spot, so Pax8-reported quantities can be compared with Breeze billing | Yes |
| **Change** | Re-point the subscription to a different contract line | Yes |
| **Pause observations** | Stop recording new Pax8 quantity observations while keeping the link intact | Yes |
| **Resume observations** | Resume recording Pax8 quantity observations and surfacing drift | Yes |
| **Unlink** | Remove the connection between the subscription and the contract line | Yes |

When **Track Pax8 reported quantity for drift** is enabled on a link, each Pax8 sync records the latest known quantity as an observation and surfaces any difference from the linked manual contract-line quantity. Breeze's order ledger and linked manual quantity remain authoritative for billing; observation sync never overwrites that billing quantity. Pausing stops new observations and drift updates while leaving the link and billing quantity intact.

Beyond subscription sync, you can also search the Pax8 catalog and import individual products into your [Product Catalog](/features/product-catalog/#pax8) -- see Product Catalog for that workflow.

sections.heading: TD SYNNEX
sections.text:
TD SYNNEX provides live product price and availability you can import straight into your catalog. The end-to-end workflow -- including EC Express live pricing -- is documented under [Product Catalog → Importing from distributor catalogs](/features/product-catalog/#importing-from-distributor-catalogs).

---

sections.heading: UniFi Network
sections.text:
UniFi is a **partner-level**, strictly read-only integration that discovers your Ubiquiti network fleet across every customer site and reconciles it into Breeze's unified network view, so gateways, switches, and access points show up alongside your agent-discovered assets without duplicating them. Configure it on the **UniFi** tab of the Integrations page, either through Ubiquiti's cloud (**Site Manager**), optionally paired with on-site deep telemetry agents, or fully **self-hosted** with a Breeze agent talking directly to your on-prem controller and no Ubiquiti cloud account at all.

The full connection walkthrough for both modes, deep telemetry, and what Breeze pulls from UniFi is documented on its own page: see [UniFi Network Integration](/features/unifi-integration/).

---

sections.heading: Testing Connections
sections.text: Every integration type provides a test endpoint. Testing verifies that the configured credentials and endpoint are reachable.

sections.heading: Communication Test
sections.text:
Pass `"test": true` in the provider configuration body:

```bash
POST /integrations/slack
{ "webhookUrl": "https://hooks.slack.com/...", "test": true }
```

sections.heading: Monitoring Test
sections.text:
```bash
POST /integrations/monitoring/test
```

sections.heading: Ticketing Test
sections.text:
```bash
POST /integrations/ticketing/test
```

sections.heading: PSA Connection Test
sections.text:
Test a specific saved PSA connection by ID:

```bash
POST /psa/connections/:id/test
```

On success, the API updates the connection's `syncSettings` with a `lastTestedAt` timestamp and sets the status to `verified`. The response confirms the result:

```json
{ "success": true, "message": "Credentials verified" }
```

This endpoint also writes an audit log entry with action `psa.connection.test`.

---

sections.heading: Listing PSA Connections
sections.text:
```bash
GET /psa/connections?orgId=<uuid>&provider=connectwise&page=1&limit=50
```

All query parameters are optional. Results are paginated and ordered by most recently updated.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| `orgId` | UUID | Filter to a specific organization |
| `provider` | string | Filter by PSA provider (`jira`, `connectwise`, etc.) |
| `page` | integer | Page number (default: 1) |
| `limit` | integer | Results per page (default: 50, max: 100) |

sections.heading: Viewing a Single Connection
sections.text:
```bash
GET /psa/connections/:id
```

Returns the connection detail including settings, sync timestamps, and `hasCredentials` flag. Credentials themselves are not included.

sections.heading: Deleting a PSA Connection
sections.text:
```bash
DELETE /psa/connections/:id
```

  Deleting a connection also removes all associated ticket mappings. This action cannot be undone.

sections.heading: Triggering a Sync
sections.text:
```bash
POST /psa/connections/:id/sync
```

  PSA ticket sync is not implemented yet. This endpoint always returns `501 Not Implemented` with `{ "error": "PSA ticket sync is not implemented yet" }` -- no ticket data moves between Breeze and the PSA today.

sections.heading: Updating Connection Status
sections.text:
Set a custom status on a connection (e.g., `active`, `paused`, `error`):

```bash
POST /psa/connections/:id/status
Content-Type: application/json

{ "status": "paused" }
```

---

sections.heading: Ticket Mappings
sections.text: PSA connections can map Breeze alerts and devices to external tickets. Ticket mappings track the relationship between internal entities and their corresponding tickets in the PSA platform.

sections.heading: Listing All Tickets
sections.text:
```bash
GET /psa/tickets?page=1&limit=50
```

Returns all ticket mappings across connections accessible to the authenticated user. Results include:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` | Internal mapping ID |
| `psaId` | The PSA connection this ticket belongs to |
| `title` | Display title derived from the external ticket ID |
| `status` | Current ticket status |
| `syncedAt` | Last sync timestamp |
| `raw.externalTicketId` | The ticket ID in the external PSA system |
| `raw.externalTicketUrl` | Direct URL to the ticket in the PSA platform |
| `raw.alertId` | Associated Breeze alert ID (if any) |
| `raw.deviceId` | Associated Breeze device ID (if any) |

sections.heading: Listing Tickets for a Connection
sections.text:
```bash
GET /psa/connections/:id/tickets?page=1&limit=50
```

Returns only ticket mappings associated with the specified PSA connection.

---

| Method | Path | Description |

| **POST** | `/integrations/monitoring/test` | Test monitoring endpoint connectivity |
| **GET** | `/integrations/ticketing` | Retrieve ticketing integration settings |
| **POST** | `/integrations/ticketing` | Save ticketing integration settings |
| **POST** | `/integrations/ticketing/test` | Test ticketing endpoint connectivity |

sections.heading: PSA Routes (`/psa`)
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| **GET** | `/psa/connections` | List PSA connections (filterable by `orgId`, `provider`) |
| **POST** | `/psa/connections` | Create a new PSA connection with encrypted credentials |
| **GET** | `/psa/connections/:id` | Get a single PSA connection detail |

  All integration and PSA routes require authentication. PSA routes additionally require the `orgs:read` permission for GET endpoints and `orgs:write` for mutating endpoints.

sections.heading: Database Schema
sections.text: PSA connections and ticket mappings are stored in two tables defined in the integrations schema.

sections.heading: `psa_connections`
sections.text:
| Column | Type | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `id` | UUID | Primary key |
| `org_id` | UUID | Organization this connection belongs to |
| `provider` | enum | PSA provider (`connectwise`, `autotask`, `jira`, `servicenow`, `freshservice`, `zendesk`) |
| `name` | varchar(255) | Display name for the connection |
| `credentials` | JSONB | Encrypted credential payload (AES-256-GCM) |
| `settings` | JSONB | Provider-specific configuration (board, project, defaults) |
| `sync_settings` | JSONB | Internal sync metadata including `lastTestedAt` and status |
| `enabled` | boolean | Whether the connection is active (default: `true`) |
| `last_sync_at` | timestamp | Last successful sync time |
| `last_sync_status` | varchar(50) | Status of the most recent sync (`queued`, `running`, `completed`, `failed`) |
| `last_sync_error` | text | Error message from the last failed sync |
| `created_by` | UUID | User who created the connection |
| `created_at` | timestamp | Creation timestamp |
| `updated_at` | timestamp | Last modification timestamp |

sections.heading: `psa_ticket_mappings`
sections.text:
| Column | Type | Description |

| `id` | UUID | Primary key |
| `connection_id` | UUID | Foreign key to `psa_connections` |
| `alert_id` | UUID | Associated Breeze alert (nullable) |

| `external_ticket_id` | varchar(100) | Ticket ID in the external PSA system |

| `status` | varchar(50) | Current ticket status |
| `last_sync_at` | timestamp | Last sync timestamp for this mapping |
| `created_at` | timestamp | Creation timestamp |
| `updated_at` | timestamp | Last modification timestamp |
