sections.heading: Troubleshooting
sections.text:
**Communication webhook not receiving notifications.**
Verify the webhook URL is correct and publicly reachable. Use the `"test": true` flag to send a test notification. Check that your messaging platform has not revoked or rotated the webhook token.

**PSA connection test fails.**
Confirm that the credentials are correct and the PSA platform's API is accessible from your Breeze API server. Some providers require IP allowlisting or VPN access. Check the `lastTestedAt` and sync status fields on the connection for additional context.

**"Failed to encrypt credentials" error on PSA connection creation.**
The `APP_ENCRYPTION_KEY` environment variable is not set or is invalid. It's required in every environment -- the API will not start without it.

**Ticket mappings not appearing.**
This is expected today -- PSA ticket sync is not implemented yet (see [PSA Integrations](/features/psa-integrations/)), so no ticket mappings are ever created.

**"Organization context required" error.**
Integration routes require an organization scope. If you are authenticated with a partner or system scope, pass the `orgId` query parameter or include it in the request body to specify which organization's integrations you are managing.

**Deleted connection -- can I recover ticket mappings?**
No. Deleting a PSA connection removes all associated ticket mappings from the database. This action is irreversible. Export or back up ticket data before deleting a connection if you need to retain it.

title: Invoices
description: Create invoices from your catalog, tracked time, and parts. Issue and send them, record payments, void and reissue, and download a clean PDF.
headings: Line grouping by ticket and category

sections.text:
Breeze's invoice engine turns the work you already track -- catalog items, time entries, and parts -- into invoices you can issue, send, and collect on without leaving the platform. Open **Billing → Invoices** to get started.

Invoices are **partner-scoped**: you can invoice any of your customer organizations from one place.

The Billing section, including Invoices, is only available when the **Service Management** module is enabled for your account; see [Service Management mode](/reference/partner-management/#service-management-mode).

sections.heading: The Invoice List
sections.text: The list shows every invoice with its number, organization, status, issue and due dates, total, and outstanding balance. An **Outstanding** summary strip at the top totals what's still owed across all invoices. Search by number or organization, filter by status, organization, or date, and sort by issued date, due date, total, or balance.

sections.heading: Invoice Statuses
sections.text:
| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| Draft | Being assembled; not yet issued and not visible to the customer |
| Sent | Issued and delivered to the customer |
| Partially paid | One or more payments recorded, but a balance remains |
| Paid | Fully paid |
| Overdue | Past its due date with a balance remaining |
| Void | Cancelled; no longer collectible |

sections.heading: Creating an Invoice
sections.text:
1. Go to **Billing → Invoices** and click **New invoice**.
2. Choose **Assemble from work** to pull in tracked time and parts, or **Blank invoice** to start empty.
3. Select the customer organization the invoice is for.
4. When assembling from work, choose the draft's **Currency**. **Organization default** uses the currency the organization bills in today; pick an explicit currency only when you need to bill work that was priced in a currency the organization no longer uses.
5. The invoice opens as a **draft** for editing.

sections.heading: Where the currency comes from
sections.text:
Every invoice is stamped with the **customer organization's billing currency**. An organization inherits that from your partner currency (**Settings → Billing**) when it is created, and the stamp then travels with the document -- clones and reissues keep it, and issuing never rewrites it.

The stamped currency can't be changed from the console. Changing a draft's currency is an API-only operation (`POST /invoices/:id/currency`) that first clears the draft's lines or reprices catalog-sourced lines into the new currency; nothing is ever converted at an exchange rate. Retargeting a draft to an organization that bills in a different currency is refused rather than silently re-priced.

sections.heading: Assembling across currencies
sections.text:
Tracked time and parts keep the currency they were priced in when they were logged. Assembling only pulls in work whose currency matches the draft's currency; nothing is ever converted. If some unbilled work in the range is priced in another currency, the draft is still created and a notice tells you how many items were left out and in which currency -- assemble a separate draft in that currency to bill them. If *all* the unbilled work is in another currency, nothing is assembled and the dialog offers an **Assemble in …** button for each currency found (with the item count and total); clicking it creates a draft in that currency containing exactly those items. The same **Assemble in** shortcut appears on a ticket's **Create invoice** action when its unbilled work is in a different currency than the organization now bills in.

Once an invoice is issued, the time entries and parts it billed are locked: their hours, rates, quantities, and prices can no longer be edited (descriptions and notes still can). Void and reissue the invoice if an amount needs to change.

sections.heading: Adding Line Items
sections.text:
The draft editor's primary way to add lines is the shared **catalog picker** -- start typing to search your [Product Catalog](/features/product-catalog/) by name or SKU, pick an item or bundle, and set the quantity. Catalog items use the customer's per-customer price when one is set. You can also add a **manual line** with a custom description, quantity, and price for anything not in the catalog.

Line items can come from several sources: catalog items, bundles, tracked time entries, parts, recurring contracts, or manual entries. The running subtotal, tax, total, and balance update live as you edit.

  If your catalog is empty, the editor links straight to **Product Catalog** so you can add the items you sell.

sections.heading: AI usage lines
sections.text: When you assemble from work, every unbilled AI usage charge for a month that has already closed and started on or before the invoice's end date is added as one line per model, for example "AI usage — (model) — (month)". A month closes shortly after it ends (UTC), so this month's usage appears on the next invoice. Charges that round to zero and usage older than 92 days are never invoiced; they show in the report's unbilled column. These lines are non-taxable by default, and you can edit them on a draft. See [AI usage chargeback](/features/ai-usage-chargeback/).

sections.heading: Time-entry line quantities
sections.text:
A line pulled in from a time entry bills the entry's **billed** quantity, not necessarily the time actually worked -- the entry's [billing profile](/features/rates/) can apply a minimum or round up to a billing increment first. When the two differ, the line's description states both, for example "On-site -- 0.50 h worked, 1.00 h billed." There is still exactly one invoice line per time entry.

Labour amounts use the billed minutes converted to hours **rounded to two decimals**, × the rate, rounded once to the currency's smallest unit: 25 minutes at $135.00/h is 0.42 h × $135.00 = $56.70 (not $56.25), so quantity × rate always equals the line total. This is not a 6-minute increment -- any whole-minute duration is accepted -- and the ticket time panel, timesheet and technician time report show each entry's hours × rate.

sections.heading: Time-entry line detail
sections.text:
You choose how time-entry lines print on customer invoices under **Settings → Billing → Documents**, in the **Time entry lines on invoices** group:

- **Show the date worked** (off by default) prints the day each entry was worked under its line. The date is the day the entry started, in your partner time zone.
- **Show the technician's note** (on by default) prints the time entry's description as the line title. Turn it off and time-entry lines read **Labor** instead; parts, manual lines and other lines keep their text. The note is withheld from the customer portal, the public invoice link and the copy pushed to QuickBooks or Xero too, not just hidden on screen.
- **Show worked vs billed time** (on by default) prints the "0.50 h worked, 1.00 h billed" note described above, on the invoice and in the line description pushed to QuickBooks or Xero.
- **Group by day** lists time-entry lines under a heading for each day, with that day's hours and amount, while dates are shown. Each entry still keeps its own line, rate and amount. Lines with no date, such as parts and the block-hours overage line, follow the dated ones.

With the defaults, the content of an invoice is the same as before: same lines, text and amounts. Two PDF layout fixes apply to every invoice PDF generated from now on. A line title that wraps onto a second line is now measured in its bold font, so the text under it no longer prints over the title's second line. A tall line that doesn't fit at the bottom of a page now moves whole to the next page instead of splitting. An issued invoice's stored PDF never changes. Drafts, and invoices whose PDF hasn't been generated yet, may print slightly differently if they have a wrapping title or a tall line near the bottom of a page.

To change these for one invoice, use **Time entry lines** in the draft editor. **Billing default** follows your partner setting. The choice is frozen when the invoice is issued. A later change to your setting never changes an invoice the customer already has, and invoices issued before this setting existed keep their original layout. A reissued invoice starts with the voided invoice's choice.

sections.heading: Line grouping by ticket and category
sections.text:
Wherever an invoice is rendered -- the web editor and document view, the generated PDF, the authenticated customer portal, and the public invoice link -- line items are grouped under the ticket they came from, then by category within that ticket (Labour, Materials, Recurring, and so on), instead of a flat list. This makes it clear to the customer which charges belong to which piece of work. Lines with no ticket are grouped together at the top.

On a draft, group headings show the ticket's current subject and category. From v0.117.0 they are **frozen when the invoice is issued**: renaming or recategorizing a ticket, deleting it, or moving it to another organization no longer changes an invoice the customer has already received. Since the same release, the logged-in customer portal also shows the category label next to each group heading, as the PDF and public invoice link already did. Invoices issued before the upgrade keep the subject and category they displayed at the time.

sections.heading: Issuing and Sending
sections.text:
**Issuing** an invoice finalizes it: it assigns the next sequential invoice number (using your partner prefix and the current year), sets the issue and due dates, and generates the PDF. The due date uses the organization's payment terms if it has its own, otherwise your partner default (30 days if neither is set). **Sending** emails the invoice to the customer.

1. Review the draft and confirm the line items and totals.
2. Click **Issue** to assign a number and lock the invoice.
3. Click **Send** to email it to the customer.

**Send** opens a composer prefilled from the organization's billing contact: recipients, Cc, subject, a personal message, and whether to attach the PDF. The email and the PDF both carry a **Pay online** link.

Partners edit the invoice email under **Settings → Partner → Email templates** (Invoice) -- subject, heading, button label, and HTML body. Merge variables: `{{invoice_number}}`, `{{partner_name}}`, `{{total}}`, `{{due_date}}`, and `{{portal_url}}`. The pay/view button always uses the server invoice link; partners cannot point it somewhere else. A personal message, the PDF note, amount due, and your email signature still appear around that body. Leave it on the default to keep the built-in wording. This does not change the email card's accent bar or pull colors from the Branding tab.

An invoice that has already been issued can be **re-sent** without changing anything about it -- its number, dates, amounts, and "sent" timestamp all stay as they were, so a reminder never looks like a second invoice. A paid invoice can be re-sent too, as a receipt. Drafts and voided invoices can't be sent this way.

When **Show the date worked** is in effect for an invoice, the date is also sent to accounting: as the line's service date in QuickBooks, and appended to the line description in Xero, which has no per-line date field. Long line descriptions are shortened before the worked-vs-billed note and the date, so those always reach the accounting copy whole.

#### Refresh from time entries

If a technician corrects a time entry's note or start time after a draft invoice was assembled, click **Refresh from time entries** in the draft editor. It updates each time-entry line's note, date worked, worked time and approval marker from its source entry.

- **Never changed:** quantities, prices, line totals and invoice totals, and any description you edited by hand. Lines are never added or removed.
- A line whose entry's billed time no longer matches the line quantity is left untouched and listed, so you can edit the quantity or assemble a new draft.
- Lines whose entry was deleted, billed on another invoice or is no longer billable on this draft are skipped and listed. A line whose entry was billed on another invoice blocks **Issue** until you remove it.
- Only drafts can be refreshed; issued and void invoices are refused.

When you upgrade to v0.123.0, time-entry lines already on draft invoices are treated as hand-edited, so a refresh never overwrites a description that existed before the upgrade.

To remind customers automatically about upcoming and overdue invoices, turn on [payment reminders](/features/online-payments/#payment-reminders). They are off by default and do not need automatic payments.

The issued-invoice view puts the **balance due** front and center, shows recorded payments, and offers a one-click **PDF download**, plus **Copy invoice link** and **Reset customer link** -- see [Online Payments](/features/online-payments/#the-customer-invoice-link).

sections.heading: Recording Payments
sections.text:
When a customer pays offline, record it against the invoice so the balance and status stay accurate. Payments collected online through [Stripe](/features/online-payments/) are recorded automatically and badged **Online**.

1. Open the issued invoice.
2. Click **Record payment**.
3. Choose the method -- cash, check, bank transfer, card, or other -- and enter the amount, date, and an optional reference.
4. Save. The invoice moves to **partially paid** or **paid** automatically based on the remaining balance.

A payment amount has to be expressible in the invoice's currency: an invoice in a currency with no minor unit (such as Japanese yen) won't accept `100.50`.

You can void a manually recorded payment if it was entered in error. Payments collected online through Stripe are reconciled from Stripe and can't be voided by hand.

sections.heading: Deposit Invoices
sections.text: When an invoice is created from an accepted [quote](/features/quotes/) that requires a deposit, it carries a **deposit due** amount -- and that deposit is what the customer pays **first**. The invoice shows the deposit as the amount due up front; once it's covered, the remaining balance becomes due per the invoice's terms. A single invoice therefore carries the whole engagement while still collecting the deposit before the balance, and the customer can pay both the deposit and the balance through [Online Payments](/features/online-payments/). See [Quotes → Deposits](/features/quotes/#deposits) for how the deposit is configured before the quote is sent.

sections.heading: Per-Organization Tax & Billing Address
sections.text:
Each customer organization has a **Billing** tab (**Settings → Organizations → [organization] → Billing**) that holds the details Breeze prints on and calculates for that customer's invoices:

- **Tax ID**, a **tax-exempt** flag, and a per-organization **tax rate**. When a rate is set here it applies to that customer's invoices; otherwise Breeze falls back to your partner default tax rate (**Settings → Billing**).
- The **billing contact** — shown here, but managed in the organization's **Contacts** tab: it is the organization-level contact with the **Billing** role. Quotes and invoices are emailed to that contact by default (you can change the recipients on each send). If no contact has the role, nothing is emailed until one does.
- A full **billing address** (address lines, city, region, postal code, and country), which appears on the invoice PDF.
- **Payment terms** (v0.117.0+) -- the number of days (0-365) between issue and due date for this customer. Leave it blank to inherit your partner default from **Settings → Billing**; the field shows the inherited value. `0` means due on receipt.

Setting these once per customer means invoices carry the right tax and address without re-entering them each time.

sections.heading: Voiding and Reissuing
sections.text:
If an issued invoice needs to be cancelled, **void** it with a reason. You can optionally **reissue** at the same time, which creates a fresh draft you can correct and issue anew -- keeping the original on record for audit purposes.

**An invoice with payments applied to it cannot be voided.** Breeze refuses the void and tells you how much is applied, rather than silently un-applying the payments and leaving the money unaccounted for: *"This invoice has <amount> of payments applied to it. Remove those payments first (and in QuickBooks, if it is synced there), then void the invoice."* Remove the payments, then void. This applies to every invoice, whether or not it is synced to an accounting integration -- see [Accounting Integrations](/features/accounting-integrations/#payment-push).

sections.heading: Billed devices
sections.text:
Every auto-counted line on a contract-generated invoice can be expanded to show the exact devices it billed, including each device's role and how it was counted: **Included**, **Overage** or **Flagged, not billed**. A device deleted or moved to another organization afterwards still appears on the past invoice by hostname and is marked **Device removed**. Reissuing an invoice copies this recorded evidence to the replacement instead of counting the fleet again.

The optional **Billed devices** appendix on the invoice PDF is **off by default**. Turn it on for every invoice with **Include billed devices appendix on invoice PDFs** under **Settings → Billing**, or choose **Include billed devices appendix** for one invoice from the send dialog while that invoice is still a draft. Flagged devices are never printed because they were not charged. The appendix prints at most 2,000 device rows and notes when additional billed devices are omitted.

The choice is **frozen when the invoice is issued**. Changing the partner default later does not alter an already-issued invoice's PDF, and the per-invoice choice cannot be changed after issue.

Invoices generated before this feature was available have no device detail and say so. Editing a draft line's quantity by hand does **not** rewrite its device evidence because the evidence records what the generation run counted. Deleting a draft line deletes its evidence with it.

sections.heading: PDF and Accounting View
sections.text:
Every issued invoice can be downloaded as a clean, single-page **PDF** to send or archive. The detail view also offers an accounting-oriented breakdown of subtotal, tax, total, payments, and balance.

The invoice's **document theme** (Classic or Condensed) and **page size** (Letter or A4) come from your partner billing settings (**Settings → Billing**). A draft previews your current choice; since v0.117.0 both are **frozen when the invoice is issued**, so changing the setting later only affects invoices issued afterwards. Invoices issued before the upgrade were stamped with the setting in effect at upgrade time, so they look the same as before.

The seller details printed on an invoice or quote -- phone, website, and address -- come from your billing letterhead in **Settings → Billing**. Since v0.117.0, any of those left blank there are filled from your company details (**Settings → Partner → Company**) instead of printing empty. The address is taken as a block: if any billing-address field is filled in, the whole billing address is used as entered; only when all of them are blank does the company address take over.

sections.heading: Bulk Actions
sections.text:
Select invoices using the checkboxes in the invoice list to reveal a bulk action bar.

| Action | Permission required | Notes |
|--------|---------------------|-------|
| **Issue** | Invoice send | Issues all selected draft invoices |
| **Void** | Invoice send | Prompts for a void reason; applies to all selected issued invoices |
| **Delete drafts** | Invoice write | Deletes all selected draft invoices |

Actions run per-item in isolation, so partial success is possible -- the bar reports what succeeded and what failed.

sections.heading: Permissions
sections.text: Invoice access is governed by role permissions: viewing requires invoice read access, creating and editing drafts requires invoice write access, and issuing, sending, voiding, and recording payments require invoice send access. Assign these through **Settings → Users & Roles**.

sections.heading: Related
sections.text:
- [Product Catalog](/features/product-catalog/) -- the price list invoices pull from
- [Recurring Contracts](/features/contracts/) -- generate invoices automatically on a schedule
- [Online Payments](/features/online-payments/) -- collect card payments online

title: IP History
description: Track IP address changes over time with interface-level detail, MAC address correlation, and assignment type detection.
headings: Viewing IP History in the Console
No IP history records for a device
All IPs show as "static" when they should be "dhcp"

sections.text:
IP History automatically tracks every IP address assignment on every managed device, recording when addresses appear, change, and disappear. Each heartbeat, the Breeze agent scans all active network interfaces, detects new or changed IP assignments, and reports the delta to the API. The API maintains a complete timeline of IP assignments per device with first-seen/last-seen timestamps, MAC address correlation, subnet mask, gateway, DNS servers, and whether the address was assigned via DHCP, statically configured, or acquired through a VPN tunnel.

This feature is essential for incident response (answering "which device had IP 10.0.5.42 at 2 PM on Tuesday?"), compliance auditing, and network troubleshooting. When a device moves between subnets, switches from DHCP to static, or connects to a VPN, the full history is preserved with interface-level granularity.

---

sections.heading: Viewing IP History in the Console
sections.text:
Open a device's detail page and select the **IP History** tab to browse its address history without querying the API directly. The table lists Interface, IP Address, Type, Assignment, First Seen, Last Seen, and Status (active/inactive) for every recorded assignment.

Above the table:

- A **search** box matches against interface name, IP address, MAC address, gateway, or DNS servers.
- **Assignment** filters to `dhcp`, `static`, `vpn`, `link-local`, or `unknown`.
- **Interface** filters to one of the interfaces seen on this device.
- **IP Type** filters to IPv4 or IPv6.
- **Active only** limits the list to currently-assigned addresses.
- **Since** / **Until** date fields narrow the list to assignments last seen on or after, or first seen on or before, the chosen dates.

Use **Clear filters** to reset all of the above, and **Refresh** to re-fetch the latest history from the API. Results are paginated in the console (25 rows per page); the underlying fetch pulls up to 500 records at a time.

---

sections.heading: IP Assignment Types
sections.text:
| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `dhcp` | Address assigned by a DHCP server (detected via lease file inspection or OS commands) |
| `static` | Manually configured address (inferred when no DHCP lease evidence is found) |
| `vpn` | Address assigned by a VPN tunnel (detected by interface name heuristics) |
| `link-local` | Auto-configured link-local address (169.254.x.x for IPv4, fe80:: for IPv6) |
| `unknown` | Assignment method could not be determined |

sections.heading: IP Types
sections.text:
| Type | Description |
|---|---|
| `ipv4` | IPv4 address |
| `ipv6` | IPv6 address |

sections.heading: IP History Record Fields
sections.text:
| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | UUID | Unique identifier for the IP history record |
| `deviceId` | UUID | Device the IP was observed on |
| `orgId` | UUID | Organization the device belongs to |
| `interfaceName` | string (max 100) | Network interface name (e.g., `eth0`, `Wi-Fi`, `Ethernet`) |
| `ipAddress` | string (max 45) | The IP address |
| `ipType` | string | `ipv4` or `ipv6` |
| `assignmentType` | enum | One of `dhcp`, `static`, `vpn`, `link-local`, `unknown` |
| `macAddress` | string (max 64) | MAC address of the interface (e.g., `00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E`) -- widened to accommodate longer hardware address formats such as Teredo/ISATAP/InfiniBand |
| `subnetMask` | string (max 45) | Subnet mask or prefix length |
| `gateway` | string (max 45) | Default gateway address |
| `dnsServers` | string[] | DNS server addresses (up to 8) |
| `firstSeen` | datetime | When this IP was first observed on this interface |
| `lastSeen` | datetime | When this IP was most recently confirmed active |
| `isActive` | boolean | Whether the IP is currently assigned to the interface |
| `deactivatedAt` | datetime | When the IP was removed from the interface (null if still active) |
| `createdAt` | datetime | When the record was created |
| `updatedAt` | datetime | When the record was last updated |

---

sections.heading: How IP Changes Are Detected
sections.text:
1. **Agent collects current network state**

   During each heartbeat, the agent's IP tracking subsystem calls the inventory collector to enumerate all active network interfaces and their IP addresses. Loopback and down interfaces are skipped. For each interface with an IP address, the agent records the interface name, IP address, IP type, MAC address, and inferred assignment type.

2. **Assignment type is determined heuristically**

   The agent uses platform-specific heuristics to classify how each IP was assigned:

   **VPN Detection:**
   The interface name is checked against known VPN interface prefixes and keywords: `tun`, `tap`, `wg`, `ppp`, `utun`, `vpn`, `tailscale`, `zerotier`, `wireguard`, `openvpn`, `anyconnect`, `globalprotect`, `fortinet`, `l2tp`, `pptp`, `ipsec`, `protonvpn`, `nordlynx`, `hamachi`.

   **Link-Local Detection:**
   IPv4 addresses in the `169.254.0.0/16` range and IPv6 link-local unicast addresses are classified as `link-local`.

   **DHCP Detection:**
   The agent checks for DHCP lease evidence using OS-specific methods:

   - **Linux**: Scans lease files in `/run/systemd/netif/leases/`, `/var/lib/NetworkManager/`, `/var/lib/dhcp/`, and `/var/lib/dhclient/` for matching interface name and IP address.
   - **macOS**: Runs `ipconfig getpacket <interface>` and checks for `yiaddr` or `lease_time` in the output.
   - **Windows**: Runs the PowerShell `Get-NetIPInterface` cmdlet (chosen over `ipconfig /all` because its `.NET` enum values are always English regardless of OS locale) and checks whether the matching interface reports DHCP as enabled.
   - **Fallback**: If no explicit evidence is found, common interface prefixes (`eth`, `en`, `eno`, `ens`, `enp`, `wlan` on Linux/macOS; `Ethernet`, `Wi-Fi`, `WLAN` on Windows) with private IP addresses are assumed to be DHCP.

   Anything that does not match VPN, link-local, or DHCP criteria is classified as `static`.

3. **Delta is computed against previous state**

   The agent maintains a local state file (`ip_state.json`) in its data directory. On each heartbeat, it compares the current IP snapshot against the saved state:

   - **Changed IPs**: Addresses that are new (not present in the previous state) or whose metadata has changed (assignment type, MAC address, subnet mask, gateway, or DNS servers).
   - **Removed IPs**: Addresses that were in the previous state but are no longer present.
   - **Current IPs**: The full set of currently active IP assignments (used for `lastSeen` timestamp updates).

   The current state is then saved to disk for the next comparison.

4. **Update is sent in the heartbeat payload**

   The IP history update is included as the `ipHistoryUpdate` field in the heartbeat request body:

```json
   {
     "ipHistoryUpdate": {
       "currentIPs": [...],
       "changedIPs": [...],
       "removedIPs": [...],
       "detectedAt": "2026-03-02T14:30:00Z"
     }
   }
```

5. **API processes the delta transactionally**

   The API's `processDeviceIPHistoryUpdate` service handles the update inside a database transaction:

   - **Removed IPs**: Matching active records are marked `isActive = false` with `deactivatedAt` set to the detection timestamp.
   - **Changed IPs (existing)**: If an active record already exists for the interface/IP/type combination, its metadata (assignment type, MAC, subnet, gateway, DNS) and `lastSeen` timestamp are updated.
   - **Changed IPs (new)**: New records are inserted with `firstSeen` and `lastSeen` set to the detection timestamp.
   - **Current IPs**: All matching active records have their `lastSeen` timestamp refreshed.
   - **Bootstrap**: If the device has no active IP history records but the agent reports `currentIPs`, all current IPs are treated as new records. This seeds the initial history for newly enrolled devices.

Each IP history entry is deduplicated by the composite key of `interfaceName + ipAddress + ipType`. If a device has the same IP on the same interface, only one active record exists. Metadata changes (e.g., gateway change) update the existing record rather than creating a new one.

---

sections.heading: Querying IP History
sections.text: Use the IP history API endpoint to retrieve historical IP assignments for a device.

sections.heading: GET /devices/:id/ip-history
sections.text:
Returns IP history records for a device, ordered by `firstSeen` descending (most recent first).

**Query parameters:**

| Parameter | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `limit` | integer | 100 | Maximum number of records to return (1-500) |
| `offset` | integer | 0 | Number of records to skip for pagination |
| `active_only` | boolean | false | If `true`, only return currently active IP assignments |

**Response (200):**

```json
{
  "deviceId": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "count": 3,
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "f5e6d7c8-...",
      "deviceId": "a1b2c3d4-...",
      "orgId": "11223344-...",
      "interfaceName": "Ethernet",
      "ipAddress": "10.0.5.42",
      "ipType": "ipv4",
      "assignmentType": "dhcp",
      "macAddress": "00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E",
      "subnetMask": "255.255.255.0",
      "gateway": "10.0.5.1",
      "dnsServers": ["10.0.5.1", "8.8.8.8"],
      "firstSeen": "2026-02-15T08:00:00.000Z",
      "lastSeen": "2026-03-02T14:30:00.000Z",
      "isActive": true,
      "deactivatedAt": null,
      "createdAt": "2026-02-15T08:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-03-02T14:30:00.000Z"
    },
    {
      "id": "a9b8c7d6-...",
      "deviceId": "a1b2c3d4-...",
      "orgId": "11223344-...",
      "interfaceName": "Ethernet",
      "ipAddress": "192.168.1.100",
      "ipType": "ipv4",
      "assignmentType": "dhcp",
      "macAddress": "00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E",
      "subnetMask": "255.255.255.0",
      "gateway": "192.168.1.1",
      "dnsServers": ["192.168.1.1"],
      "firstSeen": "2026-01-10T12:00:00.000Z",
      "lastSeen": "2026-02-14T23:59:00.000Z",
      "isActive": false,
      "deactivatedAt": "2026-02-15T08:00:00.000Z",
      "createdAt": "2026-01-10T12:00:00.000Z",
      "updatedAt": "2026-02-15T08:00:00.000Z"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

sections.heading: API Reference
sections.text:
| Method | Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `GET` | `/devices/:id/ip-history` | Retrieve IP history records for a device (requires `organization`, `partner`, or `system` scope) |
| `POST` | `/agents/:id/heartbeat` | Agent heartbeat containing `ipHistoryUpdate` field (agent auth required) |

---

sections.heading: Heartbeat Payload Schema
sections.text:
The `ipHistoryUpdate` object within the heartbeat payload uses this structure for each IP entry:

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `interfaceName` | string | Yes | Network interface name (1-100 characters) |
| `ipAddress` | string | Yes | Valid IPv4 or IPv6 address (max 45 characters) |
| `ipType` | enum | No | `ipv4` or `ipv6` (auto-detected from address if omitted) |
| `assignmentType` | enum | No | `dhcp`, `static`, `vpn`, `link-local`, or `unknown` |
| `macAddress` | string | No | MAC address (max 64 characters) |
| `subnetMask` | string | No | Subnet mask (max 45 characters) |
| `gateway` | string | No | Default gateway (max 45 characters) |
| `dnsServers` | string[] | No | DNS server addresses (max 8 entries, each max 45 characters) |

The `ipHistoryUpdate` wrapper object contains:

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `currentIPs` | array | All IP addresses currently assigned (used to refresh `lastSeen`) |
| `changedIPs` | array | New or modified IP assignments |
| `removedIPs` | array | IP assignments that are no longer present |
| `detectedAt` | ISO 8601 datetime | When the agent detected the changes |

Each array can contain up to 100 entries.

---

sections.heading: Database Indexes
sections.text:
The `device_ip_history` table has the following indexes for efficient querying:

| Index | Columns | Use Case |
|---|---|---|
| `device_ip_history_device_id_idx` | `device_id` | Query all IP history for a specific device |
| `device_ip_history_org_id_idx` | `org_id` | Query all IP history across an organization |
| `device_ip_history_ip_address_idx` | `ip_address` | Find which device had a specific IP address |
| `device_ip_history_first_seen_idx` | `first_seen` | Filter by when IPs were first observed |
| `device_ip_history_last_seen_idx` | `last_seen` | Filter by when IPs were last confirmed |
| `device_ip_history_is_active_idx` | `is_active` | Filter active vs. deactivated records |
| `device_ip_history_ip_time_idx` | `ip_address`, `first_seen`, `last_seen` | Find which device had a specific IP at a specific time |

---

sections.heading: No IP history records for a device
sections.text:
- Verify the agent is online and sending heartbeats. IP history data is included in the heartbeat payload.
- Check that the `ipHistoryUpdate` field is present in the heartbeat body. If the agent detects no network interfaces with IP addresses, the field is omitted.
- On the first heartbeat after enrollment, the API bootstraps initial records from the `currentIPs` array. If `currentIPs` is empty, no records are created.

sections.heading: All IPs show as "static" when they should be "dhcp"
sections.text:
- The agent uses heuristics to detect DHCP assignments. On Linux, it checks lease files in standard locations (`/run/systemd/netif/leases/`, `/var/lib/NetworkManager/`, `/var/lib/dhcp/`). If your DHCP client stores leases in a non-standard location, the detection may fail.
- On macOS, the agent runs `ipconfig getpacket <interface>`. If the command is not available or returns an error, the fallback heuristic (private IP on common interface prefix) is used.
- On Windows, the agent runs the PowerShell `Get-NetIPInterface` cmdlet. If the command times out (2-second limit), detection falls back to the interface name heuristic.

sections.heading: IP history shows duplicate entries
sections.text:
- Each IP assignment is uniquely identified by the combination of `interfaceName`, `ipAddress`, and `ipType`. If you see what appear to be duplicates, they likely differ in one of these fields (e.g., the same IP on different interfaces, or the same interface name with IPv4 and IPv6 variants).
- Deactivated records (where `isActive = false`) are preserved for historical reference. The same IP can appear multiple times with different `firstSeen`/`lastSeen` ranges if the address was removed and later reassigned.

sections.heading: IP changes are delayed
sections.text:
- IP history is collected during each heartbeat cycle (default: every 60 seconds). Changes are detected by comparing the current network state against the locally saved state file.
- If the agent is restarted, the state file is reloaded from disk. If the state file was lost or corrupted, the next heartbeat will treat all current IPs as new, which may trigger a bootstrap of the full current state.

sections.heading: "Invalid IP address format" validation errors
sections.text:
- IPv6 addresses with zone IDs (e.g., `fe80::1%eth0`) have the zone ID stripped before validation. If validation still fails, the IP address format is not recognized by Node.js `isIP()`.
- Ensure IP addresses do not contain whitespace or other unexpected characters.

title: Linked Profiles
description: Link the multiple OS installs of one physical machine (multi-boot) so their device records are managed as related boot profiles.

sections.text:
A physical machine that dual-boots or multi-boots runs one Breeze agent per operating system, so the same hardware shows up as several separate device records — and only one can ever be online at a time. **Linked Profiles** lets you tie those records together as boot profiles of a single machine so they're managed as a related group.

Linking is non-destructive: each profile keeps its own inventory, history, agent, and detail page. Grouping only changes how the records are presented and gives you one place to see every OS install on the machine.

Reach it at **Device detail → Linked Profiles**.

Linking, unlinking, and dissolving a group require the `devices.write` (or `devices.delete` for dissolve) permission and pass an MFA check. Every change is audit-logged.

---

sections.heading: What the tab shows
sections.text:
If the device is not part of a group, the tab explains that multi-boot machines run a separate agent per OS and points you to the **Link as multi-boot** bulk action on the device list.

Once the device is in a group, the tab lists every member profile with:

| Column | Description |
|---|---|
| **Profile** | Display name (or hostname), with the hostname beneath it. The current device is marked "This device". |
| **OS** | Operating system type and version for that boot profile. |
| **Status** | Online (green) or the profile's reported state. Only one profile is normally online at a time. |
| **Agent** | The Breeze agent version running on that install. |
| **Last seen** | Relative time since the profile last checked in. |

A badge shows the profile count, and the group's name (or a generic "Linked boot profiles" heading if none was set).

---

sections.heading: Linking profiles
sections.text:
Profiles are linked from the **device list**, not the detail tab:

1. On the devices page, select **two or more** device records that belong to the same physical machine.

2. Choose **Link as multi-boot** from the bulk actions menu.

3. The devices are grouped. All must belong to the **same organization** and be currently unlinked — the API rejects the request otherwise.

A group holds between **2 and 10** profiles. On the device list, an online member renders as a normal row with its offline siblings shown as thin "expected offline" strips beneath it; an all-offline group is marked with a subtle left-edge bar.

---

sections.heading: Unlinking and removing a link
sections.text:
The Linked Profiles tab hosts two actions:

- **Unlink this device** — removes just the current device from the group, leaving the other profiles linked.
- **Remove link** — dissolves the entire group, unlinking every profile.

If removing a profile would leave the group with only one member, Breeze automatically dissolves the group (a single-profile group is meaningless).

Unlinking never deletes a device or its data. It only removes the association between boot profiles.

---
