- **`/analytics`** -- Time-series queries, custom dashboards with widgets, capacity planning, SLA tracking, executive summaries, and OS distribution breakdowns.

---

sections.heading: Report Types
sections.text:
Every report has a `type` that determines which data is queried and how the output is structured.

| Type | Description | Key columns / metrics |
|------|-------------|----------------------|
| `device_inventory` | Full hardware and software asset listing per device | hostname, OS, agent version, CPU model, RAM, disk, serial number |
| `software_inventory` | All installed software across targeted devices | software name, version, publisher, install date, device hostname |
| `alert_summary` | Alert history with severity breakdown | title, severity, status, triggered/acknowledged/resolved timestamps, rule name |
| `compliance` | Device health and compliance posture | hostname, OS, status, last seen, compliance flag, identified issues |
| `performance` | Aggregated CPU, RAM, and disk metrics per device | avg/max CPU %, avg/max RAM %, avg/max disk % |
| `executive_summary` | High-level fleet overview with device counts, alert stats, OS distribution, and site breakdown (see [Executive Summary Report](#executive-summary-report)) | online/offline totals, health %, critical/high alert counts, resolution rate |
| `security_compliance_posture` | Per-control security and compliance evidence for one organization, built for cyber-insurance applications and vendor security questionnaires | EDR/AV coverage, disk encryption %, firewall %, patch currency %, password policy, local-admin exposure, MFA/PAM posture, backup, DNS filtering, optional CIS pass-rate (see [Security & Compliance Posture Report](#security--compliance-posture-report)) |
| `identity_access_review` | A month of Microsoft 365 sign-in and identity activity: identity inventory, conditional-access policy posture, dormant accounts, admin sign-ins, MFA registration status, and which remote-access client (if any) was running on each device | interactive sign-in counts, conditional-access coverage, dormant-account list, admin sign-in detail, MFA registration rate |
| `vulnerability_management` | Findings-level vulnerability detail: open vulnerabilities, accepted/mitigated exceptions, remediation ranking, and vulnerabilities that are actively exploited in the wild or have a high exploit probability | open/accepted/mitigated counts, remediation ranking, known-exploited and high-probability findings |
| `endpoint_management_review` | Device enrollment and compliance inventory pulled from Microsoft Intune, plus license-seat usage and a compliance-trend chart | enrollment/compliance counts, license seat usage, daily compliance trend |
| `threat_detection_review` | A record of threat detections for the period, with resolution status and the vendor's recommendation text | detection count, resolution status, recommendation text |
| `ticket_sla_attainment` | Response and resolution SLA attainment for a period, recalculated from each ticket's own timestamps rather than read off the stored breach flags, grouped by organization, priority, technician or category (see [Business Reports](#business-reports)) | response/resolution attainment %, missed targets, tickets with no SLA target |
| `technician_time_billability` | Logged time against an assumed weekly capacity, the billable / included / non-billable split, and how much billable time has been approved and billed — billable value reported per currency (see [Business Reports](#business-reports)) | utilization %, billable %, billing conversion %, logged/billable/non-billable minutes, billable value per currency |
| `ar_aging` | Unpaid invoice balances bucketed current / 1–30 / 31–60 / 61–90 / 90+ days past due, one set of totals per currency (see [Business Reports](#business-reports)) | outstanding balance per bucket, open invoice count, no-due-date balance, other open balance |
| `ai_usage_by_client` | AI requests, tokens, Breeze cost and the amount billable to each client for a period, split into billed, unbilled and unpriced (see [AI usage chargeback](/features/ai-usage-chargeback/)) | requests, tokens, Breeze cost, billable amount, billed and unbilled amount, unpriced usage |
| `mrr_renewals` | Contract monthly recurring revenue as of the run, contracts up for renewal, and 12 months of billed recurring revenue, one set of totals per currency (see [MRR & renewals](#mrr--renewals-mrr_renewals)) | MRR, ARR, base and overage, paused and pending activation, renewals due, billed recurring revenue per month |
| `quote_win_rate` | Share of sent quotes that were won, counted per opportunity (a quote and all its revisions), with the still-open count beside it, and quoted and won values per currency (see [Quote win rate](#quote-win-rate-quote_win_rate)) | win rate, close rate, viewed rate, median days to win and to loss, quoted and won value per currency |
| `client_profitability` | Per-client billed revenue, cost from the invoice-line cost snapshot with its coverage, the revenue mix and technician hours for a period, with an optional estimated contribution after labor (see [Client profitability](#client-profitability-client_profitability)) | revenue, cost, gross margin, margin %, cost coverage %, unknown-cost revenue, revenue mix, hours by coverage, effective service rate, estimated contribution after labor |

The four evidence-review report types — `identity_access_review`, `vulnerability_management`, `endpoint_management_review` and `threat_detection_review` — are built from previously synced data only — they never make a live call to the source integration while generating, so a scheduled run never depends on a third party being up. If a required source (Microsoft 365 sync, a vulnerability feed, or the Huntress integration) has never completed a sync, the affected figures render as **not measured** rather than zero, and the report states the sync gap explicitly. `identity_access_review` and `endpoint_management_review` require an M365 tenant sync connected (`endpoint_management_review` additionally needs Intune enrolled); `vulnerability_management` requires a connected vulnerability scan/feed source; `threat_detection_review` requires a connected and synced Huntress integration. These four report types are not available for customer self-service in the portal.

The three business report types below read only Breeze's own ticket, time and invoice data and depend on no integration.

---

sections.heading: Report Configuration
sections.text: When creating a saved report, you provide a `config` object that controls date ranges, filters, column selection, and sorting.

sections.heading: Date Range Presets
sections.text:
The `config.dateRange` object supports preset shortcuts or custom boundaries:

| Preset | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `last_7_days` | Data from the past 7 days |
| `last_30_days` | Data from the past 30 days |
| `last_90_days` | Data from the past 90 days |
| `custom` | Use the explicit `start` and `end` ISO date strings |

A preset is a rolling window evaluated when each run generates, so a weekly report with `last_7_days` covers the seven days before that run. Explicit `start`/`end` values take precedence over a preset. In the Executive Summary the window bounds the alert figures (alerts in window, severity counts, resolution rate); the device figures are a snapshot of the fleet at generation time.

sections.heading: Filters
sections.text:
The `config.filters` object narrows the data:

| Filter | Applies to | Accepts |
|--------|-----------|---------|
| `siteIds` | device_inventory, compliance | Array of site UUIDs |
| `deviceIds` | software_inventory | Array of device UUIDs |
| `osTypes` | device_inventory | `windows`, `macos`, `linux` |
| `status` | alert_summary | Array of status strings |
| `severity` | alert_summary | Array of severity strings |

sections.heading: Output Formats
sections.text:
| Format | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `csv` | Comma-separated values (default) |
| `pdf` | Formatted PDF document |
| `excel` | Excel spreadsheet (.xlsx) |

sections.heading: Schedule Details and Email Recipients
sections.text:
For recurring reports, the **Schedule and delivery** panel in the report builder (also available as `config.schedule` and `config.emailRecipients` via the API) controls exactly when the report runs and who gets emailed the result:

| Field | Builder UI label | Applies to | Format |
|-------|------------------|-----------|--------|
| `schedule.time` | Run time | All recurring cadences | 24-hour `HH:MM`, e.g. `09:00` |
| `schedule.day` | Day of week | `weekly` | Weekday name, e.g. `monday` |
| `schedule.date` | Day of month | `monthly` | Day of month, `1`-`31` |
| `emailRecipients` | Email distribution list | Any recurring cadence | Array of up to 50 email addresses |

See [Scheduling](#scheduling) below for how these are evaluated and what recipients receive.

---

sections.heading: Generating Reports
sections.text:
Breeze supports two generation flows: ad-hoc (stateless) and saved (tracked with run history).

**Customers can generate these themselves:**
  The **Security & Compliance Posture** and **Executive Summary** reports can also be generated by the customer from the [customer portal](/features/portal/#reports), with the same PDF and CSV downloads — once you turn **Reports** visibility on for that organization. It is off by default.

sections.heading: Ad-hoc Generation
Saved Report Generation
sections.text:
For saved reports, trigger generation with `POST /reports/:id/generate`. This creates a **report run**, computes the data, and stores the result as a point-in-time snapshot -- all in the same request, so the response comes back already `completed` (or `failed`). The snapshot is what you download later, so the file always reflects the data as of when the run executed rather than re-querying live.

1. Create a saved report definition with `POST /reports` (see the API reference below).
2. Trigger generation with `POST /reports/:id/generate`. The response returns the new `runId` with `status: "completed"` once the snapshot is stored.
3. Download the result with `GET /reports/runs/:runId/download?format=csv` (or `pdf` / `excel`).

```bash
# Trigger generation for a saved report
curl -X POST /api/v1/reports/REPORT_UUID/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN"
```

Response:

```json
{
  "message": "Report generation started",
  "runId": "a1b2c3d4-...",
  "status": "pending"
}
```

---

sections.heading: Scheduling
sections.text:
Saved reports support recurring schedules. When you set the `schedule` field, the report will be generated automatically on the configured cadence.

| Schedule | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| `one_time` | No recurring generation (default). Must be triggered manually. |
| `daily` | Generated once per day |
| `weekly` | Generated once per week |
| `monthly` | Generated once per month |

Set the schedule when creating or updating a report:

```bash
curl -X POST /api/v1/reports \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Weekly Compliance Report",
    "type": "compliance",
    "orgId": "ORG_UUID",
    "schedule": "weekly",
    "format": "pdf",
    "config": {
      "filters": { "siteIds": ["SITE_UUID"] }
    }
  }'
```

Scheduled runs fire in the organization's local time zone (falling back to the partner's time zone, then UTC if neither is configured), pinned to the `schedule.time` / `schedule.day` / `schedule.date` values from `config.schedule` -- see [Schedule Details and Email Recipients](#schedule-details-and-email-recipients) above.

A newly saved recurring report first runs at its first scheduled occurrence **after** it was saved -- a monthly report for the 1st that is saved on the 21st first runs (and emails its recipients) on the next 1st. To get a copy straight away, use **Generate now** on the report (`POST /reports/:id/generate`).

  The `lastGeneratedAt` timestamp on the report record is updated each time a generation run is triggered, regardless of whether the run ultimately succeeds or fails.

sections.heading: Email Delivery
sections.text:
Add addresses to the **Email distribution list** (or `config.emailRecipients`) to have each scheduled run emailed automatically, in addition to appearing in the reports list:

- **PDF-format** reports attach the same branded PDF you'd download from the run. If it's larger than 5 MB or fails to render, the email falls back to a link into Breeze instead of an attachment.
- **CSV and Excel-format** reports attach the data as a CSV file.
- The email leads with a one-line trend summary when a prior run exists to compare against, for example "Posture score 79 -- up from 74 last run."

The reports list also shows the next scheduled run time (e.g. "Next: Mon, Jul 6, 9:00 AM") and a recipient count badge on recurring reports.

sections.heading: Scheduled Auto-Evidence
sections.text:
You can also attach one of the report types above to a [service deliverable](/features/contracts/#service-deliverables) as its evidence source. Set this up once, partner-wide, on a deliverable template item, and every organization the template applies to gets a period-correct evidence artifact generated automatically -- no technician has to remember to run and attach a report each period. Each generated artifact is reviewed before it's shown to the customer, and only becomes visible in the portal once its deliverable occurrence is marked **Delivered**.

---

sections.heading: Report Run Status Lifecycle
sections.text:
Each time a saved report is generated, a **report run** record tracks the process through a status lifecycle.

| Status | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `pending` | The run has been created and is queued for processing |
| `running` | The report is actively being generated |
| `completed` | Generation succeeded; `outputUrl` contains the download path |
| `failed` | Generation failed; `errorMessage` contains the reason |

The run record stores:

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `id` | Unique run identifier (UUID) |
| `reportId` | The parent saved report definition |
| `status` | Current lifecycle status |
| `startedAt` | Timestamp when processing began |
| `completedAt` | Timestamp when processing finished (success or failure) |
| `outputUrl` | Download path for the generated file (set on `completed`) |
| `errorMessage` | Error description (set on `failed`) |
| `rowCount` | Number of data rows in the output |

---

sections.heading: Security & Compliance Posture Report
sections.text:
The **Security & Compliance Posture** report (`security_compliance_posture`) packages your security evidence for one organization into a single document -- purpose-built for filling out **cyber-insurance applications** and answering **vendor security questionnaires**. It joins the security data Breeze already collects into per-control answers with percent-implemented rollups: EDR/MDR and native antivirus coverage, the list of unprotected devices, disk-encryption and host-firewall coverage, patch currency, antivirus-definition freshness, password-complexity posture, local-admin exposure, MFA and privileged-access posture, backup coverage, DNS filtering, identity-provider connection, and an optional CIS hardening pass-rate.

It is scoped to a single organization (with an optional site filter) and is honest about gaps: a control that hasn't been assessed is reported as **N/A**, never as a misleading 0% or a falsely favorable score. The same principle applies to **stale readings**: a device whose firewall/encryption status hasn't been reported within the freshness window (default **30 days**, configurable 1–365 via the report's security-status age setting) is counted as **unknown** for those controls — its cells show "no data" instead of a months-old pass/fail being scored as current. The summary reports separate firewall-unknown and encryption-unknown device counts, mirroring how unmeasured patch data is handled. The PDF renders as a branded scorecard (overall score out of 100 with a STRONG / GOOD / FAIR / AT RISK band and a per-control grid) and carries point-in-time, not-a-certification disclaimers.

The **Security products in use** inventory follows the same principle. A product is listed with the number of devices it is installed on, and -- where Breeze has per-device antivirus evidence -- how many of those devices actually have **real-time protection switched on**. A product installed on 200 devices with real-time protection active on only one reads as `200 devices, 1 with real-time protection on`, so the inventory can no longer imply full coverage that the report's own metric grid contradicts. The extra count is shown only when the protected subset is smaller than the install count; products whose evidence comes from an integration rather than per-device status (DNS filtering, backup, Microsoft 365) show the install count alone.

The PDF also includes a **Recommended actions** section generated from whichever controls are currently failing, and a plain-language **glossary** so a non-technical reader -- an insurance underwriter, a customer's compliance contact -- can follow it without help. When a prior run exists to compare against, the scorecard shows how the score has moved since then (for example "+5 since Jun 1"). The cover carries your logo and name if [partner branding](/features/branding/) is configured; otherwise it uses the standard Breeze mark.

  You can start this report straight from the report builder by choosing the **Security & Compliance Posture (Insurance)** template card. The direct-create dialog asks whether backup coverage is required and -- like every template dialog from v0.124.0 -- when the report runs and who receives it: the schedule, the organization contacts to send it to, and any extra email addresses. The name, date range and output format take the template defaults, and you can change everything afterwards by editing the report; the edit page shows the same form and keeps the recipients you chose. Once created, it generates and downloads exactly like the rest of your reports (it appears in your reports list as "Security & Compliance Posture").

  **Backup coverage.** Reports created from the template card treat backup as *optional* by default, which suits workstation-oriented assessments. While it is optional the PDF still lists any detected backup products and labels missing backup as `Not required`, without raising a remediation recommendation. Tick the option to score backup as a required control instead.

  **API callers.** `POST /reports`, `PUT /reports/:id`, and `POST /reports/generate` take a `config` object: `backupRequired`, `sites` (limit to specific sites), `windowDays` (recency window for "current" patch/AV data), `minPasswordLength`, `maxLocalAdmins`, `maxAvDefinitionsAgeDays`, `maxSecurityStatusAgeDays` (freshness cutoff for firewall/encryption readings, 1–365), and `includeCis` (add the CIS pass-rate section). Anything you leave out falls back to an insurance-sensible default: backup **required**, a 30-day window, 8-character minimum password length, at most 2 local admins, 7-day AV-definition freshness, a 30-day firewall/encryption freshness cutoff, and the CIS section included.

  Note the asymmetry in that last list -- the template card opts *out* of required backup, but omitting `backupRequired` from an API call opts *in*. That is deliberate: it is also what keeps reports created before this option existed scoring backup exactly as they always did.

---

sections.heading: Executive Summary Report
sections.text:
The **Executive Summary** report (`executive_summary`) is built for handing to a customer at a quarterly business review. Its PDF leads with a designed cover: a fleet-health scorecard, device and alert metrics, OS and site composition, and a **Recommended actions** section -- the same trend-aware, branded cover treatment as the [Security & Compliance Posture](#security--compliance-posture-report) report, including the partner logo when [branding](/features/branding/) is configured and a score-change chip when a prior run exists to compare against.

---

sections.heading: Business Reports
sections.text: Several report types cover the PSA side of the business — service performance, technician time, money owed, contract revenue, and quote outcomes. Unlike the report types above, they are **internal**: they are for MSP staff only (organization-scope users, and API or MCP keys, never see them, even when they hold the underlying permission), they never appear in a customer's portal, and generating one requires the type's own permission on top of `reports:read`/`reports:write` -- `tickets:read` for ticket SLA attainment, `time_entries:read` **and** `tickets:read` for technician time & billability, `invoices:read` for AR aging, `contracts:read` for MRR & renewals, `quotes:read` for quote win rate, and `invoices:read` **and** `time_entries:read` for client profitability.

sections.heading: Ownership: one organization, or all of them
sections.text:
A business report can be owned by a single organization or by the partner. A **partner-owned** report covers every organization the MSP manages, resolved live at each run against the partner's **active and trial** organizations -- suspended, archived and deleted organizations (and the internal quick-support organization) are excluded, and are listed in the report's own notes when they are. Ownership is chosen when the report is created and cannot be changed afterwards; create a second report if you need both views. In the reports list, a partner-owned report carries a **Partner-wide** badge and appears both in the **All organizations** view and when an organization is selected (for users with access to all organizations).

Creating or running a partner-owned report requires a partner-scope login with access to **all** organizations. A user restricted to selected organizations is refused: aggregating customers they cannot open individually would be an escalation, not a convenience. Business reports -- org-owned or partner-owned -- deliver to email addresses entered on the report itself; they cannot be delivered to a customer contact.

sections.heading: Ticket SLA attainment (`ticket_sla_attainment`)
sections.text:
Measures the share of support tickets created in the period that met their response and resolution targets. Attainment is **recalculated** from each ticket's own timestamps and recorded paused minutes against its own targets, rather than read off the stored breach flags. Only support work is measured -- planned work is excluded. Tickets with no target set are never counted as met or missed; they are reported as their own figure.

Grouping is by organization, priority, technician or category; left unset, it defaults to organization for a partner-owned report and priority for an org-owned one. Two limits are disclosed on the report itself:

- **Paused time is a lifetime total** -- a ticket paused after its first reply has that pause counted against the response clock too, which slightly flatters response attainment.
- **The technician axis is the ticket's current assignee** -- reassignment history isn't tracked.

sections.heading: Technician time & billability (`technician_time_billability`)
sections.text:
Measures logged time against capacity, and how much of it converts to revenue.

- **Utilization** is logged minutes ÷ capacity minutes. Capacity is a report setting -- an assumed weekly-hours figure (1–80, default 40) -- prorated over the working days in the period. This assumes uniform capacity: PTO and part-time schedules aren't modeled, so an individual technician's figure can mislead even when the team figure is sound. At organization scope the denominator is still each technician's whole capacity, so the figure is a *share* of their capacity spent on that organization, not their overall utilization.
- **Billable share** is billable minutes ÷ logged minutes, split three ways -- billable, included in plan, and non-billable.
- **Billing conversion** is approved-and-billed minutes ÷ billable minutes. It is deliberately not called "realization" -- there is no fee-schedule baseline to compute financial realization against.

Technicians with no time in the period are listed at 0% rather than omitted -- dropping them would inflate the team average. Billable value is reported **once per currency**, never summed across currencies; billable minutes with no hourly rate or currency are called out and excluded from that total. An organization-scoped report covers ticket-linked time only -- time logged with no organization has no organization to be scoped to.

sections.heading: AR aging (`ar_aging`)
sections.text:
Buckets unpaid invoice balances by how far past due they are: current, 1–30, 31–60, 61–90 and 90+ days, plus two reconciliation buckets:

- **No due date** -- an open balance on an invoice with no due date is aged into its own bucket, never silently into "current".
- **Other open balance** -- an invoice carrying a balance in an unexpected status appears here rather than vanishing, so buckets plus this figure always reconcile to total AR.

Aging is measured as of the moment the report runs, in the report owner's resolved timezone, unless an explicit as-of date is set. **The as-of date moves only the aging reference date -- it does not reconstruct historical balances or undo payments recorded after it.** An optional note can also list invoices that were fully paid month-to-date as of that date; it's informational and never moves a bucket. Totals are reported **once per currency, with no conversion** -- there is deliberately no combined figure, because an FX-converted headline would be wrong the day after it was produced.

sections.heading: MRR & renewals (`mrr_renewals`)
sections.text:
Reports contract revenue as of the moment the report runs. Contracts keep no status history, so this report has **no period and no as-of date** -- it cannot be backdated, and sending `period` or `asOf` returns `400`. Dates are compared as UTC calendar dates, the same "today" contract billing uses.

**What MRR counts.** A contract counts while it is **in term**: started, not yet past its end date, and either still billing or in a final term that is already billed and still being served. Each contract's monthly figure is its billing-period value divided by the billing interval, rounded in the contract's own currency, and is split into:

- **Base** -- the recurring lines at their billing prices.
- **Overage** -- billed allowance overage, counted from today's device and seat quantities.
- **Final term billed** -- a contract whose last period is already invoiced (for example, a one-year contract billed annually in advance) counts at what that invoice billed. That figure is not split into base and overage.

Per-device and per-seat quantities are counted live when the report runs, so MRR is an estimate of the next invoices, not a billed amount. ARR is MRR × 12. Totals are reported **once per currency, with no conversion**.

**What sits beside MRR, never in it.** Paused contracts and draft contracts (pending activation) are valued the same way and shown next to MRR. Open-ended contracts (no end date) are part of MRR and are also shown as their own figure. Two reconciliation lists make sure nothing disappears silently:

- **Active, not in term** -- contracts marked active that are not counted, with the reason: they start later, they ended and are waiting to be marked expired, or their final period has not been billed.
- **Could not be valued** -- contracts left out of MRR because a line bills a device group that could not be evaluated, a deleted site, or a final-term invoice that is missing or voided. The report says how many were excluded.

**Renewals.** In-term contracts whose end date falls inside the renewal window (30, 60, 90 or 180 days from the run date, default 90) are listed by end date, with auto-renewing and manually renewed MRR totalled separately, and the date the advance renewal notice was sent for that end date.

**Billed recurring revenue.** The 12 calendar months ending with the current month (in the report owner's time zone) show what issued invoices billed for contracts. A billing period's line is spread evenly over the months it covers; a contract line added to an invoice by hand lands in the invoice's month. Hour-block overage is usage, not recurring revenue, and is left out. The current month is marked partial. This series is **billed** revenue, not MRR.

MRR has no stored history before the report first runs. Schedule it monthly, and each run's PDF compares MRR with the previous run ("vs previous observation").

sections.heading: Quote win rate (`quote_win_rate`)
sections.text:
Reports how many of the quotes you sent were won. The unit is an **opportunity**, not a quote row: a quote and every revision of it (decline, revise, send again) is one opportunity, and its outcome is the outcome of the latest version that was actually sent. A draft revision that has not been sent leaves the sent version's outcome standing.

**Which opportunities are in the period.** An opportunity belongs to the period in which its **first** version was sent. A quote that was never sent is not counted. The period is resolved in the report owner's time zone.

**Outcomes.** *Won* is accepted or converted, *lost* is declined, *expired* is a quote past its expiry date, and *open* is still waiting. A quote that is still marked sent or viewed after its expiry date counts as expired when the report runs (UTC calendar day), even if the nightly expiry job has not touched it yet.

**The headline.** Win rate is **won ÷ (won + lost + expired)** -- decided opportunities only -- and the number of opportunities still open is printed beside it, so a recent period that has not played out yet does not look worse than it will end up. With nothing decided, the win rate prints **N/A**, never 0%. Close rate (won ÷ all opportunities), viewed rate and the median days from first send to a win and to a loss sit underneath.

**Values.** Quoted and won values are **pre-tax**, taken from the latest sent version, and reported **once per currency, with no conversion**. One-time and monthly recurring values are separate figures; an annual recurring amount is converted to a monthly one. The value win rate (won value ÷ decided value) is per currency too.

**Grouping.** Group by organization, author (the person who created the original quote) or currency. The default is organization for a partner-wide report and author for a single organization. Detail rows list each opportunity with its version count, outcome and, for declines, the reason given.

**What it does not do.** Accepted quotes create draft contracts, and this report does not follow them any further -- see **MRR & renewals** for contracts pending activation. A broken or circular revision chain is reported as a note and left out of every rate.

sections.heading: Client profitability (`client_profitability`)
sections.text:
For each client in the period: what you billed, what the billed goods and services cost you, and how much technician time the client used. Generating it needs `invoices:read` **and** `time_entries:read`.

**Billed basis.** Revenue is what **issued** invoices billed, counted on the invoice's issue date (in the report owner's time zone). Draft and void invoices are left out; a voided invoice's replacement counts once. This is billed revenue, not accrual-recognized revenue: an annual contract invoiced in January counts entirely in January. Hours are counted when they were worked, and the invoice for that work can fall in a later period.

**Cost and margin.** Cost comes from the cost recorded on each invoice line when it was created. Only top-level, customer-visible lines are counted, so a bundle's cost is counted once (on the bundle line, not again on its components). Each line's cost is quantity × recorded cost, rounded to the currency's smallest unit.

- **Unknown cost is not zero cost.** Time, hour-block overage, AI usage and most contract lines carry no recorded cost. Their revenue is reported as **unknown-cost revenue** and is left out of the margin. A line with an explicit cost of `0.00` is a known zero.
- **Gross margin** and **margin %** are measured only over lines with a recorded cost. **Cost coverage %** -- the share of revenue that has a recorded cost -- is printed beside every margin, so a client billed mostly for labor never shows a misleading margin taken from a sliver of its revenue.
- A **bundle with a component that has no recorded cost** counts as unknown cost here, and the report says how many bundles that affected. (The invoice margin panel counts the missing component as zero; this is the one place the two differ.)
- Products sold through a quote carry their cost only if the quote was accepted after quote costs began to be copied onto invoices; earlier ones count as unknown cost.

**Revenue mix.** Each line is filed by its source: **recurring** (contract lines), **labor** (time entries, and hour-block overage, which is usage), **product** (parts, catalog and bundle lines, and catalog items sold through a quote), **AI** (AI usage) and **other** (the remaining manual lines). AI lines carry no cost here; the [AI usage by client](/features/ai-usage-chargeback/) report shows what the AI cost beside the charges.

**Hours and effective service rate.** Hours are completed time entries (running timers excluded) whose start falls in the period, split into billable, included and non-billable. The **effective service rate** is (recurring + labor revenue) ÷ hours worked; product resale and AI are left out so a hardware-heavy month does not flatter a client. **Revenue per hour** is printed beside it. Both are blank when no hours were worked. Partner-wide, time entries with no organization are shown once as **unattributed time**, never spread across clients.

**Hours and currencies.** A client's hours are attributed to a currency only when all of its revenue in the period is in one currency and every one of its time entries is in that same currency. Otherwise the hours are shown once on the client and its rate and labor-estimate figures are blank. Hours are never split or repeated across currencies.

**Estimated contribution after labor (optional).** Set a uniform internal **labor cost per hour** on the report (an amount and a currency) to add an estimate:

> estimated contribution after labor = gross margin + labor and recurring revenue with no recorded cost − all completed hours × the rate

- It counts **all** completed hours -- billable, included and non-billable -- because all of them cost you.
- Recurring revenue with no recorded cost is treated as service revenue (the included time is the cost of serving a managed contract). That share is printed on its own line ("of which recurring revenue with no recorded cost"), so a resold licence billed through a contract is visible as an assumption.
- Product, AI and other revenue with no recorded cost is left out of the estimate and printed beside it.
- It is one blended rate for every technician, and it assumes no labor is already inside a line's recorded cost. Every figure that uses it is labelled **Estimated contribution after labor (uniform rate)**.
- The rate applies only to clients whose hours are attributed to the rate's currency; no FX conversion is applied. A client with revenue but no completed time logged in the period gets no estimate -- unlogged time is not a zero labor cost. With no rate set, the report shows hours only and no estimate.
- Partner-wide, a currency's rate and estimate figures are left blank when any client billed in that currency cannot have its hours attributed to it, so they always cover the same clients as the margin beside them.

The labor rate is an option of this report, not a partner setting: it is stored on the report definition, edited in the report's options, and never appears on a customer document.

Partner-wide, one detail row is stored per client and currency (plus one hours-only row for a client whose hours cannot sit on a single currency row, and one for unattributed time); one organization's report stores one row per invoice. Totals are reported **once per currency, with no conversion**.

sections.heading: What gets stored, and what gets capped
sections.text: Every total is computed in SQL over **all** matching rows. The stored detail rows -- the per-ticket, per-technician or per-invoice lines behind the totals -- are capped at 5,000 per run; a truncated detail list never implies a truncated total. A downloaded PDF shows up to 500 detail rows; CSV and Excel downloads of a stored run carry the full (capped) set as raw numeric values -- balances and rates as plain decimals, durations as minutes, percentages as fractions -- each money row tagged with a currency-code column, so a spreadsheet can total them directly. A ratio with nothing to measure (for example, no tickets with a response target) prints **N/A**, never 0%. A user whose access is limited to specific sites gets an explanatory note instead of figures, because tickets, time entries, and invoices are not tied to sites.

sections.heading: API options
sections.text:
The web options forms set the same keys. Business reports select their data by **period** and **owner** (one organization, or partner-wide) -- never by the date range, site, device, or organization filters the other report types use. Sending any of those filters returns `400`.

| Option | Applies to | Values | Default |
|--------|-----------|--------|---------|
| `period.kind` | SLA attainment, time & billability | `last_full_month`, `last_30_days`, `last_quarter`, `custom` (with `start` and `end` as `YYYY-MM-DD`; `end` is inclusive) | `last_full_month` |
| `groupBy` | SLA attainment | `organization`, `priority`, `technician`, `category` | `organization` partner-wide, `priority` for one organization |
| `includeNoSla` | SLA attainment | Include tickets with no SLA target in the detail rows | `true` |
| `groupBy` | Time & billability | `technician`, `organization`, `work_type` | `technician` |
| `weeklyCapacityHours` | Time & billability | 1-80 | `40` |
| `asOf` | AR aging | `YYYY-MM-DD` | Today |
| `groupBy` | AR aging | `organization`, `currency` | `organization` |
| `includePaidInPeriod` | AR aging | Add an informational note on invoices fully paid month-to-date (never moves a bucket) | `false` |
| `groupBy` | MRR & renewals | `organization`, `contract` | `organization` |
| `renewalHorizonDays` | MRR & renewals | `30`, `60`, `90`, `180` | `90` |
| `period.kind` | Quote win rate | `last_full_month`, `last_30_days`, `last_quarter`, `custom` (applies to each opportunity's first send date) | `last_full_month` |
| `groupBy` | Quote win rate | `organization`, `author`, `currency` | `organization` partner-wide, `author` for one organization |
| `period.kind` | Client profitability | Same values as above | `last_full_month` |
| `groupBy` | Client profitability | `organization`, `source` (revenue category) | `organization` partner-wide, `source` for one organization |
| `laborCostPerHour` | Client profitability | `{ "amount": "45.00", "currencyCode": "USD" }` -- a positive amount with at most 2 decimals (whole units for zero-decimal currencies) in a supported currency | Not set (hours only, no estimate) |

Periods and "today" are resolved in the report owner's time zone -- the organization's, then the partner's, then UTC. If the configured time zone isn't recognized, the report runs in UTC and says so.

sections.heading: Creating a partner-wide report through the API
sections.text:
Pass `"ownerScope": "partner"` and omit `orgId`. The report belongs to your partner, not to any one organization; `ownerScope` is set at creation and can't be changed later.

```bash
curl -X POST /api/v1/reports \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "Monthly SLA attainment (all customers)",
    "type": "ticket_sla_attainment",
    "ownerScope": "partner",
    "schedule": "monthly",
    "format": "pdf",
    "config": {
      "period": { "kind": "last_full_month" },
      "groupBy": "organization",
      "schedule": { "time": "08:00", "date": 1 },
      "emailRecipients": ["ops@your-msp.example.com"]
    }
  }'
```

For a one-off, `POST /reports/generate` accepts the same `ownerScope`, `type`, and `config` and returns the data inline. To run a report for a single customer instead, leave `ownerScope` out and pass `orgId` as you would for any other report type.

Scheduled business reports are delivered only to the **email distribution list** (`config.emailRecipients`); they can't be sent to organization contacts.

---

sections.heading: Multi-org reports (one per organization)
sections.text:
A multi-org report is one definition that produces a **separate copy for every organization it covers**. Each copy is sent to that organization's own contacts. It is not a combined report: combined, cross-organization reports are the partner-owned reports described under [Business Reports](#business-reports).

Only partner users with access to every organization can create or change one.

sections.heading: Creating one
sections.text:
On **New Report** (or a Hardware Lifecycle / Security & Compliance Posture template), set **Covers** to **One report per organization**, then choose which organizations it covers:

- **All organizations** (default): every current *and future* organization is included automatically. Untick any organization to exclude it. A new organization starts receiving the report within about five minutes of being created.
- **Chosen organizations**: exactly the organizations you tick.

Only active and trial organizations receive a copy. A suspended or offboarding organization's copy is archived, and it comes back automatically if the organization is reactivated.

Site, device and group filters are unavailable here, because each organization's copy covers the whole organization.

A multi-org report always runs on a schedule (daily, weekly or monthly); it can't be one-time. When you start from a one-time template, choose how often it is sent before creating it.

sections.heading: Who receives each copy
sections.text:
- **The organization's primary contact** and/or **contacts with these roles**. This rule is worked out separately in every organization.
- **Internal copies**: fixed addresses on your team, sent every organization's copy.
- The form previews the result, for example "Resolves to 23 contacts across 17 organizations · 1 organization has no customer recipient: Acme Dental". An organization with no customer recipient is always flagged, never silently skipped.

To change who receives one organization's copy, open that copy (**Edit recipients**). For each contact, choose **Follow rule**, **Always send** or **Never send**.

sections.heading: The Saved Reports list
sections.text:
On the **All organizations** view, each multi-org report is one row. Its last-run column reads, for example, *Oct 1 · 17/18 delivered · 1 no recipient*. Expand the row to see one line per organization, with these actions:

- **Run now** generates that organization's copy immediately.
- **Edit recipients** opens that organization's copy.
- **Exclude** / **Include** stops or restarts that organization's copy. An excluded copy is archived with its run history, and including it again restores the same copy.
- **Detach** turns that organization's copy into a standalone report you can edit freely. It keeps its run history and stops following the multi-org report. While that standalone copy exists, the organization stays out of the multi-org report, even if you include it again, so it never receives two copies.

**Pause** (on the row, or at the top of the expanded list) stops every organization's copy from running until you **Resume** it. A paused report is marked **Paused** in the list.

The **All · Multi-org · Single-org · Combined** chips filter the list. With one organization selected in the switcher, its copy appears as an ordinary row with a **Multi-org** badge that links to the multi-org report.

An organization's copy is locked: only its recipients can be changed there. Organization users see it marked **Managed by your MSP**.

sections.heading: Owner
sections.text: Scheduled copies run with the **owner's** access (the creator, by default). If the owner loses access to an organization, that organization's copy shows **Blocked: owner has no access** and does not run. It is never run with anyone else's access. Use **Transfer owner** on the row to hand the report to another partner user with access to every organization.

sections.heading: Downloading and Exporting
sections.text:
When a report run reaches the `completed` status, download its stored snapshot from `GET /reports/runs/:id/download`. Pass the desired format as a query parameter -- `?format=csv`, `?format=pdf`, or `?format=excel`. Because the run captured the data at generation time, the download is stable: re-downloading the same run always yields the same data. Downloading a run that hasn't completed returns `409 Conflict`.

```bash
# Download a completed run as CSV
curl "/api/v1/reports/runs/RUN_UUID/download?format=csv" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -OJ
```

CSV and Excel files are produced on the server; PDF downloads are rendered in the browser from the same snapshot (scheduled-email PDF attachments are rendered server-side instead, using the same branded layout, so the two always match). When retrieving a single report via `GET /reports/:id`, the response includes the five most recent runs, making it easy to find the latest completed download.

---

sections.heading: Report History for Inactive Organizations
sections.text:
When a customer organization is **suspended**, **churned**, **offboarding** or **archived**, its report history stays readable to the MSP: a partner user can still open the organization's saved report definitions and its run history (status, dates, row counts, errors) -- on the organization's record page under **Report history**, or through the API with an explicit organization:

- `GET /reports?orgId=ORG_UUID` and `GET /reports/templates?orgId=ORG_UUID`
- `GET /reports/:id`
- `GET /reports/runs?orgId=ORG_UUID` and `GET /reports/runs/:id`

It is read-only. New runs, schedules, edits, recipient lists, downloads (`/reports/runs/:id/download`) and the raw data endpoints (`/reports/data/*`) stay refused for an inactive organization, and its devices, scripts and other records stay unavailable. The unfiltered lists (`GET /reports`, `GET /reports/runs` without `orgId`) keep showing active and trial organizations only.

Who can read it: an active user of an active partner whose role grants `reports:read`. A user limited to **selected organizations** sees only the inactive organizations on their list; a user with no organization access sees none. A deleted organization's history is never shown.

sections.heading: Analytics Endpoints
sections.text: The `/analytics` route group provides real-time operational intelligence beyond static reports.

sections.heading: Time-Series Queries
sections.text:
`POST /analytics/query` executes a flexible time-series query across device metrics.

```bash
curl -X POST /api/v1/analytics/query \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "deviceIds": ["DEVICE_UUID_1", "DEVICE_UUID_2"],
    "metricTypes": ["cpu", "ram"],
    "startTime": "2026-02-01T00:00:00Z",
    "endTime": "2026-02-18T00:00:00Z",
    "aggregation": "avg",
    "interval": "hour"
  }'
```

Supported aggregations: `avg`, `min`, `max`, `sum`, `count`, `p95`, `p99`.

Supported intervals: `minute`, `hour`, `day`, `week`, `month`.

An optional `groupBy` array lets you split the series by additional dimensions.

sections.heading: Custom Dashboards and Widgets
sections.text:
Dashboards are per-organization containers for widgets. Each widget has a `type` and a `config` object that determines what data it renders.

  **Create Dashboard:**
```bash
curl -X POST /api/v1/analytics/dashboards \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "orgId": "ORG_UUID",
    "name": "NOC Overview",
    "description": "Primary network operations dashboard",
    "layout": {}
  }'
```

  **Add Widget:**
```bash
curl -X POST /api/v1/analytics/dashboards/DASHBOARD_UUID/widgets \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "name": "CPU Heatmap",
    "type": "heatmap",
    "config": {
      "metricType": "cpu",
      "interval": "hour"
    },
    "layout": { "x": 0, "y": 0, "w": 6, "h": 4 }
  }'
```

sections.heading: Executive Summary
sections.text:
`GET /analytics/executive-summary` returns a high-level organizational overview including device totals (online/offline), a 12-week enrollment trend, and configurable period types.

| Query parameter | Values | Default |
|-----------------|--------|---------|
| `periodType` | `daily`, `weekly`, `monthly` | `monthly` |
| `range` | Freeform string | -- |
| `startDate` | ISO date string | -- |
| `endDate` | ISO date string | -- |

sections.heading: OS Distribution
sections.text: `GET /analytics/os-distribution` returns the count of active devices grouped by `osType` and `osVersion`, excluding decommissioned devices.

sections.heading: Capacity Planning
sections.text: `GET /analytics/capacity` returns capacity predictions based on current metric trends. Accepts optional `deviceId` and `metricType` query parameters to narrow scope.

sections.heading: SLA Tracking
sections.text:
SLA definitions set uptime or performance targets that are evaluated over a window.

| Field | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `name` | Human-readable SLA name |
| `targetPercentage` | Target compliance percentage (0--100) |
| `evaluationWindow` | `daily`, `weekly`, or `monthly` |
| `scope` | `device`, `site`, or `organization` |
| `filters` | Additional scoping filters (JSON) |

Compliance history for an SLA is retrieved via `GET /analytics/sla/:id/compliance`, which returns period-by-period entries with a status of `met`, `breached`, or `warning`.

---

sections.heading: Report Data Endpoints
sections.text:
The `/reports/data/*` endpoints provide raw, paginated data used to power report views and dashboards. These are read-only query endpoints that accept common filters.

| Endpoint | Returns |
|----------|---------|
| `GET /reports/data/device-inventory` | Device list with hardware details (CPU, RAM, disk, serial number, manufacturer, model) |
| `GET /reports/data/software-inventory` | Installed software list with per-title device counts in a `summary` array |
| `GET /reports/data/alerts-summary` | Alert statistics: counts by severity, by status, daily trend (last 30 days), and top 10 alerting rules |
| `GET /reports/data/compliance` | Compliance overview with device status breakdown, OS distribution, agent version spread, and identified issues (stale devices, outdated agents) |
| `GET /reports/data/metrics` | Performance metrics: fleet-wide averages for CPU/RAM/disk plus the top 10 consumers for each metric |

All data endpoints accept these common query parameters:

| Parameter | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| `orgId` | Filter to a specific organization (required for partner scope) |
| `siteId` | Filter to a specific site |
| `startDate` | Start of date range (ISO string) |
| `endDate` | End of date range (ISO string) |
| `limit` | Page size (default 100, max 1000) |
| `offset` | Pagination offset |

  The `limit` parameter is capped at 1000 rows per request for data endpoints. Use `offset` for pagination when querying large datasets.

---

sections.heading: Reports CRUD
sections.text:
| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/reports` | List saved reports. Filter by `type`, `schedule`, `orgId`, and `ownerScope` (`partner` = only reports owned partner-wide across all organizations, `organization` = only single-organization reports). `ownerScope` only narrows the list: a caller who cannot manage partner-wide reports (organization logins, partner users with selected-organization access) gets an empty list for `ownerScope=partner`. Paginated. |
| `POST` | `/reports` | Create a saved report definition with name, type, config, schedule, and format. Pass `ownerScope: "partner"` (and no `orgId`) for a partner-wide [business report](#business-reports). |
| `GET` | `/reports/:id` | Get a single report with its 5 most recent runs. |
| `PUT` | `/reports/:id` | Update report name, config, schedule, or format. |
| `DELETE` | `/reports/:id` | Delete a report and all associated runs. |

sections.heading: Report Generation
sections.text:
| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/reports/generate` | Ad-hoc generation. Returns data inline. Accepts `ownerScope: "partner"` for business report types. |
| `POST` | `/reports/:id/generate` | Trigger async generation for a saved report. Returns a `runId`. |

sections.heading: Report Runs
sections.text:
| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/reports/runs` | List runs. Filter by `orgId` (one organization), `reportId`, `status`. Paginated. |
| `GET` | `/reports/runs/:id` | Get a single run with parent report metadata and download URL. |
| `GET` | `/reports/runs/:id/download` | Download the run's stored snapshot. Requires `?format=csv\|pdf\|excel`. Returns `409` if the run is not `completed`. |

sections.heading: Report Data
sections.text:
| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/reports/data/device-inventory` | Raw device inventory with hardware join. |
| `GET` | `/reports/data/software-inventory` | Raw software inventory with per-title summary. |
| `GET` | `/reports/data/alerts-summary` | Alert breakdown by severity, status, daily trend, top rules. |
| `GET` | `/reports/data/compliance` | Compliance overview, stale device detection, agent version audit. |
| `GET` | `/reports/data/metrics` | Fleet performance averages and top-10 resource consumers. |

sections.heading: Analytics
sections.text:
| Method | Endpoint | Description |
|--------|----------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/analytics/query` | Execute a time-series metrics query with aggregation and interval. |
| `GET` | `/analytics/dashboards` | List dashboards. Filter by `orgId`. Paginated. |
| `POST` | `/analytics/dashboards` | Create a dashboard. |
| `GET` | `/analytics/dashboards/:id` | Get dashboard with all widgets. |
| `PATCH` | `/analytics/dashboards/:id` | Update dashboard name, description, or layout. |
| `DELETE` | `/analytics/dashboards/:id` | Delete dashboard and all its widgets. |
| `POST` | `/analytics/dashboards/:id/widgets` | Add a widget to a dashboard. |
| `PATCH` | `/analytics/widgets/:id` | Update widget name, type, config, or layout. |
| `DELETE` | `/analytics/widgets/:id` | Remove a widget from its dashboard. |
| `GET` | `/analytics/capacity` | Capacity planning predictions. |
| `GET` | `/analytics/sla` | List SLA definitions. Filter by `orgId`. Paginated. |
| `POST` | `/analytics/sla` | Create an SLA definition. |
| `GET` | `/analytics/sla/:id/compliance` | Get compliance history for an SLA. |
| `GET` | `/analytics/executive-summary` | Executive fleet summary with enrollment trends. |
| `GET` | `/analytics/os-distribution` | OS type/version distribution for active devices. |
| `GET` | `/analytics/anomalies/evaluation` | Anomaly detection quality counts and rates for a `range` of `7d`, `30d` (default), or `90d`. Filter by `orgId` or `deviceId`. See [AI Insights](/features/ml-insights/#measuring-anomaly-detection-quality). |

  All report and analytics endpoints require authentication and are scoped to `organization`, `partner`, or `system`. Every mutating operation is recorded in the audit log.

---

sections.heading: Report run returns `failed`
sections.text: `POST /reports/:id/generate` computes the report and stores its snapshot in the same request, so a run normally comes back `completed` immediately. If it comes back `failed`, inspect the run's `errorMessage` field (via `GET /reports/runs/:id`) for the cause -- most often a configuration problem such as an invalid date range or a scope the caller can't access.

sections.heading: "Organization context required" (403) on report endpoints
sections.text: This error occurs when an `organization`-scoped token is used but the token lacks an `orgId` claim. Verify that the JWT includes the `orgId` field. Partner-scoped users must pass `orgId` explicitly as a query parameter or in the request body.

sections.heading: Data endpoint returns empty results despite existing devices
sections.text: The `/reports/data/*` endpoints join against related tables (`deviceHardware`, `deviceSoftware`, `deviceMetrics`). If devices exist but related data has not been collected yet (e.g., hardware inventory has not been reported by the agent), joins may exclude those devices or return null fields. Check that agents are running and have submitted at least one heartbeat with hardware and software data.

sections.heading: Compliance score unexpectedly low
sections.text: The compliance report flags a device as non-compliant if its status is `decommissioned` or if it has not been seen in the last 7 days. Devices that are powered off or in maintenance for extended periods will lower the compliance score. The compliance data endpoint also identifies `stale_devices` (not seen in 7+ days) and `outdated_agents` (running a version other than the most common version) as separate issues. Review the `issues` array in the response to understand which factors are contributing to the score.

title: Script Builder AI
description: AI-powered script generation and editing with natural language, context-aware tooling, and a curated template library.
headings: "A message is already being processed for this session" (409)

sections.text:
The Script Builder AI is an inline AI assistant embedded in the Breeze script editor. It uses a conversational interface to help you write, modify, and test scripts through natural language. The assistant has access to your device fleet, existing script library, alert data, and script execution history -- giving it the context it needs to generate scripts tailored to your environment.

Script Builder AI sessions stream responses via Server-Sent Events (SSE), support tool approval workflows for device execution, and can directly apply code and metadata changes to the editor without copy-paste.

---

sections.heading: How It Works
sections.text:
The Script Builder AI maintains a conversational session with full context about the script you are editing. When you send a message, the AI can:

- Read the current editor state (code, language, parameters, OS targets)
- Query your device fleet to tailor scripts to specific hardware or OS versions
- Search your existing script library to avoid duplicates or build on prior work
- Browse script templates for common tasks
- Write code directly into the editor via the `apply_script_code` tool
- Update script metadata (name, description, category, parameters) via `apply_script_metadata`
- Execute saved scripts on devices (with your explicit approval)

sections.heading: Session Types
sections.text:
Script Builder sessions are distinct from general Breeze AI sessions. They are scoped to the `script_builder` type and have access to a curated set of tools specific to script authoring.

| Attribute | Value |
|-----------|-------|
| Session type | `script_builder` |
| Streaming protocol | Server-Sent Events (SSE) |
| Max message length | 10,000 characters |
| Editor snapshot size | Up to 500,000 characters |
| Auto-generated title | First message, truncated to 80 characters |

sections.heading: Supported Languages
sections.text:
| Language | Extension | Description |
|----------|-----------|-------------|
| `powershell` | `.ps1` | Windows PowerShell and cross-platform PowerShell Core |
| `bash` | `.sh` | Bash shell scripts for macOS and Linux |
| `python` | `.py` | Python scripts (cross-platform) |
| `cmd` | `.bat` | Windows command prompt batch files |

sections.heading: Parameter Types
sections.text:
The AI can infer and set script parameters with these types:

| Type | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `string` | Free-form text input |
| `number` | Numeric input |
| `boolean` | True/false toggle |
| `select` | Dropdown with predefined options |

sections.heading: Run-As Levels
sections.text:
| Level | Description |
|-------|-------------|
| `system` | Runs as the agent service account |
| `user` | Runs in the context of a connected user session |
| `elevated` | Runs with root/administrator privileges |

---

sections.heading: Starting a Session
sections.text:
1. Open the **Script Editor** in the Breeze dashboard.
2. Click the **AI** button to open the Script Builder panel.
3. A new session is created automatically. If you are editing an existing script, the editor context is attached to the session.
4. Type your request in natural language. For example: "Write a PowerShell script to clean up temp files older than 30 days on Windows endpoints."

sections.heading: Iterating on a Script
sections.text:
The AI maintains conversation history within a session, so you can refine scripts through follow-up messages:

1. Ask the AI to generate an initial script.
2. Review the code that appears in the editor.
3. Request changes: "Add error handling and logging" or "Make it also clean the Recycle Bin."
4. The AI applies updates directly to the editor.
5. Ask the AI to set metadata: "Set the category to Maintenance, target Windows, and add a parameter for the age threshold in days."

sections.heading: Executing Scripts on Devices
sections.text:
The `execute_script_on_device` tool is a Tier 3 tool, meaning it requires explicit user approval before it runs.

1. Save the script in the editor.
2. Ask the AI: "Run this script on my Windows test devices."
3. The AI sends an approval request with the script ID and target device IDs.
4. Review the request and click **Approve** or **Deny**.
5. If approved, the script executes and results are streamed back to the conversation.

  Scripts must be saved before they can be executed on devices. The AI will use the saved script ID, not the unsaved editor content.

sections.heading: Interrupting a Response
sections.text:
If the AI is generating a long response or executing a chain of tool calls, you can interrupt it:

1. Click the **Stop** button in the AI panel.
2. The current response is halted and the session returns to idle.
3. Send a new message to continue the conversation.

---

sections.heading: AI Tools
sections.text: The Script Builder has access to 11 tools organized by function and safety tier.

sections.heading: Apply Tools (Tier 1)
sections.text:
These tools write directly to the script editor. They do not execute any code on devices.

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `apply_script_code` | Replaces the script code in the editor with AI-generated content. Requires a `code` string and `language` identifier. |
| `apply_script_metadata` | Updates editor form fields: name, description, category, OS types, parameters, runAs level, and timeout. Only fields included in the call are changed. |

sections.heading: Context Tools (Tier 1)
sections.text:
These read-only tools give the AI awareness of your environment.

| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `query_devices` | Search devices by status, OS type, or hostname. Used to tailor scripts to your fleet. |
| `get_device_details` | Get full device details including hardware, OS, network, and installed software. |
| `manage_alerts` | Query active alerts to understand what issues a script should address. |
| `list_scripts` | Search the existing script library by name, category, language, or OS. |
| `get_script_details` | Get full script details including code, parameters, and execution settings. |
| `list_script_templates` | Browse available script templates for common tasks. |
| `get_script_execution_history` | View past execution results for a script to understand success rates. |
| `get_script_execution` | Fetch one script execution by ID, including status, exit code, stdout, and stderr -- for runs started outside the current tool call (the editor's Test Run button, or an execution ID from `get_script_execution_history`). |

sections.heading: Execution Tool (Tier 3 -- Requires Approval)
sections.text:
| Tool | Description |
|------|-------------|
| `execute_script_on_device` | Run a saved script on one or more devices (up to 10 at once). Requires user approval before execution. |

---

sections.heading: Script Library
sections.text: The Script Library is a centralized repository for organizing, versioning, and sharing scripts within your organization. It complements the AI assistant by providing a structured catalog that the AI can reference and build upon.

sections.heading: Categories
sections.text:
Categories group scripts by function. Each organization manages its own set of categories.

| Field | Required | Max Length | Description |
|-------|----------|------------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | 100 | Category name (unique per organization) |
| `description` | No | 500 | Description of the category |
| `color` | No | 20 | Display color (e.g., `#E9C46A`) |

sections.heading: Tags
sections.text:
Tags provide flexible cross-cutting labels. Unlike categories (one per script), a script can have multiple tags.

| Field | Required | Max Length | Description |
|-------|----------|------------|-------------|
| `name` | Yes | 50 | Tag name (unique per organization) |

sections.heading: Templates
sections.text: Templates are starter scripts for common tasks. They define a language, compatible OS types, and boilerplate code. Users create new scripts from templates with custom names and descriptions.

sections.heading: Script Versions
sections.text:
Every script tracks its version number. When you update a script's code, the previous version is saved as a snapshot. You can view the full version history and roll back to any previous version.

| Operation | Description |
|-----------|-------------|
| Create version | Saves the current code as a snapshot and updates the script with new content |
| List versions | Returns the complete version history, newest first |
| Rollback | Restores the script to a previous version's content, creating a snapshot of the current state |

sections.heading: Usage Statistics
sections.text:
Each script tracks execution metrics automatically:

| Metric | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `totalRuns` | Total number of executions |
| `successCount` | Executions that completed with exit code 0 |
| `failureCount` | Executions that failed |
| `averageDurationSeconds` | Average execution time |
| `lastRunAt` | Timestamp of the most recent execution |
| `lastRunStatus` | Status of the most recent execution |
| `recentRuns` | List of recent execution records with timestamps and durations |

---

sections.heading: Script Builder AI Sessions
sections.text:
All endpoints require authentication and `organization`, `partner`, or `system` scope. Mounted at `/api/v1/ai/script-builder`.

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `POST` | `/sessions` | Create a new Script Builder AI session |
| `GET` | `/sessions/:id` | Get session details with message history |
| `DELETE` | `/sessions/:id` | Close a session |
| `POST` | `/sessions/:id/messages` | Send a message and receive an SSE stream |
| `POST` | `/sessions/:id/interrupt` | Interrupt an active AI response |
| `POST` | `/sessions/:id/approve/:executionId` | Approve or deny a tool execution request |

sections.heading: Script Library
sections.text:
All endpoints require authentication and `organization`, `partner`, or `system` scope. Mounted at `/api/v1/script-library`.

| Method | Path | Description |
|--------|------|-------------|
| `GET` | `/categories` | List all categories |
| `POST` | `/categories` | Create a category |
| `GET` | `/categories/:id` | Get a category |
| `PATCH` | `/categories/:id` | Update a category |
| `DELETE` | `/categories/:id` | Delete a category |
| `GET` | `/tags` | List all tags |
| `POST` | `/tags` | Create a tag |
| `DELETE` | `/tags/:id` | Delete a tag |
| `GET` | `/templates` | List templates (optional `categoryId` or `category` filter) |
| `POST` | `/from-template/:templateId` | Create a new script from a template |
| `GET` | `/scripts/:id/versions` | List version history for a script |
| `POST` | `/scripts/:id/versions` | Create a new version (save current, update content) |
| `POST` | `/scripts/:id/rollback/:versionId` | Roll back to a previous version |
| `GET` | `/scripts/:id/usage-stats` | Get execution statistics for a script |

---

sections.heading: SSE Event Types
sections.text:
When you send a message to a Script Builder session, the response is streamed as Server-Sent Events. Each event has a `type` field:

| Event Type | Description |
|------------|-------------|
| `text` | Partial text content from the AI response |
| `tool_use` | The AI is calling a tool (includes tool name and arguments) |
| `tool_result` | Result returned from a tool execution |
| `title_updated` | Session title was auto-generated from the first message |
| `done` | The AI has finished its response |
| `error` | An error occurred during processing |

---

sections.heading: "A message is already being processed for this session" (409)
sections.text: Only one message can be processed at a time per session. Wait for the current response to complete or use the interrupt endpoint before sending a new message.

sections.heading: "Session not found" (404)
sections.text: The session may have been closed or expired. Script Builder sessions share the same lifecycle as general AI sessions. Create a new session to continue.

sections.heading: Rate limit or budget errors
sections.text: The AI pre-flight check enforces rate limits and token budget caps. If you see a 429 (rate limit) or 402 (budget exceeded) error, wait before retrying or contact your administrator to adjust budget limits.

sections.heading: Tool approval request not appearing
sections.text: The `execute_script_on_device` tool is the only Tier 3 tool in the Script Builder. If an approval prompt does not appear, verify that the AI's response includes an approval request event in the SSE stream.

sections.heading: Script execution fails after approval
sections.text: Ensure the script has been saved (has a valid script ID) and that the target devices are online and accessible. The AI will report execution results or errors back in the conversation.

sections.heading: Category or tag name conflicts (409)
sections.text: Category and tag names must be unique within an organization. If you receive a 409 conflict, choose a different name or update the existing entry.

title: Scripts
description: Create, manage, and run PowerShell, Bash, Python, and Cmd scripts across your fleet, with a shared system library, bundles, and partner-wide scoping.
headings: Script Execution History on a device

sections.text:
Scripts let you define reusable code that runs on managed devices across your fleet. Each script has a language, a set of compatible operating systems, optional parameters, and a configurable execution context. Scripts can be triggered manually, on a schedule via [Automations](/features/automations/), in response to alerts, or through configuration policies.

The Breeze agent writes the script to a temporary file on the target device, runs it through the appropriate shell, captures stdout and stderr (up to 1 MB each), and reports the result back. Scripts are cleaned up from disk immediately after execution.

---

sections.heading: Script Library
sections.text: The **Scripts** page in the sidebar opens the Script Library, where you manage all your organization's scripts and import shared system scripts.

sections.heading: Browsing and searching
sections.text: The Script Library displays your scripts in a searchable list with columns for name, language, category, target OS, and last run time. Use the search bar and filters to find scripts by name, language, category, or OS type.

sections.heading: Partner-wide vs. organization scripts
sections.text:
A script is owned either by a **single organization** or **partner-wide** — available to every organization you manage. Partner-scope users with more than one organization see an **Available to** picker on the script form: choose **All my organizations** to make the script partner-wide, or **A specific organization** to scope it down. An existing script can be re-scoped the same way — moved between organizations or promoted to partner-wide.

Creating, editing, or re-scoping a **partner-wide** script requires a partner account with full organization access (org access set to **"all"**) — the same rule as other partner-wide policies. Selecting every organization individually is not enough: the capability is the "all organizations" setting itself, because a partner-wide script also reaches organizations created later. A technician restricted to selected organizations can still *see and run* partner-wide scripts, but the form marks them read-only and the partner-wide option is unavailable when they create scripts.

sections.heading: Importing from the system library
sections.text:
Breeze provides a shared system library of pre-built scripts available to all organizations. To import one:

1. **Open the library.** On the Scripts page, click **Import from Library** in the top-right corner.

2. **Browse and search.** The System Script Library modal shows all available scripts with their name, description, language, category, and compatible OS types. Use the search bar and category filter to find what you need.

3. **Import a script.** Click the **Import** button next to a script. It is copied into your organization's library where you can customize it. Already-imported scripts show an "Imported" badge.

4. **Close and customize.** Click **Done** to close the library. The imported script now appears in your Scripts list and can be edited to fit your environment.

Two Windows printer clean-up scripts were added to the library in v0.124.0, under the **Maintenance** category. Both run as SYSTEM, remove printer queues only (ports and drivers are left in place), and take a `dry_run` parameter — set it to **yes** to list what would be removed without removing anything:

- **Delete Printer by Name (Windows)** — removes every printer whose name matches `printer_name` (case-insensitive; `*` and `?` wildcards, for example `HP*` or `*Front Desk*`). Exits 0 when nothing matched.
- **Delete All Printers Except Listed (Windows)** — removes every printer *except* those matching `keep_printers` (comma- or newline-separated names, wildcards allowed). Built-in printers such as *Microsoft Print to PDF* are matched like any other, so list them if you want to keep them. An empty keep list is refused before anything is removed.

Because they run as SYSTEM, both see machine-wide printers only; per-user connected network printers are not visible to them.

sections.heading: Importing and exporting script bundles
sections.text:
A **script bundle** is a versioned JSON file that carries whole script libraries between Breeze instances — or in from another RMM — including the metadata that makes a library a library: parameters, category, tags, timeout, run-as level, and exit-code severity mappings.

**Export:** on the Scripts page, click **Export**, select the scripts to include, and download the bundle as a `.json` file. Bundles are portable by design: they contain no organization, partner, or user identifiers, and system-library scripts export as ordinary scripts.

**Import:** click **Import bundle** and upload either:

- a `.json` bundle exported from Breeze, or
- loose script files (`.ps1`, `.sh`, `.py`, `.bat`, `.cmd`) — the browser converts them into a bundle, inferring the language and OS types from each file extension and the script name from the filename.

The preview shows each script as **New** or **Name conflict**; for conflicts choose to skip, import under a new name, or add the bundle's content as a new version of the existing script. Imports default to the current organization; partner users with full org access can instead import partner-wide ("all organizations").

The equivalent API endpoints are `GET /api/v1/scripts/bundle/export?ids=…`, `POST /api/v1/scripts/bundle/preview`, and `POST /api/v1/scripts/bundle/import` (`{ bundle, mode: "skip" | "rename" | "new-version", availability: "org" | "partner", orgId? }`).

:::caution
Bundles are **unsigned**: a bundle is exactly as trustworthy as the person importing it, and imported scripts can run as SYSTEM on managed devices. Only import bundles from a source you trust. Imports never execute anything by themselves, cannot carry automations or schedules, and cannot mark scripts as system-library entries — but the script content itself is whatever the bundle author wrote.
:::

Bundle format (v1):

```json
{
  "bundleVersion": 1,
  "exportedAt": "2026-08-08T00:00:00Z",
  "scripts": [
    {
      "name": "Clear print spooler",
      "description": "Stops spooler, clears queue, restarts.",
      "category": "Maintenance",
      "tags": ["printing", "windows"],
      "osTypes": ["windows"],
      "language": "powershell",
      "content": "…",
      "parameters": {},
      "timeoutSeconds": 300,
      "runAs": "system",
      "exitCodeSeverityMapping": { "1": "high" }
    }
  ]
}
```

Moving a component library from Datto RMM? [Migrating scripts from Datto RMM](/migration/scripts-from-datto/) maps input variables, site variables and UDF reads/writes onto parameters, variables and custom fields before you import.

Categories and tags travel by name and are created in the importing tenant when missing. An unknown `bundleVersion` is rejected. Bundles are capped at 200 scripts and 20 MB, script content at 256 KB, `parameters` at 64 KB (with a nesting depth of 8), and 20 tags per script.

sections.heading: Creating a script
sections.text:
1. **Start a new script.** On the Scripts page, click **New Script**. The script editor opens.

2. **Enter script details.** Fill in the script name, select a category, choose the language (PowerShell, Bash, Python, or CMD), and toggle the target operating systems (Windows, macOS, Linux).

3. **Write the script.** Use the built-in Monaco code editor with syntax highlighting. The **AI** button (or keyboard shortcut) opens a side panel where the Breeze AI can help generate, explain, or refine your script.

4. **Add parameters (optional).** Expand the **Parameters** section and click **Add parameter** to define runtime variables. Each parameter has a name, type (string, number, boolean, or select), default value, and required flag. Reference parameters in your script as `{{paramName}}`.

5. **Configure execution settings (optional).** Expand **Execution Settings** to set a custom timeout (default 300 seconds) and the run-as context (System, Logged-in User, or Elevated).

6. **Save.** Click **Create Script**. The script is now available for execution. You can use keyboard shortcut Cmd+S (or Ctrl+S) to save quickly.

  Creating and updating scripts requires an MFA-assured session: if your organization or partner MFA policy requires MFA, or your account has a factor enrolled, the save action returns an error until the session has completed MFA.
